summary: A plan of layers PR.0 to PR.7 of prismatic cohomology after Bhatt–Scholze, Bhatt–Lurie, Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze and Anschütz–Le Bras. PR.0 keeps its lemma-level δ-ring prefix (the δ/Frobenius/Witt dictionary, localization, classical completion, δ-stabilization) and adds, at target level, free δ-rings, the Witt adjunction, animated δ-rings, perfect δ-rings, distinguished elements, prisms with their four standard examples, rigidity, bounded and perfect prisms, the equivalence with perfectoid rings, PD envelopes as δ-envelopes and prismatic envelopes. PR.1 to PR.7 are planned at target level: the relative prismatic site with the Hodge–Tate, crystalline and de Rham comparisons; derived prismatic cohomology, the quasiregular semiperfectoid calculation and quasisyntomic descent; Nygaard filtrations, divided Frobenius and Breuil–Kisin twists; the étale comparison for all p-adic formal schemes over a perfectoid ring and the syntomic complexes; absolute prismatic cohomology and the Cartier–Witt stack; q-crystalline cohomology and the comparisons with q-de Rham cohomology and AΩ; prismatic F-crystals and crystalline lattices. Every definition and construction carries its uses, an API outline and unit tests; what other roadmaps own is requested from them, and what no layer of the atlas plans yet is recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Integral addition correction
nodes.statement: Define C_p(x,y) as minus the sum over 1<=i<=p-1 of (binomial(p,i)/p) x^i y^(p-i). The quotient is an exact natural/integer coefficient, then cast to R. Never divide by p in R.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring, possibly zero or with p-torsion.
proofSteps: Use the pinned prime-binomial divisibility theorem to justify each integral coefficient.
Evaluate this fixed integer polynomial in the existing ring. Finite sums, powers and the index involution i->p-i give the API.
acceptance: C_2=-xy and C_3=-xy(x+y).
The formula evaluates when p is zero or a zero divisor in R.

nodes.title: Delta structure on a ring
nodes.statement: On the existing ring R, a delta structure is a function delta:R->R with delta(0)=delta(1)=0, delta(x+y)=delta(x)+delta(y)+C_p(x,y), and delta(xy)=x^p delta(y)+y^p delta(x)+p delta(x)delta(y). Morphisms are unital ring maps commuting with delta. Retain the integrated dictionary ID for this definition; its two equivalences are separate construction nodes.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is a commutative unital ring.
The elementary polynomial prefix is generalized to rings; subsequent prismatic consumers retain the source Z_(p)-algebra hypotheses.
proofSteps: Package precisely the four polynomial axioms as data on R, not an assumed comparison theorem. Delta is not an additive map.
Prove extensionality from equality of the functions. Apply the addition law to x+(-x) and to 1+1 for the elementary API.
acceptance: The zero operation on Z is not a delta structure.
A delta structure alone is not a prism: no ideal or completion is supplied.

nodes.title: Torsion-free Frobenius reconstruction
nodes.statement: If multiplication by p on R is injective, construct an equivalence between delta structures and ordinary Frobenius lifts, with forward map associated-frobenius. CharZero alone is not sufficient.
hypotheses: p is prime. Multiplication by the cast of p on R is injective; the zero ring is permitted.
proofSteps: The congruence gives a solution delta(x) of p delta(x)=f(x)-x^p, unique by injectivity. Choose it pointwise.

Multiply each proposed delta axiom by p. Addition uses correction-identity; multiplication expands (x^p+p delta(x))(y^p+p delta(y)). The differences are the additivity and multiplicativity errors of f, hence zero. Cancel only the remaining factor p.
Both composites are identities by the same uniqueness and ring-map extensionality. The public equivalence does not depend on witness choices.
acceptance: The zero ring meets the injectivity condition vacuously.
A characteristic-zero ring with a p-torsion ideal need not meet it.

nodes.statement: For delta rings R,S and a ring map f:R->S, if multiplication by p is injective on S, then f commutes with delta exactly when it commutes with associated Frobenius. No cancellation hypothesis on R is needed.

nodes.statement: Construct the canonical delta structure on Z with D_p(a)=(a-a^p)/p, using exact integer division. Its associated Frobenius is the identity. This is the integral elementary prefix of the source p-local example.
hypotheses: p is prime. Negative integers and p=2 are included.
proofSteps: Apply FiniteField.pow_card in F_p to show that p divides a-a^p for every integer a.
The identity map on Z is an ordinary lift. Multiplication by the nonzero integer p is injective, so apply the established reconstruction.
The inverse equation gives the quotient formula and, at a=p, D_p(p)=1-p^(p-1).

nodes.title: Delta on integer scalars
nodes.statement: For every delta structure on R and integer a, delta(a*1_R) is the cast of the integer (a-a^p)/p. Consequently a nonzero ring of characteristic p has no delta structure.
hypotheses: p is prime. Do not assume p-torsionfreeness of R.
proofSteps: In Z, verify D(n+1)=D(n)+C_p(n,1) by multiplying by p and cancelling in Z.

The addition axiom gives the same recurrence after casting to R. Start at zero, induct upwards for nonnegative integers and run the recurrence backwards for negative integers. Only additive cancellation is used in R.
Evaluate at a=p: if p=0 in R then 0=delta(0)=1-p^(p-1)=1 because p>=2.
acceptance: This does not rule out some p-torsion in a mixed-characteristic ring.

nodes.title: Descent to a delta-stable quotient
nodes.statement: For a delta structure on R and an ideal I, delta(I) contained in I is equivalent to existence of a unique delta structure on R/I compatible with the quotient map.
hypotheses: p is prime; use the actual ideal and quotient ring.
proofSteps: Replacing a representative a by a+i changes delta(a) by delta(i)+C_p(a,i). Stability puts the first term in I; every monomial of the correction has a positive power of i, so the second lies in I.
Descend the four polynomial axioms. Surjectivity of the quotient gives uniqueness. Conversely, compatibility on an element of I puts its delta in the kernel.
acceptance: I=0 returns the original operation and I=R gives the zero ring.
The ideal (p) in canonical Z is Frobenius-stable but not delta-stable, since delta(p)=1-p^(p-1).

nodes.title: Correction polynomial on a square-zero extension
nodes.statement: Let B map to F_p and use its central action. In the existing square-zero extension B plus F_p, the second coordinate of C_p((a,b),(c,d)) is (abar^(p-1)-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*b+(cbar^(p-1)-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*d.
hypotheses: p is prime; B is commutative; the left action comes from the unital B->F_p map and the opposite action is central.
proofSteps: Expand powers with snd_pow and products with snd_mul. Termwise, a finite polynomial has second coordinate its first partial derivative times b plus its second partial derivative times d.
Differentiate the integral polynomial identity p C_p(X,Y)=X^p+Y^p-(X+Y)^p termwise, then cancel p in Z[X,Y]. This gives partial_X C_p=X^(p-1)-(X+Y)^(p-1) and the Y analogue.
Evaluate these already-integral identities in F_p. No division or cancellation occurs there.
acceptance: At p=2 the result is -cbar*b-abar*d, the second coordinate of -xy.

nodes.title: Delta structures on a square-zero extension
nodes.statement: For a delta ring B mapping to F_p and lambda in F_p, define delta_lambda(a,b)=(delta_B(a),(lambda-abar^(p-1))*b) on the existing central square-zero extension B plus F_p. This is a delta structure with associated Frobenius (a,b)->(phi_B(a),0).
hypotheses: p is prime. The left scalar action on F_p is induced by the displayed ring map and the opposite action is central.
proofSteps: The first coordinates of the four axioms are those for B; zero and unit in the second coordinate are immediate.
For addition insert square-zero-correction. The second coordinate simplifies to (lambda-(abar+cbar)^(p-1))*(b+d).
For multiplication the second coordinates of x^p and y^p vanish, and so does that of p delta(x)delta(y). Use abar^p=abar and cbar^p=cbar to get (lambda-(abar*cbar)^(p-1))*(abar*d+cbar*b).
The power formula also gives the stated associated Frobenius, independent of lambda.
acceptance: The proof works at p=2.
B=Z supplies integer tests; B=Z_(p) with its canonical delta supplies a source-compatible p-local example.

proofSteps: At epsilon=(0,1) the values are inr(lambda) and inr(mu), distinct by injectivity of inr.
Both associated maps send (a,b) to inl(phi_B(a)); ring-map extensionality proves equality.

For the p-local example, (a-a^p)/p lies in Z_(p) by reduction to F_p, and multiplication by p is injective. Reconstruct its canonical base structure, then apply the general family. The integer ring is not silently treated as p-local.
acceptance: The identity between the two structures is Frobenius-compatible but not delta-compatible.
For lambda=1, phi(epsilon)=epsilon^p=0 while delta(epsilon)=epsilon is nonzero, rejecting the rank-one converse.

nodes.title: Second coordinate of length-two Witt addition
nodes.statement: On TruncatedWittVector p 2 R, (x+y)_1=x_1+y_1+C_p(x_0,y_0), for arbitrary commutative R.
hypotheses: p is prime; use the existing Witt ring operations, not pointwise operations.
proofSteps: First work over the integer polynomial ring in four input coordinates. Use ghost components 0 and 1 as ring maps and the first two Witt polynomials. Subtract the zeroth-coordinate pth powers and cancel p only in this universal ring. correction-identity identifies the correction.

Evaluate the variables in R using WittVector.map and map_coeff, then truncate the infinite universal vectors. Surjectivity and unchanged coordinates give the formula for every truncated vector. Zero-padding is only a lift of sets, not a ring map.
acceptance: Over F_2, (1,0)+(1,0)=(0,1), rejecting pointwise addition.

nodes.title: Second coordinate of length-two Witt multiplication

Transport using coefficientwise Witt maps and truncation to R. The zeroth product coordinate follows from constantCoeff as a ring map. No cancellation in R is used.

nodes.title: Delta structures as Witt-vector sections
nodes.statement: For arbitrary R, construct an equivalence between delta structures and unital ring maps s:R->TruncatedWittVector p 2 R whose first coordinate is s(x)_0=x. Send delta to s(x)=(x,delta(x)); recover delta from coordinate one. This is a first-coordinate section, not a ghost-map section.
hypotheses: p is prime; no p-torsionfreeness hypothesis on R.
proofSteps: Given delta, construct the two-coordinate vector. The two preceding Witt formulas and delta axioms give preservation of addition and multiplication. Zero and one have coordinates (0,0) and (1,0).
Given a ring-map section, take its second coordinate. The ring-map laws and coordinate formulas give all four delta axioms.

Coefficient extensionality and the first-coordinate condition prove both inverse identities. The first ghost expression x^p+p delta(x) identifies the composite with associated Frobenius, without cancellation in R.
acceptance: Distinct square-zero delta structures give distinct Witt sections despite identical associated Frobenius.

nodes.title: Units in length-two Witt vectors
nodes.statement: For z=(a,b) in W_2(R), z is a unit if and only if both a and a^p+p*b are units of R.
hypotheses: p is prime; R is an arbitrary commutative ring, possibly zero.
proofSteps: An inverse z*(c,d)=1 gives ac=1. Expanding the first ghost polynomial of the product gives (a^p+p*b)(c^p+p*d)=1. Hence both factors specified in the statement are units.

Conversely, put g=a^p+p*b and use the actual inverses of the units a and g. The Witt vector (a^(-1),-b*a^(-p)*g^(-1)) has product with z equal to (1,0): its second coordinate is g*(-b*a^(-p)*g^(-1))+a^(-p)*b=0. Commutativity gives a two-sided inverse.
Zeroth-coordinate and one-coordinate rules are obtained from constantCoeff and surjective truncation. No p-cancellation or ghost injectivity over R is used.
acceptance: For p=2 over Z, (1,1) is not a unit although its first coordinate is.
Over F_p the criterion reduces to invertibility of a.
The unique vector over the zero ring is a unit.

nodes.title: Localization of a delta structure
nodes.statement: Let B be an A-algebra carrying IsLocalization S B and let i:A->B be its algebra map. Given a delta structure on A and units i(phi(s)) for every s in S, construct a delta structure localize on B compatible with i. No injectivity of i or multiplication by p is required.
hypotheses: p is prime; A,B are commutative rings; S is a submonoid of A.
The image-unit condition is in B; it is not an assertion that phi(S) is literally contained in S.
proofSteps: Compose the actual Witt section A->W_2(A) with witt2Map(i). It sends a to (i(a),i(delta(a))). For s in S its first coordinate is a unit by localization and its first ghost expression is i(phi(s)), a unit by hypothesis. The Witt unit criterion makes this section image a unit.
Apply the existing ring IsLocalization.lift to obtain a map s_B:B->W_2(B). The first-coordinate projection is a ring map, as verified using constantCoeff and surjective truncation.
The composite of that projection with s_B agrees with id_B on i(A), by lift_eq. Localization ringHom_ext proves equality on B, so s_B is a first-coordinate section.
Apply the existing inverse Witt-section equivalence to s_B. Its inverse identities and the coefficient formula give the resulting operation on B. Fraction representatives are not used to define it.
acceptance: The result is a delta structure on the given B, not a new localization ring or a p-torsionfree quotient.

nodes.statement: Under the localization construction hypotheses, every delta structure e on B compatible with i:A->B equals localize. In particular the construction is independent of proofs of the image-unit condition.

Compatibility means equality of delta operations on the image of A, not merely compatibility of Frobenius.
proofSteps: Take the Witt sections of e and localize. Their first coordinates on i(a) coincide, and their second coordinates coincide by compatibility and localized-delta-on-base.

nodes.title: Criterion for extension across a localization
nodes.statement: A delta structure on A extends compatibly to B=S^(-1)A if and only if each i(phi(s)) is a unit in B. When it extends it is unique. Equivalently each phi(s) divides some element of S.
hypotheses: p is prime; A and B are commutative rings; IsLocalization S B specifies i.
proofSteps: Sufficiency is delta-localization and localized-delta-on-base; uniqueness is delta-localization-unique.
For necessity, a compatible extension has associated ring endomorphism phi_B. Expanding x^p+p*delta(x) gives phi_B(i(s))=i(phi_A(s)). Ring homomorphisms carry the unit i(s) to a unit.
The pinned algebraMap_isUnit_iff expresses the image-unit condition as the stated divisibility/saturation condition. It needs no domain hypothesis.
acceptance: In A=Z_(p)[X] with phi(X)=X^p+p, the localization A[X^-1] has no compatible delta structure: X^p+p is not a Laurent unit.
For p=2 on Z plus F_2*epsilon and s=(3,1), phi(s)=(3,0) divides s^2 but is not a power of s. Literal stability is not necessary.

nodes.title: Universal property in delta rings
nodes.statement: Let e be any compatible extension of d from A to the localization B. For a delta-compatible ring map f:A->C sending S to units, there is a unique ring map g:B->C extending f and commuting with delta. Its underlying map is the existing IsLocalization.lift.
hypotheses: p is prime; C is a commutative ring with a specified delta structure; no p-torsionfreeness of C.
proofSteps: Take g to be the existing ring localization lift; lift_eq gives its base values.

Compare the maps witt2Map(g) composed with the Witt section of e, and the Witt section of C composed with g. On i(a), their two coordinates agree by the compatibility of e and f and the base values of g.

Use truncated Witt extensionality and localization ringHom_ext. Equality of second coordinates gives delta compatibility on all B. Any other candidate agrees with g on i(A), hence equals it as a ring map.
acceptance: Identity and composite maps are compatible by the unique extension property.
This proof works even when different delta structures can have the same Frobenius.

nodes.title: Delta of a fraction
nodes.statement: For z=mk'(B,a,s), the constructed delta satisfies i(s)^p*i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)=i(s)^p*i(delta(a))-i(a)^p*i(delta(s)). The coefficient of delta_B(z) is a unit, so this determines the value without dividing by p.
hypotheses: The data and unit condition are those of delta-localization; a is in A and s is in S.
proofSteps: The existing mk'_spec' gives i(s)*z=i(a). Apply the product axiom and localized-delta-on-base to obtain i(delta(a))=i(phi(s))*delta_B(z)+z^p*i(delta(s)).
Multiply by i(s)^p and use (i(s)*z)^p=i(a)^p. The image-unit condition and map_units show the coefficient is a unit. This calculation also proves independence of the chosen expression for z.
acceptance: For the canonical integer structure at p=2, delta(1/3)=1/9.
For phi(X)=X^p+p in the rational function field, delta(X^-1)=-1/(X^p*(X^p+p)); replacing the second denominator by X^p is false.

nodes.title: One-power loss on an ideal containing p
nodes.statement: If p is in the ideal I of the delta ring A, then delta(x) is in I^n whenever x is in I^(n+1), for every n>=0. No finite-generation or Noetherian hypothesis.
hypotheses: p is prime; I is an actual ideal in the given commutative delta ring; p means the integer cast.
proofSteps: For n=0 the target ideal is the whole ring. Induct on n, writing I^(n+2)=I^(n+1)*I and using the existing dependent product-membership induction, retaining membership of the intermediate summands.

For a in I^(n+1) and b in I, the product formula has terms a^p*delta(b), b^p*delta(a) and p*delta(a)*delta(b). By the induction hypothesis these lie respectively in I^(p*(n+1)), I^(p+n) and I^(n+1), hence all in I^(n+1).

For a sum of elements of I^(n+2), the two delta values are already in I^(n+1). Its addition correction lies in I^(n+2) by delta-adic-correction, hence in I^(n+1). This closes the dependent product induction; no assertion that delta is additive is used.
acceptance: For canonical delta on Z and I=(p), delta(p^(n+1))=p^n*(1-p^((n+1)*(p-1))) has exactly order n, so the loss is sharp.
The hypothesis p in I matters: on Z_(p)[X] with phi(X)=X^p+p, delta(X^m) has nonzero constant term p^(m-1), so it is not (X)-adically continuous.

nodes.title: Uniform ideal-adic congruence bound
nodes.statement: If p is in I and x-y is in I^(n+1), then delta(x)-delta(y) is in I^n. Thus the modulus of ideal-adic uniform continuity may be chosen as n+1.

nodes.title: Canonical delta structure on the inverse-limit completion
nodes.statement: Let I contain p. On the existing ring B=AdicCompletion I A construct a delta structure D whose normalized nth coordinate is q_n applied to the (n+1)st coordinate of the input. The construction works without finite generation. Calling B complete for its extended-ideal topology, and uniqueness among all compatible delta structures, use the separate finite-generation theorem.
hypotheses: p is prime; A is a commutative delta ring; I is an ideal with p in I.
Use the actual inverse-limit carrier, coordinate maps and ring structure from the pinned library; do not introduce a replacement completed ring.
proofSteps: Write rho_n for the existing normalized evaluation B->A/I^n. Choose a_n in A lifting rho_(n+1)(x). Coherence of x gives a_m-a_n in I^(m+1) for m<=n, so the sequence delta(a_n) is I-adic Cauchy by delta-adic-congruence.

Use the existing AdicCompletion.mk on this Cauchy sequence. Its normalized evaluation is [delta(a_n)]_n=q_n(rho_(n+1)(x)). The shifted-quotient transition theorem verifies compatibility. Independence of all choices follows from the displayed coordinate formula and ext_evalₐ.

To verify zero, one, addition and multiplication, evaluate at level n and choose representatives of x and y at the SAME level n+1. The representatives a+b and ab represent x+y and xy there. The given delta axioms in A and shiftedQuotient_mk give the desired equations modulo I^n; evaluation is a ring map and carries the fixed correction polynomial to its evaluation. ext_evalₐ gives the axioms in B.
No linear or ring inverse-limit lifting theorem is applied to delta: it is nonlinear. Only the existing Cauchy-sequence constructor and coordinatewise verification are used.
acceptance: The constructor supplies a delta operation on the inverse-limit ring even if the finite quotients do not admit delta structures.
It does not assert derived completeness or that an infinitely generated ideal is an ideal of definition of the inverse-limit topology.

nodes.title: One-step modulus in the completion kernel topology
nodes.statement: If rho_(n+1)(x)=rho_(n+1)(y), then rho_n(D(x))=rho_n(D(y)). Thus D is uniformly continuous for the inverse-limit kernel topology with explicit modulus n+1.

proofSteps: Apply completion_eval to x and y; their right sides are the same function q_n evaluated at equal inputs. The quotient kernels form the neighborhood basis in this topology, giving the stated continuity bound.

nodes.title: Unique classical completion for a finitely generated ideal
nodes.statement: If I is finitely generated and contains p, the classical completion AdicCompletion I A has a unique delta structure for which its canonical algebra map from A is delta-compatible. The constructed operation has the one-step ideal-adic continuity bound. No Noetherianity, p-torsionfreeness, reducedness or separation hypothesis on A is imposed.
hypotheses: p is prime; I.FG is retained for the kernel-power equality and hence uniqueness among ALL compatible structures, not just those already known continuous.
proofSteps: Existence and base compatibility are delta-classical-completion and delta-completion-base. The pinned isAdicComplete theorem identifies the inverse-limit ring as a complete module for I when I is finite.

Put J=I.map(i) in B. It contains p_B. The exact pow_smul_top_eq_ker_eval theorem, transported through normalized evalₐ, identifies J^r with ker(rho_r). The normalization uses (I^r times top)=I^r on A and the elementary scalar-extension identity (I^r).map(i)=J^r; no closure is silently inserted.

Let e be ANY compatible delta structure on B. For x and n, choose a in A representing rho_(n+1)(x). Then x-i(a) is in J^(n+1). Apply delta-adic-congruence to e on B with ideal J. Thus rho_n(e(x))=rho_n(e(i(a)))=[delta_A(a)]_n by compatibility.

The last expression is q_n(rho_(n+1)(x)), hence rho_n(D(x)). Equality of every coordinate makes e=D. This derives continuity of a competing structure from the algebraic estimate and kernel equality rather than assuming it.

For the constructed D, completion_congr and the same kernel equality give ideal-adic continuity with one-step modulus. This is the full classical conclusion of Lemma 2.17; no comparison with derived completion or Lemma 2.18 is asserted.
acceptance: Finite generation is not used in the initial ideal-power bound or canonical coordinate construction; it is used here.
No delta structure on A/I^n is presumed. Such a claim would already fail for Z/p^n.
With I=A the statement correctly gives the unique structure on the zero completion.

nodes.title: Frobenius image units in radical targets
nodes.statement: Let d be a delta structure on A and f:A→B any unital ring map. If p lies in the Jacobson radical of B, then f(phi_d(x)) is a unit exactly when f(x) is a unit, for every x in A. No delta structure on B or delta compatibility of f is assumed.
hypotheses: p is prime; A and B are commutative unital rings, including zero rings; p_B belongs to jacobson(0_B).
proofSteps: Expand f(phi_d(x))=f(x)^p+p_B*f(delta_A(x)). The second term lies in the radical.

For a unit u and radical element r, u+r=u*(1+u^(-1)*r) is a unit by Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot. Apply this first with u=f(x)^p. For the converse apply it with u=f(phi_d(x)) and radical element -p_B*f(delta_A(x)).
A positive power is a unit if and only if its base is a unit: an inverse to a^p gives an inverse a^(p-1)*(a^p)^(-1). This proves the reverse implication without any Frobenius on B.
acceptance: With f the identity on a delta ring having p in its radical, Frobenius reflects units.
The proof never replaces delta compatibility by Frobenius compatibility in a torsion target.

proofSteps: Use witt2-unit-criterion: the two necessary and sufficient units are a=z_0 and g=a^p+p*z_1.
When a is a unit, factor g=a^p*(1+p*z_1*a^(-p)). The second factor is a unit by the pinned Jacobson criterion. The converse is the first condition of the exact Witt criterion.

nodes.title: Delta stability from ideal generators
nodes.statement: For a subset S of A, the ordinary ideal J generated by S is delta-stable if and only if delta(s) belongs to J for every s in S.
hypotheses: p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.
proofSteps: The forward implication is restriction along the inclusion of S in its ideal span.
For the converse apply span induction to the predicate delta(x) belongs to J, keeping x in J as the induction membership. Zero follows from delta(0)=0.
For a sum, use the delta addition identity and delta-adic-correction with J: the correction term is in J because the second summand is in J.

For a scalar multiple ax, use delta(ax)=a^p delta(x)+x^p delta(a)+p delta(a)delta(x). The first and third terms lie in J by the inductive hypothesis, and the second because x lies in J and p is positive. This argument never assumes delta is additive.
acceptance: The empty generating set gives the stable zero ideal. For p=2 on the integers, the generator 2 fails the criterion because delta(2)=-1 is not in (2).

nodes.title: Delta-stabilization of an ideal
nodes.statement: For an ideal I of A, define its delta-stabilization C_d(I) to be the ordinary ideal generated by all delta^n(a), for n a nonnegative integer and a in I. The exponent means iteration of delta, with delta^0 the identity; it is not a ring power or a Witt-coordinate operation.
hypotheses: p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.
proofSteps: Use the existing ideal span of the set of all iterated delta images. The index n=0 includes the original ideal.

Stability and the least-stable-ideal characterization are separate lemma nodes. Idempotence and monotonicity follow from those lemmas, giving the usual closure-operator laws without introducing another ideal type.
For the prime-ideal acceptance test, use integer-cast-delta: delta(p)=1-p^(p-1). The zeroth and first iterates place p and delta(p) in the closure; p is at least two, so their ideal combination is 1.
acceptance: Check the zero ideal and the ideal generated by p; delta-stabilization of the latter is the unit ideal.

nodes.title: Universal property of the delta quotient
nodes.statement: Let B be a delta ring and f:A to B a unital ring map commuting with delta and annihilating I. There exists a unique ring map g:A/C_d(I) to B extending f and commuting with the quotient delta operation. Its underlying map is the existing ordinary quotient lift.
hypotheses: p is prime; A is a commutative ring with the specified delta structure d. No p-torsionfreeness, finite generation or p-locality is assumed.
proofSteps: Delta-kernel-stability makes the ordinary kernel of f delta-stable. Minimality of C_d(I), with I contained in that kernel, shows f annihilates the closure.
Construct g by the existing Ideal.Quotient.lift and use its evaluation theorem to prove g(q(a))=f(a).

For an arbitrary quotient element choose a representative using surjectivity of q. Evaluate the quotient delta via delta-universal-quotient-projection and use compatibility of f to prove compatibility of g.

nodes.title: Free δ-rings
nodes.statement: For a set S, the free δ-ring Z{S} on S is the polynomial ring Z[x_{s,n} : s ∈ S, n ≥ 0] with the unique δ-structure such that δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}; its Frobenius is φ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n}^p + p·x_{s,n+1}. For every δ-ring R and every family (f_s) in R there is a unique map of δ-rings Z{S} → R with x_{s,0} ↦ f_s; it sends x_{s,n} to δ^n(f_s). The Frobenius endomorphism of Z{S} is faithfully flat. After inverting p, Z{S}[1/p] is also the polynomial ring on the elements φ^n(x_{s,0}). The source works over Z_(p); Z_(p){S} = Z{S} ⊗_Z Z_(p), and all statements base-change.
hypotheses: p is prime; S is any set.

The source states the one-generator case over Z_(p) (all rings there are Z_(p)-algebras); the statement over Z has the same proof, since Z[x_{s,n}] is p-torsion-free and the displayed φ lifts Frobenius, and it base-changes to the source statement.
proofSteps: On A = Z[x_{s,n}] define the ring endomorphism φ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n}^p + p·x_{s,n+1}. It lifts Frobenius modulo p, and A is p-torsion-free, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives the unique δ-structure with φ as its Frobenius; it satisfies δ(x_{s,n}) = x_{s,n+1}.

Universal property: the ring map η with η(x_{s,n}) = δ^n(f_s) exists and is unique by the universal property of the polynomial ring; it commutes with δ on the generators, hence everywhere because the two δ-identities determine δ on the subring generated by the x_{s,n} (BS22, proof of Lemma 2.11).

Faithful flatness: write φ as the filtered colimit of the maps Z[x_{s,j} : j ≤ i] → Z[x_{s,j} : j ≤ i+1]. By the fibrewise criterion it suffices to treat [1/p], where the map shifts the polynomial generators φ^j(x), and the reduction modulo p, where it is Frobenius followed by a polynomial inclusion; both are faithfully flat.
acceptance: For S a point and p = 2: δ(x_0) = x_1 and δ(x_0^2) = 2 x_0^2 x_1 + 2 x_1^2, computed from the product rule.
The universal map to (Z, canonical δ) sending x_0 to 2 for p = 2 sends x_1 to δ(2) = −1.

nodes.title: Limits, colimits and Witt vectors of δ-rings
nodes.statement: The category of δ-rings (objects: commutative rings with a δ-structure; morphisms: ring maps commuting with δ) has all limits and colimits, and the forgetful functor to commutative rings preserves both. In particular products, equalizers, tensor products A ⊗_C B along δ-maps and filtered colimits of δ-rings carry unique δ-structures making the structure maps δ-maps. The forgetful functor has a left adjoint (free δ-rings) and a right adjoint, the p-typical Witt vector functor W: for a ring R, W(R) carries the δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius, and for a δ-ring A there is a natural δ-map w_A : A → W(A), the unit, whose first two Witt coordinates are (x, δ(x)).
hypotheses: p is prime; rings are commutative.
The δ-structure on W(R) for R with p-torsion is defined by cofreeness, not by dividing F(x) − x^p by p.
proofSteps: Limits: δ is defined coordinatewise on a product and restricts to an equalizer of δ-maps, since the axioms are equational.

Colimits: by delta-witt-section-equivalence a δ-structure on R is a ring section of W_2(R) → R; the natural map colim_i W_2(R_i) → W_2(colim_i R_i) turns the sections of the R_i into a section for the colimit of underlying rings (BS22 Remark 2.7).

Adjoints: the forgetful functor commutes with limits and colimits and the categories are presentable, giving both adjoints; the right adjoint is W by Joyal's theorem (cited in Remark 2.7). Concretely the Witt vector Frobenius F on W(R) satisfies F(x) ≡ x^p mod p and W(R) is the universal δ-ring over R; when R is p-torsion-free so is W(R) and the structure is δ(x) = (F(x) − x^p)/p.
The unit w_A is determined by the ghost identities φ^n(x) = δ_0(x)^{p^n} + p δ_1(x)^{p^{n−1}} + … + p^n δ_n(x) (Remark 2.13); its truncation to W_2 is the section of delta-witt-section-equivalence.
acceptance: For A = Z with its canonical δ-structure, w_Z : Z → W(Z) has ghost components (n, n, n, …).
The pushout of Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ φ(s)) and Z{t} → A (t ↦ x) is A ⊗_{Z{t}} Z{s} as a ring.

nodes.title: Simplicial commutative δ-rings
nodes.statement: A simplicial commutative δ-ring is a simplicial object in the category of δ-rings; the ∞-category of animated δ-rings is obtained from these by inverting weak equivalences of underlying simplicial sets, equivalently it is the animation (sifted-colimit completion) of the category of free δ-rings on finite sets. The forgetful functor to animated commutative rings preserves all limits and colimits; in particular a derived pushout of animated δ-rings is computed as the derived pushout of the underlying animated rings. Free adjunction: for an animated δ-ring A and x ∈ π_0(A), the animated δ-A-algebra A{x/p} is the derived pushout of A ← Z{t} → Z{s} (t ↦ x, t ↦ p·s); similarly A{J/I} for I = (d) and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r) is the derived pushout of A ← A{t_1,…,t_r} → A{s_1,…,s_r} (free δ-A-algebras) along t_i ↦ x_i and t_i ↦ d·s_i. For a finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p the derived I-complete animated δ-rings form a full subcategory, with derived I-completion left adjoint to the inclusion.
hypotheses: p is prime.
Animated commutative rings, sifted left Kan extension and derived pushouts are supplied by EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation; derived completion by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
The source uses this ∞-category without defining it (Corollary 2.39, Corollary 2.44, the proof of Proposition 3.13, Construction 6.1); the node supplies the definition those uses need.
proofSteps: Define the 1-category of simplicial δ-rings levelwise. Because the free δ-ring functor is a polynomial ring functor on underlying rings (free-delta-ring), free δ-rings on finite sets are compact projective generators and the category of δ-rings is the category of product-preserving presheaves on them; apply animation (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).

The forgetful functor is induced by the functor on compact projective generators sending Z{S} to the polynomial ring Z[S × N], a filtered colimit of finitely generated polynomial rings, so it preserves sifted colimits; with preservation of finite coproducts (delta-ring-category: coproducts of δ-rings are tensor products of underlying rings) it preserves all colimits. Limits are computed levelwise.

Define A{x/p} and A{J/I} by the displayed pushouts; by the previous step their underlying animated rings are the corresponding derived tensor products, which is how Lemma 2.38 enters the proof of Corollary 2.39.

Derived completion of an animated δ-ring along a finitely generated ideal containing p carries a unique compatible δ-structure: apply delta-etale-extension's argument levelwise in the W_2-description, since W_2 commutes with the relevant limits.
acceptance: A discrete δ-ring, viewed as a constant simplicial δ-ring, has π_0 the original δ-ring and no higher homotopy.
For A = Z_(p){x}, the animated δ-ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p is discrete (BS22 Remark 2.37); and A{x/p} is Z_(p){s} with x = p·s, a pushout along an isomorphism.

nodes.title: p-local localization of a δ-ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a δ-ring and S ⊂ A a multiplicative subset. Let T be the multiplicative subset generated by S, φ(S), φ^2(S), …. Then (S^{-1}A)_(p) := the localization of S^{-1}A along V(p) (inverting 1 + p·a for all a) coincides with (T^{-1}A)_(p); it carries a unique δ-structure compatible with the one on A, has p in its Jacobson radical, and A → (S^{-1}A)_(p) is the initial δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) in which every element of S is invertible. The same holds for the localization along V(p, I) for an ideal I, which is the form used for prisms.
hypotheses: p is prime; A is a δ-ring; S is a submonoid of A.
An arbitrary localization S^{-1}A need not carry a compatible δ-structure; the statement concerns its p-localization.
proofSteps: If p ∈ rad(B) and f ∈ B is a unit then φ(f) = f^p + p·δ(f) is a unit (frobenius-image-unit-jacobson). Hence in any δ-A-algebra B with p ∈ rad(B) where S is invertible, all of T is invertible.
T is φ-stable, so delta-localization-phi-stable gives the unique compatible δ-structure on T^{-1}A, initial among δ-A-algebras inverting T.

The submonoid 1 + p·T^{-1}A is φ-stable because φ is a ring map: φ(1 + p·a) = 1 + p·φ(a); localize again by delta-localization-phi-stable. The result has p in its radical and, by step 1, the stated initial property; the comparison with (S^{-1}A)_(p) follows because both are initial for the same property among rings with p in the radical (BS22 Remark 2.16).
acceptance: For A = Z and S generated by 3 with p = 2: the result is Z_(2) with its canonical δ-structure.
For A = Z{x} and S = {x^n}: T contains φ(x) = x^p + p δ(x), which is not a unit of Z{x}[1/x] but is a unit of its p-localization.

nodes.title: The pullback square for W_2 of a simplicial commutative ring
nodes.statement: (1) For a p-torsion-free ring R the square of rings formed by the restriction W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x, the Witt vector Frobenius F : W_2(R) → R, (x, y) ↦ x^p + p·y, the projection R → R/p and the composite R → R/p → R/p of the projection with the Frobenius of R/p is a pullback square: W_2(R) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ R × R : b ≡ a^p modulo p}. (2) For every simplicial commutative ring B there is a pullback square of simplicial commutative rings, functorial in B, with the same two maps out of W_2(B) (W_2 applied levelwise) and with R/p replaced by B ⊗^L_Z F_p. In particular, for a cosimplicial simplicial ring B^• with discrete colim lim, colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ W_2(B^•) is W_2 of colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ B^•.
hypotheses: p is prime. In (1) R is p-torsion-free; in (2) B is any simplicial commutative ring (an animated ring, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).
W_2 is the ring of length-two p-typical Witt vectors with the addition and multiplication of PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate and PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate.
Only the square is planned here. The reformulation of δ-structures as derived Frobenius lifts (the rest of BS22 Remark 2.5) is not: no target needs it.
proofSteps: (1) The map W_2(R) → R × R, (x, y) ↦ (x, x^p + p·y), is a ring homomorphism by the coordinate formulas (PR.0/witt2-add-coordinate, PR.0/witt2-mul-coordinate); it is injective because p is a nonzerodivisor of R, and its image is the set of pairs (a, b) with b ≡ a^p modulo p.

(2) Both W_2 (whose underlying set-valued functor is R ↦ R × R) and R ↦ R ×_{R/p} R, restricted to polynomial rings over Z, extend to sifted-colimit-preserving functors on animated rings; a finitely generated polynomial ring is p-torsion-free, so (1) identifies the two functors there, and the identification extends (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation). The extension of R ↦ R/p is B ↦ B ⊗^L_Z F_p (BS22 Remark 2.5: "Passing to simplicial resolutions").

The last sentence: regard the square as a pullback square of E_∞-rings; on underlying spectra a pullback square is preserved by limits and by colimits, and the totalisation and the realisation are computed levelwise in the three other corners. Discreteness of colim lim B^• is what identifies the result with W_2 of a ring.
acceptance: R = Z: W_2(Z) ≅ {(a, b) ∈ Z × Z : b ≡ a^p mod p}; the pair (p, 0) is the image of the Witt vector (p, −p^{p−1}), and (1, 0) is not in the image.
R = F_p (not p-torsion-free): the underived square fails, W_2(F_p) = Z/p² is not F_p ×_{F_p} F_p = F_p; the derived square holds with F_p ⊗^L_Z F_p in the corner.

nodes.title: δ-structures on completely étale algebras and derived completions
nodes.statement: Let A be a δ-ring and I ⊂ A a finitely generated ideal containing p. For an A-algebra B which is derived complete and completely étale for I, exactly one δ-operation on B makes the structure map A→B a δ-map. In particular the δ-structure of A extends uniquely to the derived I-completion of A, for every finitely generated ideal I containing a power of p.
hypotheses: A is a δ-ring; I is finitely generated and contains p (for the last sentence: a power of p).
Derived I-completeness and I-complete étaleness are the notions of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the classical completion statement is delta-classical-completion, which this node does not replace.
proofSteps: Use delta-witt-section-equivalence: a compatible δ-structure on B is a ring map w_B : B → W_2(B) over w_A lifting the identity of B.

By Elkik's algebraization theorem (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1) B is the derived I-completion of an étale A-algebra B′. By van der Kallen's theorem W_2(A) → W_2(B′) is étale; from 0 → φ_*B′ → W_2(B′) → B′ → 0 and the equality of derived I- and φ(I)-completion (p ∈ I), W_2(B) is the derived I-completion of W_2(B′).
Since A → B′ is étale and W_2(B) → B is a pro-infinitesimal thickening, there is a unique lift B′ → W_2(B) of B′ → B over A → W_2(B); it extends uniquely to B because W_2(B) is derived I-complete.
acceptance: For A = Z_(p) and I = (p): the derived p-completion Z_p carries the unique δ-structure with φ = id.
For A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p and B the p-completion of A[1/x]: the δ-structure extends with φ(1/x) = 1/x^p.

nodes.title: Distinguished elements
nodes.statement: An element d of a δ-ring A is distinguished if δ(d) is a unit of A. Every map of δ-rings preserves distinguished elements. Examples: p ∈ Z_p (δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}); [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) ∈ Z_p[[q−1]] with φ(q) = q^p; any generator ξ of the kernel of θ : A_inf(O_C) → O_C; any generator of the kernel of W[[u]] → O_K, u ↦ π, with φ(u) = u^p.
hypotheses: A is a δ-ring for the prime p.
proofSteps: Definition. Preservation under δ-maps: f(δ(d)) = δ(f(d)) and ring maps preserve units.

δ(p) = (p − p^p)/p = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit of Z_(p). For [p]_q: δ([p]_q) ≡ δ(p) modulo (q − 1), and (q − 1)-adic completeness lifts units. For ξ and for the Breuil–Kisin generator: specialise along the δ-maps A_inf → W(k) and W[[u]] → W, u ↦ 0, under which the element maps to p times a unit (BS22 Example 2.20).
acceptance: δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} in Z_(p); for p = 2 this is −1.
p^2 is not distinguished in Z_p: δ(p^2) = p − p^{2p−1} is divisible by p.
In the free δ-ring on d, the generator d is not distinguished; it becomes distinguished after inverting δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates (BS22 Example 2.21).

nodes.title: Factors of distinguished elements
nodes.statement: Let A be a δ-ring. (1) If d ∈ A is distinguished, u ∈ A is a unit and d, p ∈ rad(A), then u·d is distinguished. (2) If d = f·h is distinguished with f, p ∈ rad(A), then f is distinguished and h is a unit.
hypotheses: A is a δ-ring; rad(A) is the Jacobson radical.
For (1): d, p ∈ rad(A). For (2): f, p ∈ rad(A).
proofSteps: (1) δ(u d) = u^p δ(d) + d^p δ(u) + p δ(u) δ(d); the first term is a unit and the other two lie in rad(A).
(2) δ(f h) = f^p δ(h) + h^p δ(f) + p δ(f) δ(h) is a unit and the first and third terms lie in rad(A), so h^p δ(f) is a unit; hence h and δ(f) are units.
acceptance: In Z_(p): p = p·1 and (−p) = (−1)·p are distinguished.
The hypothesis f ∈ rad(A) in (2) is needed: in Z_(p), p = 1·p with f = 1 ∉ rad; f is not distinguished (δ(1) = 0) and h = p is not a unit.

nodes.title: Local distinguished generators of a prism ideal
nodes.statement: Let A be a δ-ring. (a) (Lemma 2.25) If d, p ∈ rad(A), then d is distinguished if and only if p ∈ (d, φ(d)); in particular distinguishedness depends only on the ideal (d). (b) (Lemma 3.1) Let I ⊂ A be a locally principal ideal with p, I ⊂ rad(A). The following are equivalent: (1) p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A; (2) p ∈ I + φ(I)A; (3) one can choose a δ-map A→A′, obtained as an ind-Zariski localization and faithfully flat, for which IA′=(d), δ(d) is a unit, and both d and p lie in rad(A′).
hypotheses: A is a δ-ring; in (a) d, p ∈ rad(A); in (b) I is locally principal and p, I ⊂ rad(A).
No global generator of I is assumed in (b).
proofSteps: (a) If δ(d) is a unit then p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p shows p ∈ (d, φ(d)). Conversely let p = a d + b φ(d). As d, p ∈ rad(A) it suffices to show A/(p, d, δ(d)) = 0; after a suitable ind-Zariski localization one may assume p, d, δ(d) ∈ rad(A). Substituting φ(d) = d^p + p δ(d) gives p(1 − b δ(d)) = c d; the left side is distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (1), so d is distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (2), and then δ(d) is a unit lying in the radical, forcing the localized ring to vanish (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.25).

(b) (1) ⇒ (2) is clear. (2) ⇒ (3): choose g_1,…,g_n generating the unit ideal with IA[1/g_i] principal; localize each A[1/g_i] along V(p, I) using delta-radical-localization, and let A′ be the product; on each factor apply (a).
(3) ⇒ (1): on A′, p·δ(d) = φ(d) − d^p gives p ∈ I^p A′ + φ(I)A′; descend the containment along the faithfully flat map A → A′.
acceptance: For A = Z_p[[q − 1]] and I = ([p]_q): p ∈ (I, φ(I)) because φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q.
For I = (p^2) ⊂ Z_p: p ∉ I + φ(I)A, consistent with p^2 not being distinguished.

nodes.title: p-torsion in δ-rings
nodes.statement: A δ-ring A is p-torsion-free if its Frobenius φ is injective (for instance if A is perfect), and also if A is reduced. Neither hypothesis implies the other: A = Z_p[x]/(x^p − 1) with φ(x) = x^p is reduced and φ(x − 1) = 0; B = Z_p[x]/(x^2) with φ(x) = p·x is not reduced and φ is injective.
hypotheses: A is any δ-ring. (The source assumes Z_(p)-algebras and uses that δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1} is a unit; this is not needed, because p·x = 0 gives p^{p−1}φ(x) = φ(p^{p−1}x) = 0 and δ(p)φ(x) = 0, hence φ(x) = 0.)
proofSteps: Stronger claim: if p x = 0 then φ(x) = 0. Apply δ to p x = 0: 0 = p^p δ(x) + x^p δ(p) + p δ(x) δ(p) = p^p δ(x) + φ(x) δ(p). Since δ(p) is a unit (the rings are Z_(p)-algebras) it suffices that p^p δ(x) = 0; but p^p δ(x) = p^{p−1}(φ(x) − x^p) = φ(p^{p−1} x) − p^{p−1} x^p = 0 because p x = 0 and p ≥ 2. If φ is injective, x = 0.
If A is reduced and p x = 0: p^p δ(x) = 0 gives p δ(x) = 0 by reducedness; φ(x) = 0 gives x^p = −p δ(x) = 0, so x = 0 (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.28).
acceptance: Z ⊕ F_2·ε with the λ = 1 structure of square-zero-delta-family has 2-torsion and is neither reduced nor has injective Frobenius.
The two examples of Remark 2.29.

nodes.title: Perfect δ-rings and Witt vectors of perfect rings
nodes.statement: A δ-ring A is perfect if φ is an isomorphism. The following categories are equivalent: (1) perfect p-complete δ-rings; (2) p-adically complete, p-torsion-free rings A with A/p perfect; (3) perfect F_p-algebras. The functor (1) → (2) forgets δ; in particular every ring map between perfect p-complete δ-rings is a δ-map. The functors between (2) and (3) are A ↦ A/p and R ↦ W(R); in particular W(R) has exactly one δ-structure for R perfect of characteristic p. The inclusion of perfect δ-rings into δ-rings has the left adjoint A ↦ colim_φ A and the right adjoint A ↦ lim_φ A.
hypotheses: p is prime. "p-complete" in (1) and (2) is classical p-adic completeness; for perfect δ-rings it agrees with derived p-completeness because they are p-torsion-free.
proofSteps: A perfect δ-ring is p-torsion-free by p-torsion-freeness-criteria, and φ reduces to the Frobenius of A/p, which is therefore bijective; this gives (1) → (2), fully faithful by torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence once ring maps are shown to commute with the unique Frobenius lifts.

(2) ≃ (3): for R perfect, W(R) is p-torsion-free and p-adically complete with W(R)/p = R (Mathlib: WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP and the p-torsion-freeness in the same file); conversely a p-complete p-torsion-free A with A/p perfect is W(A/p) by the uniqueness of deformations of perfect F_p-algebras (vanishing cotangent complex, BS22 proof of Corollary 2.31).
On W(R) the Witt vector Frobenius is bijective for R perfect (WittVector.frobenius_bijective) and is the unique lift of Frobenius, giving (2) → (1).
The adjoints: colim_φ A and lim_φ A are computed on underlying rings by delta-ring-category and φ becomes bijective on them (Remark 2.27).
acceptance: W(F_p) = Z_p with φ = id is perfect; Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p is not (x is not in the image of φ).
For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}], W(R) is the p-completion of Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}] with φ(x^{1/p^n}) = x^{1/p^{n−1}}.

nodes.title: Perfect elements have rank one
nodes.statement: Let A be a δ-ring and x ∈ A. Then δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A for all n ≥ 0. In particular, if A is p-adically separated and y ∈ A admits a p^n-th root for every n, then δ(y) = 0 (y has rank 1); in particular φ(y) = y^p (the converse needs A p-torsion-free).
hypotheses: A is a δ-ring; for the second statement A is p-adically separated.
proofSteps: Reduce to the universal case x = x_0 in the free δ-ring (free-delta-ring), which is p-torsion-free. There δ(x^{p^n}) ∈ p^n A is equivalent to φ(x^{p^n}) ≡ x^{p^{n+1}} modulo p^{n+1}. For n = 0 this is the definition of φ; inductively, a ≡ b modulo p^k implies a^p ≡ b^p modulo p^{k+1} by the binomial theorem, applied to φ(x) ≡ x^p modulo p (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.32).
If y = z_n^{p^n} for every n then δ(y) ∈ ∩_n p^n A = 0. The separatedness hypothesis is needed: on Q[x^{1/p^∞}] the identity is a Frobenius lift and δ(x) = (x − x^p)/p ≠ 0.
acceptance: In W(R) for R perfect, the Teichmüller representatives [a] have rank 1: φ([a]) = [a]^p.
q ∈ Z_p[[q − 1]] with δ(q) = 0 has rank 1 without having p-power roots: the converse of the lemma fails.

nodes.title: Distinguished elements of perfect δ-rings
nodes.statement: Let A be a perfect p-complete δ-ring, so A = W(R) with R = A/p perfect, and let d = Σ_{i≥0} [a_i] p^i be the Teichmüller expansion of d ∈ A. Then d is distinguished if and only if a_1 is a unit of R. Moreover (Lemma 2.34) if A is a p-torsion-free, p-adically separated δ-ring with A/p reduced and d ∈ A is distinguished, then d is a nonzerodivisor and R = A/d satisfies R[p^∞] = R[p].
hypotheses: First statement: A perfect and p-complete. Second statement: A p-torsion-free, p-adically separated, A/p reduced (for example A perfect and p-complete); d distinguished.
proofSteps: With A = W(R) by perfect-delta-rings, δ(d) = (1/p)(Σ [a_i^p] p^i − (Σ [a_i] p^i)^p), so δ(d) ≡ a_1^p modulo p; by p-completeness d is distinguished exactly when a_1 is a unit of R (BS22 proof of Lemma 2.33).

For regularity, a nonzero annihilator f of d can be chosen outside pA, using p-torsion-freeness and separatedness. The δ-product identity then reads f^p δ(d) + δ(f) φ(d) = 0. Because φ(f)φ(d)=0, multiplication by φ(f) removes the second summand; invertibility of δ(d) forces f^p φ(f)=0. Modulo p this becomes f^(2p)=0, contradicting reducedness of A/p and the choice of f (BS22 Lemma 2.34(1)).

Bounded torsion: it suffices that R[p] = R[p^2]. If p^2 f = g d then δ(d) g^p + δ(g) φ(d) ∈ pA; multiplying by φ(g) and using φ(d g) ∈ pA gives δ(d) g^p φ(g) ∈ pA, so g^{2p} ∈ pA and g ∈ pA; hence p f ∈ dA (proof of Lemma 2.34(2)).
acceptance: In W(F_p) = Z_p: d = p has a_0 = 0, a_1 = 1; d = p^2 has a_1 = 0 and is not distinguished.
ξ = p − [p^♭] ∈ A_inf(O_C) has unit coefficient of p in its Teichmüller expansion and is distinguished; A_inf/ξ = O_C is p-torsion-free.

nodes.title: The PD envelope of the free δ-ring as a δ-pushout
nodes.statement: (1) (Lemma 2.35) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-ring and z ∈ A with γ_p(z) = z^p/p! ∈ A. Then γ_n(z) = z^n/n! ∈ A for all n ≥ 0. (2) (Lemma 2.36) The δ-ring C = Z_(p){x, φ(x)/p}, defined as the pushout of Z_(p){z} ← Z_(p){y} → Z_(p){x} along y ↦ p·z and y ↦ φ(x), is identified with the PD envelope D = D_(x)(Z_(p){x}); both are the smallest δ-subring of Z_(p){x}[1/p] containing Z_(p){x} and x^p/p. (3) (Remark 2.37) The same square is a pushout of simplicial commutative rings: the animated ring obtained by freely adjoining φ(x)/p to Z_(p){x} is discrete.
hypotheses: p is prime; divided powers γ_n(z) = z^n/n! are computed in A[1/p], A being p-torsion-free.
The printed Remark 2.37 writes D_(x)(Z_(p)) for D_(x)(Z_(p){x}); the corrected form is used (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E3).
proofSteps: (1) First γ_{p^2}(z) ∈ A: δ(z^p/p) = (z^p + pδ(z))^p/p^2 − z^{p^2}/p^{p+1} ∈ A, and the first term equals p^{p−2}((z^p + pδ(z))/p)^p ∈ A. Then induct on n using γ_{kp} = u·γ_k∘γ_p with u a unit of Z_(p): γ_p(z) is again admissible.

(2) The left vertical map of the pushout square is φ on Z_(p){x}, faithfully flat by free-delta-ring, so C is p-torsion-free and embeds in Z_(p){x}[1/p]. D ⊂ C by (1). For C ⊂ D show that φ preserves D and reduces to Frobenius modulo p: φ(x^n/n!) expands with coefficients ((pi)!/i!)·(p^{n−i}/(n−i)!) ∈ Z_(p), divisible by p for 0 < i or i < n, and (x^n/n!)^p = p!·γ_p(x^n/n!) ≡ 0 modulo p.
(3) The pushout of animated rings is computed by the derived tensor product; flatness of φ (free-delta-ring) makes it discrete.
acceptance: For p = 2 and z = x: δ(x^2/2) = x^4/8 + x^2·δ(x) + δ(x)^2, which exhibits x^4/8 = 3·γ_4(x) as an element of C.

nodes.title: PD envelopes of regular sequences are δ-envelopes
nodes.statement: (1) (Lemma 2.38) Let B be a p-torsion-free ring and f_1,…,f_r ∈ B a Koszul-regular sequence on B/p. The derived pushout D′ of D_(x)(Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r]) ← Z_(p)[x_1,…,x_r] → B (x_i ↦ f_i) in animated rings is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to the PD envelope D_(f_1,…,f_r)(B); its formation commutes with base change B → B′ to p-torsion-free rings in which the f_i stay Koszul-regular modulo p. (2) (Corollary 2.39) Let A be a p-torsion-free δ-ring and f_1,…,f_r ∈ A a regular sequence in A/p. The animated δ-ring A{φ(f_1)/p,…,φ(f_r)/p} (animated-delta-rings) is discrete, p-torsion-free and equal to D_I(A), I = (f_1,…,f_r); so D_I(A) is a δ-ring, finitely presented as a δ-A-algebra. (3) (Remark 2.40) D_I(A) is the φ-pullback of A{f_1/p,…,f_r/p}, which depends only on I and is the universal p-torsion-free δ-A-algebra in which p divides I. (4) (Warning 2.41) The Frobenius twist cannot be removed: for A = Z_(p)[x], f = x, the subrings A{x/p} ⊂ A[1/p] for the δ-structures with φ(x) = x^p and φ(x) = x^p + p are not comparable.
hypotheses: B, A p-torsion-free; the f_i Koszul-regular on B/p (resp. regular in A/p).
PD envelopes and their universal property are supplied by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0.
The misprints in the printed proofs (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E9) do not affect the statements.
proofSteps: (1) Modulo p, F_p[x] → D_(x)(F_p[x]) is free over F_p[x]/(x_i^p) = Kos(F_p[x]; x_i^p); so D′ ⊗^L F_p is free over Kos(B/p; f_i^p), which is discrete because Kos(B/p; f_i^{n_i}) is discrete for all n_i by induction. Hence D′ is discrete and p-torsion-free. The maps a : D_(f)(B) → D′ (universal property) and b : D′ → D_(f)(B) (pushout) are mutually inverse: check after inverting p and on PD generators.
(2) Factor the pushout square as two squares; by free-delta-pd-envelope the middle row is Z_(p){x_i} → D_(x)(Z_(p){x_i}); apply (1) with flat base change Z_(p)[x] → Z_(p){x}.
(3), (4) as in the source: A{f_i/p} is characterised by its universal property; the explicit elements δ_1(x/p) and δ_2(x/p) differ by 1/p.
acceptance: A = Z_p[x] with φ(x) = x^p, f = x: A{x^p/p} is the divided power polynomial algebra on x over Z_p.

nodes.title: Completely regular sequences relative to a base
nodes.statement: Let A be an animated commutative ring and I = (f_1,…,f_n) ⊂ π_0(A) a finitely generated ideal. Let B be a derived I-complete animated A-algebra. A sequence x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) is I-completely regular relative to A if the map Kos(A; f_1,…,f_n) → Kos(B; f_1,…,f_n, x_1,…,x_r) is a flat map of animated rings. For discrete A and B and I = 0 this says that (x_1,…,x_r) is Koszul-regular on B and B/(x) is flat over A.
hypotheses: A animated; I finitely generated; B derived I-complete.
Kos(A; f) is the derived quotient A ⊗^L_{Z[t_1..t_n]} Z; flatness of a map of animated rings is the notion of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation / DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
The definition does not depend on the choice of generators of I.
proofSteps: Definition (BS22 Definition 2.42).

Independence of the generators of I: Kos(B; f, x) ≃ Kos(B; x) ⊗^L_A Kos(A; f) and π_0(Kos(A; f)) = π_0(A)/I, so flatness of Kos(A; f) → Kos(B; f, x) says exactly that Kos(B; x) ⊗^L_A π_0(A)/I is discrete and flat over π_0(A)/I (that is, Kos(B; x) is I-completely flat over A); this does not mention the generators. The source uses this independence without comment.
acceptance: For A = Z_p, I = (p), B = Z_p⟨x⟩: the sequence (x) is p-completely regular relative to A.
For A = Z_p, I = (p), B = Z_p: the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A, since Kos(Z_p; p) → Kos(Z_p; p, p) is not flat.

nodes.title: Complete flatness of PD envelopes and of p-adic δ-envelopes
nodes.statement: (1) (Lemma 2.43) Let A be an animated ring and B a p-complete animated A-algebra with x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) such that x_1^p,…,x_r^p is p-completely regular relative to A. Let D be the pushout of D_(y)(Z_p[y_1,…,y_r])^∧ ← Z_p[y_1,…,y_r]^∧ → B (y_i ↦ x_i) in derived p-complete animated rings. Then A → D is p-completely flat. (2) (Corollary 2.44) Let A be a p-complete animated δ-ring, B a p-complete animated δ-A-algebra and x_1,…,x_r ∈ π_0(B) p-completely regular relative to A. Then C = B{x_1/p,…,x_r/p}^∧, the pushout of Z_p{z_i}^∧ ← Z_p{x_i}^∧ → B (x_i ↦ p·z_i), is p-completely flat over A.
hypotheses: Derived p-completion and p-complete flatness are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
In (1) the hypothesis is on the p-th powers x_i^p; in (2) on the x_i themselves.
proofSteps: (1) Reduce modulo p: D_(y)(F_p[y]) is free over F_p[y]/(y_i^p), so D ⊗^L F_p is a free module over Kos(B ⊗^L F_p; x_i^p), which is flat over A ⊗^L F_p by hypothesis.

(2) Apply Frobenius: by pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Remark 2.40) the φ-pullback of B{x_i/p} is the PD envelope of (x_i), to which (1) applies after noting that φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p; then descend complete flatness along the p-completely faithfully flat Frobenius of the free δ-ring (free-delta-ring), as in the source.
acceptance: A = Z_p, B = Z_p⟨x⟩: C = Z_p{x, x/p}^∧ is p-completely flat over Z_p.
The hypothesis is not automatic: for B = A = Z_p the sequence (p) is not p-completely regular relative to A (complete-regular-sequence), and the corollary does not apply to B{p/p}^∧.

nodes.title: Prisms
nodes.statement: A prism is a δ-ring A with an ideal I satisfying three conditions: I is an invertible A-module, A is derived (p,I)-complete, and p∈I+φ(I)A. A generator is not part of the structure. Derived completeness puts p and I in the Jacobson radical. The stronger statements about distinguished local generators and the principal ideal φ(I)A are proved by the subsequent nodes local-distinguished-prism-generators and prism-frobenius-ideal-principal.
hypotheses: p is prime; A is a δ-ring.
Derived (p, I)-completeness is the notion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; it implies p, I ⊂ rad(A).
A prism is not a δ-ring alone, and no generator of I is part of the data.
proofSteps: Definition (BS22 Definition 3.2(1)).
p, I ⊂ rad(A): for f in an ideal along which A is derived complete, 1 + f·a is a unit (DD.1).
acceptance: (Z_p, (p)), (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), (A_inf, ker θ) and (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) are prisms.
(Z_p, (p^2)) is not a prism: p ∉ (p^2) + φ(p^2)Z_p. (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) is not a prism: p ∉ (q−1, q^p−1). (Z, (p)) is not a prism: Z is not derived p-complete.

nodes.title: Maps of prisms; perfect, bounded, orientable and crystalline prisms
nodes.statement: A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) is a map of δ-rings A → B carrying I into J; prisms form a full subcategory of δ-pairs. A prism (A, I) is perfect if φ is an isomorphism; bounded if A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, that is, (A/I)[p^∞] = (A/I)[p^n] for some n; orientable if I is principal, an orientation being a choice of generator; crystalline if I = (p). A crystalline prism is bounded and orientable. A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) is (faithfully) flat if A → B is (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat.
hypotheses: (A, I), (B, J) prisms.
(p, I)-complete (faithful) flatness is the notion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
proofSteps: Definitions (BS22 Definition 3.2).
Crystalline ⇒ bounded and orientable: A is p-torsion-free because I = (p) is invertible, and A/p is killed by p.
acceptance: (Z_p, (p)) is perfect, bounded, oriented by p and crystalline; (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) is bounded and orientable, not perfect, not crystalline.

A δ-map is a map of prisms only if it carries I into J: the map Z_p[[q−1]] → Z_p, q ↦ 1, is a map of prisms ([p]_q) → (p), and there is no map of prisms in the other direction because p is not sent into ([p]_q) by the structure map Z_p → Z_p[[q−1]].

nodes.title: Crystalline prisms
nodes.statement: For every p-torsion-free, p-adically complete δ-ring A, the pair (A, (p)) is a crystalline prism, and every crystalline prism is of this form. Examples: (Z_p, (p)) with φ = id; (W(k), (p)) for a perfect field (or perfect F_p-algebra) k with the Witt vector Frobenius; (Z_p⟨x⟩, (p)) with φ(x) = x^p.
hypotheses: A is a δ-ring, p-torsion-free and classically p-adically complete.
proofSteps: (p) is invertible because p is a nonzerodivisor; A is derived p-complete because it is classically complete and p-torsion-free (DD.1); p ∈ (p).
Conversely if (A, (p)) is a prism then (p) invertible forces p to be a nonzerodivisor, and derived p-completeness with p-torsion-freeness gives classical completeness.
acceptance: (Z_p, (p)): δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}, a unit, so p is distinguished.
(F_p, (0)) is not a prism: (0) is not invertible; (Z/p^2, (p)) is not a prism: p is a zero divisor.

nodes.title: The perfect prism of a perfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let R be an integral perfectoid ring (in the sense of BMS1 §3, supplied by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra), R^♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R/p its tilt, A_inf(R) = W(R^♭) and θ : A_inf(R) → R Fontaine's map. Then A_inf(R) with the Witt vector Frobenius and I = ker θ is a perfect prism with A_inf(R)/I = R: ker θ is generated by a distinguished nonzerodivisor ξ, and A_inf(R) is classically (p, ξ)-complete. For R = O_C with C a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing a compatible system p^♭ of p-power roots of p (for instance C algebraically closed), one may take ξ = p − [p^♭].
hypotheses: R is integral perfectoid: π-adically complete for some π with π^p dividing p (equivalently p-adically complete with π^p = p·unit for some π), Frobenius on R/p surjective and ker θ principal (BMS1 Definition 3.5; BMS2 Definition 4.18).
proofSteps: W(R^♭) is a perfect p-complete δ-ring by perfect-delta-rings. θ is surjective (Mathlib: surjective_fontaineTheta) and ker θ = (ξ) with ξ having unit first Teichmüller coefficient (BMS1 Remark 3.11, supplied by Q0:integral-algebra), so ξ is distinguished by distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings and a nonzerodivisor by the same node.

Completeness: W(R^♭) is p-adically complete and R^♭ is complete for the image of ξ; this gives classical, hence derived, (p, ξ)-completeness. p ∈ (ξ, φ(ξ)) by local-distinguished-prism-generators (a).
acceptance: R = Z_p^cycl-completion, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …): ξ = [p]_q at q = [ε^{1/p}], that is ξ = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + … + [ε^{(p−1)/p}], and θ(ξ) = 1 + ζ_p + … + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0.
R perfect of characteristic p: A_inf(R) = W(R), ker θ = (p), and the prism is the crystalline prism (W(R), (p)).

nodes.title: The Breuil–Kisin prism
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, W = W(k), π a uniformizer of O_K and E(u) ∈ W[u] its Eisenstein minimal polynomial over W[1/p]. Then A = W[[u]] with the δ-structure extending the canonical one on W and satisfying φ(u) = u^p, and I = (E(u)), is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I ≅ O_K via u ↦ π. Every generator of the kernel of A → O_K is distinguished.
hypotheses: k perfect of characteristic p; K finite totally ramified over W[1/p]; E Eisenstein of degree e = [K : W[1/p]].

The source says "discretely valued extension K/Q_p" and "maximal unramified subring"; the perfect residue field hypothesis makes W = W(k) (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E8 records the imprecision).
proofSteps: A is p-torsion-free and the displayed φ lifts Frobenius, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives δ. A is (p, u)-adically complete, hence (p, E)-adically complete since E ≡ u^e modulo p.

E is a nonzerodivisor of the domain A. Under the δ-map A → W, u ↦ 0, E maps to E(0) = p·(unit), which is distinguished in W; since units and δ are detected modulo u in the u-complete ring A, δ(E) is a unit.
A/E ≅ O_K is p-torsion-free, so the prism is bounded; φ is not surjective (u is not in its image).
acceptance: K = Q_p, π = p: A = Z_p[[u]], E = u − p, δ(u − p) = δ(−p) + (correction) is a unit congruent to δ(−p) modulo u.

nodes.title: The q-de Rham prism
nodes.statement: A = Z_p[[q − 1]] with the δ-structure determined by φ(q) = q^p (equivalently δ(q) = 0), and I = ([p]_q), where [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1} is the p-th cyclotomic polynomial evaluated at q. Then (A, I) is a bounded, oriented, non-perfect prism with A/I = Z_p[ζ_p]. The ideal of the prism is ([p]_q), not (q − 1): (A, (q − 1)) is not a prism.
hypotheses: p is prime.
proofSteps: A is p-torsion-free and φ(q) = q^p extends uniquely to a continuous ring endomorphism lifting Frobenius, so torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence gives δ with δ(q) = 0. A is (p, q − 1)-complete, hence (p, [p]_q)-complete because [p]_q ≡ (q − 1)^{p−1} modulo p.
[p]_q ≡ p modulo (q − 1), so δ([p]_q) ≡ δ(p) modulo (q − 1); δ(p) is a unit and A is (q − 1)-adically complete, so δ([p]_q) is a unit. [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor of the domain A.
A/[p]_q = Z_p[ζ_p] is p-torsion-free: bounded. For (q − 1): p ∉ (q − 1, q^p − 1) = (q − 1).
acceptance: [p]_q evaluated at q = 1 is p; φ([p]_q) = [p]_{q^p} ≡ p modulo [p]_q.

nodes.title: The universal oriented prism
nodes.statement: Let A_0 = Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{-1}} be the localization of the free δ-ring on d at the multiplicative set generated by δ(d), φ(δ(d)), φ^2(δ(d)), …; it is the initial δ-ring over Z_(p) with a distinguished element, and d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p. Let A be the (p, d)-completion of A_0 and I = (d). Then (A, I) is a bounded prism oriented by d, and it is the universal oriented prism: for every prism (B, J) with a chosen generator e of J there is a unique map of prisms A → B with d ↦ e. In A the sequence (p, d) is regular and the Frobenius of A/p is d-completely flat.
hypotheses: p is prime.
It is universal among oriented prisms, not among orientable ones.

The flatness of Frobenius asserted here is weaker than the faithful flatness that Construction 6.1 assumes; register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E13 records that gap, and PrismaticCohomology:PR.1 handles it.
proofSteps: A_0 exists and has the stated universal property by free-delta-ring and delta-localization-phi-stable; it is a localization of a polynomial ring, and d is a variable, so d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p and (p, d) is regular.
Completion: delta-classical-completion gives the δ-structure on the (p, d)-completion; regularity of (p, d) persists, A/d is p-torsion-free, so (A, (d)) is a bounded prism with d distinguished.

Universal property: a generator e of J is distinguished (prism, local-distinguished-prism-generators (a)); the δ-map Z_(p){d} → B, d ↦ e, inverts δ(d) and its Frobenius iterates since units are preserved by φ when p ∈ rad(B), and extends to the completion because B is derived (p, J)-complete.
acceptance: The map to (Z_p, (p)) with d ↦ p, and the map to (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) with d ↦ [p]_q.
There is no map from the universal oriented prism to (Z_p, (p)) sending d to p^2.

nodes.title: Rigidity of maps of prisms
nodes.statement: If (A, I) → (B, J) is a map of prisms, the natural map I ⊗_A B → J is an isomorphism; in particular J = IB. Conversely, if (A, I) is a prism and A → B is a map of δ-rings with B derived (p, I)-complete, then (B, IB) is a prism if and only if B[I] = 0, that is, I ⊗_A B → B is injective.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a prism; in the converse B is a δ-A-algebra that is derived (p, I)-complete.
proofSteps: Both I ⊗_A B and J are invertible B-modules and the map between them can be checked to be an isomorphism after faithfully flat base change; by local-distinguished-prism-generators choose compatible ind-Zariski covers on which I = (d) and J = (e) with d, e distinguished.
Then d = e·f for some f; by distinguished-factor-rigidity (2) f is a unit, so (d) = (e).
Converse: B[I] = 0 says that IB ≅ I ⊗_A B is invertible; derived completeness is assumed and p ∈ IB + φ(IB)B is inherited from A.
acceptance: Every map of prisms out of a crystalline prism lands in a crystalline prism.
The unique δ-map Z_p[[q−1]] → Z_p (with φ = id on Z_p) sends q to 1 and [p]_q to p; it is a map of prisms to (Z_p, (p)), and indeed J = IB = (p).

nodes.title: The Frobenius pullback of a prism ideal is principal
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism. Then φ(I)A is a principal ideal and each of its generators is a distinguished element. Both φ^*I=I⊗_{A,φ}A and the ideal I^p are free A-modules of rank one.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a prism.
proofSteps: Write p = a + b with a ∈ I^p, b ∈ φ(I)A (prism: p ∈ I^p + φ(I)A). On a cover A → B with IB = (d), d distinguished, write a = x d^p, b = y φ(d); if y were not a unit, after localizing so that d, p, y ∈ rad(B), the identity p(1 − y δ(d)) = d·(d^{p−1}(x + y)) and distinguished-factor-rigidity would make d a unit, contradicting d ∈ rad(B). So b generates φ(I)A and is distinguished (source: proof of Lemma 3.6, which cites the criterion as "Proposition 3.1"; it is Lemma 3.1).

φ^*I ≅ I^p modulo p, hence globally since p ∈ rad(A); and A → φ^*I, 1 ↦ f for f lifting a generator of φ(I)A, is an isomorphism, checked after base change to the p-completed perfection where distinguished elements are nonzerodivisors (distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings).
acceptance: For a perfect prism the lemma gives that I itself is principal.

nodes.title: Properties of bounded prisms
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) A is classically (p, I)-complete. (2) If M ∈ D(A) is derived (p, I)-complete and (p, I)-completely flat, then M is discrete and classically (p, I)-complete; for every n ≥ 0, M[I^n] = 0 and M/I^n M has bounded p^∞-torsion. (3) The functor B ↦ (B, IB) is an equivalence from (p, I)-completely (faithfully) flat, derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras to (faithfully) flat maps of prisms (A, I) → (B, J). (4) There is a (p, I)-completely faithfully flat map A → B of δ-rings, the derived (p, I)-completion of an ind-Zariski localization, with IB = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d; so (A, I) → (B, (d)) is a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms.
hypotheses: (A, I) is bounded: A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion.

In (2) and (3) derived (p, I)-completeness of M and of B is a hypothesis: the printed statement of Lemma 3.7(2)–(3) omits it, its proof uses it, and without it the statement is false (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E10).
proofSteps: Write derived (p, I)-completion as R lim_n R lim_m of Koszul-type quotients by I^n and p^m; since I is invertible, reduce the I-direction to A/I^n, which has bounded p^∞-torsion by dévissage from A/I.
Apply the bounded-torsion criterion for p-complete flatness (BMS2 Lemma 4.7, supplied by DD.1) to M ⊗^L_A A/I^n: it is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion, giving M[I^n] = 0; pass to the limit over n.
(3) follows from (2) and rigidity-prism-ideal: B[I] = 0. (4): complete the ind-Zariski cover of local-distinguished-prism-generators (b) and apply (3).
acceptance: M = A: recovers (1). For the q-de Rham prism, A/[p]_q^n is p-torsion-free for all n.
For a (p,f)-complete ring R with f a nonzerodivisor, bounded p^∞-torsion of R/f does not give bounded p^∞-torsion of R (unbounded-torsion-example; that ring is not claimed to be a prism).

nodes.title: Properties of perfect prisms
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism. (1) I is principal and every generator is a distinguished nonzerodivisor. (2) (A, I) is bounded, with (A/I)[p^∞] = (A/I)[p]; in particular A is classically (p, I)-complete.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a prism with φ bijective.
proofSteps: (1) By prism-frobenius-ideal-principal, φ(I)A = φ(I) = (b) with b distinguished; φ^{-1} is an automorphism commuting with δ, so I = (φ^{-1}(b)) and φ^{-1}(b) is distinguished. A generator is a nonzerodivisor because I is invertible; any other generator is a unit multiple, distinguished by distinguished-factor-rigidity (1).

Before applying BS22 Lemma 2.34, derive classical p-completeness and p-adic separatedness from derived p-completeness and p-torsion-freeness via DD.1. Reducedness of A/p alone does not supply separatedness.

(2) A is p-torsion-free (p-torsion-freeness-criteria) and A/p is perfect, hence reduced; apply distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings (Lemma 2.34) to a generator d, then bounded-prism-complete-flatness (1).
acceptance: (A_inf(O_C), (ξ)): A_inf/ξ = O_C is p-torsion-free.
(W(R), (p)) for R perfect.

nodes.title: Perfection of a prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and A_perf = colim_φ A the perfection of the δ-ring A. Then I·A_perf = (d) for a distinguished element d; p is a nonzerodivisor of A_perf; d is a nonzerodivisor of the p-adic completion of A_perf and of A_perf/N, N = ∩_n p^n A_perf, but in general not of A_perf itself; (A_perf/d)[p^∞] = (A_perf/d)[p]. The derived (p, I)-completion A_∞ of A_perf agrees with its classical (p, I)-adic completion, and (A, I)_perf := (A_∞, I·A_∞) is a perfect prism with a map from (A, I) that is initial among maps from (A, I) to perfect prisms.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a prism.
In the printed proof "A/d[p^∞] = A/d[p]" stands for A_perf/d (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E11).
proofSteps: A → A_perf factors through φ : A → A, so I·A_perf is generated by a distinguished element by prism-frobenius-ideal-principal.

A_perf is a perfect δ-ring: p-torsion-free by p-torsion-freeness-criteria. A_perf need not be p-adically separated; let N = ∩ p^n A_perf (a δ-stable ideal, a Q_p-vector space). A' = A_perf/N is p-torsion-free, p-adically separated, perfect, with A'/p = A_perf/p reduced, so distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings applies to A' and to the p-adic completion of A_perf: d is a nonzerodivisor there and (A'/d)[p^∞] = (A'/d)[p]. Since N ∩ dA_perf = dN and N/dN is p-torsion-free, (A_perf/d)[p^∞] = (A_perf/d)[p].

Complete p-adically first (derived = classical by torsion-freeness), then d-adically (each A_perf/d^n has bounded p^∞-torsion). The universal property follows from perfect-delta-rings (left adjoint colim_φ) and completeness of perfect prisms.
acceptance: The perfection of the Breuil–Kisin prism is (A_inf(O_{K_∞}^∧), ker θ) with K_∞ = K(π^{1/p^∞}).

nodes.title: Perfect prisms and perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: The functors R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker θ) and (A, I) ↦ A/I are mutually inverse equivalences between the category of integral perfectoid rings (BMS1 §3) and the category of perfect prisms. This is a theorem: neither category is defined through the other.
hypotheses: Perfectoid rings are those of PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; perfect prisms those of prism-category.
proofSteps: R ↦ (A_inf(R), ker θ) lands in perfect prisms by ainf-prism.

For a perfect prism (A, I): by perfect-prism-properties I = (d) with d distinguished; A = W(S) for S = A/p perfect (perfect-delta-rings) and d = [a_0] + p·u with u a unit (distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings). R = A/d is classically p-complete, its Frobenius modulo p is surjective and π = image of [a_0^{1/p}] satisfies π^p = p·unit. The kernel of θ_R is principal: R/p = S/a_0, so R^♭ = lim_φ S/a_0 is the a_0-adic completion of S, which is S; hence A_inf(R) = W(S) = A, θ_R is the quotient map A → A/d by uniqueness of lifts of S → S/a_0, and ker θ_R = (d). So R is perfectoid, and this already identifies (A_inf(A/I), ker θ) with (A, I).

A_inf(A/I) ≅ A compatibly with the maps to A/I by the previous step (R^♭ ≅ S); it is a δ-map by perfect-delta-rings, and it carries ker θ onto I. The other composite is ainf-prism's A_inf(R)/ker θ = R.
acceptance: O_C ↔ (A_inf, (ξ)); a perfect F_p-algebra R ↔ (W(R), (p)); Z_p^cycl ↔ (Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}]^∧, ([p]_q)).
Z_p is not perfectoid, and correspondingly there is no perfect prism with A/I = Z_p.

nodes.title: Tor-independence of perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: Let S ← R → T be maps of perfectoid rings, with corresponding perfect prisms (B, IB) ← (A, I) → (C, IC). Then D = B ⊗̂^L_A C (derived (p, I)-completed) is concentrated in degree 0 and is a perfect δ-ring, (D, ID) is a perfect prism, and S ⊗̂^L_R T = D/ID is concentrated in degree 0 and perfectoid. In particular pushouts exist in the category of perfectoid rings and are computed by p-completed derived tensor products.
hypotheses: R, S, T integral perfectoid; completions are derived p-completions (resp. (p, I)-completions) in the sense of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
proofSteps: Check discreteness and perfectness of D after derived reduction modulo p: B/p ⊗^L_{A/p} C/p is discrete and perfect by Tor-independence of perfect F_p-algebras (Bhatt–Scholze, Projectivity of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, Lemma 3.16; routed to EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1 by the extraction of that paper).

D is then a perfect p-complete δ-ring (delta-ring-category, perfect-delta-rings); ID is generated by a distinguished element, a nonzerodivisor by distinguished-in-perfect-delta-rings, so (D, ID) is a perfect prism and D/ID = S ⊗̂^L_R T; conclude by perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings.
acceptance: For non-perfectoid rings the completed tensor product can have higher Tor: Z_p ⊗^L_{Z_p[x]} Z_p along x ↦ 0 twice.
