nodes.title: Prismatic envelopes of regular ideals
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, B a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra (derived (p, I)-complete), and J ⊂ B an ideal containing IB such that, Zariski locally on Spf(B), J = (I, x_1,…,x_r) with (x_1,…,x_r) (p, I)-completely regular relative to A (complete-regular-sequence). Then there is a universal map of δ-pairs (B, J) → (C, IC) to a prism over (A, I); write C = B{J/I}^∧. Moreover: (1) C is (p, I)-completely flat over A; (2) the formation of C commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (A′, IA′); (3) for a (p, I)-completely flat map of δ-A-algebras B → B′, C ⊗̂^L_B B′ ≅ B′{JB′/I}^∧. When I = (d) and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r), C is the derived (p, d)-completion of the animated δ-ring B{x_1/d,…,x_r/d}, which is discrete and d-torsion-free.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded; B a (p, I)-completely flat, derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebra; J as stated.
C is in general not (p, I)-completely flat over B.

The typical case (BS22 Example 3.14): R p-completely smooth over A/I, B_0 → R a surjection from a (p, I)-completely smooth A-algebra, B_0 → B (p, I)-completely flat with B a δ-A-algebra, J the kernel of B → R ⊗̂^L_{B_0} B.
proofSteps: Reduce to I = (d) oriented and J = (d, x_1,…,x_r) globally using bounded-prism-complete-flatness (4), faithfully flat descent of derived complete modules (DD.1) and property (3), which makes the construction a sheaf in B.

Define C′ = B{x_i/d}^∧ in derived (p, d)-complete animated δ-rings (animated-delta-rings). Show C′ is (p, d)-completely flat over A: push out along ψ: Z_p{z}^∧ → Z_p{y}^∧, z ↦ φ(y), where Z_p{z}^∧ → A is z ↦ d; ψ is the Frobenius of the completed free δ-ring, (p,z)-completely faithfully flat by free-delta-ring. On A' = A ⊗̂ Z_p{y}^∧ adjoin φ(y)/p to get D, where φ(y) = p·unit (distinguished-factor-rigidity), so C'' = B''{x_i/p}^∧ is flat over D by pd-envelope-complete-flatness (Corollary 2.44); D is the PD envelope of (y) in A' (pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), which maps to Kos(A'; p, y), so flatness over A' is detected after base change to D.

By bounded-prism-complete-flatness (2) C′ is discrete, classically complete and d-torsion-free, so (C′, dC′) is a prism by rigidity-prism-ideal; the universal property is that of the pushout, since a map to a prism (C″, dC″) makes x_i uniquely divisible by d.
(2) and (3) follow from the pushout description and completed base change.
acceptance: (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)), B = Z_p⟨x⟩ with φ(x) = x^p, J = (p, x): C = Z_p{x/p}^∧, whose Frobenius pullback is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra.

Over the q-de Rham prism with B = A⟨x⟩, δ(x) = 0 and J = ([p]_q, x): C = B{x/[p]_q}^∧; its base change along the A-linear δ-map B → B, x ↦ x^p, is B{φ(x)/[p]_q}^∧ = B{x^p/[p]_q}^∧, the q-PD envelope of (B, (q − 1, x)) (BS22 Lemma 16.10); this is not the Frobenius twist of C, which is B{x^p/[p]_{q^p}}^∧.
For J = IB the envelope is B itself.

nodes.title: Presentation of a prismatic envelope for a rank-one element
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, d ∈ A a distinguished element and x ∈ A an element of rank 1 (δ(x) = 0). Then for every n ≥ 0 there are elements z_n ∈ A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}, natural in (A, x), with φ^n(d)·φ^{n−1}(d)^p ⋯ d^{p^n}·z_n = x^{p^n}; and δ^n(x/d) lies in the subring A[z_0,…,z_n] of A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded prism; d distinguished; δ(x) = 0. A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} is the derived (p, d)-completed δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining x/d.
proofSteps: Argue in the universal case A = Z_p[x]{d, δ(d)^{-1}}^{∧(p,d)} with δ(x) = 0, which is transversal ((p, d) regular) and in which (x, d) is regular; by transversal-prism-regular-sequences the sequences (φ^r(d), φ^{r−1}(d)) are regular.

Set z_n = x^{p^n}/(φ^n(d)·φ^{n−1}(d)^p ⋯ d^{p^n}); z_0 = x/d. Since φ(x) = x^p, φ(z_n) = x^{p^{n+1}}/s with s = φ^{n+1}(d) ⋯ φ(d)^{p^n}. The numerator is divisible by d^{p^{n+1}} in A{x/d}, and (d^{p^{n+1}}, s) is a regular sequence in A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)}: φ^m(d) ≡ p·u_m modulo d with u_m a unit, so s ≡ u·p^k modulo d, and (d, p) is regular there because the universal oriented prism T = Z_p{d, δ(d)^{-1}}^{∧(p,d)} is transversal (universal-oriented-prism) and T → A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} is (p, d)-completely flat (regular-prismatic-envelopes (1) with base (T, (d)), B = T⟨x⟩ = A and J = (d, x)); A → A{x/d}^{∧(p,d)} itself is not completely flat. Hence d^{p^{n+1}} divides φ(z_n), which gives z_{n+1}.

δ^n(x/d) ∈ A[z_0,…,z_n] by induction, from δ(z_n) = (φ(z_n) − z_n^p)/p and the relation between φ(z_n) and z_{n+1} (Anschütz–Le Bras, proof of Lemma 4.9.4). The source expects, and does not prove, that the natural surjection from A[y_1, y_2, …]/(x − d y_1, y_1^p − φ(d) y_2, …) is an isomorphism after completion; that is not part of this node.
acceptance: For d = p (so φ(d) = p) and x of rank one: z_1 = x^p/p^{p+1} and δ(x/p) = (φ(x/p) − (x/p)^p)/p = p^{p−1}·z_1 − z_1 ∈ A[z_0, z_1].

nodes.title: Regular sequences in a transversal prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and d ∈ I a distinguished element. If (p, d) is a regular sequence in A, then for all r, s ≥ 0 with r ≠ s the sequences (p, φ^r(d)) and (φ^r(d), φ^s(d)) are regular.
hypotheses: (A, I) prism; d ∈ I distinguished; (p, d) regular (the prism is transversal: A/I is p-torsion-free).
The proof uses that p lies in the Jacobson radical and that A is p-adically separated, both consequences of derived (p, I)-completeness with p-torsion-freeness.
proofSteps: (p, φ^r(d)): modulo p, φ^r(d) ≡ d^{p^r}, and a power of a nonzerodivisor of A/p is a nonzerodivisor.

(φ^r(d), φ^s(d)): replacing d by φ^{min(r,s)}(d), which is again distinguished with (p, φ^{min(r,s)}(d)) regular, one may assume min(r, s) = 0 (this reduction is the source's). For e distinguished, φ(e) = e^p + p·δ(e) gives φ^m(e) ≡ p·u_m modulo e with u_m a unit, by induction on m. So regularity of (e, φ^m(e)) is regularity of (e, p), and (e, p) is regular because (p, e) is regular and both are nonzerodivisors of A (A is p-torsion-free and p-adically separated): vanishing of the first Koszul homology is symmetric in the two elements. The same symmetry gives the other order (φ^m(e), e).

The source proves the statement by this reduction and by citing Lemmas 3.3 and 3.6 of Anschütz–Le Bras, The cyclotomic trace in degree 2; the argument above is the direct proof and uses only the listed prerequisites.
acceptance: q-de Rham prism: ([p]_q, [p]_{q^p}) is a regular sequence in Z_p[[q−1]]; so is (p, [p]_{q^{p^r}}).
In a crystalline prism d = p and (p, d) is not regular: the hypothesis excludes it.

nodes.title: A (p,f)-complete ring with bounded torsion modulo f and unbounded torsion
nodes.statement: Let R be the (p, f)-adic completion of Z[f, x_{i,j} : i ≥ 0, 0 ≤ j ≤ i]/J_0, where J_0 is generated by the elements p·x_{i,j} − f·x_{i,j+1} (with x_{i,i+1} := 0) and by all products x_{i,j}·x_{k,l}. (The source omits the products; without them f·x_{1,1}^2 = 0 and x_{1,1}^2 ≠ 0, so f is a zero divisor and x_{1,1}^2 is (p,f)-torsion. With them R/f is the p-adic completion of Z ⊕ ⊕ (Z/p)·x_{i,j}.) Then R is classically (p, f)-complete (it is a completion), f is a nonzerodivisor of R (each M_i has a presentation matrix that is p·Id modulo f), all p^∞-torsion of R/f is killed by p, yet p^i·x_{i,0} = p^{i−1}·f·x_{i,1} = … = f^i·x_{i,i} ≠ 0 and p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = f^i·p·x_{i,i} = 0, so R has unbounded p^∞-torsion. The (p, f)^∞-torsion of R is zero.
hypotheses: The displayed chain is the corrected one: the source prints p^i·f·x_{i,1} for its second term (register entry PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23/E3).
proofSteps: The relations give p·x_{i,j} = f·x_{i,j+1}, hence p^k·x_{i,0} = f^k·x_{i,k} for k ≤ i by induction on k, and p·x_{i,i} = f·x_{i,i+1} = 0, hence p^{i+1}·x_{i,0} = 0.
R/f is the p-adic completion of Z ⊕ ⊕_{i,j} (Z/p)·x_{i,j} (square-zero), whose p-power torsion is killed by p.

Nonvanishing: the ring map from R to the square-zero extension T ⊕ ε·T, T = (Z/p^{i+1})[f]/(f^{i+1}), sending x_{i,j} to ε·p^j·f^{i−j} and every other x_{k,l} to 0, respects the relations (p·p^j f^{i−j} = f·p^{j+1} f^{i−j−1}, and p·p^i = 0 in T) and is defined on the completion because T is (p, f)-adically discrete; it sends f^i·x_{i,i} to ε·p^i·f^i ≠ 0. This verification is supplied here; the source asserts the nonvanishing without proof.

The source asserts that f is a nonzerodivisor of R; for the ring it prints this is false (f·x_{1,1}^2 = 0 ≠ x_{1,1}^2). For the square-zero version: M_i is the cokernel of an injective square matrix over Z[f] congruent to p·Id modulo f, so Tor_1(M_i, Z[f]/f) = 0, f is a nonzerodivisor on M_i, and the completed direct sum embeds in the product of the f-adic completions.
acceptance: i = 1: p·x_{1,0} = f·x_{1,1} ≠ 0 and p^2·x_{1,0} = f·p·x_{1,1} = 0: an element of exact p-torsion order 2.
For (p,f)-complete rings, bounded p^∞-torsion of R/f is not inherited by R; R is not claimed to carry a δ-structure.

nodes.title: The site of all bounded prisms and its structure sheaves
nodes.statement: Let Prism_bdd be the category of bounded prisms (B,J) and maps of prisms. A map (B,J) → (C,JC) is a flat cover when C is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat over B. (1) The opposite category Prism_bdd^op, with the flat topology: the Grothendieck topology generated by the finite families {(B,J) -> (C_s,JC_s)}_{s in S} of maps of bounded prisms for which B -> prod_s C_s is (p,J)-completely faithfully flat (Bhatt-Lurie Remarks 4.1.2 and 4.4.28; S may be empty, covering the zero prism; one flat cover is the case |S|=1), is a site: isomorphisms are covers, covers compose, and a cover (A,I) → (B,IB) has a pushout along every map (A,I) → (C,IC) of bounded prisms, namely (D,ID) with D the derived (p,I)-completion of B ⊗^L_A C, and (C,IC) → (D,ID) is again a flat cover. (2) The presheaves O : (B,J) ↦ B and Ō : (B,J) ↦ B/J are sheaves. (3) For a flat cover (A,I) → (B,IB) with Čech nerve (B^•,IB^•) in bounded prisms (B^n is the derived (p,I)-completion of the (n+1)-fold derived tensor power of B over A, and is discrete), the augmented cosimplicial objects A → B^• and A/I → B^•/IB^• are limit diagrams in D(A); so the Čech complex of O (and of Ō) for every flat cover is exact in positive degrees, and H^i((A,I),O) = H^i((A,I),Ō) = 0 for i > 0 on every object.
hypotheses: Every object is a bounded prism: A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion. Without boundedness the completed pushout need not be discrete, and the statement is not made.

Complete (faithful) flatness is taken in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze §1.2: M ⊗^L_A N is concentrated in degree 0 for every (p,I)-torsion module N (and M ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) is faithfully flat over A/(p,I)). Covers are in addition derived (p,I)-complete, which is automatic for prisms (register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E10 adds the word 'complete' to Lemma 3.7).
Variance: morphisms of the site go opposite to ring maps; the final object of a slice (∗/A)_Δ is (A,I).
Set theory: the category of all bounded prisms is large; a cut-off cardinal κ is fixed as in Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.2, and no statement depends on κ.
proofSteps: Site axioms (Corollary 3.12, first paragraph). Isomorphisms and composites are immediate. For the pushout, rigidity (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal) reduces to a diagram (C,IC) ← (A,I) → (B,IB) with A → B a cover; put D = (B ⊗^L_A C)^∧. Complete faithful flatness is stable under completed base change (requested from DD.1; the source says 'by standard properties'), so D is (p,I)-completely faithfully flat over C.

By PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness (Lemma 3.7 (2),(3)), D is discrete, classically (p,I)-complete and I-torsion-free with D/ID of bounded p^∞-torsion; its δ-structure is the one of the completed pushout of δ-rings (PR.0/delta-ring-category, PR.0/animated-delta-rings). So (D,ID) is a bounded prism and one checks the universal property of the pushout in bounded prisms.

Sheaf axiom and acyclicity (second paragraph). The Čech nerve B^• in bounded prisms is the termwise derived (p,I)-completion of the derived Čech nerve of A → B. For each n, Kos(A;p^n,I^n) → Kos(B^•;p^n,I^n) is a limit diagram in D(A) by faithfully flat descent for maps of animated rings (the source cites it without proof; requested from DD.1 as completed faithfully flat descent). Passing to the limit over n gives A ≃ lim B^• in D(A).
Tensoring A ≃ lim B^• with the perfect complex A/I (I is invertible) gives A/I ≃ lim B^•/IB^•, hence the statements for Ō.

A presheaf of modules whose Čech complex is exact for every cover of every object has vanishing higher cohomology on every object (Cartan's criterion; requested from E2 in the form needed for a site with fibre products).
acceptance: For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and the cover Z_p → W(F̄_p), the Čech complex W(F̄_p) → W(F̄_p ⊗ F̄_p) → … is exact in positive degrees with H^0 = Z_p.
The variance of the opposite category and the explicit structure maps of O and Ō are checked on a composite of two covers.
Ordinary site cohomology of a singular X is not identified here with the derived theory of PR.2.

nodes.title: The relative prismatic site (X/A)_Δ
nodes.statement: Fix a bounded prism (A,I) and a p-adic formal scheme X over Spf(A/I). The prismatic site (X/A)_Δ has as objects the triples (B, g, f): a bounded prism (B,IB) with a map of prisms g : (A,I) → (B,IB), and a map f : Spf(B/IB) → X over Spf(A/I). A morphism (C,g',f') → (B,g,f) is a map of prisms (B,IB) → (C,IC) under (A,I) whose reduction Spf(C/IC) → Spf(B/IB) commutes with the maps to X. It is a flat cover when (B,IB) → (C,IC) is a faithfully flat map of prisms. The topology is the flat topology generated by the finite families {(B,g,f) ← (C_s,g_s,f_s)} with B → ∏_s C_s (p,I)-completely faithfully flat (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.1.2). The structure sheaf O_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras; the reduced structure sheaf Ō_Δ : (B,g,f) ↦ B/IB is a sheaf of O(X)-algebras, and Ō_Δ = O_Δ ⊗_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes (R/A)_Δ, with objects (B → B/IB ← R). Equivalently, with (∗/A)_Δ the slice of the site of all bounded prisms over (A,I) and h_X the presheaf (B,IB) ↦ Hom_{A/I}(Spf(B/IB), X) on it, h_X is a sheaf and (X/A)_Δ is the category of pairs ((B,IB), η ∈ h_X(B,IB)) with the induced topology, so Shv((X/A)_Δ) = Shv((∗/A)_Δ)_{/h_X}. A map X → Y of p-adic formal schemes over A/I induces h_X → h_Y and hence a morphism of topoi Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv((Y/A)_Δ).
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism; formal schemes over A/I carry the p-adic topology.

The definition is made for every p-adic formal scheme X over A/I; the comparison theorems of this stage assume X smooth over A/I (Remark 4.2), and for general X the cohomology of this site is not the derived theory of PR.2.
By rigidity (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal) the prism ideal of every object is IB, so only B, g and f are data.

In the affine case the algebraic language of Notation 4.16 is used: an object mapping to every other object of (R/A)_Δ, viewed as rings, is called weakly initial (it is weakly final in the site). The text of Notation 4.16 is read with the corrections of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E12 (R = A/I; Spf in place of Spec).
proofSteps: Definition 4.1: the objects, morphisms and covers are as stated; the site axioms and the sheaf property of O_Δ and Ō_Δ are inherited from the site of all bounded prisms (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf), because pushouts of objects of (X/A)_Δ along covers are computed on underlying prisms and carry the induced map to X.

Remark 4.3: h_X is a sheaf on (∗/A)_Δ. For a flat cover (B,IB) → (C,IC) with Čech nerve C^•, B/IB → C^•/IC^• is a limit diagram of p-complete rings by the reduced form of Corollary 3.12, and maps of formal schemes Spf(−) → X glue along p-completely faithfully flat covers (fpqc descent for morphisms, on the reductions modulo p^n; requested from SF.4).

The identification of (X/A)_Δ with the category of elements of h_X is a direct unwinding; Shv of a category of elements of a sheaf is the slice topos (requested from E2 with the localisation of a topos at an object).
Functoriality: X → Y gives h_X → h_Y and the morphism of slice topoi; for X = Spf(R), Y = Spf(R') and R' → R the functor (R/A)_Δ → (R'/A)_Δ composes the structure map with R' → R.
acceptance: For X = Spf(A/I) the site is the slice (∗/A)_Δ of all bounded prisms over (A,I), with final object (A,I).
For a perfect prism (A,I) and X = Spf(A/I⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) the object given by the perfect prism of the perfectoid ring A/I⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ lies in the site.
A triple with prism ideal J ≠ IB does not occur, by rigidity.

nodes.title: The morphism from the prismatic topos to the étale topos
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I and let fSch_{/X} be the category of p-adic formal schemes with an adic map to X, with the étale topology. The functor μ : (X/A)_Δ → fSch_{/X}, (B,g,f) ↦ (Spf(B/IB) → X), is cocontinuous. It therefore induces a morphism of topoi μ_X : Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(fSch_{/X}); composing with the restriction Shv(fSch_{/X}) → Shv(X_ét) gives ν_X : Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(X_ét). For an étale map U → X the site (U/A)_Δ is the slice of (X/A)_Δ over U, restriction to it preserves sheaves, and for every sheaf F on (X/A)_Δ one has (ν_* F)(U → X) = H^0((U/A)_Δ, F|_{(U/A)_Δ}); for a sheaf of abelian groups, R^iν_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^i((U/A)_Δ, F).
hypotheses: X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I (the construction only uses that X is a p-adic formal scheme; smoothness is the standing hypothesis of §4.1).
The étale site of a p-adic formal scheme is that of its reduction modulo p; it is requested from SF.2.
μ is cocontinuous, not continuous: only the pushforward ν_* and its derived functors are used.
proofSteps: Cocontinuity (Construction 4.4). Given an object (B,g,f) and an étale cover of Spf(B/IB), refine it to a p-completely étale cover B/IB → C̄. By Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18 (étale extension of δ-structures, with Elkik algebraization; stage PR.0 and DD.1) there is a unique (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra C with C/IC = C̄; each (C_i,IC_i) is a bounded prism by PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness, and the finite family {(B,IB) → (C_i,IC_i)} is a covering family of the flat topology (B → ∏ C_i is completely faithfully flat) lying in the pulled-back sieve.
A cocontinuous functor of sites induces a morphism of topoi whose pushforward is the right Kan extension (Stacks, Tag 00XO; in Mathlib the pushforward of a cocontinuous functor).

For étale U → X the objects of (X/A)_Δ whose map to X factors through U form the slice over the sheaf h_U, which is (U/A)_Δ; the formula for ν_* is the right Kan extension formula evaluated on U, and the description of R^iν_* follows by sheafifying.
acceptance: For X = Spf(R) and a p-completely étale R → S, (ν_*O_Δ)(Spf S) = H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ).
For U = X the formula gives ν_*F(X) = H^0((X/A)_Δ, F), the global sections.
The lift of a Zariski cover Spf(R_f) of Spf(B/IB) is the (p,I)-completed localisation of B at a lift of f, with its unique δ-structure.

nodes.title: Relative prismatic cohomology Δ_{X/A}
nodes.statement: For a bounded prism (A,I) and a smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I put Δ_{X/A} := Rν_*O_Δ ∈ D(X_ét, A) and RΓ_Δ(X/A) := RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = RΓ(X_ét, Δ_{X/A}) ∈ D(A). For a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R put Δ_{R/A} := RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = RΓ(Spf(R), Δ_{Spf(R)/A}) ∈ D(A). These are commutative algebra objects (E_∞-A-algebras), derived (p,I)-complete, concentrated in cohomological degrees ≥ 0, and equipped with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism (PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology). Functoriality: a map X → Y over A/I gives Δ_{Y/A} → Rf_*Δ_{X/A}; a map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (B,IB) with a compatible map of formal schemes gives a map from Δ_{X/A} to the restriction of scalars of Δ_{X'/B}; every object (B,g,f) of (R/A)_Δ gives an evaluation map Δ_{R/A} → B of E_∞-A-algebras, and Δ_{R/A} is the limit of O_Δ over a Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology).
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism.

X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I; R is a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra: R is derived p-complete and R ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p is a smooth (A/I)/p-algebra in degree 0. For other X the same formula defines site cohomology, which this stage uses only for p-completely syntomic algebras (PR.1/crystalline-comparison-syntomic, PR.1/p-torsion-free-h0-syntomic).
The commutative algebra structure is in the derived ∞-category; in a 1-categorical derived category only the commutative ring structure on cohomology and the cosimplicial ring models are visible.
Derived (p,I)-completeness follows because Δ_{R/A} is a limit of the (p,I)-complete rings B.
proofSteps: Definition: Construction 4.9 (first displayed formula) and Notation 4.16. O_Δ is a sheaf of rings on (X/A)_Δ (PR.1/relative-prismatic-site), so Rν_*O_Δ and RΓ are defined and are commutative algebra objects; RΓ(X_ét, Rν_*O_Δ) = RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) by the Leray composition for the morphism of topoi ν (PR.1/prismatic-to-etale-morphism).

Coconnectivity is automatic for the cohomology of a sheaf of modules. Completeness: for f ∈ (p,I), RHom_A(A[1/f], RΓ(O_Δ)) = RΓ of the presheaf B ↦ RHom_A(A[1/f], RΓ(B,O)) = RHom_A(A[1/f], B) = 0, using the acyclicity of O on objects (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3)) and derived completeness of each B (DD.1). The Frobenius is added by PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology.

Functoriality in X is the functoriality of the slice topoi (Remark 4.3); functoriality in the prism sends (C,g',f') over (B,IB) to itself viewed over (A,I); evaluation at an object is restriction of global sections.
The Frobenius comes from the endomorphism φ of the sheaf O_Δ (PR.1/frobenius-on-prismatic-cohomology).
acceptance: Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A, with the identity Frobenius-semilinear structure φ_A.
For R = A/I⟨X⟩ the complex Δ_{R/A} is not concentrated in degree 0: H^1(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1} ≠ 0.
For a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) (PR.1/crystalline-comparison).

nodes.title: Hodge–Tate cohomology Δ̄_{X/A} and Breuil–Kisin twists of A/I-modules
nodes.statement: For (A,I) bounded and X smooth over A/I put Δ̄_{X/A} := Rν_*Ō_Δ ∈ D(X_ét, O_X), a commutative algebra object with structure map O_X → Δ̄_{X/A}, and for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R put Δ̄_{R/A} := RΓ((R/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) ∈ D(R). Then Δ̄_{X/A} ≃ Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I and Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For an A/I-module M and i ∈ Z put M{i} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗i}, where I/I² is an invertible A/I-module and negative powers are powers of the dual; for i ≥ 0, M{i} = M ⊗_{A/I} I^i/I^{i+1}. A generator d of I identifies M{i} with M through d^i. For every i ≥ 0 there is a distinguished triangle Δ̄_{X/A}{i+1} → Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{X/A}{i}.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra.

The twist M{i} of this stage is the twist of A/I-modules of Bhatt–Scholze Construction 4.9. The Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of the prism itself, with A{1}/I = I/I², belong to PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist and are not used here.
The Hodge–Tate comparison carries the twist {−i} on Ω^i and no Frobenius twist.
proofSteps: Definition: Construction 4.9. Ō_Δ is a sheaf of O(X)-algebras, so Rν_*Ō_Δ is a commutative algebra object of D(X_ét, O_X).

The formula Δ̄ ≃ Δ ⊗^L_A A/I: on each object B/IB = B ⊗^L_A A/I because I ⊗_A B → B is injective with image IB (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal). Since A/I is a perfect A-complex (I is invertible), − ⊗^L_A A/I commutes with Rν_* and with RΓ.
The triangle is Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A applied to the exact sequence 0 → I^{i+1}/I^{i+2} → I^i/I^{i+2} → I^i/I^{i+1} → 0 of A-modules, using I^j/I^{j+1} = (I/I²)^{⊗j} and Δ ⊗^L_A I^j/I^{j+1} = Δ̄{j}.
Twists: I is an invertible A-module (PR.0/prism), so I/I² = I ⊗_A A/I is invertible over A/I and the tensor powers are defined for all integers.
acceptance: For an oriented prism (A,(d)) every twist M{i} is identified with M by d^i, and the triangle for i = 0 is the reduction of Δ →d Δ modulo d².
For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), I/I² is free on the class of [p]_q.

nodes.title: Flat, étale, Nisnevich and Zariski topologies compute the same cohomology
nodes.statement: On the category underlying (X/A)_Δ consider the topologies whose covers are the maps of prisms (B,IB) → (C,IC) that are (p,I)-completely étale covers, Nisnevich covers or Zariski covers. There are morphisms of topoi Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,ét}) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,Nis}) → Shv((X/A)_{Δ,Zar}), and the derived pushforward along each of them carries O_Δ to O_Δ and Ō_Δ to Ō_Δ. Hence RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) and RΓ((X/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) may be computed in any of the four topologies. The same holds for coefficients in a crystal in (p,I)-complete complexes, that is an assignment (B,g,f) ↦ M(B) ∈ D_{(p,I)-comp}(B) compatible with completed base change.
hypotheses: (A,I) is bounded and X is a p-adic formal scheme over A/I.
Zariski, Nisnevich and étale covers of Spf(B) lift uniquely to (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebras, so each of these topologies is coarser than the flat topology.
Only the two structure sheaves and crystals are compared; arbitrary sheaves on the four sites have different cohomology.
proofSteps: Each of the coarser topologies has covers that are flat covers, so the identity functor is a continuous morphism of sites and induces the displayed morphisms of topoi (Remark 4.5).

For the derived pushforward ε_* from the flat to a coarser topology, R^iε_*O_Δ is the sheafification of (B,g,f) ↦ H^i((B,g,f), O_Δ) in the flat topology of the slice, and this slice is a slice of the site of all bounded prisms; by PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3) these groups vanish for i > 0 and equal B for i = 0. The same argument applies to Ō_Δ.
For crystals one uses (p,I)-completely faithfully flat descent for D_{(p,I)-comp}(−) (requested from DD.1) in place of Corollary 3.12.
acceptance: For R = A/I the cohomology of O_Δ in the Zariski topology of ((A/I)/A)_Δ is A in degree 0.
The étale-topology version is the one used when a statement is checked on an étale chart of X.

nodes.title: Weakly initial objects and Čech–Alexander complexes
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. A presentation is a surjection B_0 → R of A-algebras with B_0 the (p,I)-completion of a polynomial A-algebra A[x_s : s ∈ S]. Put B := Free_{δ,A}(B_0)^∧, the (p,I)-completed free δ-A-algebra on B_0; J_0 := ker(B_0 → R); R′ := (B/J_0B)^∧ (p-adic completion), a p-completely ind-smooth A/I-algebra; and C := B{J/I}^∧, the prismatic envelope over (A,I) of the δ-pair (B, J), J = ker(B → R′). Then (C → C/IC ← R) is an object of (R/A)_Δ, C is (p,I)-completely flat over A, and the object is weakly initial: it admits a map to every object of (R/A)_Δ (in the algebraic language). The construction is functorial in the presentation and carries completed tensor products of presentations over A to coproducts in (R/A)_Δ (algebraic language; products in the site). The Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object of the presentation is (C^• → C^•/IC^• ← R), obtained by applying the construction to the (p,I)-completed Čech nerve B_0^• of A → B_0 with its surjections B_0^n → R; it is the Čech nerve of (C^0 → C^0/IC^0 ← R), and C^n is the envelope of the completed (n+1)-fold tensor power of B over A along the kernel of the map to R′-type quotients. Taking B_0 = A[x_r : r ∈ R]^∧ with x_r ↦ r gives a strictly functorial cosimplicial δ-A-algebra C^•_R and cochain complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ); this functorial choice does not commute with base change in the prism. For R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ the choice B_0 = A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ gives a cosimplicial δ-A-algebra that commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. The same construction applies verbatim to a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra, because the hypothesis of the envelope theorem still holds (Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8).

Proposition 3.13 is stated for an ideal that is Zariski-locally (I, x_1,…,x_r) with a finite sequence completely regular relative to A. For a presentation with finitely many variables this is Example 3.14. For infinitely many variables (in particular the functorial choice S = R) the ideal J is a filtered union of such ideals, and the envelope exists and is completely flat as the completed filtered colimit of the envelopes; this step is not in the printed text and is recorded as source issue PrismaticCohomology/E12.
Derived and classical (p,I)-completions of B_0, B and of the tensor powers agree because A is bounded (Lemma 3.7).
proofSteps: Envelope. For a finite set S' ⊂ S with A[x_s : s ∈ S']^∧ → R surjective, choose lifts f_s of the images of x_s for s ∉ S'. Then J_0 is generated by ker(A[x_{S'}]^∧ → R), which is Zariski-locally (I, a regular sequence relative to A) since R is p-completely smooth, and by the elements x_s − f_s. For finite S'' ⊃ S' the ideal J_{S''} ⊂ B generated by the first kernel and the x_s − f_s, s ∈ S'' \ S', satisfies the hypothesis of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (B is completely flat over A[x_{S''}]^∧). The envelope of (B,J) is the (p,I)-completed colimit of the envelopes B{J_{S''}/I}^∧; it has the universal property and is (p,I)-completely flat over A.
Object of the site: C/IC receives R′, hence R; (C,IC) is a bounded prism over (A,I) by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes and PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness.

Weak initiality (Construction 4.17). Given (D → D/ID ← R), lift R → D/ID to an A-algebra map B_0 → D, possible since B_0 is a completed polynomial algebra and D is (p,I)-complete; extend uniquely to a δ-A-algebra map B → D by the universal property of free δ-rings (PR.0/free-delta-ring); it carries J into ID, so it factors uniquely through C by the universal property of the envelope; the induced map on reductions is compatible with the maps from R.

Coproducts and Čech nerve: the universal properties of Free_δ and of the envelope show that the construction sends B_0 ⊗̂_A B_0' (with the induced surjection to R) to the coproduct; hence applying it to the Čech nerve of A → B_0 gives the Čech nerve of the object C^0.

Functorial choice and Remark 4.19: for S = R the assignment R ↦ (B_0 → R) is functorial; for the completed polynomial ring the presentation A⟨X⟩ → A/I⟨X⟩ is compatible with base change, and so is the envelope by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (2).
acceptance: For R = A/I and the empty set of variables, C^• is the constant cosimplicial ring A.
For R = A/I⟨X⟩ and B_0 = A⟨X⟩: C^0 = A{X}^∧ and C^1 = A{X,Y}{(X−Y)/I}^∧.
For a crystalline prism the same recipe with PD envelopes in place of prismatic envelopes computes crystalline cohomology, and the two are related by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope.

nodes.title: Čech–Alexander complexes compute prismatic cohomology; independence of the presentation
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R. Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} → lim_Δ C^•/IC^• are isomorphisms in D(A) (of E_∞-A-algebras), so Δ_{R/A} is computed by the cochain complex of C^• and Δ̄_{R/A} by that of C^•/IC^•. For two presentations B_0 → R and B_0′ → R the presentation B_0 ⊗̂_A B_0′ → R receives maps from both, and the induced maps of cosimplicial rings are compatible with the identifications with Δ_{R/A}; hence the isomorphism class and the comparison isomorphisms do not depend on the presentation (the category of presentations is sifted). In particular the strictly functorial complex C^•((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) represents the functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A}.
hypotheses: (A,I) bounded; R p-completely smooth over A/I (or p-completely syntomic, with the same proof).

The statement uses the general fact: for a topos 𝒳, an abelian sheaf F and a weakly final object X_0 with Čech nerve X_0^•, RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim RΓ(X_0^•,F); if F is acyclic on each X_0^n this is the complex F(X_0^•) (Bhatt–Scholze, footnote to Construction 4.18).
proofSteps: Čech descent: the map from the weakly final object X_0 to the final object of the topos is an epimorphism, so RΓ(𝒳,F) ≃ R lim_Δ RΓ(X_0^•,F) by cohomological descent along its Čech nerve (requested from E2; the source adapts Stacks, Tag 07JM).

Acyclicity: each (C^n, IC^n) is an object of the site of bounded prisms and O, Ō have no higher cohomology on any object (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (3)), so RΓ(X_0^n, O_Δ) = C^n and RΓ(X_0^n, Ō_Δ) = C^n/IC^n.

Independence: products of presentations exist, so the category of presentations is sifted (non-empty with binary coproducts); a map of presentations induces a map of Čech nerves of weakly final objects over the final object, hence the identity on RΓ.
acceptance: For R = A/I the theorem gives Δ_{R/A} = A.
Two presentations of A/I⟨X⟩, by A⟨X⟩ and by A⟨X,Y⟩ with Y ↦ 0, give quasi-isomorphic complexes through the presentation A⟨X,Y,X′⟩.
H^0(Δ_{R/A}) is the equaliser of the two coface maps C^0 ⇉ C^1.

nodes.title: The Frobenius of prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: The structure sheaf O_Δ of (X/A)_Δ is a sheaf of δ-A-algebras: on each object (B,g,f) the ring B carries its δ-structure, with Frobenius lift φ_B(x) = x^p + pδ(x), and maps of prisms commute with δ. Hence φ : O_Δ → O_Δ is an endomorphism of sheaves of rings which is φ_A-semilinear, that is A-linear as a map O_Δ → φ_{A,*}O_Δ. It induces φ_X : Δ_{X/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) and φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A} in D(A), maps of commutative algebra objects, natural in X (or R) and compatible with base change of the prism. By adjunction φ_R is the same as its linearisation φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, where φ_A^* = − ⊗^L_{A,φ_A} A (derived (p,I)-completed where stated). On a Čech–Alexander model, φ_R is induced by the termwise Frobenius lifts of the cosimplicial δ-ring C^•.
hypotheses: (A,I) bounded prism, X a p-adic formal scheme over A/I (smooth where comparison theorems are used).
φ_A need not be flat or an isomorphism; φ_A^* is a derived functor and is not assumed to commute with totalisations unless proved (Theorem 5.2, proof).

φ carries I into φ(I)A, which is contained in I only for crystalline prisms; so in general Ō_Δ has no induced endomorphism (for I = (p) it has the Frobenius); reduction modulo I after φ gives the maps used in the de Rham comparison.
proofSteps: Maps of prisms are maps of δ-rings (PR.0/prism-category), so the Frobenius lifts φ_B are natural in the object: φ is an endomorphism of the presheaf O_Δ, semilinear over φ_A because g is a δ-map.
Apply Rν_* and RΓ: restriction of scalars along φ_A is exact, so R ν_*(φ_{A,*}O_Δ) = φ_{A,*}Rν_*O_Δ, giving φ_X and φ_R as maps of commutative algebra objects.
The linearisation is the adjoint map under the adjunction between derived extension of scalars along φ_A and restriction of scalars (requested from DD.1 with its completed form).
On C^•: each C^n is a δ-A-algebra and cofaces and codegeneracies are δ-maps, so φ is a map of cosimplicial rings over φ_A; under PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology it induces φ_R.
acceptance: On Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A the Frobenius is φ_A.
For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) the Frobenius of Δ_{R/Z_p} is Z_p-linear.
For a crystalline prism, φ corresponds under the crystalline comparison to the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology (PR.1/crystalline-comparison).

nodes.title: Base change along maps of finite complete Tor amplitude
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) → (A′,IA′) be a map of bounded prisms such that A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude, let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra and R′ := R ⊗̂_A A′ its p-completed base change (a p-completely smooth A′/IA′-algebra). Then the natural maps Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ → Δ_{R′/A′} and Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} A′/IA′ → Δ̄_{R′/A′} are isomorphisms, the completions being derived (p,I)-adic and p-adic. More precisely, for every map of bounded prisms the termwise completed base change C^• ⊗̂_A A′ of the functorial Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of R computes Δ_{R′/A′}, and the Tor amplitude hypothesis is used only to commute the completed base change with the totalisation.
hypotheses: Both prisms are bounded; A → A′ has finite (p,I)-complete Tor amplitude: A′ ⊗^L_A A/(p,I) has finite Tor amplitude over A/(p,I).
R is p-completely smooth over A/I.
The Tor amplitude hypothesis is removed by PR.1/prismatic-base-change, which uses the Hodge–Tate comparison; the present statement is an input of that comparison and cannot be replaced by it.
proofSteps: Termwise statement (Lemma 4.20, proof): C^n is the prismatic envelope of a completed free δ-A-algebra; by PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (2) envelopes commute with base change along every map of bounded prisms, and the base change of a weakly initial object and of its Čech nerve is again one for R′. So C^• ⊗̂_A A′ computes Δ_{R′/A′} by PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology.

Lemma 4.22: for a ring C with a finitely generated ideal J and a map C → C′ of finite J-complete Tor amplitude, the J-completed base change commutes with totalisations of cosimplicial objects of D^{≥0}. Proof in the source: finite skeleta commute, and the functor K ↦ (K ⊗^L_C C′) ⊗^L Kos(C′;x_1^m,…,x_r^m) lowers the degree of coconnectivity by a constant independent of m. Requested from DD.1.
Apply Lemma 4.22 to C^• over (A,(p,I)), and reduce modulo I for Δ̄.
acceptance: A completely flat map of bounded prisms satisfies the hypothesis with amplitude 0.
The map α of PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism satisfies the hypothesis.
For A → A′ with infinite complete Tor dimension the statement is not available at this point of the theory.

nodes.title: Étale localisation of Hodge–Tate cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R → S a p-completely étale map of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Then the natural map Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an isomorphism (derived p-completed tensor product). The restriction functor (S/A)_Δ → (R/A)_Δ has, in the algebraic language, a left adjoint F : (R/A)_Δ → (S/A)_Δ sending (B → B/IB ← R) to (B_S → B_S/IB_S ← S), where B_S is the unique (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra with B_S/IB_S = B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S; F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects.
hypotheses: (A,I) is bounded; R and S are p-completely smooth over A/I and R → S is p-completely étale: S is derived p-complete and S ⊗^L_R R/p is étale over R/p.
The statement is for Δ̄; the corresponding statement for Δ follows only after completion along I and is not an S-linear statement, since Δ_{R/A} is not an R-module.
proofSteps: Construction of F (Lemma 4.21, proof): for an object (B → B/IB ← R) the map B/IB → B/IB ⊗̂^L_R S is p-completely étale; by Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 2.18 with Elkik algebraization (stage PR.0, DD.1) it deforms uniquely to a (p,I)-completely étale δ-B-algebra B_S, and (B_S, IB_S) is a bounded prism by PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness. Adjointness follows from the uniqueness of étale lifts.

As a left adjoint F preserves coproducts and weakly initial objects. Apply it to the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial object C^• of R: D^• := F(C^•) is the Čech nerve of a weakly initial object of (S/A)_Δ, so D^•/ID^• computes Δ̄_{S/A} (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology, whose proof only needs a weakly initial object and its Čech nerve).
Termwise C^n/IC^n ⊗̂^L_R S ≅ D^n/ID^n by the definition of F; the p-completed base change along the p-completely flat map R → S commutes with the totalisation by Lemma 4.22 (DD.1).
acceptance: For a p-completed localisation S = R⟨1/f⟩: Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R⟨1/f⟩.
Étale chart: for a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, Δ̄_{S/A} = Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S; with the Hodge–Tate comparison for the polynomial ring this gives H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^i_{S/(A/I)}{−i}.
For R = S the functor F is the identity.

nodes.title: The Bockstein differential on twisted Hodge–Tate cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra (or X smooth over A/I, with sheaves on X_ét). For i ≥ 0 the connecting map of the triangle Δ̄_{R/A}{i+1} → Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+2} → Δ̄_{R/A}{i} is the Bockstein differential β_I : H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} → H^{i+1}(Δ̄_{R/A}){i+1}. With the cup product of the commutative algebra object Δ̄_{R/A}, the graded group H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} = ⊕_i H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is a graded-commutative differential graded A/I-algebra: β_I is A/I-linear, β_I ∘ β_I = 0 and β_I(xy) = β_I(x)y + (−1)^{deg x} x β_I(y). Its degree-0 part is an R-algebra through η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}), and β_I ∘ η^0_R : R → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} is an A/I-linear derivation into a derived p-complete R-module. It therefore induces the R-linear map η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1}, f dg ↦ f·β_I(η^0_R(g)), where Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} is the p-completed module of differentials, finite projective over R.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I.
β_I is A/I-linear but not R-linear.

Graded commutativity is xy = (−1)^{deg x · deg y} yx. The vanishing of squares of odd elements is not part of this node; for elements β_I(f), f ∈ R, it is Lemma 4.10 and is proved in PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line.
When I = (d) the twists are trivialised by d and β_I is the Bockstein of the triangle Δ → Δ → Δ̄ given by multiplication by d (the convention of the source for d = p).
proofSteps: Construction 4.9: the triangle is that of PR.1/hodge-tate-cohomology; its connecting map Δ̄{i} → Δ̄{i+1}[1] induces β_I on cohomology.

β_I ∘ β_I = 0: the two triangles for i and i+1 come from the filtration of Δ ⊗^L_A I^i/I^{i+3} by powers of I, and a composite of consecutive connecting maps of a three-step filtration vanishes on cohomology.

Leibniz rule: the I-adic filtration of the commutative algebra object Δ_{R/A} is multiplicative, so the connecting maps of its graded pieces form a derivation on ⊕_i H^*(gr^i) (the standard multiplicativity of the Bockstein spectral sequence of a filtered commutative algebra object; requested from DD.1 as the multiplicative I-adic filtration).

η^0 is H^0 of the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}. The derivation β_I η^0 factors through the completed differentials because its target is derived p-complete (universal property of Ω^1, completed form requested from DD.2).
acceptance: For R = A/I the cohomology is A/I in degree 0 and β_I = 0.
For R = A/I⟨X⟩, β_I(X) is a generator of H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} ≅ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} (PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line).
For a crystalline prism and I = (p), β_p is the Bockstein of crystalline cohomology modulo p², which on the de Rham complex of a lift sends the class of x^p to the class of x^{p−1}dx.

nodes.title: The relative Frobenius of a polynomial Čech nerve is a cosimplicial quasi-isomorphism on modules
nodes.statement: Let k be a commutative ring of characteristic p, B a polynomial k-algebra (in any set of variables), B^• the Čech nerve of k → B (B^n = B^{⊗_k (n+1)}), and B^{•,(1)} := B^• ⊗_{k,Frob} k its Frobenius twist, with the relative Frobenius B^{•,(1)} → B^•, a map of cosimplicial k-algebras. For every cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module N the natural map N → N ⊗_{B^{•,(1)}} B^• induces a quasi-isomorphism on the associated unnormalised cochain complexes of k-modules.
hypotheses: k is a ring with p = 0; B is a polynomial k-algebra; no finiteness on the number of variables.
N is a cosimplicial module over the cosimplicial ring B^{•,(1)}; the tensor product is termwise.
In the proof the displayed decomposition of the monoid M = N^r reads ⊔_{s ∈ S} (pM + s) = M with S = {0,…,p−1}^r; the printed index set is M (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E11).
proofSteps: Filtered colimits reduce to finitely many variables: B = k[M], M = N^r. The Čech nerve is k[EM] for the cosimplicial monoid EM, [n] ↦ M^{[n]}, and B^{•,(1)} → B^• is k[E(pM)] → k[EM].

With S = {0,…,p−1}^r, the subsets S^{[n]} ⊂ M^{[n]} are preserved by the coface maps (they only insert 0), so ES ⊂ EM is a semi-cosimplicial subset and k[E(pM)] ⊗_k k[ES] ≅ k[EM] as semi-cosimplicial k[E(pM)]-modules; the unit corresponds to id ⊗ η with η : k → k[ES] induced by 0 ∈ S.
The unnormalised complex depends only on the semi-cosimplicial structure, so it suffices that id_N ⊗ η : N → N ⊗_k k[ES] is a quasi-isomorphism.

k[ES] is the semi-cosimplicial module underlying the Čech nerve C^• of k → k[M^{grp}/pM^{grp}], and η underlies its unit, which is a cosimplicial homotopy equivalence because the algebra map has a section; homotopy equivalences of cosimplicial k-modules are preserved by N ⊗_k −.
acceptance: For B = k (no variables) the map is the identity.
For B = k[x] and N = B^{•,(1)} the lemma says that k[x^p]-type Čech complex and the Čech complex of k → k[x] are quasi-isomorphic; both are resolutions of k.
The decomposition k[E(pM)] ⊗_k k[ES] ≅ k[EM] is an isomorphism of semi-cosimplicial modules only: codegeneracies do not preserve S (p = 2, r = 1: (1,1) ↦ 2 ∉ S).

nodes.title: The crystalline comparison
nodes.statement: Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism (A is a p-torsion-free, p-complete δ-ring) and let I ⊂ A be an ideal with divided powers and p ∈ I. The Frobenius of A/p kills I/pA, so it induces ψ : A/I → A/p. Let R be a smooth A/I-algebra and R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/I,ψ} A/p, a smooth A/p-algebra. Let RΓ_crys(R/A) be the crystalline cohomology of Spec(R) relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/I) ⊂ Spf(A) (p-adically: the derived limit over n of the crystalline cohomology over A/p^n). Then there is a canonical isomorphism Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) of E_∞-A-algebras, compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms (the Frobenius of prismatic cohomology on the left, the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology induced by the Frobenius of Spec(R) and φ_A on the right). In the case I = (p), with C^• the Čech–Alexander cosimplicial ring of a presentation B_0 → R and D^• the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of the same presentation, the isomorphism is induced by a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras φ_A^*C^• → D^•, where φ_A^*C^• (termwise base change along φ_A) computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}.
hypotheses: (A,(p)) is a crystalline prism, hence bounded; I is a PD ideal containing p (its divided powers are unique since A is p-torsion-free, and they are compatible with the canonical ones on (p)).
R is a smooth A/I-algebra in the usual sense (A/I has characteristic p).

The Frobenius twist is on the prismatic side: it is R^{(1)}, not R, whose prismatic cohomology is the crystalline cohomology of R. For I = (p) and with base change (PR.1/prismatic-base-change) this reads φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A); the untwisted statement Δ_{R/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A) is false in general.
The statement φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is termwise; it is not claimed here that φ_A^* commutes with the totalisation of C^•.
proofSteps: Crystalline side, I = (p) (requested from CR.1 and CR.2). For a presentation B_0 → R with kernel J_0, B := Free_δ(B_0)^∧ and R′ := B/J_0B, let D_0, D be the p-completed PD envelopes of J_0 ⊂ B_0 and J_0B ⊂ B; they are p-torsion-free (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, Lemma 2.38), and the pro-object {(D/p^n → R′ ← R)}_n of the big crystalline site is weakly initial and compatible with coproducts. Hence RΓ_crys(R/A) ≃ lim D^•, D^• the envelope of the Čech nerve, independently of the presentation; big and small sites agree (Berthelot, III.4.1.4).

Prismatic side. C^• = B^•{J_0^•B^•/p}^∧ computes Δ_{R/A} (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), and its termwise base change φ_A^*C^• computes Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} (PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude, termwise part). By PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Corollary 2.39), D^• = B^•{φ(J_0^•)B^•/p}^∧. The relative Frobenius of A → B^• therefore induces η : φ_A^*C^• → D^•, and D^• is the pullback of the cosimplicial B^{•,(1)}-module φ_A^*C^• along the flat relative Frobenius B^{•,(1)} → B^•.
Both sides of η are p-torsion-free. By PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma applied to N = φ_A^*C^•/p, η is a quasi-isomorphism modulo p, hence a quasi-isomorphism by derived Nakayama (DD.1).

Frobenius. η is a map of cosimplicial δ-A-algebras; the Frobenius of crystalline cohomology corresponds to the δ-Frobenius of D^• under RΓ_crys ≃ lim D^•, by functoriality of crystalline cohomology for the Frobenius endomorphism of the simplicial PD thickening (requested from CR.3).

General I. The map A/p → A/I is surjective with locally nilpotent kernel, so R lifts to a smooth A/p-algebra R̃, and R̃ ⊗_{A/p,Frob} A/p = R^{(1)}; the case I = (p) for R̃ and the invariance of crystalline cohomology under enlarging the PD ideal of the base give the isomorphism. It is canonical: for a presentation B_0 → R with B_0 a δ-A-algebra, the PD envelope D^• of the Čech nerve has φ_{D^•}(ker(D^• → R)) ⊂ pD^•, giving a cosimplicial object (D^• → D^•/p ← R^{(1)}) of (R^{(1)}/A)_Δ and hence a map Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} → lim D^• independent of choices; it agrees with the previous map because η is a morphism of cosimplicial objects of the site (R^{(1)}/A)_Δ (the source leaves this compatibility to the reader).
acceptance: A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[x]: Δ_{F_p[x]/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[x]/Z_p), the de Rham complex of Z_p⟨x⟩; here R^{(1)} = R.
A = W(k) with k perfect and R̃ smooth over k: Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)); the twist is by the Frobenius of k.
A = A_crys(O_C/p) and I = ker(A_crys → O_C/p), a PD ideal strictly containing (p): for R smooth over O_C/p, Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_crys} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A_crys), with ψ : O_C/p → A_crys/p induced by the Frobenius.

nodes.title: The crystalline comparison for syntomic algebras
nodes.statement: Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism, J ⊂ A a PD ideal with p ∈ J, and R a syntomic A/J-algebra (flat, of finite presentation, with local complete intersection fibres). Put R^{(1)} := R ⊗_{A/J,ψ} A/p. Then there is a canonical Frobenius-compatible isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras RΓ((R^{(1)}/A)_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), where the left side is the cohomology of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} and the right side is crystalline cohomology relative to the PD thickening Spec(A/J) ⊂ Spf(A). For R smooth this is PR.1/crystalline-comparison.
hypotheses: (A,(p)) crystalline; J a PD ideal containing p; R syntomic over A/J.

The left side is site cohomology. Its identification with derived prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)}, and the extension of the comparison from quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras to all quasisyntomic F_p-algebras by descent, belong to PrismaticCohomology:PR.2 (nodes derived-agrees-with-site, qrsp-prism and quasisyntomic-descent) and consume this node; they are not asserted here.

For J ≠ (p) the reduction to J = (p) uses a syntomic lift of R to A/p, which exists Zariski-locally (a relative global complete intersection lifts by lifting its equations, and flatness is checked on the unchanged fibres); the canonical map of the smooth case glues the local isomorphisms.
proofSteps: Presentation: choose B_0 → R̃ with B_0 a p-completed polynomial A-algebra and R̃ a (local) syntomic lift over A/p. In each cosimplicial degree the kernel of B^n → R̃ is the filtered union of ideals (p, x_1,…,x_r) with (x_1,…,x_r) p-completely regular relative to A (Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.1.8). Hence PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes applies along the colimit: the envelopes C^n exist, are p-completely flat over A and form a weakly initial Čech nerve, exactly as in PR.1/cech-alexander-complex.

The cohomology of the site (R̃/A)_Δ is lim C^• by the argument of PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology, which only uses a weakly initial object and the acyclicity of O_Δ on objects; termwise base change gives φ_A^*C^• for R^{(1)}.
The crystalline side is computed by the cosimplicial PD envelope D^• for any R (CR.2), and D^• = B^•{φ(J^•)/p}^∧ by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, since the kernels are ind-regular modulo p.

The comparison map φ_A^*C^• → D^• and the proof that it is a quasi-isomorphism (PR.1/relative-frobenius-cosimplicial-lemma, which concerns only the polynomial Čech nerve, then derived Nakayama) and Frobenius-compatible are those of PR.1/crystalline-comparison.
acceptance: R = F_p[x]/(x^n) over (Z_p,(p)): the prismatic site cohomology of R^{(1)} = R is RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), computed by the PD envelope of (x^n) in Z_p⟨x⟩ with its de Rham complex.
R = k[x,y]/(xy) over W(k): a syntomic, non-smooth example.
For R smooth the statement and the map coincide with PR.1/crystalline-comparison.

nodes.title: The Hodge–Tate comparison in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Let (A,(p)) be a crystalline prism and S a smooth A/p-algebra. (1) For every f ∈ S the class β_p(f) ∈ H^1(Δ̄_{S/A}) has square zero, so the maps η^0_S, η^1_S of PR.1/bockstein-differential extend uniquely to a map of commutative differential graded A/p-algebras η^*_S : (Ω^*_{S/(A/p)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{S/A}), β_p), the twists being trivialised by the generator p of I. (2) η^*_S is an isomorphism: H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/p)}{−i} for all i. (3) The functor S ↦ Δ_{S/A} commutes with p-completed base change along every map of crystalline prisms (A,(p)) → (A′,(p)): Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≃ Δ_{S ⊗_A A′/A′}.
hypotheses: (A,(p)) is a crystalline prism; S is smooth over A/p.

The source states (2) for 'the comparison map from Theorem 4.11', whose construction for p = 2 rests on Lemma 4.10, itself deduced from Proposition 6.2, whose proof uses this corollary. The order adopted here removes the circle: (1) is proved together with (2) from the Cartier isomorphism, and Proposition 6.2 then only uses the statement for η^0 and η^1 of the affine line.
The Cartier isomorphism is imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/26).
proofSteps: Reductions. By PR.1/etale-localization and the local structure of smooth algebras (Zariski-locally étale over a polynomial algebra) both sides localise, so S = A/p[X_1,…,X_n]. A is p-torsion-free, so Z_p → A is p-completely flat and PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude reduces to A = Z_p, S = F_p[X_1,…,X_n].

S = R^{(1)} for R = F_p[X_1,…,X_n], and PR.1/crystalline-comparison gives Δ_{S/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), hence Δ̄_{S/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) ⊗^L F_p ≃ Ω^•_{R/F_p}, the de Rham complex of R (crystalline cohomology of R is the de Rham complex of the lift Z_p⟨X⟩; requested from CR.2). The S-algebra structure of H^0 corresponds to the relative Frobenius S = R^{(1)} → H^0(Ω^•_{R/F_p}).

Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map): C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R^{(1)}/F_p} ≅ H^i(Ω^•_{R/F_p}) is an isomorphism of graded R^{(1)}-algebras. So H^*(Δ̄_{S/Z_p}) ≅ Ω^*_S as graded S-algebras; this algebra is strictly graded-commutative, which gives (1).

Identification with η^*. On the lift Z_p⟨X⟩ with φ(X_j) = X_j^p, the Bockstein of the class of x^p is the class of d(φ(x̃))/p = x^{p−1}dx + dδ(x̃), which is C^{−1}(dx). So η^1_S = C^{−1} on generators, and η^*_S = C^{−1} by multiplicativity; this proves (2).
(3): by derived Nakayama it suffices to compare modulo p, where both sides have cohomology Ω^i, which commutes with base change.
acceptance: S = F_p[X] over Z_p: H^0(Δ̄) = F_p[X], H^1(Δ̄) = F_p[X]·β_p(X), H^i = 0 for i ≥ 2; under the crystalline comparison β_p(X) is the class of X^{p−1}dX.
Base change: for a map of crystalline prisms Z_p → W(k), Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p} ⊗̂ W(k) ≃ Δ_{k[X]/W(k)}.

nodes.title: Mapping an oriented prism to a crystalline one
nodes.statement: Let (A,(d)) be an oriented prism such that A/(d) is p-torsion-free and the Frobenius A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p), x ↦ x^p, is flat (for example the universal oriented prism, the (p,d)-completion of Z_(p){d, δ(d)^{−1}}). Let B := A{φ(d)/p}^∧ be the p-complete animated δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining φ(d)/p. Then: (a) B is discrete and p-torsion-free, it is the p-completed PD envelope of (d) ⊂ A, and φ(d) = p·u in B with u a unit; B is (p,d)-complete. (b) The composite α : A → B of φ_A : A → A with the canonical map A → B satisfies α(d) ∈ pB, so α is a map of prisms (A,(d)) → (B,(p)) and (B,(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism. (c) Modulo p, α factors as A/p → A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) → B/p = D_{(d)}(A/p), where the first map has finite Tor amplitude, the second is the Frobenius and is faithfully flat, and the third is free. (d) The completed base change functor α̂^* : D_{comp}(A) → D_{comp}(B) on derived (p,d)-complete objects is conservative and has finite (p,d)-complete Tor amplitude. (e) For every p-completely smooth A/(d)-algebra R with p-completed base change R_B, α̂^*Δ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R_B/B} and α̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}.
hypotheses: (A,(d)) is an oriented prism with A/(d) p-torsion-free; then p is a nonzerodivisor on A and (p,d) is a regular sequence.

The Frobenius hypothesis is the corrected one of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E13: only the flatness of A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p) is used, and this is what Example 3.4 provides for the universal oriented prism; the printed hypothesis 'the Frobenius on A/p is flat' is stronger than what is proved there.
α is the Frobenius-twisted canonical map; the canonical map A → B itself is not a map of prisms to (B,(p)), since the image of d is not divisible by p.
proofSteps: (a): by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (Corollary 2.39 with the regular element d of A/p), A{φ(d)/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope of (d), discrete and p-torsion-free; φ(d) = p·u with u a unit by PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity (Lemma 2.24), because φ(d) is distinguished and divisible by p. Since d^p ∈ (p, φ(d)), p-completeness implies (p,d)-completeness.
(b): α(d) = φ(d) = pu ∈ pB; α is a δ-map as a composite of δ-maps; (B,(p)) is a crystalline prism by PR.0/crystalline-prism.
(c): B/p is the PD envelope of (d) in A/p, free over A/(p,d^p) with basis the divided powers γ_{kp}(d) (CR.0); the composite A/p → B/p is induced by φ, which factors through A/(p,d) → A/(p,d^p).

(d): by derived Nakayama conservativity and Tor amplitude are checked modulo p for d-completed base change along the three maps of (c): the first is a quotient by a regular element, the others are faithfully flat (DD.1).
(e): PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude applied to α, using (d).
acceptance: For the universal oriented prism A_0 the ring D_0 = A_0{φ(d)/p}^∧ receives Z_p, and (Z_p,(p)) → (D_0,(p)) is a map of crystalline prisms.
For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]],(E(u))) the construction gives the p-completed PD envelope of (E(u)), a ring of Breuil type, with α induced by φ.
α(d) = φ(d) is p times a unit; the canonical image of d is not in pB.

nodes.title: The Hodge–Tate comparison for the affine line and the vanishing of β(f)²
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and R = A/I⟨X⟩ the p-adic completion of the polynomial ring in one variable. Then η^0_R : R → H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) and η^1_R : Ω^1_{R/(A/I)} → H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} are isomorphisms and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) = 0 for i > 1. Consequently (Lemma 4.10): for every bounded prism (A,I), every smooth p-adic formal scheme X over A/I and every local section f of O_X, the element β_I(f) ∈ H^1(Δ̄_{X/A}){1} has square zero.
hypotheses: (A,I) is an arbitrary bounded prism; no orientation and no torsion-freeness is assumed.
Only the maps η^0 and η^1 of PR.1/bockstein-differential occur in the statement; the full map η^* is constructed afterwards (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map).
The printed proof refers to Ω^1_{R/(A/d)} for a general prism; it is Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}.
proofSteps: Choose η : R ⊕ Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R) inducing η^0 and η^1{−1} on cohomology, possible since both modules are finite free over R; it suffices that η is an isomorphism. The consequence follows by functoriality: f defines A/I⟨X⟩ → O_X(U), and β_I(X)² lies in H^2 = 0.
I = (p): this is PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p for S = A/p[X] in degrees 0 and 1.

Universal oriented prism (A_0,(d)): the base change α̂^* of PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism is conservative and carries Δ̄_{R/A_0} to Δ̄_{R_{D_0}/D_0} and η to the corresponding map over the crystalline prism (D_0,(p)), which is an isomorphism by the previous step.

General oriented bounded prism (A,(d)): the orientation gives A_0 → A; with a : A_0 → D_0 the map α and E := A ⊗̂^L_{A_0} D_0, b : A → E, c : Z_p → E, the functor b̂^* is conservative on (p,d)-complete objects. Using the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of the affine line (PR.1/cech-alexander-complex, Remark 4.19) and Lemma 4.22 (b and c have finite complete Tor amplitude), b̂^*Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ ĉ^*Δ̄_{F_p[X]/Z_p}, compatibly with the maps η; the claim reduces to the case A = Z_p already treated.

General bounded prism: there is a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms (A,I) → (A′,(d)) with A′ oriented (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness, Lemma 3.7 (4)); flat base change (PR.1/base-change-finite-tor-amplitude) and faithful flatness reduce to the oriented case.
acceptance: A = Z_p: Δ̄_{F_p[X]/Z_p} has H^0 = F_p[X], H^1 = F_p[X]·β(X), nothing else.
q-de Rham prism: for R = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨X⟩ over (Z_p[[q−1]],([p]_q)), H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) is free of rank one over R.
p = 2: β_I(f)² = 0 for every f, which graded commutativity alone does not give.

nodes.title: The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. There is a unique map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) of sheaves of commutative differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét which in degree 0 is the structure map η^0_X : O_X → H^0(Δ̄_{X/A}); in degree 1 it is η^1_X, f dg ↦ f β_I(g), and η^i(f_0 df_1 ∧ … ∧ df_i) = f_0 β_I(f_1) ⋯ β_I(f_i). It is O_X-linear in each degree, compatible with the O_X-module structures, functorial in X and compatible with maps of bounded prisms. Its construction depends functorially only on the commutative algebra object Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) together with the O_X-algebra structure on Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I. For X = Spf(R) one writes η^i_R : Ω^i_{R/(A/I)} → H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i}. Here Ω^i is the p-completed module of differential forms.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism and X is smooth over A/I.

The existence of η^* uses Lemma 4.10: β_I(f)² = 0 for every local section f of O_X. For p odd this follows from graded commutativity; for p = 2 it is deduced from the affine line (PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line), by functoriality along A/I⟨T⟩ → O_X(U), T ↦ f.

The universal property used is that of the de Rham complex: Ω^*_{R/k} is initial among graded-commutative differential graded k-algebras E with a k-algebra map R → E^0 such that squares of the elements d(r) vanish (completed form for p-completely smooth R).
proofSteps: By PR.1/bockstein-differential the target is a graded-commutative dg A/I-algebra with O_X → H^0 and with η^0 ⊕ η^1 compatible with d and β_I.

Lemma 4.10 (from PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line): β_I(f)² = 0. Hence the elements β_I(f) generate a strictly graded-commutative sub-dg-algebra, and the universal property of the de Rham complex (requested from DD.2, built on DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2/ordinary-de-rham-complex) extends η^0 ⊕ η^1 uniquely to η^*.
Functoriality in X and in the prism follows from uniqueness; the sheaf version is obtained from the affine maps η^*_R by Zariski and étale gluing.
acceptance: η^1_R(f dg) = f·β_I(g).
For R = A/I the map is the identity of A/I in degree 0.
For an étale map R → S the maps η^*_R and η^*_S are compatible with Ω^i_R ⊗_R S ≅ Ω^i_S and with PR.1/etale-localization.

nodes.title: The Hodge–Tate comparison theorem
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map η^*_X : (Ω^*_{X/(A/I)}, d) → (H^*(Δ̄_{X/A}){∗}, β_I) is an isomorphism of sheaves of differential graded A/I-algebras on X_ét. In particular Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is a perfect complex with H^i(Δ̄_{X/A}) ≅ Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}{−i}, zero for i larger than the relative dimension. For X = Spf(R) affine: Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I) as R-modules, for every i.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism; X is smooth over A/I (R p-completely smooth over A/I). Without smoothness the statement fails for site cohomology.
The twist is {−i} = ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ −i}; there is no Frobenius twist in this comparison.
Ω^i denotes p-completed differential forms, a finite locally free O_X-module.
proofSteps: The map is globally defined (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map), so the statement is local: it suffices to prove that η^i_R is an isomorphism for every p-completely smooth R.
Both sides localise for the étale topology: Ω^i_R ⊗_R S = Ω^i_S and PR.1/etale-localization. Since X is Zariski-locally étale over a completed affine space, one may take R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩.

Choose η : ⊕_{i=0}^n Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i] → Δ̄_{R/A} in D(R) lifting the maps η^i{−i} (the modules are finite free) and prove it is an isomorphism exactly as in PR.1/hodge-tate-affine-line: for I = (p) by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p; for the universal oriented prism by PR.1/crystallization-of-oriented-prism; for an oriented prism by the pushout E and the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩; in general by faithfully flat base change to an oriented prism.
Perfectness: Δ̄_{X/A} has finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, each finite locally free.
acceptance: Smooth polynomial algebra: for R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) is free over R on the classes β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i, twisted by {−i}.
Torus: R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} free over R on η^1(dX/X) = X^{−1}β_I(X).
A_inf prism and R = O_C⟨X⟩: H^1(Δ̄) ≅ Ω^1_{R/O_C}{−1}, the Breuil–Kisin–Fargues twist of BMS1.

nodes.title: Base change for prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) → (B,IB) be a map of bounded prisms, X a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, X_B := X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Spf(B/IB) and g : X_B → X the projection. Then (g^*Δ_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ_{X_B/B} in D(X_{B,ét}, B), the completion being derived (p,I)-adic, and (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B} with p-adic completion. For X = Spf(R): Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ Δ_{R ⊗̂_A B/B}. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated then RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_A B ≃ RΓ_Δ(X_B/B). Consequence (the φ_A-twisted crystalline comparison): for a crystalline prism (A,(p)) and R smooth over A/p, base change along the map of prisms φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) gives φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(R/A), compatibly with Frobenius; for X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over A/p, RΓ_crys(X/A) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A.
hypotheses: Both prisms are bounded; no flatness or Tor amplitude hypothesis on A → B.

X is smooth over A/I. The statement for global sections requires X quasi-compact and quasi-separated: completed base change does not commute with infinite products. Theorem 1.8 (5) of the source omits this hypothesis (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E13); the sheaf statement, Corollary 4.12, needs no such hypothesis.
φ_A : A → A is a map of prisms (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) only for crystalline prisms; for a general prism the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{X/A} is not the prismatic cohomology of a base change over (A,I).
proofSteps: By derived Nakayama (DD.1) it suffices to prove the statement modulo I: (g^*Δ̄_{X/A})^∧ ≅ Δ̄_{X_B/B}.

Both sides are perfect complexes with cohomology sheaves Ω^i{−i} by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison, the base change map is compatible with the maps η^* (functoriality of PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map in the prism), and completed differential forms commute with base change (DD.2).
Global sections: for X quasi-compact and quasi-separated RΓ is a finite limit of the affine values, and completed base change commutes with finite limits.
Consequence: apply the affine statement to φ_A : (A,(p)) → (A,(p)) and PR.1/crystalline-comparison with I = (p), noting R ⊗_{A/p,Frob} A/p = R^{(1)}.
acceptance: Crystalline base: for (Z_p,(p)) → (W(k),(p)), Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p} ⊗̂ W(k) ≃ Δ_{k[X]/W(k)}.

For the map of prisms α = can∘φ : (A_inf, ker θ) → (A_crys,(p)) (Construction 6.1 with d = ξ) and X smooth, quasi-compact and quasi-separated over O_C: RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf) ⊗̂^L_{A_inf,α} A_crys ≃ RΓ_Δ(Y/A_crys) with Y = X ×_{Spf O_C} Spf(A_crys/p) = (X_{O_C/p})^{(1)}; by PR.1/crystalline-comparison for the PD ideal ker(A_crys → O_C/p) the right side is RΓ_crys(X_{O_C/p}/A_crys), the A_crys-comparison of BMS1.
Non-example: for X an infinite disjoint union of copies of Spf(F_p) over (Z_p,(p)) and B = Z_p⟨x⟩, the map (∏ Z_p) ⊗̂ Z_p⟨x⟩ → ∏ Z_p⟨x⟩ is not surjective.

nodes.title: The de Rham comparison (W(A/I) p-torsion-free)
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism such that the ring of p-typical Witt vectors W(A/I) is p-torsion-free, and let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I. Then there is a natural isomorphism Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, A/I), where A/I is an A-algebra through A → A → A/I, the first map being φ_A, the completion is p-adic, and the right side is the p-completed de Rham complex. More precisely, for a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra R there is a functorial isomorphism Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) of commutative algebra objects of D(W(A/I)), where ψ : A → W(A/I) is the composite of the δ-map A → W(A/I) lifting A → A/I with the Witt vector Frobenius, and the crystalline cohomology is relative to the PD ideal ker(W(A/I) → A/(I,p)); reducing along W(A/I) → A/I gives the first isomorphism. If X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, RΓ_dR(X/(A/I)) ≃ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A/I.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism and W(A/I) is p-torsion-free. This holds if A/I is p-torsion-free, or if I = (p) and A/p is reduced. This is the hypothesis of Theorem 6.4 (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/27).

The statement for every bounded prism, without the hypothesis on W(A/I), is Corollary 15.4 of the source; it is deduced from the Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius and is the node PrismaticCohomology:PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general. It is not asserted here.

The reduction is along the Frobenius-twisted map A → A/I. The untwisted reduction Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is Hodge–Tate cohomology, whose cohomology sheaves are Ω^i{−i} with the Bockstein as differential; the two are different objects.
The proof of Theorem 6.4 is read with the correction of register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E14: ψ carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I).
proofSteps: Reduce to the affine case by functoriality. The kernel J of W(A/I) → A/I → A/(I,p) is a PD ideal, and RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)) ⊗̂^L_{W(A/I)} A/I ≃ Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}, because R is a p-completely smooth lift of R/p over the PD thickening W(A/I) → A/I (crystalline cohomology is the de Rham cohomology of a smooth lift, with base change; requested from CR.2).

The map A → A/I lifts uniquely to a δ-map w : A → W(A/I) (PR.0/delta-ring-category: W is right adjoint to the forgetful functor). It carries I into V W(A/I), so ψ = F ∘ w carries I into FV W(A/I) = pW(A/I). As W(A/I) is p-torsion-free and p-complete, (W(A/I),(p)) is a bounded crystalline prism (PR.0/crystalline-prism) and ψ : (A,I) → (W(A/I),(p)) is a map of bounded prisms.
PR.1/prismatic-base-change along ψ: Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,ψ} W(A/I) ≃ Δ_{R′/W(A/I)} with R′ := R ⊗̂_{A/I,ψ} W(A/I)/p.

PR.1/crystalline-comparison for the crystalline prism W(A/I), the PD ideal J and the smooth W(A/I)/J = A/(I,p)-algebra R/p: its Frobenius twist (R/p)^{(1)} is R′, since A/(I,p) → W(A/I)/p is induced by the Witt vector Frobenius. Hence Δ_{R′/W(A/I)} ≃ RΓ_crys((R/p)/W(A/I)).
The composite A → W(A/I) → A/I of ψ with the projection is a ↦ φ_A(a) mod I (zeroth Witt component of F(w(a))), which gives the stated twist.
acceptance: A = Z_p[[u]], I = (E(u)), A/I = O_K p-torsion-free: Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_{A,φ} O_K ≃ Ω^*_{X/O_K}.
A = W(k), I = (p), k perfect: Δ_{R/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R/k}; with the Cartier isomorphism this is consistent with Δ̄_{R/W(k)} having cohomology Ω^i_{R/k}.
A hypothesis check: W(F_p[x]/(x²)) has p-torsion, and for A a p-torsion-free δ-lift of F_p[x]/(x²) the theorem does not apply; the statement is then PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general.

nodes.title: Perfectness of prismatic cohomology of proper smooth formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and X a proper smooth p-adic formal scheme over Spf(A/I). Then RΓ_Δ(X/A) is a perfect complex of A-modules, and RΓ(X_ét, Δ̄_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is a perfect complex of A/I-modules with a finite filtration whose graded pieces are RΓ(X, Ω^i_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i], 0 ≤ i ≤ dim(X/(A/I)). In particular RΓ_Δ(X/A) has Tor amplitude in [0, 2 dim], and its formation commutes with base change along every map of bounded prisms.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism; A/I need not be noetherian.
X is proper and smooth over Spf(A/I): quasi-compact, separated, of finite relative dimension, with X ⊗ Z/p^n proper and smooth over A/(I,p^n) for all n.
Perfectness is asserted for the complex of global sections, not for the individual cohomology modules H^i_Δ(X/A), which need not be finitely presented or flat.
proofSteps: By PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison, Δ̄_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, O_X) is perfect with cohomology sheaves Ω^i{−i}; the canonical filtration gives the filtration of RΓ(X, Δ̄_{X/A}) with the stated graded pieces.

For X proper and smooth over the p-complete ring A/I of bounded p^∞-torsion, RΓ(X, E) is a perfect complex of A/I-modules for every vector bundle E, and commutes with base change (finiteness for proper flat finitely presented morphisms without noetherian hypotheses, passed to the p-adic limit; requested from DD.5, with formal schemes from SF.4).

RΓ_Δ(X/A) is derived (p,I)-complete, A is classically (p,I)-complete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness (1)) and RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗^L_A A/I is perfect over A/I; a derived I-complete complex over an I-adically complete ring whose reduction modulo I is perfect is perfect (requested from DD.1).
Base change: PR.1/prismatic-base-change for the quasi-compact and separated X; for perfect complexes the completed and the ordinary derived tensor product agree.
acceptance: X = P^1 over A/I: RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≃ A ⊕ A{−1}[−2] as a complex, of rank 2.
X an abelian formal scheme of dimension g: RΓ_Δ(X/A) is perfect of amplitude [0,2g] with H^1 of rank 2g after base change to a field.
For X affine of positive dimension (not proper), RΓ_Δ(X/A) is not perfect: H^0(Δ̄) = O(X) is not finitely generated over A/I.

nodes.title: p-torsion-freeness of H^0 for p-completely syntomic algebras
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism with A p-torsion-free, and let S be a p-completely syntomic A/I-algebra: S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, S/p ≅ S ⊗^L_{A/I} (A/I)/p, and (A/I)/p → S/p is syntomic. Then H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) is p-torsion-free. Under the identification of site cohomology with derived prismatic cohomology for such S (PrismaticCohomology:PR.2), this is the statement that H^0(Δ_{S/A}) is p-torsion-free.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a bounded prism and A is p-torsion-free.
S is p-completely syntomic over A/I in the sense of Anschütz–Le Bras, footnote to Lemma 5.1.6.

The proof planned here is complete when the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero, which holds whenever A/p has bounded I^∞-torsion ((A/d^n)[p] ≅ (A/p)[d^n] with transition maps multiplication by d): every crystalline prism, every prism with (p,d) regular (Breuil–Kisin, q-de Rham), every perfect prism (A/p is reduced; this is the case A = A_inf(R), R any perfectoid ring, used by the source) and every noetherian A. For an arbitrary p-torsion-free bounded prism the step 'a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module is p-torsion-free' is asserted in the source by calling the module p-completely flat over A; this is recorded as a gap of the packet and as source issue PrismaticCohomology/E14.
The identification with derived prismatic cohomology uses descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and belongs to PR.2; this node is about the site.
proofSteps: Čech–Alexander complex: since S is p-completely syntomic, the kernel of a presentation is (ind-)Zariski-locally generated by I and a sequence completely regular relative to A, so PR.1/cech-alexander-complex applies and gives a weakly initial object C^0 of (S/A)_Δ with C^0 derived (p,I)-complete and (p,I)-completely flat over A (PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (1)).
H^0((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) is the equaliser of C^0 ⇉ C^1 (PR.1/cech-alexander-computes-cohomology), a subring of C^0; so it suffices that C^0 is p-torsion-free.

For a derived (p,I)-complete, (p,I)-completely flat A-module B over the p-torsion-free bounded prism A: B is discrete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness), B[p] = H^{−1}(B ⊗^L_A A/p), and by derived I-completeness and complete flatness B[p] ≅ lim_n B ⊗_A (A/I^n)[p], with transition maps induced by A/I^{n+1} → A/I^n. If the pro-system ((A/I^n)[p])_n is pro-zero the limit vanishes. For I = (p) this is the source's argument: B is p-completely flat over Z_p, hence p-torsion-free.
acceptance: A = A_inf, S = O_C⟨x⟩/(x^n − p)-type syntomic algebras, and the application of the source: S the ring of a finite locally free group scheme over a quasisyntomic base.
A = Z_p, S = F_p: H^0 = Z_p is p-torsion-free while H^0 of Ō_Δ is F_p; the statement is about O_Δ.
If A has p-torsion the statement fails already for S = A/I, where H^0 = A.

nodes.title: A perfect prism is initial among prisms over its reduction
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be a perfect prism with associated perfectoid ring R = A/I. For every prism (B,J), every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J). Equivalently, the category of prisms (B,J) with a map R → B/J is the category of prisms under (A,I): (R)_Δ = (R/A)_Δ, with (A,I) as initial object in the algebraic language. The converse fails: for a prism (A,I) and a perfect prism (B,J) there may be several maps (A,I) → (B,J) inducing the same map A/I → B/J.
hypotheses: (A,I) is a perfect prism, so A = W(A/p) with A/p perfect, and A/I is a perfectoid ring (PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings).
(B,J) is an arbitrary prism, not necessarily bounded; B may have p-torsion, so compatibility with Frobenius lifts does not by itself give a δ-map.
The absolute prismatic site (R)_Δ as a site is defined in PrismaticCohomology:PR.5; the statement here is about maps of prisms only.
proofSteps: The p-completed cotangent complex of A over Z_p vanishes because A = W(perfect ring) (DD.0), and B is derived (p,J)-complete (it is a prism) while B/J is derived p-complete; by deformation theory along the (p,J)-adic tower Hom(A,B) ≃ Hom(A,B/J) ≃ Hom(A,B/(J,p)). So A → A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a ring map α : A → B, compatible with the Frobenius lifts, and α(I) ⊂ J.

α is a δ-map: since φ_A is bijective, α factors uniquely through B^{perf} := lim_φ B; B^{perf} is a perfect δ-ring, hence p-torsion-free (PR.0/perfect-delta-rings, Lemma 2.28), so the φ-equivariant map A → B^{perf} is a δ-map, and B^{perf} → B is a δ-map.
Uniqueness as a map of prisms follows from uniqueness as a ring map.
acceptance: (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)): every prism (B,J) with p ∈ J, that is every crystalline prism, receives exactly one map from (Z_p,(p)).
(A,I) = (A_inf, ker θ): a ring map O_C → B/J determines the map A_inf → B.

Failure of the converse: for the Breuil–Kisin prism (Z_p[[u]],(u − p)) and the perfect prism (A_inf(O_C), ker θ), the maps u ↦ [p^♭] attached to the different compatible systems p^♭ of p-power roots of p are distinct maps of prisms inducing the same map Z_p → O_C.
