nodes.title: Acceptance computations: polynomial algebra, étale chart, crystalline base, Frobenius twist
nodes.statement: (1) Smooth polynomial algebra. For a bounded prism (A,I) and R = A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, Δ_{R/A} is computed by the base-change-compatible Čech–Alexander complex of A⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩, and H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} is the free R-module on the products β_I(X_{j_1}) ⋯ β_I(X_{j_i}), j_1 < … < j_i; so H^*(Δ̄_{R/A}){∗} is the exterior algebra over R on β_I(X_1),…,β_I(X_n) with differential determined by β_I(X_j^m) = m X_j^{m−1} β_I(X_j). (2) Étale chart. For a p-completely étale map A/I⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩ → S, H^i(Δ̄_{S/A}){i} ≅ Ω^i_{S/(A/I)} is free over S on the same classes, and Δ̄_{S/A} ≃ Δ̄_{A/I⟨X⟩/A} ⊗̂^L S. (3) Crystalline base. For (A,I) = (Z_p,(p)) and R = F_p[X], Δ_{R/Z_p} ≃ RΓ_crys(F_p[X]/Z_p) is the de Rham complex Z_p⟨X⟩ → Z_p⟨X⟩dX: H^0 = Z_p and H^1 is the cokernel of d, X^m ↦ mX^{m−1}dX; its reduction modulo p, which is Δ̄_{R/Z_p}, has cohomology F_p[X^p] in degree 0 and F_p[X^p]·X^{p−1}dX in degree 1, with β_p(X) the class of X^{p−1}dX. (4) Nontrivial Frobenius-twisted coefficient map. For A = W(k) with k = F_{p²} and R̃ = k[X,Y]/(Y² − X³ − aX − b) an affine elliptic curve whose j-invariant is not in F_p (p ≥ 5), the algebras R̃ and R̃^{(1)} = R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob} k are not isomorphic over k, and Δ_{R̃^{(1)}/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)) while φ_A^*Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ≃ RΓ_crys(R̃/W(k)): the comparison holds only after the scalar extension along φ_A, which is not the identity on W(k). Likewise Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k),φ} k ≃ Ω^*_{R̃/k}, whereas the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{R̃/W(k)} = Δ_{R̃/W(k)} ⊗^L_{W(k)} k has cohomology modules Ω^i_{R̃/k} and is the de Rham complex of the Frobenius untwist R̃ ⊗_{k,Frob^{−1}} k, a curve not isomorphic to R̃.
hypotheses: (1), (2): any bounded prism. (3): the crystalline prism (Z_p,(p)). (4): k = F_{p²}, p ≥ 5, a, b ∈ k with j-invariant outside F_p.
In (3) the twist is invisible because F_p[X]^{(1)} = F_p[X] over F_p; (4) is chosen so that the twist changes the algebra.
In (4) the two W(k)-module structures on RΓ_crys differ by φ; the complexes are abstractly isomorphic as complexes of abelian groups since φ is an automorphism of W(k).
proofSteps: (1): PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison for the polynomial ring, with the complex of PR.1/cech-alexander-complex (Remark 4.19) and the Leibniz rule of PR.1/bockstein-differential.
(2): PR.1/etale-localization and (1).

(3): PR.1/crystalline-comparison with A = Z_p, I = (p), R = F_p[X] = R^{(1)}, the de Rham computation of crystalline cohomology of the affine line (CR.2), and the identification of β_p in PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-char-p.

(4): PR.1/crystalline-comparison for I = (p) over W(k), PR.1/prismatic-base-change along φ_A and PR.1/de-rham-comparison (W(k) is p-torsion-free and k is reduced); R̃^{(1)} is the curve with coefficients a^p, b^p, of j-invariant j^p ≠ j.
acceptance: Each of the four computations is a test of the corresponding comparison theorem with a wrong twist: (1) fails with the twist {i} in place of {−i} for a non-orientable prism, (3) fails if β is omitted, (4) fails without φ_A.
The torus R = A/I⟨X^{±1}⟩ is an étale chart of the affine line and gives H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}){1} = R·η^1(dX/X).

nodes.title: Derived prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Let Poly_{A/I} be the category of p-completed polynomial algebras (A/I)⟨x_1,…,x_n⟩, n ≥ 0, and Sm_{A/I} the category of p-completely smooth A/I-algebras. Let CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) be the ∞-category of commutative algebra objects E of D_comp(A) equipped with a map of commutative algebras φ_E : E → φ_{A,*}E. PR.1 gives a functor Sm_{A/I} → CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)), R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R). Derived prismatic cohomology is its left Kan extension Δ_{−/A} to the ∞-category of derived p-complete simplicial commutative A/I-algebras, with colimits in the target derived (p, I)-completed. Equivalently Δ_{−/A} is the unique functor on derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras that preserves sifted colimits and restricts to PR.1's functor on Poly_{A/I}; for a simplicial resolution P_• → R by objects of Poly_{A/I} (or by p-completely ind-smooth algebras) one has Δ_{R/A} ≃ (colim_{[n] ∈ Δ^op} Δ_{P_n/A})^∧, independently of the resolution. Derived Hodge–Tate cohomology is Δ̄_{R/A} := Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I, a derived p-complete commutative algebra in D(R). The functor carries: (1) the unit A → Δ_{R/A}, with Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A; (2) the structure map R → Δ̄_{R/A}; (3) the φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_R : Δ_{R/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{R/A}, natural in R. For R in Sm_{A/I} the value is the site cohomology of PR.1 (node derived-agrees-with-site). Δ_{R/A} is an invariant of the animated ring R and not of π_0(R) alone (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

D(A) is the derived ∞-category of A-modules with cohomological indexing; D_comp(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects with its completed tensor product; "discrete" means concentrated in degree 0.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
PR.1's functor is used as a functor of ∞-categories; its coherence in R is supplied by the functorial Čech–Alexander complexes.
The left Kan extension from Sm_{A/I} and the one from Poly_{A/I} agree; this is part of the statement and is proved through the Hodge–Tate comparison (BS22 Construction 7.6 (1)).
proofSteps: Coherent source functor: the functorial Čech–Alexander complex (PR.1) makes R ↦ (Δ_{R/A}, φ_R) a functor from Sm_{A/I} to cosimplicial derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras, hence to CAlg_φ(D_comp(A)) after totalisation.

Animation: derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras are the derived p-complete objects (DD.1) of the animation of finitely generated polynomial A/I-algebras (E5:animation). By the universal property of animation (HTT 5.5.8.15) and the left Kan extension theorem of E3, the functor P ↦ Δ_{P^∧/A} on polynomial algebras extends uniquely to a sifted-colimit-preserving functor with values in D_comp(A); it inverts derived p-completion maps because its reduction modulo I has p-completed graded pieces, so it is defined on derived p-complete inputs.

Agreement of the two extensions: on Sm_{A/I} the complex Δ̄_{R/A} has the finite filtration τ^{≤i} with graded pieces Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i] (PR.1, Hodge–Tate comparison), and R ↦ (Ω^i_{R/(A/I)})^∧ is left Kan extended from Poly_{A/I} (DD.0). By derived Nakayama for I (DD.1) the functor Δ_{−/A} on Sm_{A/I} is itself left Kan extended from Poly_{A/I}; hence the value on Sm_{A/I} is unchanged.

Structure maps: the unit, R → Δ̄_{R/A} and φ_R are the left Kan extensions of the corresponding natural transformations of PR.1; reduction modulo I commutes with the colimits because A/I is a perfect A-module (I is invertible).
acceptance: Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A with φ = φ_A, and Δ̄_{(A/I)/A} = A/I.
For R = (A/I)⟨x⟩ the value is PR.1's complex: H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) = R, H^1(Δ̄_{R/A}) = Ω^1_{R/(A/I)}{−1} free of rank 1, and no other cohomology.
For R = A/I × A/I (p-completely étale over A/I) the value is A × A.
For a discrete p-complete R, two polynomial simplicial resolutions give canonically equivalent values.
A non-discrete input is computed in node derived-input-higher-homotopy.

nodes.title: Conjugate filtration on derived Hodge–Tate cohomology
nodes.statement: For a bounded prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra R, the conjugate filtration is the functorial increasing N-indexed filtration Fil_0^conj → Fil_1^conj → ⋯ → Δ̄_{R/A} by derived p-complete objects of D(R), defined as the derived p-completed left Kan extension, from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras, of the canonical filtration Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} := τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{R/A}. It is exhaustive (Δ̄_{R/A} is the derived p-completed colimit of the Fil_i^conj), multiplicative (there are maps Fil_i^conj ⊗^L_R Fil_j^conj → Fil_{i+j}^conj compatible with the product of Δ̄_{R/A}), natural in R (compatibility with base change of prisms is node derived-prismatic-base-change), and Fil_0^conj = R with Fil_0^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} the structure map. Its graded pieces gr_i^conj := cofib(Fil_{i−1}^conj → Fil_i^conj) are computed by node derived-hodge-tate-comparison. The filtration is not the Postnikov filtration of Δ̄_{R/A} outside the smooth case: for a nonzero regular quotient R = (A/I)/(f) with bounded p^∞-torsion, Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete while no Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
Filtered objects are functors (N, ≤) → D(R); completed filtered tensor products and graded pieces are those of DD.1.
proofSteps: On Sm_{A/I} the canonical filtration τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A} of the commutative algebra Δ̄_{R/A} ∈ D(R) is functorial and lax multiplicative, with gr_i = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A})[−i].

Left Kan extend the functor R ↦ (R, Fil_•^conj Δ̄_{R/A}) to derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras in filtered derived p-complete modules over the varying algebra (DD.1 for filtered objects; E3 and E5:animation for the extension).

Exhaustiveness: the extension commutes with colimits and colim_i τ^{≤i} is the identity on Sm_{A/I}. Fil_0: by PR.1, H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) = R on Sm_{A/I}, and the left Kan extension of R ↦ R is the identity functor.

The non-example: for R = (A/I)/(f) the graded pieces are the free modules Γ^i_R(R·f̄){−i} of rank 1 (node derived-hodge-tate-comparison), so the cofibre of Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} is a nonzero p-completely flat R-module.
acceptance: Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} = R for every R.
For p-completely smooth R the filtration is τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A}, so Fil_i^conj ∈ D^{≤i}.
For R = A/I every Fil_i^conj → Δ̄_{R/A} = A/I is an isomorphism.
For a nonzero regular quotient the filtration is strictly increasing although Δ̄ is discrete.

nodes.title: Derived Hodge–Tate comparison
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. For every derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra R and every i ≥ 0 there is an isomorphism in D(R), natural in R and multiplicative in i, gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ (∧^i_R L_{R/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧, where L_{R/(A/I)} is the cotangent complex, ∧^i the derived exterior power (DD.0), {−i} the Breuil–Kisin twist and ^∧ derived p-completion. For i = 0 it is Fil_0^conj = R; for p-completely smooth R it is the Hodge–Tate isomorphism Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}) of PR.1. Consequences. (a) If R is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{R/(A/I)} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], then gr_i^conj ∈ D^{[0,i]}(R) and Δ̄_{R/A}, Δ_{R/A} ∈ D^{≥0}. (b) If R is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{R/(A/I)}[−1] is p-completely flat over R, then gr_i^conj ≃ Γ^i_R(L_{R/(A/I)}[−1]){−i}^∧ is a p-completely flat R-module in degree 0, Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete, has bounded p^∞-torsion and R → Δ̄_{R/A} is p-completely faithfully flat, and Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free. (c) If the derived p-completion of L_{R/(A/I)} vanishes, then R ≃ Δ̄_{R/A}.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
Derived exterior and divided powers and the décalage isomorphism ∧^i(M[1]) ≃ Γ^i(M)[i] are those of DD.0; p-complete Tor-amplitude and p-complete flatness are those of BMS2 §4.1.
proofSteps: Smooth case: PR.1 gives gr_i = H^i(Δ̄_{R/A})[−i] ≅ Ω^i_{R/(A/I)}{−i}[−i], functorially in R ∈ Sm_{A/I} and compatibly with products.

Left Kan extension: graded pieces commute with colimits, so gr_i^conj is the left Kan extension of R ↦ (Ω^i_{R/(A/I)})^∧{−i}[−i]; by definition of the derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex (DD.0) and compatibility of derived completion with colimits (DD.1) this is (∧^i L_{R/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧.

(a): ∧^i L has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−i, 0], so its completion lies in D^{[−i,0]} (BMS2 Lemma 4.6, via DD.1); each Fil_i^conj has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [0, i] over R, hence so does the colimit M of the Fil_i^conj; as R has bounded p^∞-torsion, Δ̄ = M^∧ = Rlim_n (M ⊗^L_R R/p^n) is a limit of objects of D^{≥0} (proof of BMS2 Lemma 4.6), so Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}.

(b): décalage gives ∧^i(L)[−i] ≃ Γ^i(L[−1]); divided powers of a p-completely flat module are p-completely flat; BMS2 Lemma 4.7 gives discreteness and bounded torsion; R/p → Δ̄/p is injective with flat cokernel, hence faithfully flat. If Δ̄ = Δ ⊗^L_A A/I is discrete then, I being locally generated by a nonzerodivisor d and Δ being derived d-complete, multiplication by d is bijective on H^j(Δ) for j ≠ 0, 1, surjective on H^1 and injective on H^0; derived Nakayama gives H^j(Δ) = 0 for j ≠ 0.
(c): all gr_i^conj with i > 0 vanish.
acceptance: Polynomial algebra: recovers Ω^i{−i} ≅ H^i(Δ̄).
R = A/I: gr_i^conj = 0 for i > 0.
R = (A/I)/(f), f a nonzerodivisor, R of bounded p^∞-torsion: gr_i^conj = Γ^i_R(R·f̄){−i}, free of rank 1.
S perfectoid over a perfect prism: L^∧_{S/(A/I)} = 0, so Δ̄_{S/A} = S and Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S).
R = A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I: gr_i^conj ≃ R{−i} for all i (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).

nodes.title: The first conjugate piece is the cotangent complex over the prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. There is a canonical isomorphism in D(R), natural in R, α_R : (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ ≃ Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{R/A}, where L_{R/A} is the cotangent complex of R over A (not over A/I). It is an isomorphism of extensions: the transitivity triangle R ≃ (R ⊗^L_{A/I} L_{(A/I)/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → (L_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧, formed with L_{(A/I)/A} ≃ I/I²[1], is carried to Fil_0^conj → Fil_1^conj → gr_1^conj with the identifications gr_0^conj = R and gr_1^conj = (L_{R/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧ of the derived Hodge–Tate comparison. For p-completely smooth R it reads L_{R/A}^∧ ≃ (τ^{≤1}Δ̄_{R/A}){1}[1]. For a p-adic formal scheme X over A/I that is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion the isomorphisms glue to α_X : (L_{X/Spf(A)}{−1}[−1])^∧ ≃ Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} in D(X).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
All cotangent complexes are derived p-completed; the hypothesis on X is the one added in Proposition 3.1.11 of the arXiv v4 text of ALB23.
proofSteps: Both sides are left Kan extended from p-completely smooth A/I-algebras (DD.0 for the left side), so it suffices to construct α_R naturally for R in Sm_{A/I}.

For (B, J) in (R/A)_Δ pull back 0 → J/J² → B/J² → B/J → 0 along R → B/J. This is a square-zero extension of R by B/J{1} in A-algebras, classified by L_{R/A}^∧ → B/J{1}[1] (derivation description of the cotangent complex, DD.0). The limit over the site gives α_R : (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1])^∧ → Δ̄_{R/A}, which factors through τ^{≤1}.

For R = (A/I)⟨x⟩ one has L_{R/A}^∧ = R ⊗ I/I²[1] ⊕ R dx; on the first summand the map is the base extension of I/I² → J/J², on dx it is the Bockstein of the image of x. So H^0(α_R) is the Hodge–Tate map Ω^1 ≅ H^1(Δ̄){1} and H^{−1}(α_R) is the canonical map R ⊗ I/I² → H^0(Δ̄){1}.
By functoriality, and because Ω^1 is generated by the dr, α_R induces the canonical maps on cohomology for every R in Sm_{A/I}; hence it is an isomorphism, compatible with the two triangles.
acceptance: R = A/I: both sides are A/I.
R = (A/I)⟨x⟩: Fil_1^conj = τ^{≤1}Δ̄ = Δ̄ and the class of the extension of Ω^1{−1}[−1] by R vanishes, in accordance with the lift A⟨x⟩ over A/I².
R = (A/I)/(f) with f a nonzerodivisor: Fil_1^conj is the discrete module (L_{R/A}{−1}[−1]) = J/J²{−1} for J = (I, f), an extension of R·f̄{−1} by R.

nodes.title: Splitting of the first conjugate piece and liftings modulo I²
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a p-completely flat p-adic formal scheme over A/I. The extension Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{X/A} = O_X → Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} → gr_1^conj Δ̄_{X/A} = (L_{X/(A/I)}{−1}[−1])^∧ has a splitting in D(X) exactly when a p-completely flat lift of X across A/I²→A/I exists. More precisely, the class of this extension in Ext^1_{O_X}(gr_1^conj, gr_0^conj) = Ext^2_{O_X}((L_{X/(A/I)})^∧{−1}, O_X) is, up to sign, the obstruction class to lifting X over A/I².
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
X is locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion (automatic for p-completely flat X over the bounded A/I).
ALB23 phrase the splitting as "isomorphic in D(X) to a complex with zero differentials"; the node uses the precise form from their proof, the vanishing of the extension class.
proofSteps: By node first-conjugate-piece-cotangent the extension class equals the class of the transitivity triangle O_X ⊗ I/I²[1] → L_{X/Spf(A)}^∧ → L_{X/(A/I)}^∧, twisted by {−1}.

Illusie, Complexe cotangent III.2.1.2.3 (ALB23 Proposition 3.2.2; requested from DD.0): for a ring S, an invertible ideal I and a flat S/I-scheme Y, the class of L_{Y/S} in Ext^2(L_{Y/(S/I)}, I/I² ⊗ O_Y) is, up to sign, the obstruction to lifting Y to a flat S/I²-scheme.

Reduce modulo p^n: since A/I is classically p-complete, a p-completely flat lift of X over A/I² is a compatible system of flat lifts of X ⊗ A/(I, p^n) over A/(I², p^n); derived p-completion does not change the derived reductions of the cotangent complex. A splitting of the completed triangle induces compatible splittings for all n, and a splitting (not only the vanishing of the class) determines the lift, so the lifts are compatible.
acceptance: If X lifts to a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-scheme, the Higgs specialisation of BS22 Remark 4.13 splits O_X → Δ̄_{X/A}, in particular Fil_1^conj.
For (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) the statement is the Deligne–Illusie criterion: Fil_1^conj splits exactly when X lifts to Z/p².
X = Spf(A/I): the class lies in the zero group.

nodes.title: Étale descent and derived prismatic cohomology of formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (1) Étale base change: for a p-completely étale map R → R′ of derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras, Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R′ ≃ Δ̄_{R′/A}, compatibly with conjugate filtrations. (2) Sheaf property: for a p-completely étale cover R → R′ with derived p-completed Čech nerve R′^•, the map Δ_{R/A} → lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{R′^n/A} is an equivalence of commutative algebras with Frobenius in D_comp(A); so R ↦ Δ_{R/A} is a sheaf for the p-completely étale topology on derived p-complete A/I-algebras. (3) Globalisation: for a p-adic formal scheme X over Spf(A/I), locally the formal spectrum of a p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion, there is a functorially defined derived (p, I)-complete commutative algebra Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) with a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_X, such that RΓ(U, Δ_{X/A}) ≃ Δ_{R/A} for every affine object U = Spf(R) of X_ét, compatibly with Frobenius; Δ̄_{X/A} := Δ_{X/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is an object of D(X_ét, O_X) with an increasing exhaustive multiplicative filtration Fil_•^conj and gr_i^conj Δ̄_{X/A} ≃ (∧^i L_{X/(A/I)}){−i}[−i]^∧.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
The bounded-torsion hypothesis on X in (3) is the one of the arXiv v4 text of ALB23 Proposition 3.1.11; BS22 state the globalisation for every p-adic formal scheme.
proofSteps: (1): L_{R′/R} vanishes after derived p-completion, so the transitivity triangle gives (∧^i L_{R/(A/I)})^∧ ⊗̂^L_R R′ ≃ (∧^i L_{R′/(A/I)})^∧ (DD.0); the natural map of filtered objects is an isomorphism on graded pieces by the derived Hodge–Tate comparison, hence an isomorphism.

(2): by (1) the cosimplicial object Δ̄_{R′^•/A} is Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_R R′^•, and M ≃ lim M ⊗̂^L_R R′^• for every derived p-complete M ∈ D(R) by p-completely faithfully flat descent (DD.1). Limits commute with − ⊗^L_A A/I, and a map of derived I-complete objects that is an isomorphism modulo I is an isomorphism.

(3): the sheaf on the affine objects of X_ét determines Δ_{X/A}; Frobenius, the filtration and its graded pieces are sheaves by the same argument (flat descent for the completed cotangent powers, DD.5).
acceptance: For X smooth the object Δ_{X/A} is the one of PR.1.
For X = Spf(R) affine, RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) = Δ_{R/A}.
For a finite disjoint union the value is the product: Δ_{(R_1 × R_2)/A} = Δ_{R_1/A} × Δ_{R_2/A}.

nodes.title: Base change for derived prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) → (B, J) be a map of bounded prisms (so J = IB) and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. Let R_B := (R ⊗^L_A B)^∧ = (R ⊗^L_{A/I} B/J)^∧ be the derived p-completion. Then the natural map Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_A B → Δ_{R_B/B} is an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D_comp(B), the completion on the left being the derived (p, J)-completion. It is compatible with Frobenius, and its reduction modulo J, Δ̄_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A/I} B/J ≃ Δ̄_{R_B/B}, is compatible with the conjugate filtrations and, through L_{R_B/(B/J)} ≃ L_{R/(A/I)} ⊗^L_R R_B, with the identifications of the graded pieces.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
No flatness of A → B is assumed; R ⊗^L_A B is computed in animated rings, and A/I ⊗^L_A B = B/J because I is invertible and B is I-torsion-free.
proofSteps: For p-completely smooth R this is base change for the site cohomology (PR.1).

Both sides commute with sifted colimits in R: the left side by construction and because − ⊗̂^L_A B commutes with completed colimits (DD.1), the right side because R ↦ R_B commutes with colimits. A natural transformation between sifted-colimit-preserving functors that is an isomorphism on Poly_{A/I} is an isomorphism.
The compatibility with filtrations follows from base change for the cotangent complex and its derived exterior powers (DD.0).
acceptance: B = A: the identity.
Base change to the perfection (A, I) → (A, I)_perf and to an orientable cover (A, I) → (B, (d)).
For a map of perfect prisms A → A′ and S an A/I-algebra: Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_A A′ ≃ Δ_{(S ⊗̂^L A′/I)/A′}, the formula used by PerfectoidQuotients Q2–Q4 to descend surjectivity of perfectoidization.
The universal case of Example 7.9 is reached by base change from Z_p{d, f_1,…,f_r}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧.

nodes.title: Colimit preservation and the Künneth formula
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. The functor R ↦ Δ_{R/A} from derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebras to commutative algebras in D_comp(A) (derived (p, I)-complete E_∞-A-algebras) commutes with all colimits. In particular it is symmetric monoidal: Δ_{(A/I)/A} = A, and for every diagram R_1 ← R_3 → R_2 the canonical map Δ_{R_1/A} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{R_3/A}} Δ_{R_2/A} → Δ_{(R_1 ⊗̂^L_{R_3} R_2)/A} is an equivalence of commutative algebras with Frobenius, where the completion on the left is derived (p, I)-adic and on the right derived p-adic.

nodes.title: Künneth formula for smooth formal schemes
nodes.statement: Fix a bounded (A,I). Require the formal schemes X and Y over Spf(A/I) to be quasi-compact, quasi-separated and p-completely smooth. Their prismatic complexes satisfy RΓ(X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y, Δ_{X ×_{Spf(A/I)} Y/A}) ≃ RΓ(X, Δ_{X/A}) ⊗̂^L_A RΓ(Y, Δ_{Y/A}), an isomorphism of commutative algebras in D_comp(A) compatible with Frobenius, the completed tensor product being derived (p, I)-adic.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.
The hypothesis quasi-compact quasi-separated is part of the statement in the arXiv v4 text of ALB23.
proofSteps: The external product map is defined by functoriality; on affine opens it is the isomorphism of node kunneth-formula.
Both sides are derived I-complete, so it suffices to compare after − ⊗^L_A A/I; for quasi-compact quasi-separated X this reduction commutes with RΓ.

On Δ̄ the conjugate filtration is finite (the canonical filtration), with graded pieces Ω^i{−i}[−i]; the claim follows from Ω^i_{X×Y} = ⊕_{a+b=i} Ω^a_X ⊠ Ω^b_Y and the projection formula and flat base change for quasi-coherent cohomology of quasi-compact quasi-separated formal schemes (requested from DD.5).
acceptance: X = Y = Spf(A/I)⟨x⟩ recovers the affine formula.
For X, Y proper smooth both sides are perfect complexes of A-modules (PR.1) and the completed tensor product is the ordinary derived tensor product.
X = Spf(A/I): the identity.

nodes.title: The comparison map from derived prismatic cohomology to prisms and to site cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra. For every prism (B, J) over (A, I), bounded or not, equipped with an A/I-algebra map π_0(R) → B/J, there is a map ev_{(B,J)} : Δ_{R/A} → B of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), natural in (B, J) and in R, commuting with Frobenius (φ_B ∘ ev = ev ∘ φ_R), whose reduction modulo I is a map Δ̄_{R/A} → B/J of R-algebras. These maps assemble to the comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → lim_{(B,J)} B = RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) to the cohomology of the prismatic site of π_0(R). Construction: the functor R ↦ RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) restricts on p-completed polynomial algebras to PR.1's functor, and c is the unique natural transformation out of the left Kan extension extending the identity there; concretely, for a resolution R_• → R by p-completely ind-smooth algebras, Δ_{R/A} = colim_{Δ^op} lim_{C ∈ (R_•/A)_Δ} C and (B, J) defines compatible objects of all (R_n/A)_Δ, which gives Δ_{R/A} → colim_{Δ^op} B = B. The map c_R is an isomorphism for p-completely smooth R (node derived-agrees-with-site), for regular quotients (node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope) and for quasiregular semiperfectoid R over a perfect prism (node qrsp-prism). It is not an isomorphism in general: the target depends only on π_0(R) and lies in D^{≥0}, whereas Δ_{R/A} does not (node derived-input-higher-homotopy).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
The cohomology of O_Δ on the site of bounded prisms is the limit over the category, because O_Δ is a sheaf with vanishing higher Čech cohomology (PR.1, BS22 Corollary 3.12 and Remark 4.5).
When Δ_{R/A} is discrete, ev_{(B,J)} is a map of δ-rings (node derived-agrees-with-site).
proofSteps: Čech–Alexander theory (PR.1): for p-completely ind-smooth P, Δ_{P/A} = lim_{C ∈ (P/A)_Δ} C, also over the category of all prisms, since the weakly initial object and its Čech nerve are bounded and their universal property holds for all prisms.

Left Kan extension: the functor R ↦ lim over prisms under π_0(R) receives the canonical transformation from the left Kan extension of its restriction to polynomial algebras (E3); project to the factor indexed by (B, J).
Frobenius and multiplicativity: each projection lim_C C → B is a map of commutative algebras commuting with the Frobenius lifts of the prisms; reduction modulo I is compatible with the maps from R.
acceptance: R = A/I: Δ_{R/A} = A and ev_{(A,I)} is the identity.
For p-completely smooth R the map c_R is an isomorphism.
For R = A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I the map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → A is not an isomorphism.
For a perfect prism and (B, J) perfect, ev_{(B,J)} factors through the perfection Δ_{R/A,perf}.

nodes.title: Agreement with site cohomology: smooth algebras and the discrete case
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. (a) If R is a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, the derived Δ_{R/A} is the site cohomology RΓ((R/A)_Δ, O_Δ) of PR.1, compatibly with Frobenius and with the Hodge–Tate comparison; the conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration. (b) Let R be a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra such that Δ̄_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0. Then: (1) Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free, and the Frobenius φ_R lifts naturally to a δ-A-algebra structure on the ring Δ_{R/A}; (2) (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is a prism over (A, I), equipped with a map R → Δ̄_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A}/IΔ_{R/A}; it is bounded exactly when Δ̄_{R/A} has bounded p^∞-torsion; (3) among prisms over (A,I) with a specified R→B/J there exists an initial prism; (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is weakly initial in it (the maps being those of node comparison-to-prisms, which are δ-maps), and the initial object is the image of an idempotent endomorphism of (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}). The statement does not assert that (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is initial; Bhatt and Scholze conjecture this. It is proved in the cases of nodes regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope and qrsp-prism, where consequently Δ_{R/A} computes the cohomology of the prismatic site of R.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
In (b) the category in (3) consists of all prisms over (A, I), bounded or not.
A discrete Δ_{R/A} is not called "the initial object" here: the source proves weak initiality, and that the initial object is a retract.
proofSteps: (a) is the third step of the construction (node derived-prismatic-cohomology).

(b)(1): Čech–Alexander complexes and canonical simplicial resolutions give a functor R ↦ F_A(R) to simplicial cosimplicial derived (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebras with colim_{Δ^op} lim_Δ F_A(R) ≃ Δ_{R/A}. The δ-structure is a section F_A(R) → W_2(F_A(R)) of the restriction, lying over A → W_2(A) (PR.0). Using the functorial pullback square expressing W_2(B) as B ×_{B ⊗^L F_p} B (through the ghost map and φ) for simplicial commutative rings, and the discreteness of Δ_{R/A}, one identifies colim lim W_2(F_A(R)) with W_2(Δ_{R/A}); the section gives the δ-structure refining φ_R.

(b)(2): Δ_{R/A} is derived (p, I)-complete and Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I is discrete, so Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free (node derived-hodge-tate-comparison, last step of (b)); IΔ_{R/A} is invertible and contains a distinguished element locally.

(b)(3): the maps of node comparison-to-prisms are δ-maps by the argument of (1). Apply node idempotent-retract-initial-object to the category of prisms over (A, I) with a map from R, which is idempotent complete, with X = (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}).

R p-completely smooth of positive relative dimension: Δ̄_{R/A} is not discrete and (b) does not apply.
R = (A/I)/(f): (b) applies and the idempotent is the identity (node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope).
R perfectoid over a perfect prism: Δ_{R/A} = A_inf(R) with its unique δ-structure.

nodes.title: Initial objects as idempotent retracts
nodes.statement: Let C be an idempotent complete category and X an object of C. Let X/C be the category of objects Y of C equipped with a map X → Y. Assume that the identity functor of C factors through the projection X/C → C by a functor F : C → X/C. Then F(X) = (e : X → X) is an idempotent endomorphism of X, and the corresponding retract X′ of X is an initial object of C. In particular C has an initial object, and X is initial if and only if e is the identity.
hypotheses: C is an ordinary category in which every idempotent splits.
The factorisation may be given up to a natural isomorphism of the composite with the identity; this reduces to the strict case by transporting the structure maps along the isomorphism.
proofSteps: Write F(X) = (e : X → X). Applying F to the morphism e of C gives a morphism (X →e X) → (X →e X) in X/C with underlying map e, that is e ∘ e = e.
Split e as X → X′ → X. Then F(X′) = (X → X′) and this map is a (split) epimorphism.
F is faithful, so Hom_C(X′, Y) injects into Hom_{X/C}(X → X′, X → Y), which has at most one element because X → X′ is an epimorphism. There is at least one map X′ → X → Y. Hence X′ is initial.
acceptance: C the category of sets and X = ∅ with F(Y) = (∅ → Y): e is the identity and X is initial.
C the category of pointed sets and X a two-point pointed set with F(Y) the constant map to the base point: e is the constant map and the retract is the one-point set.
C = prisms over (A, I) with a map from R and X = (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}): BS22 Lemma 7.7 (3).

nodes.title: Prismatic cohomology of a regular quotient is the prismatic envelope
nodes.statement: Fix a bounded prism (A, I). Let f_1,…,f_r ∈ A have images forming a Koszul-regular sequence on A/I, let J = (I, f_1,…,f_r), and assume that R := A/J has bounded p^∞-torsion. Then: (1) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ Γ^i_R(J/(J² + I)){−i}, a finite free R-module, for all i; Δ̄_{R/A} is discrete and p-completely faithfully flat over R, and Δ_{R/A} is discrete and I-torsion-free. (2) (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is a bounded prism and is the initial object of (R/A)_Δ; it is also initial among all prisms (B, IB) over (A, I) with a map R → B/IB, so the idempotent of node derived-agrees-with-site is the identity. (3) If I = (d), the natural map A{f_1/d,…,f_r/d}^∧ → Δ_{R/A}, from the derived (p, I)-complete simplicial δ-A-algebra obtained by freely adjoining the f_i/d, is an isomorphism; in particular the source is discrete, and it is the universal prism over (A, I) under the δ-pair (A, J); it is the prismatic envelope of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes whenever A is flat over a bounded prism relative to which (f_i) is completely regular (the universal case of the proof; the rings of node regular-semiperfectoid-example).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
A regular sequence is Koszul-regular; the source assumes "bounded p-torsion", meaning bounded p^∞-torsion.
In (3) the element f_i/d is adjoined in animated δ-A-algebras (PR.0, animated-delta-rings) and the result is derived (p, I)-completed.
proofSteps: L_{R/(A/I)} ≃ J/(J² + I)[1] with J/(J² + I) free on the f_i (DD.0), so gr_i^conj = Γ^i(J/(J² + I)){−i} by décalage; apply consequence (b) of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison and node derived-agrees-with-site.

The claims are local on Spf(A); assume I = (d). Since f_i = 0 in Δ̄_{R/A}, the universal property of free adjunction gives B := A{f_1/d,…,f_r/d}^∧ → Δ_{R/A}. If this is an isomorphism, the universal property of B shows that (B, IB) is initial.

Both sides commute with base change in (A, d, f) (node derived-prismatic-base-change), so pass to the universal case A = Z_p{d, f_1,…,f_r}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧, where A/I and R are p-torsion-free and f is (p, I)-completely regular relative to A_0 = Z_p{d}[δ(d)^{−1}]^∧. There B is the prismatic envelope A{J/I}^∧ (PR.0), discrete, and (B, IB) is initial in (R/A)_Δ.

By weak initiality B → Δ_{R/A} has a retraction; so B/IB → Δ̄_{R/A} has a p-torsion-free cokernel and it suffices to show that B/IB[1/p] → Δ̄_{R/A}[1/p] is surjective. The target is generated as a Banach R[1/p]-algebra by gr_1^conj = J/(J² + I){−1}, and J/I maps onto gr_1^conj by the computation with a free resolution of R over A/I (the prismatic analogue of Bhatt, p-adic derived de Rham cohomology, Claim 3.30).
acceptance: r = 0: R = A/I and Δ_{R/A} = A.
(A, I) = (Z_p⟨x⟩, (p)) with δ(x) = 0 and f = x^p: R = F_p[x]/(x^p) and Δ_{R/A} = Z_p⟨x⟩{x^p/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope of (x) in Z_p⟨x⟩ (PR.0, pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope).
(A, I) = (A_inf(O_C), (ξ)) and f = p: R = O_C/p and Δ_{R/A} = A_inf{p/ξ}^∧ (node regular-semiperfectoid-example).
The graded pieces gr_i^conj are free of rank binom(r+i−1, i).

nodes.title: Acceptance example: a derived input with nonzero higher homotopy
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism with A/I ≠ 0 and R := A/I ⊗^L_{(A/I)⟨x⟩} A/I, both maps sending x to 0; R is the free derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra on one generator in degree 1, with π_0(R) = A/I and π_1(R) ≅ A/I. Then: (1) L_{R/(A/I)} ≃ R[1] and gr_i^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≃ R{−i} for every i ≥ 0; (2) Δ̄_{R/A} ∈ D^{[−1,0]} and H^{−1}(Δ̄_{R/A}) contains π_1(R) = A/I, so it is nonzero; (3) Δ_{R/A} ≃ A ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{(A/I)⟨x⟩/A}} A; (4) the comparison map c_R : Δ_{R/A} → RΓ((π_0(R)/A)_Δ, O_Δ) = A is not an isomorphism, Δ_{R/A} is not discrete and is not determined by π_0(R); node derived-agrees-with-site (b) does not apply to R.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.

(2): each gr_i^conj ≃ R{−i} lies in D^{[−1,0]}, so do all Fil_i^conj and their completed colimit; since H^{−2}(gr_i^conj) = 0 the maps H^{−1}(Fil_{i−1}^conj) → H^{−1}(Fil_i^conj) are injective, and H^{−1}(Fil_0^conj) = π_1(R).
(3): node kunneth-formula applied to A/I ← (A/I)⟨x⟩ → A/I.

nodes.title: The prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, R any perfectoid ring with a map R → S, and (A, I) = (A_inf(R), ker θ). Then: (1) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A} ≃ Γ^i_S(L_{S/R}[−1]){−i}^∧ is a p-completely flat S-module; Δ̄_{S/A} is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion, and the map S → Δ̄_{S/A} is p-completely faithfully flat. (2) Δ_{S/A} is discrete, carries a δ-A-algebra structure refining φ_S, and (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}) is a bounded, orientable prism. (3) (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}), with the map S → Δ_{S/A}/I, is the initial object of the category of all prisms (B, J) equipped with a ring map S → B/J: it is the initial prism Δ_S^init of S. Being bounded, it is also the initial object of the absolute prismatic site (S)_Δ and of (S/A)_Δ. (4) Hence Δ_{S/A}, with its δ-structure, Frobenius and map from S, does not depend on R; it is denoted Δ_S, and Δ̄_S := Δ_S/I. (5) If A/I → S is surjective and K = ker(A → S), the canonical maps Δ_{S/A} → Δ^{init,unbdd}_{S/A} := RΓ((S/A)_{Δ,unbdd}, O_Δ) → Δ^init_{S/A} := RΓ((S/A)_Δ, O_Δ) (evaluation on all prisms, then restriction to bounded prisms) are isomorphisms of δ-rings, and Δ^{init,unbdd}_{S/A} is the prismatic envelope A{K/I}^∧ of the δ-pair (A, K).
hypotheses: Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
In (3) the category contains unbounded prisms; it is not the absolute prismatic site of BS22 Remark 4.7, whose objects are bounded (the registered correction PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E5).

The existence of an initial prism for an arbitrary semiperfectoid ring (BS22 Proposition 7.2) belongs to PerfectoidQuotients Q2 and is not used: for quasiregular S existence follows from node derived-agrees-with-site.
(S/A)_{Δ,unbdd} is the category of all prisms over (A, I) with a map S → B/J, with the chaotic topology (ALB23 §3.4).
proofSteps: L_{S/R}[−1] is p-completely flat over S for every perfectoid R → S (BMS2 Lemma 4.25, from DD.5). Consequence (b) of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison gives (1), and node derived-agrees-with-site gives (2) and a weakly initial prism whose initial retract is cut out by an idempotent e_S; it remains to show e_S = id.

Replace R by R⟨Y_i^{1/p^∞}⟩ for a set of variables: this does not change the completed cotangent complexes, hence not Δ_{S/R}; so R → S may be assumed surjective. Choose generators f_j of its kernel. The map S′ := R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j − f_j)^∧ → S, X_j ↦ 0, is surjective and surjective on cotangent complexes, so Δ_{S′/A} → Δ_{S/A} is surjective by the Hodge–Tate comparison; by naturality of the idempotent it suffices to treat S′.

S′ is a completed filtered colimit of rings T = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1 − f_1,…,X_r − f_r), and Δ commutes with filtered colimits (node kunneth-formula). For T, Δ_{T/A} ≃ Δ_{T/A′} with A′ = A_inf(R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩), compatibly with idempotents, and node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope gives e_T = id.

(3) and (4): by BS22 Lemma 4.8 (node PrismaticCohomology:PR.1/perfect-prism-initial) every ring map A/I → B/J to the reduction of a prism lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J); so prisms over (A, I) with a map from S are the same as prisms with a ring map S → B/J.

(5): Δ^{init,unbdd}_{S/A} = A{K/I}^∧ by the universal property of the envelope; it is the initial object of the category in (3), hence equal to Δ_{S/A}, which is bounded and therefore also computes the cohomology of the site of bounded prisms.
acceptance: S = R perfectoid: Δ_S = A_inf(R).
S = O_C/p: Δ_S = A_inf{p/ξ}^∧ (node regular-semiperfectoid-example).
S = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy): node singular-qrsp-example.
Independence: for S = O_C/p the perfect prisms A_inf(O_C) and A_inf(O_C⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩) with Y ↦ 0 give the same Δ_S.
For pS = 0, Δ_S is A_crys(S) up to the Frobenius twist (node qrsp-char-p-acrys).

nodes.title: In characteristic p the prism of a quasiregular semiperfect ring is A_crys
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with pS = 0 (a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra), k := S^♭ the inverse-limit perfection of S, so that k → S is surjective, and A := W(k) with the crystalline perfect prism (A, (p)). Let A_crys(S) be the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of A → S (PD structure compatible with that of (p)), the universal p-complete PD thickening of S (CR.0). Then: (1) there is a canonical isomorphism of p-complete δ-A-algebras, compatible with Frobenius, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂_{A,φ_A} A ≃ A_crys(S). (2) Since φ_A is bijective this gives a φ-equivariant isomorphism of δ-rings Δ_S ≃ A_crys(S); it is φ_A-semilinear over W(k) and not W(k)-linear. Under it the structure map S → Δ̄_S = Δ_S/p corresponds to the map S → A_crys(S)/p through which the Frobenius of A_crys(S)/p factors. (3) If S = k/(x) for a nonzerodivisor x ∈ k, then Δ_{S/W(k)} = W(k){[x]/p}^∧ and A_crys(S) = W(k){[x]^p/p}^∧. (4) For every quasisyntomic k-algebra B the isomorphism of node derived-crystalline-comparison, φ_A^*Δ_{B/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(B/A) (derived crystalline cohomology, node derived-crystalline-comparison), is the unfolding of the isomorphisms (1) over the Čech nerve of a quasisyntomic cover B → S by a quasiregular semiperfect ring: the crystalline comparison extends by descent from quasiregular semiperfect rings to all quasisyntomic F_p-algebras.
hypotheses: Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here.
For every perfect prism (A′, I′) with a map A′/I′ → S one has Δ_{S/A′} = Δ_S (node qrsp-prism), so (2) holds for all such bases, as in ALB23 Lemma 3.4.2.
ALB23 prove (2) using the map θ : Δ_S → S of BS22 Theorem 12.2 (PR.3). The route planned here does not use the Nygaard filtration.
proofSteps: By node derived-crystalline-comparison, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂_{A,φ_A} A ≃ RΓ_crys(S/A), the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A (not the p-completed derived de Rham complex of S over A).

For quasiregular semiperfect S the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A (the p-completed left Kan extension of P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) from polynomial k-algebras; the derived de Rham–Witt complex LWΩ_S of BMS2 §8.2) is concentrated in degree 0, p-torsion-free and naturally isomorphic to A_crys(S) compatibly with Frobenius (BMS2 Proposition 8.13 and Theorem 8.14 (1), (3)); its reduction modulo p is LΩ_{S/F_p} ≅ A_crys(S)/p (BMS2 Proposition 8.12). These statements are requested from DD.4; the identification of LWΩ_S with the left Kan extension used here is the recorded gap "Derived crystalline cohomology of quasiregular semiperfect rings". This gives (1); (2) is its untwisted form, and the description of S → A_crys(S)/p follows from semilinearity.

(3): node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope gives Δ_{S/A} = A{[x]/p}^∧; base change along φ_A gives A{[x]^p/p}^∧, which is the p-completed PD envelope of ([x]) by PR.0 (pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope).

(4): both sides are quasisyntomic sheaves on quasisyntomic k-algebras (node quasisyntomic-descent; RΓ_crys(−/A) is a quasisyntomic sheaf because its reduction modulo p, dR_{−/k}, has a conjugate filtration with graded pieces ∧^i L_{−/k}[−i] (DD.3), which satisfy descent by DD.5), and the isomorphism is natural.
acceptance: S = k perfect: both sides are W(k) and the isomorphism of (2) is φ.
S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Δ_S is the p-completed PD envelope of (x^{1/p}) in Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}]^∧, and A_crys(S) that of (x).
S = O_C/p: Δ_S = A_inf{ξ/p}^∧ = φ^{−1}(A_crys) and A_crys(S) = A_inf{φ(ξ)/p}^∧ is Fontaine's A_crys.
The identification is not W(k)-linear: for S = k/(x), [x]/p lies in Δ_S but not in A_crys(S) ⊂ W(k)[1/p].

nodes.title: Acceptance example: a regular semiperfectoid quotient
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) = (A_inf(R), ker θ), let f_1,…,f_r ∈ R, R_∞ := R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and T := R_∞/(X_1 − f_1,…,X_r − f_r). Then: (1) T is a p-completely free R-module (topologically free on the monomials X^a with exponents in [0,1) ∩ Z[1/p]), X_1 − f_1,…,X_r − f_r is a regular sequence in R_∞, and T is quasiregular semiperfectoid. (2) With A′ := A_inf(R_∞) and g_i := [X_i^♭] − f̃_i for lifts f̃_i ∈ A′ of f_i, Δ_T ≃ A′{g_1/d,…,g_r/d}^∧, the prismatic envelope of (d, g_1,…,g_r), which is (p, d)-completely flat over A = A_inf(R) (and not over A′ when R ≠ 0 and r ≥ 1). (3) Δ̄_T is a p-completely faithfully flat T-algebra with gr_i^conj ≃ Γ^i_T(T^r){−i}. (4) Characteristic p: for R = F_p, r = 1, f = 0, T = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X), one has Δ_T = (Z_p[X^{1/p^∞}]^∧){X/p}^∧, the p-completed PD envelope of the ideal (X^{1/p}), which contains (X^{1/p})^n/n! for all n. (5) Mixed characteristic: for C a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, R = O_C and S = O_C/p, one has Δ_S = A_inf{p/ξ}^∧ = A_inf{ξ/p}^∧; in Δ_S the ideals (ξ) and (p) coincide, and φ maps Δ_S isomorphically onto Fontaine's A_crys = A_inf{φ(ξ)/p}^∧.
hypotheses: Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
proofSteps: (1): R_∞ is topologically free over R⟨X_1,…,X_r⟩ on the monomials with exponents in [0,1); dividing by X_i − f_i identifies T with the completed direct sum of copies of R. L_{T/R_∞} is free of rank r in degree −1, so T is quasiregular semiperfectoid by BMS2 Lemma 4.25 (DD.5).
(2), (3): node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope over the perfect prism (A′, (d)) and independence of the perfectoid base (node qrsp-prism).
(4): [X] has δ([X]) = 0, so A′{X/p} = A′{φ(X^{1/p})/p} is the PD envelope of (X^{1/p}) (PR.0, pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope).

(5): in Δ_S the distinguished element ξ divides the distinguished element p, so they differ by a unit (PR.0, distinguished-factor-rigidity); hence ξ/p ∈ Δ_S and Δ_S = A_inf{ξ/p}^∧. Apply φ and node qrsp-char-p-acrys.
acceptance: r = 0: T = R and Δ_T = A_inf(R).
In (4), x^{n/p}/n! ∈ Δ_T for every n ≥ 0 and x/p ∈ Δ_T.
In (5), ξ/p ∈ Δ_{O_C/p} but ξ/p ∉ A_crys.
gr_1^conj Δ̄_T is free of rank r over T.

nodes.title: Acceptance example: a singular quasiregular semiperfectoid algebra
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)), B := R⟨x, y⟩/(xy) the p-completed node, and S := R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy). Then: (1) B is quasisyntomic and not p-completely smooth over R; B → S is a quasisyntomic cover; S is quasiregular semiperfectoid and not perfectoid, since x^{1/p}y^{1/p} is a nonzero nilpotent when R ≠ 0. (2) Δ_S ≃ A′{[x^♭][y^♭]/d}^∧ with A′ = A_inf(R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩); Δ̄_S is p-completely faithfully flat over S, with gr_i^conj ≃ S{−i} generated by the i-th divided power of the class of xy. (3) Δ_{B/A} ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S^n}, where S^n is the (n+1)-fold completed tensor power of S over B; each S^n is quasiregular semiperfectoid, for instance S^1 = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}, x′^{1/p^∞}, y′^{1/p^∞}⟩/(xy, x − x′, y − y′). (4) gr_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A} ≃ (∧^i L_{B/R}){−i}[−i] with L_{B/R} ≃ [B → B dx ⊕ B dy], 1 ↦ y dx + x dy, in degrees −1, 0; for i ≥ 2 the complex ∧^i L_{B/R}[−i] is the Koszul complex of (y, x) on B placed in degrees 0, 1, 2, with H^0 = 0, H^2 = B/(x, y) = R and H^1 ≠ 0. So the conjugate filtration of the singular B has infinitely many nonzero graded pieces, in contrast with a p-completely smooth algebra of relative dimension 1. (5) A quasiregular semiperfectoid ring that is not a quotient by a finite regular sequence: S′ = R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞} : j ∈ J⟩/(X_j − f_j : j ∈ J)^∧ for an infinite family (f_j); Δ_{S′} is the completed filtered colimit of the envelopes of the finite subfamilies.
hypotheses: Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are those of BMS2 Definition 4.20, equivalently of BS22 Notation 7.1 (BMS2 Remarks 4.21–4.22, Lemma 4.25): S is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion, receives a surjection from a perfectoid ring, and L_{S/Z_p}[−1] is p-completely flat over S. The definition and these equivalences are supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0/DD.5 and are not restated as a node here.
M{n} := M ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗n} is the Breuil–Kisin twist of an A/I-module or complex M, for n ∈ Z; I/I² is an invertible A/I-module.
R ≠ 0 in the non-vanishing assertions.
proofSteps: (1): B is the quotient of the p-completely smooth R⟨x, y⟩ by the nonzerodivisor xy, so L_{B/R} has Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; S is the p-completed base change of B along R⟨x, y⟩ → R⟨x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}⟩, a quasisyntomic cover (BMS2 Lemma 4.16), and S is a regular quotient of a perfectoid ring.
(2): node regular-quotient-prismatic-envelope with r = 1 and node qrsp-prism.
(3): node quasisyntomic-descent, part (3).

(4): node derived-hodge-tate-comparison; the derived exterior power of the cofibre of B → B² is the Koszul-type complex Γ^i(B) → Γ^{i−1}(B) ⊗ B² → Γ^{i−2}(B) ⊗ ∧²B² (DD.0). In B, x a = y b forces both sides to vanish, which gives H^0 = 0 and identifies H^1 with a nonzero quotient of (y) ⊕ (x).
(5): the proof of BS22 Proposition 7.10 and node kunneth-formula for filtered colimits.
acceptance: gr_1^conj Δ̄_S is free of rank 1 over S.
H^2(gr_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A}) = R{−i} for every i ≥ 2.
For R = F_p: S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}]/(xy) and Δ_S is the p-completed PD envelope of ((xy)^{1/p}) in Z_p[x^{1/p^∞}, y^{1/p^∞}]^∧.
S^1 is a quotient of a perfectoid ring by a regular sequence of length 3.

nodes.title: Lifting quasisyntomic covers to the prismatic site
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a quasisyntomic A/I-algebra: R is p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and A/I → R is a quasisyntomic map (p-completely flat, with L_{R/(A/I)} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; BMS2 Definition 4.10). Then there is an object (B → B/IB ← R) of (R/A)_Δ such that R → B/IB is p-completely faithfully flat. One may take B = Δ_{S/A}, where S := (A/I)⟨x_j^{1/p^∞} : j ∈ J⟩ ⊗̂^L_{(A/I)⟨x_j : j ∈ J⟩} R for a surjection (A/I)⟨x_j : j ∈ J⟩ → R; then R → S is a quasisyntomic cover, S/p is relatively semiperfect over A/(I, p), (L_{S/(A/I)})^∧[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and S → Δ̄_{S/A} is p-completely faithfully flat. Consequently: (1) the map A→B is completely flat for (p,I), and is completely faithfully flat whenever A/I→R is so for p; (2) if A is perfect, (A, I) → (B, IB)_perf is flat, and faithfully flat if A/I → R is p-completely faithfully flat.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.
Quasisyntomic maps are those of DD.0; in this statement "quasisyntomic A/I-algebra" is the relative notion, as the proof uses p-complete flatness of A/I → R.
PerfectoidQuotients Q3 uses this statement for André's lemma; it is planned once, here.
proofSteps: R → S is the p-completed base change of the quasisyntomic cover (A/I)⟨x_j⟩ → (A/I)⟨x_j^{1/p^∞}⟩, hence a quasisyntomic cover (BMS2 Lemma 4.16); S is discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion.

S/p is a quotient of the flat A/(I, p)-algebra (A/(I, p))[x_j^{1/p^∞}], which has bijective relative Frobenius, so Ω^1_{S/(A/I)}/p = 0; together with Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0] this makes (L_{S/(A/I)})^∧[−1] p-completely flat.

Consequence (b) of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison: Δ̄_{S/A} is discrete and p-completely faithfully flat over S; node derived-agrees-with-site gives the δ-structure, so B = Δ_{S/A} is a bounded prism with R → S → B/IB p-completely faithfully flat.

(1): each map in A/I → R → S → B/IB is p-completely flat, so A → B is (p, I)-completely flat (PR.0, bounded prisms). (2): the perfection is the completed filtered colimit of B along φ; for perfect A each φ^n-twist of B is (p, I)-completely flat over A, and completed filtered colimits preserve complete (faithful) flatness.
acceptance: R = A/I: B = A.
R = (A/I)⟨x⟩: S = (A/I)⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩ and B = Δ_{S/A} is the (p, I)-completed A[x^{1/p^∞}] with φ(x^{1/p^n}) = x^{1/p^{n−1}}, a relatively perfect δ-A-algebra with B/IB = S.
For a quasisyntomic cover A/I → R of a perfect prism the resulting perfect prism over (A, I) is faithfully flat: the step used in André's lemma.

For R = (A/I)⟨x⟩ the construction gives B = Δ_{S/A} with B/IB = S = (A/I)⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩ ≠ R; the object Δ_{R/A} itself is not a prism (Δ̄_{R/A} has H^1 ≠ 0), although other objects with B/IB = R exist (A⟨x⟩ with δ(x) = 0).

nodes.title: Quasisyntomic descent and unfolding
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism. Let C_{A/I} be the category of p-complete A/I-algebras B with bounded p^∞-torsion such that L_{B/(A/I)} has p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0], and call B → C in C_{A/I} a cover if it is a quasisyntomic cover (p-completely faithfully flat with L_{C/B} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]). (1) For every cover B → C with p-completed Čech nerve C^• (each C^n is discrete, of bounded p^∞-torsion and in C_{A/I}), the maps Δ_{B/A} → lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{C^n/A}, Δ̄_{B/A} → lim Δ̄_{C^n/A} and Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{B/A} → lim Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{C^n/A}, for every i, are equivalences. So B ↦ Δ_{B/A} is a sheaf on C_{A/I}^op with values in commutative algebras with Frobenius in D_comp(A). (2) If (A, I) is perfect, C_{A/I} contains the category QSyn_{A/I} of all maps A/I → B with B a quasisyntomic ring (BMS2 Variant 4.33 and Lemma 4.34), so B ↦ Δ_{B/A} is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology on QSyn_{A/I}. (3) Unfolding: for perfect (A, I) and B in QSyn_{A/I}, choose a quasisyntomic cover B → S with S quasiregular semiperfectoid. All terms S^n of its Čech nerve are quasiregular semiperfectoid and Δ_{B/A} ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S^n}, a limit of discrete δ-rings; thus Δ_{−/A} on QSyn_{A/I} is the unfolding (BMS2 Proposition 4.31) of S ↦ Δ_S on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. In particular Δ_{B/A} ∈ D^{≥0}, and Δ_{B/A} with its Frobenius does not depend on the perfect prism (A, I) under B.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.

BS22 state (2), for a perfect prism. Part (1) is the statement the same proof gives for a bounded prism under the cotangent hypothesis that BMS2 Lemma 4.34 supplies in the perfect case (its proof read with the registered correction PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E2).
The quasisyntomic site, covers by quasiregular semiperfectoid rings, unfolding and flat descent for completed cotangent powers are supplied by DD.5.

Descent is asserted for the quasisyntomic topology only: for a p-completely faithfully flat map without control of the cotangent complex the graded pieces are not uniformly coconnective and the argument does not apply.
proofSteps: Reduce to Δ̄: limits commute with − ⊗^L_A A/I, and a map of derived I-complete objects that is an isomorphism modulo I is an isomorphism (DD.1).

Graded pieces: B ↦ (∧^i L_{B/(A/I)})^∧ satisfies descent along p-completely faithfully flat maps of p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion (BMS2 Theorem 3.1 and Remark 4.9; DD.5); twisting and shifting preserve this. By induction each Fil_i^conj satisfies descent.

Passage to the colimit: on C_{A/I}, gr_i^conj ∈ D^{[0,i]} (node derived-hodge-tate-comparison (a)), so all Fil_i^conj lie in D^{≥0}. Totalisations of cosimplicial objects of D^{≥0} commute with filtered colimits, and with derived p-completion, so Δ̄ satisfies descent.

(2): BMS2 Lemma 4.34. (3): BMS2 Lemmas 4.28 and 4.30 give the cover and its Čech nerve (DD.5), node qrsp-prism gives discreteness and independence of the base, and BMS2 Proposition 4.31 identifies sheaves on the two sites.
acceptance: B = S quasiregular semiperfectoid: the constant cover gives Δ_S.
B = R⟨x⟩ over a perfect prism with the cover R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩: Δ_{B/A} is the totalisation of the cosimplicial δ-ring Δ of the terms R⟨x_0^{1/p^∞},…,x_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(x_0 − x_i).
The singular algebra R⟨x, y⟩/(xy): node singular-qrsp-example (3).
The étale topology is coarser, and node derived-prismatic-etale-descent holds without any hypothesis on the cotangent complex.

nodes.title: Derived crystalline comparison
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect F_p-algebra and (A, I) = (W(k), (p)) the corresponding crystalline perfect prism. For a derived p-complete simplicial k-algebra S put S^{(1)} := S ⊗^L_{k,φ} k, and let RΓ_crys(S/A) be the derived crystalline cohomology of S over A: the p-completed left Kan extension of P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) from finitely generated polynomial k-algebras (for k = F_p the derived de Rham–Witt complex LWΩ_S of BMS2 §8.2); its reduction modulo p is the derived de Rham complex dR_{S/k} relative to k. It is not the p-completed derived de Rham cohomology of S over A: dR^∧_{k/W(k)} = (W(k)⟨x⟩/(x − p))^∧ ≠ W(k). Then there are natural isomorphisms of commutative algebras in D_comp(A), compatible with Frobenius, Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A,φ_A} A ≃ Δ_{S^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(S/A), extending the crystalline comparison Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(P/A) of PR.1 for smooth k-algebras P. The Frobenius twist is part of the statement: Δ_{S/A} itself is not A-linearly isomorphic to RΓ_crys(S/A) in general.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; k is perfect of characteristic p, so W(k) is a perfect p-torsion-free δ-ring and (W(k), (p)) is a bounded prism.

A derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra is an animated commutative A/I-algebra (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:animation) whose underlying complex is derived p-complete (DD.1); tensor products of such algebras are derived and derived p-completed.

The comparison of RΓ_crys(S/A) with site-theoretic crystalline cohomology of singular S is not part of this node; modulo p, RΓ_crys(S/A) is the derived de Rham complex dR_{S/k} of DD.2, by crystalline base change for polynomial algebras (CR.2).
proofSteps: First isomorphism: base change (node derived-prismatic-base-change) along the map of prisms φ_A : (A, (p)) → (A, (p)); the base change of S is S^{(1)}.

Second isomorphism on polynomial algebras: PR.1's crystalline comparison (BS22 Theorem 5.2 with the PD ideal J = (p)) gives Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} ≃ RΓ_crys(P/A), functorially in P and compatibly with Frobenius.

Left Kan extension: P ↦ Δ_{P^{(1)}/A} extends to S ↦ Δ_{S^{(1)}/A} because S ↦ S^{(1)} commutes with colimits; P ↦ RΓ_crys(P/A) ≃ (Ω^*_{P̃/A})^∧, for a p-complete smooth lift P̃, extends to RΓ_crys(S/A) by definition; the isomorphism of STEP2 is natural in P, hence extends.
acceptance: S = k: Δ_{k/A} = W(k) = RΓ_crys(k/A); by contrast dR^∧_{k/W(k)} = (W(k)⟨x⟩/(x − p))^∧ is not W(k), so the derived de Rham complex over W(k) cannot replace derived crystalline cohomology.
S = k[x]: the right side is the p-completed de Rham complex of W(k)⟨x⟩ and the left side is Δ_{k[x]/W(k)} twisted by φ.
S quasiregular semiperfect: the right side is A_crys(S) (node qrsp-char-p-acrys).
S = k/(x): Δ_{S/A} = A{[x]/p}^∧ and RΓ_crys(S/A) = A{[x]^p/p}^∧ are different subrings of A[1/p]-algebras; the twist cannot be removed.

nodes.title: Perfection of derived prismatic cohomology and perfectoidization
nodes.statement: Fix a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I) = (A_inf(R), ker θ), I = (d), and a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S. (1) The perfection of Δ_{S/A} is Δ_{S/A,perf} := (colim(Δ_{S/A} → φ_*Δ_{S/A} → φ²_*Δ_{S/A} → ⋯))^∧ in D(A): the derived (p, I)-completed colimit of the transition maps φ_S, where φ^n_* is restriction of scalars along φ_A^n. It is a derived (p, I)-complete commutative algebra in D(A) with a φ_A-semilinear automorphism φ induced by φ_S and a canonical map can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf} of commutative algebras commuting with Frobenius. (2) The perfectoidization of S is S_perfd := Δ_{S/A,perf} ⊗^L_A A/I in D(R), a derived p-complete commutative algebra with a map S → Δ̄_{S/A} → S_perfd. Both constructions are functorial in S. They are objects distinct from Δ_{S/A} and Δ̄_{S/A}: can is an equivalence exactly when φ_S is one (node perfection-comparison). The definition is made relative to the base (A, I); see the hypotheses.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0).
S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed.

Independence of the perfect base prism, dependence on π_0(S) only, and the description through the perfect prismatic site are BS22 Proposition 8.5, which is not planned in this stage (recorded gap); every statement here is relative to the fixed perfect prism (A, I).

The universal perfectoid ring of a semiperfectoid ring (BS22 Corollary 7.3) is a different construction, owned by PerfectoidQuotients Q2; the two agree whenever S_perfd is connective (node connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid).
proofSteps: The transition maps: φ_S : Δ_{S/A} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{S/A} is a map of commutative algebras in D(A) (node derived-prismatic-cohomology); apply φ^n_{A,*} and form the sequential colimit in D(A), then complete (DD.1).
Automorphism: the shift of the sequential diagram induces φ : Δ_{S/A,perf} → φ_{A,*}Δ_{S/A,perf}, an equivalence because the shifted diagram is cofinal; it is compatible with can by construction.
Reduction modulo I: A/I is a perfect A-module, so S_perfd is derived p-complete and receives Δ̄_{S/A}.
acceptance: S = R: Δ_{R/A} = A, can is an isomorphism and R_perfd = R.
S perfectoid: Δ_{S/A,perf} = A_inf(S) and S_perfd = S.
(A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) and S = F_p[x]: S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}], discrete, while Δ̄_{S/Z_p} has H^1 = Ω^1 ≠ 0.
φ is an automorphism of Δ_{S/A,perf} for every S.

nodes.title: Comparison of the perfected and the unperfected theory
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism, R = A/I, and S a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. (1) can : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A,perf} is initial among maps of commutative algebras with Frobenius from Δ_{S/A} to objects E of D_comp(A) whose Frobenius φ_E is an equivalence; it is an equivalence if and only if φ_S is. (2) If S is a perfectoid R-algebra then L_{S/R} vanishes after derived p-completion, Δ̄_{S/A} = S, Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), can is an equivalence and S_perfd = S. (3) For every perfect prism (B, J) over (A, I) with a map π_0(S) → B/J, the map ev_{(B,J)} of node comparison-to-prisms factors uniquely through can; these factorisations assemble to Δ_{S/A,perf} → RΓ((S/A)_Δ^perf, O_Δ) = lim_{S → R′} A_inf(R′), the limit over all maps from S to perfectoid rings R′. (4) Characteristic p (BS22 Example 8.3): for a crystalline perfect prism (A, I) = (W(k), (p)), k a perfect F_p-algebra (in the source k = F_p), and a k-algebra S, the Frobenius of Δ_{S/A}/p preserves the conjugate filtration and acts on gr_i^conj = ∧^i L_{S/k}[−i] through the map induced by the Frobenius of S, which is zero for i ≠ 0; hence S_perf := colim_φ S ≃ S_perfd through the Frobenius-equivariant map S → Δ̄_{S/A}. (5) The two theories differ: for S = F_p[x] over (Z_p, (p)), H^0(Δ̄_{S/A}) = F_p[x] and H^1(Δ̄_{S/A}) = Ω^1_{F_p[x]/F_p} ≠ 0, while S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] is discrete. Neither theory is obtained from the other by a formal substitution: Δ_{S/A,perf} forgets the conjugate filtration in positive degrees, and Δ_{S/A} is not recovered from Δ_{S/A,perf}.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0).
S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed.
That the map in (3) is an equivalence is BS22 Proposition 8.5 (recorded gap); (3) only constructs it.
In (4) the base is crystalline; for a perfect base of mixed characteristic and pS = 0 the source reduces to the base (Z_p, (p)) by independence of the base, which is the same gap.
proofSteps: (1): universal property of the sequential colimit along φ and of completion.

(2): the completed cotangent complexes of R and S over Z_p are R[1] and S[1] compatibly (BMS2 Proposition 4.19 and the proof of Lemma 4.25; from Q0:integral-algebra and DD.5), so L_{S/R}^∧ = 0; node derived-hodge-tate-comparison (c) gives Δ̄_{S/A} = S. The map ev to the prism (A_inf(S), I A_inf(S)) is an isomorphism modulo I, hence an isomorphism; A_inf(S) is perfect.

(3): φ_B is an automorphism, so ev extends over the colimit and the completion; for the identification of the perfect prismatic site with perfectoid rings under S use the equivalence of PR.0 and BS22 Lemma 4.8.
(4): reduce to S = F_p[x] by left Kan extension; there the Frobenius of Δ̄ on H^1 = Ω^1 is induced by x ↦ x^p, which kills dx. Reduction modulo p commutes with the colimit and the completion.
(5): PR.1's Hodge–Tate comparison for F_p[x] and (4).
acceptance: S = R: both theories give A.
S = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩: perfectoid, so the two theories agree.
S = F_p[x] over Z_p: they differ, as in (5).
S = F_p[x]/(x²) over Z_p: S_perfd = (S)_perf = F_p.

nodes.title: Coconnectivity of perfectoidizations
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I and d a generator of I. For every derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S, both Δ_{S/A,perf} and S_perfd lie in D^{≥0}. Moreover H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}) is a p-torsion-free, p-complete, perfect δ-ring on which φ is the unique Frobenius lift; A → H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}) is a map of δ-rings; d is a nonzerodivisor of H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}); and H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf})/p is a subring of H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}/p).
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0).
S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed.
The proof uses the operation P^0 on the homotopy groups of E_∞-F_p-algebras (Lurie, Rational and p-adic homotopy theory, §2.2); no atlas stage supplies it (recorded gap).
proofSteps: Δ_{S/A,perf}/p is the realisation of a simplicial cosimplicial F_p-algebra, the colimit along the levelwise Frobenius of the functorial model F_A(S)/p of node derived-agrees-with-site. The levelwise Frobenius of a simplicial cosimplicial F_p-algebra induces P^0 on its realisation, so P^0 acts invertibly on π_*(Δ_{S/A,perf}/p).
P^0 annihilates all homotopy classes of positive degree of an E_∞-F_p-algebra (Lurie, loc. cit., Remark 2.2.7). Hence Δ_{S/A,perf}/p ∈ D^{≥0}, and Δ_{S/A,perf} ∈ D^{≥0} by derived p-completeness.

H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}) is p-torsion-free because Δ_{S/A,perf}/p ∈ D^{≥0}; φ lifts the Frobenius of H^0/p ⊂ H^0(Δ_{S/A,perf}/p) by the same argument. So H^0 is a perfect p-complete δ-ring with unique Frobenius lift (PR.0, perfect δ-rings), the map from A is a δ-map and d is carried to a distinguished element.

A distinguished element of a p-torsion-free, p-adically separated δ-ring with reduced reduction modulo p is a nonzerodivisor (BS22 Lemma 2.34, PR.0). Therefore S_perfd = cofib(d on Δ_{S/A,perf}) ∈ D^{≥0}.
acceptance: S perfectoid: S_perfd = S in degree 0.
S = F_p[x] over Z_p: S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] in degree 0.
For S = O_C⟨x⟩ the object S_perfd is coconnective and not discrete (last example of node connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid): the theorem gives no bound from above.
The unperfected Δ̄_{R/A} of node derived-input-higher-homotopy has H^{−1} ≠ 0; its perfection lies in D^{≥0}.

nodes.title: Strong descent for the passage to the perfection
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I), T = R[X_1,…,X_n]^∧ and T_∞ = R[X_1^{1/p^∞},…,X_n^{1/p^∞}]^∧, the p-adic completions. The natural maps Δ_{T/A} → Δ_{T_∞/A} and Δ_{T/A,perf} → Δ_{T_∞/A,perf} are descendable, in the sense of Mathew, as maps of commutative algebras in D_comp(A). Consequence used by the source: for a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S with a map T → S, with S̃ := (T_∞ ⊗^L_T S)^∧ and S̃^• the derived p-completed Čech nerve of S → S̃, one has Δ_{S/A} ≃ lim_{[m] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S̃^m/A} and Δ_{S/A,perf} ≃ lim_{[m] ∈ Δ} Δ_{S̃^m/A,perf}.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0).

Descendability, its stability under base change and tensor products, and the bound for colimits along compatible endomorphisms (Bhatt–Scholze, Projectivity of the Witt vector affine Grassmannian, Lemma 11.22) are requested from EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract.

The source says that after reduction "R is a perfect ring of characteristic p"; the ring obtained is A/(p, φ^{−1}(d)) ≅ R/p, which is only semiperfect. The argument uses only that it is an F_p-algebra (recorded as a source issue).
proofSteps: The perfected statement follows from the unperfected one: if B → C is descendable of index ≤ n with compatible endomorphisms, then colim_φ B → colim_φ C is descendable of index ≤ 2n.

Δ_{−/A} commutes with coproducts (node kunneth-formula), and tensor products of descendable maps are descendable, so n = 1. Let F be the fibre of Δ_{T/A} → Δ_{T_∞/A}; it suffices that every map F^{⊗2} → Δ_{T/A} of Δ_{T/A}-modules is null, which follows from RHom_{Δ_{T/A}}(F^{⊗2}, Δ_{T/A}) ∈ D^{<0}.

By completeness this is checked after base change along A → A/(p, φ^{−1}(d)) =: k. There Δ_{T/A} ⊗^L_A k ≃ (φ_A^*Δ_{T/A} ⊗̂^L_A A/I) ⊗^L_{A/I} A/(I, p) is the de Rham complex of k[X] over k by the de Rham comparison of PR.1 (its hypothesis holds: A/I is perfectoid, hence reduced, and the ring of Witt vectors of a reduced ring is p-torsion-free), and by the Cartier isomorphism for a polynomial algebra this is the split square-zero extension Ω = T′ ⊕ Ω^1_{T′/k}[−1] with T′ = k[X]; likewise Δ_{T_∞/A} ⊗^L_A k ≃ T′_∞ := k[X^{1/p^∞}].

The fibre of Ω → T′ is T′[−1] as an Ω-module, and T′_∞ is a free T′-module with 1 in a basis, so the fibre of Ω → T′_∞ is a direct sum of copies of T′[−1]. The claim reduces to RHom_Ω((T′[−1])^{⊗2}, Ω) ∈ D^{<0}, computed with the resolution (⋯ → Ω[−3] → Ω[−2] → Ω[−1]) of T′[−1] whose maps are given by dX.
The consequence: descendability is stable under base change, and Δ_{S̃/A} = Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{T/A}} Δ_{T_∞/A} by node kunneth-formula; a descendable map B → C satisfies B ≃ lim C^{⊗(•+1)}.
acceptance: n = 0: both maps are identities.
After perfection the target is Δ_{T_∞/A,perf} = A_inf(T_∞), the perfect prism of the perfectoid ring T_∞.
In characteristic p, (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)): Δ_{F_p[X]/Z_p,perf} = Z_p⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩ = Δ_{F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/Z_p,perf}, and the second map is an isomorphism.
The map T → T_∞ is a quasisyntomic cover, so the limit formula for Δ_{S/A} is also an instance of node quasisyntomic-descent when S is quasisyntomic; descendability gives it for every S.

nodes.title: Perfectoidization is symmetric monoidal
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I. The functors S ↦ Δ_{S/A,perf} and S ↦ S_perfd, from derived p-complete simplicial R-algebras to commutative algebras in D_comp(A), respectively to derived p-complete commutative algebras in D(R), are symmetric monoidal: for every diagram S_1 ← S_3 → S_2 the induced maps Δ_{S_1/A,perf} ⊗̂^L_{Δ_{S_3/A,perf}} Δ_{S_2/A,perf} → Δ_{(S_1 ⊗̂^L_{S_3} S_2)/A,perf} and S_{1,perfd} ⊗̂^L_{S_{3,perfd}} S_{2,perfd} → (S_1 ⊗̂^L_{S_3} S_2)_perfd are equivalences. In BS22 the source category is that of derived p-complete simplicial rings admitting a map from a perfectoid ring: given S_1 ← S_3 → S_2 one chooses a perfectoid ring mapping to S_3 and applies the statement above.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0).
S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed.

Independence of the perfect base prism, dependence on π_0(S) only, and the description through the perfect prismatic site are BS22 Proposition 8.5, which is not planned in this stage (recorded gap); every statement here is relative to the fixed perfect prism (A, I).
proofSteps: Δ_{−/A} is symmetric monoidal (node kunneth-formula).

Sequential colimits along Frobenius are sifted, so they commute with relative tensor products; derived (p, I)-completion is symmetric monoidal for the completed tensor product (DD.1). Hence the perfection is symmetric monoidal.
Reduction modulo I is the symmetric monoidal base change − ⊗^L_A A/I.
acceptance: S_3 = R: (S_1 ⊗̂^L_R S_2)_perfd = S_{1,perfd} ⊗̂^L_R S_{2,perfd}.
S_1, S_2, S_3 perfectoid: the completed derived tensor product of perfectoid rings is perfectoid and discrete (PR.0, perfectoid-tor-independence), in accordance with the formula.
S_1 = S_2 = S_perfd over S when S_perfd is discrete: (S_perfd ⊗̂^L_S S_perfd)_perfd = S_perfd, the step used in node connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid.
In characteristic p over (Z_p, (p)): perfection of F_p-algebras commutes with derived tensor products, which are discrete for perfect rings.
