nodes.title: Connective perfectoidizations are perfectoid and universal
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with R = A/I and S a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra. Assume that S_perfd is connective; equivalently, by node perfectoidization-coconnective, that it is concentrated in degree 0. Then Δ_{S/A,perf} is discrete and is a perfect (p, I)-complete δ-A-algebra, (Δ_{S/A,perf}, IΔ_{S/A,perf}) is a perfect prism, S_perfd is a perfectoid ring, and S → S_perfd is the universal map from S to a perfectoid ring: every map from π_0(S) to a perfectoid ring S′ factors uniquely through S_perfd. In particular S_perfd is then independent of the perfect base, and for a semiperfectoid ring S whose S_perfd is connective it is the universal perfectoid ring of PerfectoidQuotients Q2 (BS22 Corollary 7.3).
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism: φ_A is bijective; then I = (d) for a distinguished nonzerodivisor d, R := A/I is an integral perfectoid ring and A = A_inf(R) (PR.0).
S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra, R = A/I; all tensor products are derived and completed.
Connectivity of S_perfd is a hypothesis: for S = O_C⟨x⟩ it fails (last acceptance example).
That S_perfd is connective for every semiperfectoid S is part of BS22 Proposition 8.5 and Theorem 7.4, which belong to other roadmaps; it is not asserted here.
proofSteps: If S_perfd is discrete then Δ_{S/A,perf} is discrete by derived Nakayama (last step of node derived-hodge-tate-comparison (b)). By node perfectoidization-coconnective it is a perfect p-complete δ-A-algebra, and d is a distinguished nonzerodivisor in it; so (Δ_{S/A,perf}, (d)) is a perfect prism and S_perfd is perfectoid (PR.0).
Existence of factorisations: a map S → S′ to a perfectoid ring induces S_perfd → S′_perfd = S′ (node perfection-comparison (2)).

Uniqueness: two factorisations give a map η : S_perfd ⊗̂^L_S S_perfd → S′, which factors through (S_perfd ⊗̂^L_S S_perfd)_perfd because S′ = S′_perfd. By node perfectoidization-symmetric-monoidal and (S_perfd)_perfd = S_perfd this is S_perfd via the multiplication map, so η factors through the multiplication.
acceptance: S perfectoid: S_perfd = S with the identity.
S = F_p[x] over (Z_p, (p)): S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}] is the universal perfect F_p[x]-algebra.
S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) over (Z_p, (p)): S_perfd = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x^{1/p^n} : n ≥ 0) = F_p, the quotient by the radical.

S = O_C⟨x⟩, C complete and algebraically closed over Q_p: there is no universal perfectoid S-algebra U. Indeed the automorphisms t^{1/p^n} ↦ ζ_{p^n} t^{1/p^n} of O_C⟨t^{1/p^∞}⟩ fix t, so the map U → O_C⟨t^{1/p^∞}⟩ classifying t would land in the invariants O_C⟨t⟩; but the image of x is a p-th power modulo p in U and t is not one in (O_C/p)[t]. Hence S_perfd is not connective.

nodes.title: Finite projective modules over derived p-complete rings and their descent
nodes.statement: Let R be a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion. Then the natural functor from finite projective R-modules to the 2-limit over n of the categories of finite projective R/p^n-modules is an equivalence. Finite projective modules therefore have effective descent for p-completely faithfully flat covers between derived p-complete rings of bounded p-power torsion: for a p-completely faithfully flat map R → R′ of such rings, finite projective R-modules are equivalent to finite projective R′-modules with a descent datum over the p-completed tensor products R′ ⊗̂_R R′ and R′ ⊗̂_R R′ ⊗̂_R R′.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a derived p-complete ring with bounded p^∞-torsion is classically p-adically complete (DD.1).
The completed tensor products are discrete with bounded p^∞-torsion (BMS2 Lemma 4.7 and Corollary 4.8).
proofSteps: R is classically p-complete, so finite projective modules lift uniquely along the tower R/p^n (Stacks Project, Tag 0D4B; requested from DD.1).

For a p-completely faithfully flat map R → R′ of p-complete rings with bounded p^∞-torsion, R/p^n → R′/p^n is faithfully flat for all n (BMS2 Corollary 4.8 (3); flatness from Lemma 4.7, surjectivity on spectra from n = 1).
Faithfully flat descent for finite projective modules along R/p^n → R′/p^n (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1), and a 2-limit of stacks is a stack.
acceptance: R = Z_p: finite free Z_p-modules are compatible systems of finite free Z/p^n-modules.
R → R′ = R⟨x^{1/p^∞}⟩: a finite projective R′-module with descent datum descends to R.
The hypothesis of bounded p^∞-torsion is used to pass between derived and classical completeness and to make R/p^n → R′/p^n flat.

nodes.title: Descent of finite projective modules along faithfully flat maps of prisms
nodes.statement: For bounded prisms, assigning to (A,I) the category of finite projective A-modules satisfies effective completely faithfully flat descent. Explicitly: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB) with A → B (p, I)-completely faithfully flat, with Čech nerve B^• (B^n the (n+1)-fold derived (p, I)-completed tensor power of B over A, again a bounded prism), the category of finite projective A-modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective B-modules M equipped with an isomorphism of the two base changes of M to B^1 satisfying the cocycle condition over B^2.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime and (A, I) is a bounded prism (PR.0): A/I has bounded p^∞-torsion, and A is derived and classically (p, I)-complete.
A map of prisms is faithfully flat when A → B is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat (PR.0); the appendix of ALB23 recalls this with the word "faithfully" omitted (recorded as a source issue).
proofSteps: A bounded prism is classically (p, I)-complete (PR.0), hence classically I-adically complete because I is finitely generated; so finite projective A-modules are compatible systems of finite projective A/I^n-modules (Stacks Project, Tag 0D4B).
A 2-limit of stacks is a stack, so it suffices that (A, I) ↦ {finite projective A/I^n-modules} is a stack for every n.

For a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms, A/I^n → B/I^nB = B ⊗^L_A A/I^n is a p-completely faithfully flat map of rings with bounded p^∞-torsion (A/I^n is a successive extension of the modules I^k/I^{k+1}, invertible over A/I); apply node finite-projective-modules-p-complete.
acceptance: Finite projective modules over A_inf descend along the faithfully flat cover of prisms produced by node quasisyntomic-covers-lift-to-prisms.
Rank one: invertible modules, in particular Breuil–Kisin twists, satisfy descent on the site of bounded prisms.
Prismatic crystals in vector bundles on the absolute prismatic site form a stack (used by PR.7 and by ALB23 for prismatic Dieudonné crystals).

nodes.title: Nygaard filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let (B, J) be a prism with Frobenius φ_B. For i ≥ 0 put Fil^i_N B = φ_B^{-1}(J^i) = {x ∈ B : φ_B(x) ∈ J^i}, an ideal of B, and Fil^i_N B = B for i ≤ 0; gr^i_N B = Fil^i_N B / Fil^{i+1}_N B. For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring S the Nygaard filtration of S is this filtration on its initial prism (Δ_S, IΔ_S) (PR.2/qrsp-prism): Fil^i_N Δ_S = {x ∈ Δ_S : φ(x) ∈ I^i Δ_S} = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^i Δ_S}, where d is the image of a generator of ker(θ : A_inf(R) → R) for any perfectoid ring R mapping to S (the ideal IΔ_S is principal and does not depend on R). It is an N-indexed decreasing filtration by ideals, multiplicative (Fil^i_N · Fil^j_N ⊂ Fil^{i+j}_N), and functorial: a map of prisms (B, J) → (B', J') carries Fil^i_N B into Fil^i_N B', so a map S → S' of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings carries Fil^i_N Δ_S into Fil^i_N Δ_{S'}. The filtration is by the Frobenius-divisibility condition itself; it is not the IΔ_S-adic filtration, not the powers of Fil^1_N, and not a divided-power filtration. It is not separated in general, and Δ_S need not be complete for it (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; prisms are those of PR.0/prism (δ-ring, invertible ideal, derived (p, I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)).
S is quasiregular semiperfectoid in the sense used by PR.2/qrsp-prism (BMS2 Definition 4.20); Δ_S is its initial prism, a discrete ring.
No orientation is chosen in the definition: the condition φ(x) ∈ J^i uses only the ideal J. When J = (d) it reads φ(x) ∈ d^i B.
The index set is N; negative indices give the whole ring.
proofSteps: Fil^i_N B is the preimage of the ideal J^i under the ring map φ_B, hence an ideal (Mathlib: comap of an ideal); it decreases with i because J^{i+1} ⊂ J^i.
Multiplicativity: φ(xy) = φ(x)φ(y) ∈ J^i J^j = J^{i+j}. Functoriality: a map of prisms f commutes with φ and f(J) ⊂ J', so f(φ^{-1}(J^i)) ⊂ φ^{-1}(J'^i).

For S quasiregular semiperfectoid apply this to (Δ_S, IΔ_S) of PR.2/qrsp-prism (BS22 Proposition 7.10); the ideal is generated by the image d of a generator of the perfect prism of any perfectoid R → S (perfect prisms are orientable, PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings), which gives the printed form of BS22 Definition 12.1.

The failure of completeness is computed in PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example (there the filtration is separated). Non-separatedness is quoted from the warning after BS22 Definition 12.1 and is not exhibited by a node; since Δ_S is d-adically separated, ∩_i Fil^i_N Δ_S = ker(φ), so the filtration is separated exactly when φ is injective on Δ_S.
acceptance: For S perfectoid, Δ_S = A_inf(S) and Fil^i_N = (φ^{-1}(d))^i A_inf(S); for S = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ this is ([p]_{q^{1/p}})^i.
For the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ the filtration is the one of PR.3/nygaard-key-case.
The definition is intrinsic to S: it does not use a perfectoid ring mapping to S, while the conjugate filtration it is compared with does (BS22 Example 12.3).

nodes.title: The key case: q-divided powers and the Nygaard filtration of Z_p^cycl⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/X
nodes.statement: Let A be the (p, [p]_q)-adic completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}] with δ(q^{1/p^n}) = 0, I = ([p]_q), [p]_q = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1}; (A, I) is the perfect prism of R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧, with q^{1/p^n} ↦ ζ_{p^{n+1}}. Let S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧. Write [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1), [n]_q! = ∏_{i=1}^n [i]_q. (a) Δ_S = A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/[p]_q}^∧ (prismatic envelope), with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and S → Δ̄_S sending X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; Δ_S is flat over Z_p[[q−1]]. (b) (q-divided powers, BS22 Lemma 12.5) If D is a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, (p, [p]_q)-completely flat Z_p[[q−1]]-algebra with a ring endomorphism φ, φ(q) = q^p, and x ∈ D satisfies φ(x) = x^p ∈ [p]_q D, then x^n ∈ [n]_q! D for all n ≥ 0. (c) (BS22 Lemma 12.6) In Z_p[[q−1]]: [mp]_q! = u · φ([m]_q!) · [p]_q^m with u a unit, for m ∈ N; and [⌊i⌋p]_q! = v · [⌊ip⌋]_q! with v a unit, for i ∈ N[1/p]. (d) (BS22 Lemma 12.4) Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ Δ_S for all n, and Δ_S is the (p, [p]_q)-adic completion of the free A-module ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} A · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!. On this basis φ(Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!) = u_i · [p]_q^{⌊i⌋} · Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q! with u_i a unit. (e) (BS22 Lemma 12.7) Fil^n_N Δ_S is the completion of ⊕_i [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} · A · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!. The image of φ/[p]_q^n : Fil^n_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S = (⊕_i R · Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!)^∧ is the span of the summands with i < p(n+1), and the conjugate filtration Fil_n Δ̄_S relative to R is the same span. In particular Theorem 12.2 holds for S, and Δ_S/Fil^1_N Δ_S = ⊕_{i<1} (A/[p]_{q^{1/p}}) · Y^i, which φ maps isomorphically onto the image ⊕_{j<p} R · Y^j of S in Δ̄_S (Y^i ↦ Y^{pi}, the image of X^i).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; R, A, S, Y as in the statement; N[1/p] is the monoid of non-negative elements of Z[1/p].
The normalisation X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}} is that of BS22 §12.2 (so X ↦ Y^p).
In (e) the exponent of [p]_{q^{1/p}} is max(n − ⌊i⌋, 0): the factor is 1 as soon as i ≥ n.
In the proof of BS22 Lemma 12.6 the display reads ∏[ip]_q! where ∏[ip]_q is meant (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E21); the node states the corrected identity.
proofSteps: (a): Δ_S is the prismatic envelope of (I, Y^p) in A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ by PR.2/qrsp-prism and PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (BS22 Proposition 3.13); it is (p, I)-completely flat over A, hence flat over the noetherian ring Z_p[[q−1]].

(c): [k]_q is a unit of Z_p[[q−1]] when p ∤ k, and ∏_{i=1}^m [ip]_q = ∏ (q^{ip}−1)/(q^p−1) · (q^p−1)/(q−1) = φ([m]_q!) [p]_q^m. (b): reduce to showing x^m ∈ [m]_q! D ⇒ x^{mp} ∈ [mp]_q! D; φ([m]_q!) is a nonzerodivisor modulo [p]_q in D by flatness, x^{mp} = φ(x^m) ∈ φ([m]_q!)D and x^{mp} = (x^p)^m ∈ [p]_q^m D.

(d): (b) gives Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ Δ_S; the map from the completed free module is an isomorphism because it is one after base change along A → A/(q−1), where the envelope becomes the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope, BS22 Corollary 2.39) with its standard basis (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0).

(e): φ is graded for the N[1/p]-grading, multiplying degrees by p, so Fil^n_N is graded; the formula of (d) for φ on basis elements and bijectivity of φ on A identify Fil^n_N degree by degree and give the image of φ/[p]_q^n. For the conjugate filtration: Fil_0 is the image of S (summands i < p), gr_1 is generated by Y^p/[p]_q (BS22 Example 7.9, PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison), and multiplicativity with (c) gives Fil_n.
acceptance: n = 0: Fil^0_N = Δ_S and the image of φ in Δ̄_S is the span of Y^i, i < p, which is the image of S.

n = 1: for i < 2 the generator [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{1−⌊i⌋} Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q! of Fil^1_N in degree i maps under φ/[p]_q to a unit multiple of Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q!, and for i ≥ 2 to a multiple of [p]_q; the image in Δ̄_S is the span of the degrees j < 2p.

Reduction modulo q − 1 recovers a divided power algebra: Δ_S/(q−1) is the p-completion of ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} (A/(q−1)) · Y^i/⌊i⌋!, the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) in A/(q−1)⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ (A/(q−1) is the p-completion of Z_p[q^{1/p^∞}]/(q−1), not Z_p). Its base change along A → Z_p, q^{1/p^n} ↦ 1, is the p-completion of ⊕ Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋! (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example).
Perfectoid quotient acceptance example of the stage: S is the quotient of the perfectoid ring R⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩ by the regular element X.

nodes.title: Good filtrations and the Nygaard filtration of regular semiperfectoid quotients
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)). For a quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebra S, a multiplicative filtration Fil^•_M of Δ_S by ideals (i ≥ 0) is good if φ(Fil^i_M) ⊂ d^i Δ_S for all i and φ/d^i induces an isomorphism of gr^i_M Δ_S onto Fil_i Δ̄_S ⊂ Δ̄_S (conjugate filtration relative to R). (1) A good filtration equals the Nygaard filtration. (2) If Δ_S carries a good filtration then Theorem 12.2 holds for S. (3) Let S → S′ be relatively perfect (the base change of a map of perfectoid R-algebras). If Fil^•_M is good on Δ_S then Fil^i_M Δ_S ⊗̂^L_{Δ_S} Δ_{S′} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a good filtration of Δ_{S′}; hence Fil^i_N Δ_{S′} = Fil^i_N Δ_S ⊗̂_{Δ_S} Δ_{S′}. (4) Let S → T be relatively perfect and p-completely faithfully flat. If Δ_T carries a good filtration then so does Δ_S. (5) Consequently Theorem 12.2 holds for S = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with f_1, …, f_m a p-completely regular sequence relative to R, and the Nygaard filtration of S(m) = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_m^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1, …, X_m) is the completed tensor product over A of the Nygaard filtrations of the factors R⟨X_j^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_j).
hypotheses: R is perfectoid, (A, (d)) its perfect prism, S, S′, T quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras.

The regular sequence in (5) is p-completely regular relative to R (BS22 Definition 2.42 with I = (p)); this is the reading used when the same class of rings is quoted in the proof of BS22 Theorem 13.1.
Completed tensor products are derived (p, d)-completed (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1).
In the proof of BS22 Proposition 12.8 'p-power roots in f_i' reads 'in R′' (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E22).
proofSteps: (1): induction on i with the map of short exact sequences 0 → Fil^{i+1}_M → Fil^i_M → gr^i_M → 0 to 0 → d^{i+1}Δ_S → d^iΔ_S → d^iΔ_S/d^{i+1}Δ_S → 0 given by φ; the right vertical map is injective, so Fil^{i+1}_M = {x ∈ Fil^i_M : φ(x) ∈ d^{i+1}Δ_S}. (2) follows from (1).

(3): the conjugate filtration is compatible with base change along relatively perfect maps (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison), so gr^i_{M′} ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_{S′} is discrete, the quotients Δ_{S′}/Fil^i_{M′} are discrete and Fil^i_{M′} are ideals; the Frobenius of Δ_{S′} is the base change of that of Δ_S.

(4): on the Čech nerve T^• every term carries, by (3) and (1), its Nygaard filtration, which is a cartesian cosimplicial (p, d)-complete complex over Δ_{T^•}; (p, d)-completely faithfully flat descent along Δ_S → Δ_T (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1, PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent) gives a filtration of Δ_S in the filtered derived category, which is by ideals (connective by faithful flatness, coconnective by the limit formula) and good.

(5): PR.3/nygaard-key-case gives S(1) over R_0 = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧; for a perfectoid R_0-algebra R, S(1)_R = S(1)_{R_0} ⊗̂_{R_0} R is relatively perfect over it and (3) applies (the conjugate filtrations relative to R_0 and to R agree because the p-completed cotangent complex of R over R_0 vanishes); for a general perfectoid R choose R → R_∞ by André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3), which contains compatible p-power roots of unity, and apply (4) to S(1)_R → S(1)_{R_∞}; the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula) gives S(m), the tensor product filtration being good; a quotient R′/(f_1, …, f_r) with R′ perfectoid and f_i having compatible p-power roots receives a relatively perfect map from S(r), so (3) applies; André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3, BS22 Theorem 7.14) gives a relatively perfect p-completely faithfully flat cover of the general S by such rings, so (4) applies.
acceptance: For S = R perfectoid the filtration (φ^{-1}(d))^i A is good: φ/d^i maps (e^i)/(e^{i+1}) isomorphically onto A/d = R = Fil_i Δ̄_R.
For R → F_p (q ↦ 1) and S the key case, (3) gives the Nygaard filtration of F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/X used in PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example.

S(2) = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, X_2^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_1, X_2) with R a perfectoid Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra: Fil^n_N is spanned by [p]_{q^{1/p}}^{max(n−⌊i_1⌋−⌊i_2⌋, 0)} Y_1^{i_1}Y_2^{i_2}/([⌊i_1⌋]_q![⌊i_2⌋]_q!), the formula used in the proof of BS22 Lemma 14.4.

nodes.title: Nygaard filtration on prismatic cohomology over a perfectoid base
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, I), I = (d). (a) For a p-completely smooth R-algebra B choose a surjection R⟨X_1, …, X_n⟩ → B and put B̃ = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗̂_{R⟨X_1,…,X_n⟩} B, with Čech nerve B̃^• of B → B̃; all B̃^k are semiperfectoid and Zariski locally of the form of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (5), and Δ_{B/A} ≅ Tot(Δ_{B̃^•}). Define Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} = Tot(Fil^i_N Δ_{B̃^•}) → Δ_{B/A}. It is independent of the surjection and functorial in B, a decreasing N-indexed multiplicative filtration of Δ_{B/A} in D(A) with gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤ i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, the isomorphism induced by φ/d^i (it is φ_A-semilinear). (b) For a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra S define Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} as the derived (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of B ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} from p-completed polynomial R-algebras. Then Fil^0_N = Δ_{S/A}, the filtration is multiplicative and functorial, and φ/d^i induces a φ_A-semilinear isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i} (conjugate filtration relative to R), that is, an A-linear isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{S/A} ≅ (φ_A)_* Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}. (c) Each functor S ↦ Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} on quasisyntomic R-algebras is a sheaf for the quasisyntomic topology with values in D(A).
hypotheses: R is perfectoid and (A, I) is its perfect prism; B is p-completely smooth over R; S is a derived p-complete simplicial R-algebra.
Filtered objects are objects of the filtered derived category DF(A) of functors (Z, ≥) → D(A) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1); the filtration is N-indexed in the sense that Fil^i = Fil^0 for i ≤ 0.
BS22 Proposition 12.10 prints gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i} Δ_{B/A}; the correct target is τ^{≤i} Δ̄_{B/A}{i} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E23), which is what the node states.
The identification of this filtration, on quasiregular semiperfectoid S, with the ideals of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp is part of PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces (BS22 Proposition 12.11).
proofSteps: (a): each B̃^k satisfies Theorem 12.2 by PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid and Zariski localisation; Δ_{B̃^•} computes Δ_{B/A} by the Hodge–Tate comparison and quasisyntomic descent (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent). Totalising gr^i_N Δ_{B̃^•} ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_{B̃^•}{i} gives τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, because the conjugate filtration of the smooth algebra B is the canonical filtration (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison) and Fil_i^conj is a quasisyntomic sheaf.

Independence of the surjection: adding variables gives a comparison map of the two filtrations which is an isomorphism on every gr^i, hence on every Fil^i by induction on i using Δ/Fil^i (BS22, the paragraph after Proposition 12.10).

(b): left Kan extension (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3) commutes with cofibres, so gr^i of the extension is the left Kan extension of B ↦ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}, which is Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i} by the construction of the conjugate filtration (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison).

(c): Δ_{−/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent); Δ_{S/A}/Fil^i_N has a finite filtration with graded pieces Fil_j^conj Δ̄{j}, j < i, which are sheaves by flat descent for the exterior powers of the cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5).
acceptance: For B = R: Fil^i_N Δ_{R/A} = (φ^{-1}(d))^i A and gr^i is identified with R{i} by φ/d^i, concentrated in degree 0.
For B = R⟨T^{±1}⟩ and i ≥ 1: gr^i_N has cohomology B{i} in degree 0 and Ω^1_{B/R}{i−1} in degree 1.
For S quasiregular semiperfectoid the filtration is the one of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces).
Comparison with the relative filtration: for the perfect prism (A, I), φ_A^* Fil^•_N Δ_{S/A} = Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{S/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration).

nodes.title: Graded pieces of the Nygaard filtration (BS22 Theorem 12.2)
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, R a perfectoid ring mapping to S with perfect prism (A, (d)), and Fil_i Δ̄_S ⊂ Δ̄_S the conjugate filtration relative to R (increasing, exhaustive, multiplicative, gr_i Δ̄_S ≅ (∧^i L_{S/R}[−i])^∧{−i}). For every i ≥ 0: (1) the image of Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S, x ↦ (φ(x)/d^i mod d), is Fil_i Δ̄_S, and its kernel is Fil^{i+1}_N Δ_S; (2) hence x ↦ φ(x) mod I^{i+1}Δ_S induces a natural isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i}, where Δ̄_S{i} = I^iΔ_S/I^{i+1}Δ_S; it is φ-semilinear (Δ_S acts on the target through φ), and the left side does not depend on R; (3) in particular Δ_S / Fil^1_N Δ_S ≅ S, the isomorphism being induced by φ : Δ_S → Δ̄_S, whose image is S = Fil_0 Δ̄_S; (4) (BS22 Proposition 12.11) the derived Nygaard filtration Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} of PR.3/nygaard-filtration (b) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ideal Fil^i_N Δ_S ⊂ Δ_S of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp; consequently on quasisyntomic R-algebras the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration is the quasisyntomic unfolding of S′ ↦ Fil^•_N Δ_{S′} from quasiregular semiperfectoid S′, and it does not depend on R. Each gr^i_N Δ_S is a derived p-complete, p-completely flat S-module.
hypotheses: S is quasiregular semiperfectoid; R → S is any map from a perfectoid ring; d is the image of a generator of ker θ.
The conjugate filtration depends on R in general (BS22 Example 12.3, S = O_{C_p} ⊗̂_{Z_p} O_{C_p}); the Nygaard filtration and its graded pieces do not.

BS22 §12.5 prints that the derived filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring is concentrated in degrees 0 and −1; the correct degrees are 0 and 1 (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E24). The argument below uses the corrected range.
The twist {i} is ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ i}; it is trivialised by d^i, which is how the printed statement, with φ/d^i, reads.
proofSteps: Induction on i on the statement Fil^i_{N′} = Fil^i_N, where N′ is the derived filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration (b); i = 0 is clear. Since gr^j_{N′} ≅ Fil_j Δ̄_S{j} is discrete for all j, each Fil^i_{N′} has cohomology only in degrees 0 and 1.

Assume Fil^i_{N′} = Fil^i_N. The image of φ/d^i : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ̄_S is contained in Fil_i Δ̄_S because the map factors through gr^i_{N′}. It contains Fil_i Δ̄_S: choose a surjection S′ = R⟨X_a^{1/p^∞}, Y_b^{1/p^∞}⟩/(Y_b) → S that is surjective on cotangent complexes (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0), so Fil_i Δ̄_{S′} → Fil_i Δ̄_S is surjective, and use PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid for S′ (and filtered colimits for infinitely many variables).

Therefore Fil^i_{N′} → gr^i_{N′} is surjective, its fibre Fil^{i+1}_{N′} is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the kernel of φ/d^i on Fil^i_N, which is Fil^{i+1}_N by definition. This proves (1), (2), (4).
(3) is the case i = 0: Fil_0 Δ̄_S = gr_0 = S. Flatness: Fil_i Δ̄_S is a finite extension of the modules (∧^j L_{S/R}[−j])^∧, which are p-completely flat over S (PR.2/qrsp-prism).
acceptance: S perfectoid with A = A_inf(S): gr^i_N = (e^i)/(e^{i+1}) ≅ S and A_inf(S)/Fil^1_N ≅ S via θ ∘ φ.
Key case: the summands with i < p(n+1) (PR.3/nygaard-key-case (e)).
Anschütz–Le Bras Theorem 3.4.4 is this statement; they use Δ_R/N^{≥1}Δ_R ≅ R to present the structure sheaf of the quasisyntomic site as a quotient of the prismatic sheaf.

nodes.title: Divided Frobenius
nodes.statement: (a) Let (B, J) be a prism with J = (d). For i ≥ 0 the divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/d^i : Fil^i_N B → B is the unique map with d^i φ_i(x) = φ(x) (d is a nonzerodivisor). It is additive and φ-semilinear, φ_0 = φ, φ_{i+j}(xy) = φ_i(x)φ_j(y) for x ∈ Fil^i_N, y ∈ Fil^j_N, φ_i(x) = d · φ_{i+1}(x) for x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N, and φ_i(x) ∈ dB if and only if x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N. Replacing d by ud (u a unit) replaces φ_i by u^{−i}φ_i. (b) Without an orientation the invariant object is the filtered Frobenius Fil^i(φ) : Fil^i_N B → J^i, x ↦ φ(x). With the Breuil–Kisin twists of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist it becomes the twisted divided Frobenius φ_i : Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i} → B{i}, x ⊗ e ↦ φ(x) · φ_{B{i}}(e), where φ_{B{i}} : B{i} → J^{−i} ⊗ B{i}; it is φ-semilinear and independent of all choices. For J = (d) and a generator e of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e it is φ/d^i ⊗ 1. (c) For S quasiregular semiperfectoid these are the maps φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S and φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_S{i} → Δ_S{i}, and φ_i induces the isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} of PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces. (d) Over a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, (d)), the maps φ/d^i on the terms of the Čech nerve of PR.3/nygaard-filtration (a) totalise to a natural φ_A-semilinear map φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_{B/A} → Δ_{B/A} for B p-completely smooth over R, projecting to the isomorphism gr^i_N Δ_{B/A} ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i}; left Kan extension gives φ_i : Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} for all derived p-complete simplicial R-algebras S, with φ_i ∘ (Fil^{i+1} → Fil^i) = d · φ_{i+1}.
hypotheses: (B, J) is a prism; in (a) J is principal with chosen generator d.
The twist B{i} is the i-th tensor power of the Breuil–Kisin twist B{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist); Fil^i_N B{i} means Fil^i_N B ⊗_B B{i}, a submodule of B{i} because B{i} is invertible.
Semilinearity is over the Frobenius of B (and of A in (d)).
BS22 Proposition 12.10 is quoted with the corrected target τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{B/A}{i} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E23).
proofSteps: (a): J = (d) is invertible, so d is a nonzerodivisor and x ∈ Fil^i_N means φ(x) ∈ d^iB; φ_i(x) is the unique quotient. The identities follow by cancelling powers of d; φ_i(x) ∈ dB ⇔ φ(x) ∈ d^{i+1}B ⇔ x ∈ Fil^{i+1}_N.
(b): φ_{B{i}} is the i-th tensor power of the Frobenius of B{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist, BL22 Remark 2.5.9); φ(x) ∈ J^i and φ_{B{i}}(e) ∈ J^{−i} ⊗ B{i} multiply to an element of B{i}.
(c): apply (a), (b) to (Δ_S, IΔ_S); the statement on graded pieces is PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces (1).
(d): BS22 Proposition 12.10: totalise φ/d^i over the cosimplicial δ-ring Δ_{B̃^•}; the relation with d · φ_{i+1} holds termwise. Left Kan extension as in PR.3/nygaard-filtration (b).
acceptance: Perfect prism (A, (d)), e = φ^{-1}(d): φ_i(e^i a) = φ(a), so φ_i : Fil^i_N A → A is bijective.
Key case: φ_n([p]_{q^{1/p}}^{n−⌊i⌋} Y^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!) is a unit multiple of Y^{ip}/[⌊ip⌋]_q! for i < n+1.

BMS2 Theorem 7.2 (4): on π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p) the cyclotomic Frobenius restricted to the i-th Nygaard level is ξ̃^i times a divided Frobenius; under the identification of BS22 Theorem 13.1, which RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 proves from PR.3/bms2-comparison, it is the completion of φ_i.

nodes.title: Transversal prisms and the ideals I_r
nodes.statement: A prism (A, I) is transversal if A/I is p-torsion-free; more generally a preprism (a δ-ring A with an ideal I that is an invertible A-module) is transversal under the same condition. For a transversal prism: (1) A is p-torsion-free and (A, I) is bounded; (A, I) is transversal if and only if A is p-torsion-free and I/pI → A/pA is injective, and then the image is an invertible ideal of A/pA. (2) For every r ≥ 0 the map (φ_A^r)^*(I) → A induced by I ⊂ A is injective with p-torsion-free cokernel; its image is the ideal φ_A^r(I)A, again written (φ_A^r)^*(I). Put I_r = I · φ_A^*(I) ⋯ (φ_A^{r−1})^*(I), an invertible ideal (I_0 = A, I_1 = I). (3) I_r and I^{(p^r−1)/(p−1)} have the same image in A/pA; A/I_r is p-torsion-free; A = lim_r A/I_r = lim_r A/φ_A^*(I_r). (4) For r > 0 the natural map (φ_A^r)^*(I)/I_{r+1} → A/I_r is injective with image the principal ideal (p); and I_r = ∩_{0 ≤ s < r} (φ_A^s)^*(I). (5) I_r/I_r² is p-torsion-free; the canonical map I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² is p times a unique surjection c_r, and c_r induces an isomorphism I_{r+1}/I_rI_{r+1} ≅ I_r/I_r² of invertible A/I_r-modules. (6) For a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J), J_r = I_r B; a flat map of prisms out of a transversal prism has transversal target, and the converse holds for faithfully flat maps.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; (A, I) is a prism in the sense of PR.0/prism. Bhatt–Lurie's Definition 2.1.3 (ρ : φ^*(I) → A/I surjective, A derived p- and I-complete) defines the same class of objects.
For an oriented prism (A, (d)) transversality says that (d, p) is a regular sequence, the hypothesis of PR.0/transversal-prism-regular-sequences (Anschütz–Le Bras).
Flat and faithfully flat maps of prisms are those for which A/I → B/J is p-completely (faithfully) flat.
In the proof of BL22 Corollary 2.2.9 the last line reads 'x belongs to I_r' where 'I_{r+1}' is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E31).
proofSteps: (1): I^m/I^{m+1} is an invertible A/I-module, hence p-torsion-free, so A/I^n is p-torsion-free for all n and A, being I-complete, is p-torsion-free (BL22 Remark 2.1.7); the criterion is Remark 2.1.8.

(2), (3): (φ^r)^*(I) is invertible, hence p-adically separated, and modulo p it maps isomorphically onto Ī^{p^r} ⊂ A/p (BL22 Lemma 2.2.1, Remark 2.2.3); A/I_{r+1} is an extension of A/I_r by I_r ⊗ A/(φ^r)^*(I) (Lemma 2.2.5); the limit statements reduce modulo p to Ī-adic completeness of A/p (Remarks 2.2.6, 2.2.7).

(4): (φ^r)^*(I) ⊂ (p) + I_r by (3); writing f = p f_0 one computes f_0(x) ≡ φ^{r−1}(δ(x)) modulo (φ^{r−1})^*(I) for x ∈ I, and the δ(x), x ∈ I, generate the unit ideal because (A, I) is a prism (BL22 Lemma 2.2.8). The intersection formula follows by induction (Corollary 2.2.9).
(5) follows from (3) and (4) (BL22 Corollary 2.2.10). (6): Remarks 2.2.4 and 2.4.4.
acceptance: The q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) is transversal, with I_r = ([p^r]_q).
A nonzero crystalline prism (A, (p)) is not transversal: A/I = A/p is killed by p.
The Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) is transversal: the quotient O_K is p-torsion-free.
A perfect prism (A_inf(R), ker θ) is transversal exactly when R is p-torsion-free.

nodes.title: Approximation of prisms by transversal prisms
nodes.statement: (1) (BL22 Proposition 2.1.10) For a transversal preprism (A, I) there is a preprism map f : (A, I) → (B, J) to a prism (B, J) such that every preprism map from (A, I) to a prism factors uniquely through f; (B, J) is transversal and Spec(B/(J + (p))) → Spec(A/(I + (p))) is an open immersion. (2) (Proposition 2.4.1) For every prism (A, I) there is a map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) with (B, J) transversal. (3) (Proposition 2.4.5, Corollary 2.4.7, Proposition 2.4.9) If (A, I) is transversal and (B, J) is bounded, the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists in the category of prisms and (B, J) → (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) is flat; it is faithfully flat when A ≠ 0; if (B, J) is also transversal then so is the coproduct. (4) (Corollary 2.4.8) For every prism (A, I), the category of transversal prisms (A_0, I_0) with a map of prisms to (A, I) is non-empty and has pairwise coproducts; hence it is sifted and its nerve is weakly contractible. (5) (Corollary 2.4.10) A bounded prism (A, I) is transversal if and only if for every bounded prism (B, J) the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) exists and is flat over (B, J), if and only if this holds for one nonzero transversal (B, J).
hypotheses: Prisms are those of PR.0/prism; (2) and (4) hold for every prism, bounded or not.

In (3) the coproduct is the prismatic envelope of PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes applied to the (J, p)-completion of A ⊗_Z B and the image of a generator of I, after localising so that I is principal.
The free p-complete δ-ring on a ring R is the p-completion of the free δ-ring (PR.0/free-delta-ring).
In the proof of BL22 Lemma 2.4.2 the scheme of idempotent n × n matrices is a closed subscheme of the affine space of dimension n², printed as A^{2n} (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E32).
proofSteps: (1): lift ρ : φ^*(I) → A/I to ρ̃ : φ^*(I) → A, let Spec A′ ⊂ Spec A be the non-vanishing locus of ρ̃ and B the (I, p)-completion of A′; the Frobenius extends because φ is the identity on the underlying space of A/(I^k, p^k), the δ-structure exists because B is p-torsion-free, and the universal property is checked through Witt vectors of length two.

(2): write I as the base change of an invertible module J_0 over a smooth Z-algebra B_0 (BL22 Lemma 2.4.2), let B_1 = Sym_{B_0}(J_0), B_2 the free p-complete δ-ring on B_1, which is flat over B_1 (Lemma 2.4.3: a retraction argument through W_n and formal smoothness of B_1/p), so (B_2, J_1B_2) is a transversal preprism mapping to (A, I); apply (1).

(3): reduce to I = (d); d is (J, p)-completely regular relative to B in the completion of A ⊗_Z B because A/d is flat over Z; apply PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes (BS22 Proposition 3.13) and PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal. Faithful flatness: lift a point of Spec(B/(p, J)) to a map of prisms to (W(k), (p)) and use the coproduct property.
(4) is (2) and (3); (5) follows from (3) and part (6) of PR.3/transversal-prism.
acceptance: For a crystalline prism (A, (p)): the map q ↦ 1 from the q-de Rham prism is a transversal approximation.
For a perfect prism of a perfectoid ring with p-torsion (for example (Z_p, (p)), R = F_p) a transversal approximation exists although the prism is not transversal.
The coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself is transversal; it is the prism on which the two generators e_A of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples are compared.

nodes.title: Breuil–Kisin twist of a transversal prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a transversal prism with the ideals I_r and the surjections c_r : I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}² → I_r/I_r² (the canonical map divided by p) of PR.3/transversal-prism. Define A{1} = lim (⋯ → I_3/I_3² → I_2/I_2² → I/I²), the inverse limit along the maps c_r, with projections π_r : A{1} → I_r/I_r². Then: (1) A{1} is an invertible A-module, and π_r induces an isomorphism A{1}/I_rA{1} ≅ I_r/I_r² for every r ≥ 0; in particular A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I². (2) For a map f of transversal prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a unique A-linear f{1} : A{1} → B{1} compatible with the maps I_r/I_r² → J_r/J_r², and it induces B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}. (3) The canonical isomorphisms φ_A^*(I_r) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ I_{r+1} induce, modulo φ_A^*(I_r) and in the limit over r, an isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}, that is, a φ_A-semilinear Frobenius φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}. On compatible systems it sends (x_r mod I_r²)_r, x_r ∈ I_r, to the system of the classes of φ_A(x_r) ∈ φ_A^*(I_r) = I^{−1} I_{r+1}.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a transversal prism; all the statements of PR.3/transversal-prism are available.
The transition maps are the canonical maps divided by p; the canonical maps themselves are divisible by p and their inverse limit is not the twist.
I^{−1} denotes the dual invertible module Hom_A(I, A); I^{−1} ⊗ M is written I^{−1}M.
proofSteps: A{1} is p-complete and p-torsion-free because each I_r/I_r² is; by the criterion for invertibility modulo p^n it suffices that A{1}/p is invertible over A/p, where it is the limit of the modules Ī^{m_r}/Ī^{2m_r}, m_r = (p^r − 1)/(p − 1), invertible over (A/p)/Ī^{m_r}, and A/p is Ī-adically complete (BL22 Proposition 2.2.12).
(2): uniqueness and existence of f{1} are formal from J_r = I_rB; the base change statement is checked modulo each J_r (BL22 Remark 2.2.13).
(3): φ_A^*(I_r) = φ^*(I) ⋯ (φ^r)^*(I) = I^{−1}I_{r+1}; reduce modulo φ_A^*(I_r) ⊃ I_{r+1}, use (1) for r and r + 1, and pass to the limit using A = lim A/φ_A^*(I_r) (BL22 Construction 2.2.14).
acceptance: For the q-de Rham prism the classes of [p^r]_q form a compatible system, since [p^{r+1}]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r², and define a generator (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples).
Reduction: A{1} ⊗_A A/I ≅ I/I², the twist of BS22 used in the Hodge–Tate comparison.
Frobenius has a simple pole along I: φ_{A{1}} takes values in I^{−1} ⊗ A{1}, not in A{1}.

nodes.title: Breuil–Kisin twists A{n} of a prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and C the category of transversal prisms (A_0, I_0) with a map of prisms to (A, I) (PR.3/transversal-approximation (4)). The diagram C → Mod_A, (A_0, I_0) ↦ A ⊗_{A_0} A_0{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal) has invertible transition maps and a colimit A{1}, the Breuil–Kisin twist of A; for every object of C the map A ⊗_{A_0} A_0{1} → A{1} is an isomorphism. (1) A{1} is an invertible A-module. For n ∈ Z put A{n} = A{1}^{⊗ n} (negative powers are duals) and, for an A-module or an object M of D(A), M{n} = M ⊗_A A{n}. (2) Functoriality: a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) induces an isomorphism B ⊗_A A{1} ≅ B{1}, compatibly with composition and identities. Hence for a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB), A{1} is the equaliser of B{1} ⇉ (B ⊗̂_A B){1}: when I is not principal the twist is obtained by descent from a cover on which I is oriented. (3) There is a canonical isomorphism β : A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I² of invertible A/I-modules, functorial in the prism and equal to that of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal (1) for transversal prisms. Consequently, for an A/I-module N, N{n} ≅ N ⊗_{A/I} (I/I²)^{⊗ n}, the twist of Bhatt–Scholze. (4) A{1} is a free A-module if and only if I is principal. (5) Frobenius: there is a canonical φ_A-semilinear map φ_{A{1}} : A{1} → I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1} inducing an A-linear isomorphism φ_A^*(A{1}) ≅ I^{−1} ⊗_A A{1}, functorial in the prism and equal to that of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal (3) for transversal prisms; its tensor powers are φ_{A{n}} : A{n} → I^{−n} ⊗_A A{n}, n ∈ Z.
hypotheses: (A, I) is any prism; boundedness is needed only for the descent statement in (2).
For a transversal prism the definition returns the inverse limit of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, because the identity is then an object of C.
A{1} has no canonical generator even when I is principal; a generator is extra structure (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples).
The prismatic logarithm log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} of Bhatt–Lurie §§2.3, 2.5, 2.7 is not part of this node; no target of the stage uses it.
proofSteps: Existence: C has weakly contractible nerve (PR.3/transversal-approximation (4)) and the diagram has invertible transition maps by part (2) of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, so the colimit exists and every structure map is an isomorphism (BL22 Proposition 2.5.1).

(1): invertibility is inherited from the transversal case. (2): for (A, I) → (B, J), a transversal approximation of (A, I) is one of (B, J); compatibility with composition is formal. The descent statement follows because A → B ⇉ B ⊗̂_A B is an equaliser (PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf) and A{1} is flat over A.

(3), (5): the isomorphisms and maps of the transversal case are compatible with maps of transversal prisms, hence descend along the colimit; uniqueness is forced by functoriality (BL22 Remarks 2.5.7, 2.5.9).
(4): by (3) and I-completeness of A, both conditions are equivalent to triviality of the invertible A/I-module I/I² (BL22 Remark 2.5.8).
acceptance: A{0} = A and (M{m}){n} ≅ M{m+n}.
For A/I-modules the twist agrees with M ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (2): H^i(Δ̄_{R/A}){i} in the Hodge–Tate comparison is unchanged.
Over the q-de Rham prism A{1} = A · e_A with φ(e_A) = e_A/[p]_q; over a crystalline prism φ(e_A) = e_A/p (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-examples).
Consumers: PR.4 (Z_p(n) uses Δ̂{n}), PR.5 (absolute prismatic cohomology with twists, the line bundle O_WCart{1}).

nodes.title: Breuil–Kisin twists over the q-de Rham prism and over crystalline prisms
nodes.statement: (1) Let (A, I) = (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) be the q-de Rham prism. It is transversal with I_r = ([p^r]_q), [p^r]_q = (q^{p^r} − 1)/(q − 1), and [p^{r+1}]_q = [p]_{q^{p^r}} [p^r]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q modulo I_r². There is a unique e_A ∈ A{1} whose image in I_r/I_r² is the class of [p^r]_q for every r; A{1} is the free A-module on e_A, and φ_{A{1}}(e_A) = [p]_q^{−1} e_A. (2) For a map of prisms f : (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)) → (B, J), the image e_B of e_A generates B{1} and φ_{B{1}}(λ e_B) = φ_B(λ) f([p]_q)^{−1} e_B; e_B depends on f and not only on (B, J). (3) For a crystalline prism (B, (p)) the map q ↦ 1 gives a canonical generator e_B of B{1} with φ_{B{1}}(e_B) = e_B/p; hence (B{n}, φ_{B{n}}) ≅ (B, p^{−n} φ_B) for all n ∈ Z, and the twisted divided Frobenius of PR.3/divided-frobenius is φ/p^i. (4) For an oriented prism (B, (d)) and a generator e of B{1}, φ_{B{1}}(e) = u d^{−1} e for a unit u; replacing e by v e replaces u by φ(v) v^{−1} u.
hypotheses: The q-de Rham prism is PR.0/q-de-rham-prism: φ(q) = q^p, δ(q) = 0.
Bhatt–Lurie characterise e_A by (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p); the node uses the equivalent description by the classes of [p^r]_q, which is the one their proof establishes, so that no logarithm is needed.
BL22 Remark 2.6.2 and Notation 2.6.3 write the target of the Frobenius as I^{−1}{1}; by Notation 2.5.4 this is A{1} ⊗_A I^{−1}, the module written I^{−1}A{1} in Remark 2.5.9.
proofSteps: (1): I_r is generated by φ^s([p]_q) = [p]_{q^{p^s}}, s < r, whose product is [p^r]_q; q^{p^r} ≡ 1 modulo I_r gives [p]_{q^{p^r}} ≡ p modulo I_r, hence the congruence modulo I_r². The compatible system defines e_A by PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist-transversal, and it generates because its image generates each I_r/I_r².

Frobenius: φ_A([p^r]_q) = [p^r]_{q^p} = [p^{r+1}]_q/[p]_q, which under φ_A^*(I_r) = I^{−1}I_{r+1} is [p]_q^{−1} times the class of [p^{r+1}]_q (BL22 Remark 2.6.2 obtains the same formula from φ(log_Δ) = log_Δ).
(2), (3): functoriality of the twist and of its Frobenius (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (2), (5)); for a crystalline prism q ↦ 1 is a map of prisms with [p]_q ↦ p (BL22 Example 2.6.4).
(4): B{1} is free by PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (4) and φ_B^*(B{1}) ≅ d^{−1} B{1}.
acceptance: Crystalline prism acceptance example of the stage: for (Z_p, (p)), Z_p{n} = Z_p · e^n with φ(e^n) = p^{−n} e^n.
Under reduction modulo I the generator e_A maps to the class of [p]_q in I/I².
The two generators of the twist of the coproduct of the q-de Rham prism with itself differ by a unit that is not 1, which is why e_B depends on f.

nodes.title: Large quasisyntomic algebras over A/I
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and Ā = A/I. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra is a derived p-complete Ā-algebra S that is p-completely flat over Ā and whose cotangent complex L_{S/Ā} has p-complete Tor amplitude in [−1, 0]; such an S is classically p-complete. A quasisyntomic Ā-algebra S is large if there is a surjection Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞} | t ∈ T⟩ → S for some set T; equivalently, S/pS is generated as an Ā-algebra by the images of elements of S that admit compatible systems of p-power roots in S. For a large quasisyntomic S: Ω^1_{S/Ā} vanishes after p-completion, so L_{S/Ā}[−1] is a p-completely flat S-module, and every (∧^i L_{S/Ā})[−i]^∧ is a p-completely flat S-module. Large quasisyntomic algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site of Ā: every quasisyntomic Ā-algebra has a quasisyntomic cover by a large one, and the terms of the Čech nerve of such a cover are large. The standard examples are Ā⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) with (f_1, …, f_m) p-completely regular relative to Ā.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism; Ā has bounded p^∞-torsion.
Quasisyntomic algebras, covers and the site are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5 (BMS2 §4) over the base Ā.
Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ is the p-adic completion of the perfected polynomial ring Ā[X_t^{1/p^∞}].

The second formulation is the one of Bhatt–Lurie (S/pS generated by the images of Ā and of (S/pS)^♭); for p-complete S the two agree because compatible systems of p-power roots lift uniquely from S/pS to S.
proofSteps: Equivalence: a surjection from Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ exhibits generators with compatible roots; conversely generators x_t of S/p with compatible roots in S define Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩ → S, surjective modulo p and hence surjective by p-completeness. The map S^♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} S → (S/p)^♭ is bijective for p-complete S.

Ω^1: if x = y^p then dx = p y^{p−1} dy, so Ω^1_{S/Ā}/p is generated by zero; with the Tor amplitude condition this gives p-complete flatness of L_{S/Ā}[−1] and of its divided and exterior powers (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).

Basis: for quasisyntomic S choose generators and adjoin compatible p-power roots, S → S ⊗̂_{Ā⟨X_t⟩} Ā⟨X_t^{1/p^∞}⟩, a quasisyntomic cover with large target (BS22, the paragraph after Definition 15.1; BMS2 Lemma 4.28).
acceptance: Ā itself is large (T empty).
For a perfect prism, a quasiregular semiperfectoid Ā-algebra that is quasisyntomic over Ā is large; large algebras replace quasiregular semiperfectoid rings when the base prism is not perfect.
Ā⟨X⟩ is not large: dX is not divisible by p in Ω^1.

nodes.title: Relative Nygaard filtration of a large quasisyntomic algebra (BS22 Theorem 15.2)
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and S a large quasisyntomic A/I-algebra. (1) The derived prismatic cohomology Δ_{S/A} is concentrated in degree 0 and is a (p, I)-completely flat δ-A-algebra; (Δ_{S/A}, IΔ_{S/A}) is the initial object of the relative prismatic site (S/A)_Δ. Let Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = Δ_{S/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A (the Frobenius twist, a discrete (p, I)-completely flat A-algebra) and φ_{S/A} : Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A} the relative Frobenius, an A-algebra map. Put Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = {x ∈ Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} : φ_{S/A}(x) ∈ I^i Δ_{S/A}}. (2) φ_{S/A} induces an injection gr^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} → Δ̄_{S/A}{i} = I^iΔ_{S/A}/I^{i+1}Δ_{S/A} whose image is Fil_i^conj Δ̄_{S/A}{i}, for every i ≥ 0. (3) The formation of Fil^i_N commutes with base change in A: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) and S_B the p-completion of S ⊗_A B, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} ⊗̂_A B ≅ Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B}.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism; S is large and quasisyntomic over A/I (PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra).

The filtration lives on the Frobenius twist Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{S/A}, not on Δ_{S/A}: the relative Frobenius is A-linear only as a map out of the twist. For a perfect prism φ_A is an isomorphism and Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = φ_A^* Fil^i_N Δ_{S/A}.
The conjugate filtration is the one of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison relative to A/I; on large S its pieces are discrete, p-completely flat S-modules.
Completed tensor products are derived (p, I)-completed; on completely flat modules over a bounded prism they are classical completions (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness).
proofSteps: (1): by the derived Hodge–Tate comparison the graded pieces of the conjugate filtration of Δ̄_{S/A} are (∧^i L_{S/(A/I)})[−i]^∧{−i}, discrete and p-completely flat over S, so Δ_{S/A} is discrete and (p, I)-completely flat; initiality follows from PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site (BS22 Lemma 7.7) once a functorial idempotent endomorphism of Δ_{S/A} is shown to be the identity, as in the proof of PR.2/qrsp-prism (BS22 Proposition 7.10).

(3): if (2) holds for S over A, the base change of Fil^•_N to B is a filtration of Δ^{(1)}_{S_B/B} satisfying (2), and a filtration by ideals satisfying (2) is the Nygaard filtration by the induction of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (1).

(2), reduction: by descent to smooth algebras and left Kan extension it suffices to treat S = (A/I)⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_n^{1/p^∞}⟩/(f_1, …, f_m); by PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent (BS22 Proposition 7.11) a flat base change in A gives compatible p-power roots of the f_j; the devissage of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid reduces to S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X).

(2), the key case over a general base: localise on A so that I = (d) (PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators), base change from the universal oriented prism, whose Frobenius is faithfully flat (PR.0/free-delta-ring), so its perfection A → A_∞ is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat (PR.0/prism-perfection); over the perfect prism A_∞ the statement is PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces, and it descends along A → A_∞ because on the Čech nerve the filtration is the base change from A_∞ by (3).
acceptance: S = A/I: Δ^{(1)}_{S/A} = A, φ_{S/A} = id, Fil^i_N = I^i and gr^i = I^i/I^{i+1} = (A/I){i} = Fil_i^conj Δ̄{i} (BL22 Example 5.1.4).
S = (A/I)⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X) over the q-de Rham prism: the base change to the perfection is the key case of PR.3/nygaard-key-case.

nodes.title: Relative Nygaard filtration on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I. For an animated commutative Ā-algebra R write φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = Δ^{(1)}_{R/A} = Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A for the Frobenius twist of derived prismatic cohomology and φ_{R/A} : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} for the relative Frobenius, a map of commutative algebra objects of the (p, I)-complete derived category of A. The relative Nygaard filtration is a decreasing filtration Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, an object of the I-complete filtered derived category DF(A), with a refinement Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^• ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} of φ_{R/A} to a map of filtered objects, constructed in three steps. (a) For R large quasisyntomic, Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is the ideal {x : φ_{R/A}(x) ∈ I^iΔ_{R/A}} of PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic. (b) For R quasisyntomic over Ā it is the right Kan extension of (a) along the inclusion of large algebras, equivalently the quasisyntomic unfolding: each R ↦ Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf and Fil^0_N = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. For X = Spf R affine and smooth over Ā this reads RΓ_Δ(X/A) ≅ RΓ(X_qsyn, Δ_{−/A}) and Fil^i_N RΓ_Δ(X/A)^{(1)} = RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}); for a smooth formal Ā-scheme X the filtrations on affine opens glue to a filtered object Fil^•_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} of D(X_ét, A). (c) For all animated R it is the (p, I)-completed left Kan extension of its restriction to finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebras; on quasisyntomic algebras this agrees with (b). Characterisation (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.1.1): the pair (Fil^•_N, Fil^•(φ)), functorial in R, is determined up to essentially unique isomorphism by: (1) each R ↦ Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} commutes with sifted colimits; (2) for R a finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebra, gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ̄_{R/A}{n} is an isomorphism on H^m for m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 for m > n. Properties: gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0, so the filtration is N-indexed; it is multiplicative (a commutative algebra object of DF(A) refining φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), giving in particular v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^•_N → Fil^{•+1}_N whose composite with Fil^{•+1}_N → Fil^•_N is induced by I ⊂ A; for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil^•_N φ_B^*Δ_{(B ⊗^L_A R)/B}; for R = Ā, Fil^n_N = I^n ⊂ A; for a perfect prism, Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = φ_A^*(Fil^•_N Δ_{R/A}) with the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism; R is an animated commutative Ā-algebra (derived prismatic cohomology depends only on the derived p-completion of R).
The filtration is on the Frobenius twist φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. It is not a filtration of Δ_{R/A} unless φ_A is an isomorphism.

DF(A) is the filtered derived category of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; the I-adic filtration I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A} is Z-indexed, with i-th term I^{⊗ i} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} for all i ∈ Z (negative powers are powers of the dual), as in BMS2 Proposition 5.8 and Bhatt–Lurie. Since gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0 the filtered Frobenius factors through its truncation to i ≥ 0, and for p-completely smooth R (Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}) the Beilinson connective covers of the two filtrations agree.

BL22 Proposition 5.1.1 (1) prints the target of R ↦ Fil^n_N as the complete derived category of Ā; the objects are A-complexes (for R = Ā they are the ideals I^n), so the target is the (p, I)-complete derived category of A (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E34).
Bhatt–Lurie's and Bhatt–Scholze's constructions agree wherever both apply: BL22 defines the filtration on large algebras by the formula of BS22 Theorem 15.2 and extends it by the same Kan extensions.
proofSteps: (a) is PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic. (b): large algebras form a basis of the quasisyntomic site (PR.3/large-quasisyntomic-algebra); R ↦ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} and R ↦ I^•Δ_{R/A} satisfy quasisyntomic descent (BL22 Lemma 5.1.7, from the conjugate filtration and flat descent for exterior powers of the cotangent complex, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5; PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent), hence are right Kan extended from large algebras, and so is the filtered Frobenius. For smooth X, BS22 Theorem 15.3 states the same definition on X_qsyn.

(c): by induction on n, R ↦ Fil^n_N on quasisyntomic algebras is left Kan extended from polynomial algebras, because gr^n_N ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} is (PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (2) on large algebras, extended by descent); then extend to animated rings by the universal property of animation (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:animation).

Uniqueness: a second pair satisfying (1), (2) is, on large algebras, an honest filtration by subgroups equal to the Frobenius-divisibility ideals, by induction on n using the fibre sequence Fil′^{n+1} → Fil′^n → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n}; the resulting comparison map is an isomorphism on polynomial algebras by (2), hence in general by (1) (BL22, proof of Proposition 5.1.1).

Multiplicativity, the map v and change of prism are checked on large algebras, where they are statements about ideals (φ(xy) = φ(x)φ(y); PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (3)), and extended by the Kan extensions (BL22 Remarks 5.1.8–5.1.10).
acceptance: R = Ā: φ_A^*Δ = A and Fil^n_N = I^n.

Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)), k a perfect field, and R smooth over k: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A) (PR.1/crystalline-comparison) and Fil^•_N is the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology; in coordinates it is p^{max(i−•, 0)} Ω^• (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates).
Perfect prism: agreement with PR.3/nygaard-filtration after applying φ_A^*.
Change of prism along the q-de Rham prism → its perfection recovers the key case.

nodes.title: Graded pieces of the relative Nygaard filtration
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) For every n ≥ 0 the map gr^n(φ) : gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^n/I^{n+1} ⊗^L_A Δ_{R/A} = Δ̄_{R/A}{n} factors through an isomorphism gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}, functorial in R; gr^n_N = 0 for n < 0. (2) gr^0_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ R̂, the derived p-completion of R. (3) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth over Ā (for example X = Spf R affine smooth), then gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ τ^{≤ n} Δ̄_{R/A}{n}: H^m(gr^n_N) ≅ Ω̂^m_{R/Ā}{n − m} for 0 ≤ m ≤ n and H^m(gr^n_N) = 0 otherwise. (4) gr^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}[−1]^∧, the shifted p-completed cotangent complex of R over A. (5) For every R the filtered object Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is connective for the Beilinson t-structure of DF(A): gr^n_N lies in D^{≤ n} for all n.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; the conjugate filtration and the twist {n} = ⊗ (I/I²)^{⊗ n} are those of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison.
The isomorphism in (1) is A-linear: the semilinearity of the perfectoid statement PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces has been absorbed into the Frobenius twist.
(4) is BS22 Remark 15.6, which prints L_{X/A} ≃ gr^1_N Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} without the shift and cites Theorem 1.16 (2) for (3) (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E26); the node states the corrected form.
The Beilinson t-structure is requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 (BMS2 Definition 5.3).
proofSteps: (1) on large quasisyntomic algebras is PR.3/relative-nygaard-large-quasisyntomic (2); both sides are right Kan extended from large algebras on quasisyntomic ones and left Kan extended from polynomial algebras in general (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; the conjugate filtration commutes with sifted colimits), which gives the functorial isomorphism for all R (BL22 Remark 5.1.2 and the proof of Proposition 5.1.1).

(2): Fil_0^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≅ R̂ (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison). (3): for p-completely smooth R the conjugate filtration is the canonical filtration and H^m(Δ̄_{R/A}) ≅ Ω̂^m{−m} (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison); this is BS22 Theorem 15.3, second display, obtained there by descent from Theorem 15.2 (2).
(4): combine (1) for n = 1 with PR.2/first-conjugate-piece-cotangent (Fil_1^conj Δ̄_{R/A} ≅ L_{R/A}{−1}[−1]^∧).
(5): Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A} has graded pieces (∧^j L_{R/Ā})[−j]^∧, j ≤ n, which lie in D^{≤ j} ⊂ D^{≤ n}.
acceptance: R = Ā: gr^n = I^n/I^{n+1} = Ā{n}.
R = Ā⟨T⟩: gr^n_N has H^0 = R{n} and, for n ≥ 1, H^1 = Ω̂^1_{R/Ā}{n−1}.
R large quasisyntomic: gr^n_N is the discrete module Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n}.

Comparison with the Hodge–Tate side: the associated graded of the Nygaard filtration is the conjugate (Hodge–Tate) filtration, twisted; comparison with the de Rham side is PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison.

nodes.title: The Lη_I factorisation of Frobenius (BS22 Theorem 15.3)
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra, X = Spf R, Δ = Δ_{R/A} = RΓ_Δ(X/A). (1) The filtered Frobenius Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ → I^• ⊗ Δ factors uniquely through the connective cover τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ) for the Beilinson t-structure, whose underlying complex is Lη_I Δ. On underlying complexes this gives a canonical map φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} such that the relative Frobenius factors as φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Lη_I Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A}, the second map being the canonical one (it exists because Δ lies in D^{≥0} and H^0(Δ) is I-torsion-free). (2) φ̃ is an isomorphism. (3) The filtered map Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ Δ_{R/A}) is an isomorphism of filtered objects: Fil^•(φ) exhibits the Nygaard filtration as the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration. For an I-torsion-free complex K^• representing Δ, Fil^i_N corresponds under φ̃ to the subcomplex I^iK^• ∩ η_I K^• of η_I K^•. In particular lim_i Fil^i_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} = 0. (4) φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects, compatible with base change in (A, I) and with étale localisation on R; for a smooth formal A/I-scheme X it globalises to an isomorphism φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A).
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism; R is p-completely smooth over A/I. No orientation of I and no hypothesis on W(A/I) is made.

Lη_I is the derived décalage functor of AInfCohomology:AI.1 for the invertible ideal I ⊂ A (on the ringed topos (X_ét, A) in the global statement); it is not exact, and the statement is one about objects and maps in D(A).

The Beilinson t-structure, τ^{≤0}_B, and the identification of Lη_I K with the underlying complex of τ^{≤0}_B(I^• ⊗ K) (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 and Proposition 5.8) are requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1 and AInfCohomology:AI.1.
proofSteps: (1): by PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces (3), gr^i_N ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄{i} ∈ D^{≤i}, so Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ is Beilinson connective and the filtered Frobenius factors uniquely through τ^{≤0}_B(I^•Δ); its underlying complex is Lη_IΔ (BMS2 Proposition 5.8). Since Δ̄ ∈ D^{≥0}, the graded pieces of τ^{≤0}_B(I^•Δ) vanish in negative degrees, so the cover is N-indexed and its map to I^0Δ = Δ is the map Lη_IΔ → Δ of BMS1 Lemma 6.10.

(2): by derived Nakayama it suffices to check modulo I. Lη_IΔ ⊗^L_A A/I is the Bockstein complex (H^•(Δ̄){•}, β_I) (AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction, BMS1 Proposition 6.12), which is Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} by the Hodge–Tate comparison (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison). Both sides commute with base change in A and with étale localisation; reduce to a polynomial algebra, then by base change to an oriented prism, to the universal oriented prism, to a crystalline prism (BS22 Construction 6.1, as in PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison) and to A = Z_p, where the claim is the crystalline comparison (PR.1/crystalline-comparison) and the Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3/polynomial-cartier-map).

(3): the filtered map is an isomorphism on every gr^i, by (1) of PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces and gr^i τ^{≤0}_B = τ^{≤i} gr^i. Its fibre is therefore a constant filtered object, equal to the fibre of φ̃ in filtration degree 0, which vanishes by (2). The subcomplex description is the filtration G^i = I^iK^• ∩ η_IK^• in the proof of BMS2 Proposition 5.8, and lim_i G^i = lim_i I^iΔ = 0.

(4): τ^{≤0}_B is lax symmetric monoidal because the Beilinson t-structure is compatible with the tensor product (BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (1)); base change and étale localisation follow from PR.1/prismatic-base-change, PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration (change of prism) and flat base change for Lη (AInfCohomology:AI.1).
acceptance: R = A/I: φ_A^*Δ = A = Lη_I A and φ̃ is the identity.

Crystalline prism (W(k), (p)): the statement is the Berthelot–Ogus isomorphism φ : RΓ_crys ≅ Lη_p RΓ_crys, with the Nygaard filtration on the source and the décalage filtration on the target (BMS2 Proposition 8.5 and its corollary).
Cohomology: H^i(φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ≅ (H^i(Δ_{R/A})/H^i(Δ_{R/A})[I]) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} (AInfCohomology:AI.1/decalage-cohomology).
Consumers: PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general, PR.3/image-of-frobenius, PR.6 (AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ carries the décalage filtration to the Nygaard filtration), PR.8.

nodes.title: De Rham comparison for every bounded prism (BS22 Corollary 15.4)
nodes.statement: (1) Fix a bounded (A,I), and let X be formally smooth over A/I. On X_ét, the following canonical equivalence respects its E_∞-algebra structure: Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A/I ≅ Ω^•_{X/(A/I)}, the p-completed de Rham complex. No hypothesis on W(A/I) is needed. (2) For R p-completely smooth over A/I the isomorphism φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≅ Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)} is the composite of φ̃ ⊗ A/I (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation), the Bockstein reduction Lη_IΔ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/I ≃ (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I), and the Hodge–Tate comparison (H^•(Δ̄_{R/A}){•}, β_I) ≅ (Ω̂^•_{R/(A/I)}, d). (3) (Derived form, Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.2.5) For every animated commutative A/I-algebra R there is a natural isomorphism A/I ⊗^L_A φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} with the p-completed derived de Rham complex, the left Kan extension of (2) from polynomial algebras.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism; X is a smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, not necessarily affine or proper.
The scalar extension is along φ_A followed by A → A/I and is derived (p, I)-completed; it is not the untwisted reduction Δ̄_{X/A}, whose cohomology is the Hodge–Tate cohomology.
BS22 Corollary 15.4 prints the right-hand side as Ω^*_{R/(A/I)}; it is Ω^*_{X/(A/I)} (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E1).

PR.1/de-rham-comparison is the same statement under the hypothesis that W(A/I) is p-torsion-free (BS22 Theorem 6.4), proved without Lη. The sources do not compare the two isomorphisms when both are defined, and the node does not assert that they coincide (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/27).
Bhatt–Lurie prove (3) through the Hodge–Tate divisor of the Cartier–Witt stack; the plan uses the Bhatt–Scholze route, which needs nothing from PR.5.
proofSteps: (2): reduce φ̃ : φ_A^*Δ ≅ Lη_IΔ modulo I and apply AInfCohomology:AI.1/bockstein-reduction (BMS1 Proposition 6.12): Lη_IΔ ⊗^L A/I is represented by the complex with terms H^i(Δ̄){i} and the Bockstein differential β_I. The Hodge–Tate comparison map of PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map is by construction a map of differential graded algebras (Ω̂^•, d) → (H^•(Δ̄){•}, β_I), an isomorphism by PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison.

Multiplicativity: φ̃ is a map of commutative algebra objects (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (4)); the Bockstein reduction is multiplicative (BMS1 Lemma 6.13 and the remark before it, requested from AInfCohomology:AI.1; equivalently H^0_B is symmetric monoidal on Beilinson-connective objects, BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (3)).

(1): the affine isomorphisms are functorial for étale maps and Lη_I, the Bockstein complex and the de Rham complex are compatible with étale localisation, so they glue on X_ét (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (4)).

(3): both sides commute with sifted colimits in R (the left side by PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology, the right side by definition of derived de Rham cohomology, DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2), and (2) for polynomial algebras is natural; left Kan extend (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3).
acceptance: Crystalline prism: reduces modulo p the crystalline comparison φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_crys(R/A).
The q-de Rham prism: Δ_{R/A} ⊗̂_{A, φ} A/([p]_q) is de Rham cohomology over Z_p[ζ_p]; here A/I = Z_p[ζ_p] is p-torsion-free, so PR.1/de-rham-comparison also applies.
A prism where Theorem 6.4 does not apply: a crystalline prism (A, (p)) with A/p non-reduced has p-torsion in W(A/p); the present node still applies.
R = A/I: both sides are A/I.

nodes.title: The image of Frobenius on prismatic cohomology (BS22 Corollary 15.5)
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and X a smooth formal A/I-scheme. For every i ≥ 0 there is a natural map V_i : τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} in D(X_ét, A) such that φ ∘ V_i is the natural map τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ_{X/A} induced by I^{⊗ i} → A, and V_i ∘ (φ ⊗ 1) : τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → τ^{≤ i}Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} is the natural map. In particular V_i induces V_i : H^i_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i} → H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}), an inverse of φ up to I^{⊗ i}; when I = (d), V_i φ = φ V_i = d^i on H^i. For X quasi-compact and quasi-separated, H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A)) and the linearised Frobenius φ_A^* RΓ_Δ(X/A) → RΓ_Δ(X/A) becomes an isomorphism after inverting I.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded prism; X smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I; Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} = Δ_{X/A} ⊗̂^L_{A, φ_A} A as a sheaf on X_ét.

BS22 Corollary 15.5 prints the induced map as H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) ⊗ I^{⊗ i} → H^i_Δ(X/A); source and target are interchanged (register id PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E25). The node states the corrected direction, which is that of BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6).

The identification H^i(X_ét, Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) = H^i(φ_A^*RΓ_Δ(X/A)) uses that completed base change commutes with the finite limits computing RΓ on a quasi-compact quasi-separated X; the sheaf-level statement needs no such hypothesis.
proofSteps: By PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation, φ̃ : Δ^{(1)}_{X/A} ≅ Lη_I Δ_{X/A} and φ = (Lη_IΔ → Δ) ∘ φ̃.

BMS1 Lemma 6.9 (requested from AInfCohomology:AI.1) gives natural transformations I^{⊗ m} ⊗ τ^{≤ m} → τ^{≤ m} Lη_I and, on objects with I-torsion-free H^n, τ^{≥ n} Lη_I → I^{⊗ n} ⊗ τ^{≥ n}, whose composites in both orders on τ^{[n, m]} are the natural inclusions. Take n = 0, m = i and K = Δ_{X/A}, which lies in D^{≥0} with I-torsion-free H^0; define V_i as φ̃^{-1} composed with the first transformation.
H^i(X_ét, τ^{≤ i}K) → H^i(X_ét, K) is an isomorphism for every K, which gives the statement on H^i; after inverting I the maps φ and V_i are mutually inverse up to the unit d^i locally.
acceptance: i = 0: V_0 φ = φ V_0 = 1 on τ^{≤0}, so φ : H^0(Δ^{(1)}_{X/A}) → H^0(Δ_{X/A}) is an isomorphism.
Crystalline prism: V_i is the classical operator with V_i φ = φ V_i = p^i on H^i_crys (Berthelot–Ogus).
X = P^1 and i = 2: φ on H^2_Δ(P^1/A) = A{−1} is divisible by exactly I, consistent with φ_{A{−1}} : A{−1} → I ⊗ A{−1}.
Consumer: finiteness and isogeny statements for prismatic cohomology (BS22 Theorem 1.8 (6)); PR.7 uses the isogeny property of Frobenius on prismatic F-crystals of geometric origin.

nodes.title: Comparison of the Nygaard filtration with the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism, Ā = A/I, and R an animated commutative Ā-algebra. (1) (Bockstein and de Rham complex) Let β : H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) → H^{n+1}(gr^{n+1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) be the boundary map of gr^{n+1}_N → Fil^n_N/Fil^{n+2}_N → gr^n_N. Then (⊕_n H^n(gr^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}), β) is a commutative differential graded algebra and there is a unique isomorphism of commutative differential graded algebras θ onto the p-completed de Rham complex (Ω̂^•_{R/Ā}, d) that in degree 0 is the isomorphism H^0(gr^0_N) ≅ H^0(R̂). (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects of DF(A), Fil^•(γ_R) : Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, to the p-completed derived de Rham complex with its Hodge filtration, determined by functoriality in R and by gr^0(γ_R) being the isomorphism gr^0_N ≅ R̂ ≅ gr^0_Hodge. (3) There is a functorial fibre sequence in DF(A): I ⊗^L_A Fil^{•−1}_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}, the first map being the multiplication v of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration and the second Fil^•(γ_R). In filtration degree 0 it is the de Rham comparison PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general (3). (4) Consequently Ā ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge dR^∧_{R/Ā}; and if the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d over Ā then v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^n_N → Fil^{n+1}_N is an isomorphism for n ≥ d, so Fil^n_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗_A Fil^d_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} for n ≥ d.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded prism; R animated Ā-algebra; dR^∧_{R/Ā} and its Hodge filtration are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2, p-completed; for p-completely smooth R they are the p-completed de Rham complex with its stupid filtration.

In (1) the de Rham complex is that of π_0(R) relative to Ā, and Ω̂^n is H^0 of the derived p-completion of Ω^n_{π_0(R)/Ā} (Bhatt–Lurie's convention; it need not be p-adically separated and agrees with the classical completion when Ω^n has bounded p^∞-torsion).
In the proof of BL22 Corollary 5.2.8 the Hodge–Tate comparison is printed gr_n^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{n} ≃ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[n]; the shift is [−n] (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E35).
The fibre sequence compares three filtrations at once: on graded pieces it reads Fil_{n−1}^conj Δ̄{n} → Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n} → gr_n^conj Δ̄{n} ≅ LΩ̂^n_{R/Ā}[−n].
proofSteps: (1): H^n(gr^n_N) ≅ H^n(Fil_n^conj Δ̄{n}) ≅ Ω̂^n_{R/Ā} by PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces and the connectivity of the conjugate filtration; the Bockstein is identified with d on polynomial algebras through the Hodge–Tate comparison (PR.1/hodge-tate-comparison-map), hence in general; uniqueness because the de Rham complex is generated in degree 0 (BL22 Proposition 5.2.2).

(2): left Kan extend from polynomial algebras, where Fil^•_Hodge is the object (Ω̂^{≥ •}, d) of the heart of the Beilinson t-structure and Fil^•_N is Beilinson connective (PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces (5)), so maps Fil^•_N → Fil^•_Hodge are maps of complexes H^0_B(Fil^•_N) = (⊕ H^n(gr^n_N), β) → (Ω̂^•, d); take θ (BL22 Proposition 5.2.3).

(3): the composite Fil^•(γ) ∘ v is canonically null because I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N lies in DF^{≤ −1} and the target in the heart, on polynomial algebras; the induced map from the cofibre of v to Fil^•_Hodge is an isomorphism in degrees ≤ 0 by PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general (3) and on graded pieces by the Hodge–Tate comparison, hence in all degrees by induction (BL22 Corollary 5.2.8).
(4): take limits in (3) (BL22 Corollary 5.2.9); for smooth R of dimension ≤ d, Fil^{n}_Hodge = Ω̂^{≥ n} vanishes for n > d (BL22 Corollary 5.2.15).

Identify γ_R under Fil_N=τ_B^(≤0)(I^•Δ) with the map τ_B^(≤0)→H_B^0. Its reduction modulo I in filtration degree zero is exactly the canonical Lη_I reduction of BMS1 Proposition 6.12 followed by the Hodge–Tate identification, not merely some isomorphism of the same objects. Derived Nakayama therefore applies to this specified map.
acceptance: R = Ā: the sequence is I ⊗ I^{n−1} → I^n → 0 for n ≥ 1 and I ⊗ A → A → Ā for n = 0.
Crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)) and R regular Noetherian over F_p: the sequence is p · N^{n−1}WΩ → N^nWΩ → Ω^{≥ n}, the defining property of Nygaard's filtration on the de Rham–Witt complex.
R p-completely smooth of dimension d: the Nygaard filtration is I-adic from degree d on.

nodes.title: Nygaard completion
nodes.statement: (a) For a prism (B, J) the Nygaard completion is the ring B̂ = lim_i B/Fil^i_N B (inverse limit along the surjections B/Fil^{i+1}_N → B/Fil^i_N), with the canonical map c : B → B̂ and the filtration Fil^i_N B̂ = ker(B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B). Then ker(c) = ∩_i Fil^i_N B; B̂/Fil^i_N B̂ = B/Fil^i_N B; gr^i_N B̂ = gr^i_N B; and B̂ is complete for its filtration. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ̂_S denotes the Nygaard completion of Δ_S; Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N Δ̂_S ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces). (b) Frobenius. Assume J = (d) (then B is d-adically complete). Since φ(Fil^n_N B) ⊂ d^n B, φ induces a ring map φ̂ : B̂ → lim_n B/d^n B = B with φ̂ ∘ c = φ; the Frobenius of B̂ is c ∘ φ̂, so it factors through B. Likewise the divided Frobenius extends to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ → B with d^i φ_i = φ̂ on Fil^i_N B̂, and with twists to φ_i : Fil^i_N B̂ ⊗_B B{i} → B̂{i}. (c) Filtered objects. For a filtered object Fil^• of DF(A) with underlying object M = Fil^0 (N-indexed), the completion is M̂ = lim_i M/Fil^i with Fil^i M̂ = lim_{j ≥ i} Fil^i/Fil^j; M → M̂ is an isomorphism if and only if lim_i Fil^i = 0, and then M is called Nygaard-complete. This defines the Nygaard completions of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration) and of Δ_{S/A} over a perfectoid base (PR.3/nygaard-filtration); for a tower of surjections of discrete modules the derived limit is the limit, so (a) is a special case. (d) On quasisyntomic algebras over a perfectoid ring R, S ↦ Fil^•_N Δ̂_{S/A} is a quasisyntomic sheaf of complete filtered objects, the unfolding of (a) from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings. The map Δ → Δ̂ is not an isomorphism in general; PR.3/nygaard-completeness states when it is, and PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example gives a ring S for which Δ_S → Δ̂_S is injective and not surjective.
hypotheses: (B, J) is a prism; in (b) J is principal, which holds for the initial prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring.
Completion means completion with respect to the Nygaard filtration only; no (p, J)-adic completion is applied, and by BS22 Lemma 13.2 (2) none is needed for Δ_S (PR.3/bms2-comparison).

Statement (b) is not printed in the sources in this form; it is immediate from the definition of the filtration and is recorded because the syntomic complexes of PR.4 need φ_i on the completion without passing through topological Hochschild homology.
Δ and Δ̂ are distinct objects: no statement of the stage identifies them outside the cases listed in PR.3/nygaard-completeness.
proofSteps: (a): the inverse limit of rings along surjections; the kernel of B̂ → B/Fil^i_N B is the limit of Fil^i_N/Fil^j_N, the transition maps are surjective, so B̂ → B/Fil^i_N is surjective and the quotients and graded pieces are unchanged; completeness of B̂ is the standard statement for limits of towers.

(b): a prism is derived J-complete and d is a nonzerodivisor, so B is classically d-adically complete. For x ∈ Fil^i_N B̂ represented by x_n ∈ Fil^i_N B with x_{n+1} − x_n ∈ Fil^n_N B, the elements φ_i(x_n) satisfy φ_i(x_{n+1}) − φ_i(x_n) ∈ d^{n−i}B and converge d-adically; the limit is φ_i(x). Twists: tensor with the invertible module B{i} (PR.3/divided-frobenius (b)).
(c): completion of filtered objects (BMS2 Lemma 5.2 (2), requested from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1): F̂(i) = F(i)/F(∞), and gr^i is unchanged.
(d): each gr^i_N is a quasisyntomic sheaf (PR.3/nygaard-filtration (c)); a limit of sheaves is a sheaf.
acceptance: S perfectoid: Δ̂_S = A_inf(S) (PR.3/nygaard-completeness (2)).
S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): Δ̂_S is strictly larger than Δ_S (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example).
φ̂ ∘ c = φ and the Frobenius of Δ̂_S has image in the image of Δ_S.
Export: Δ̂_S with its filtration, Frobenius and divided Frobenius is the object that RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6 compares with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), and the object from which PR.4 builds Z_p(n).
