nodes.title: Completeness of the Nygaard filtration: exact statements
nodes.statement: (1) (Criterion) For a prism (B, J): c : B → B̂ is injective iff ∩_i Fil^i_N B = 0, and bijective iff moreover lim^1_i Fil^i_N B = 0; for a filtered object, M → M̂ is an isomorphism iff lim_i Fil^i = 0. (2) (Perfectoid rings) If S is perfectoid then Δ_S = A_inf(S) is Nygaard-complete: Fil^i_N = (e^i) with e = φ^{-1}(d), and A_inf(S) is e-adically complete. (3) (Relative criterion, Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.2.10) For a bounded prism (A, I) and an animated A/I-algebra R: φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete if and only if the p-completed derived de Rham complex dR^∧_{R/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete (lim_m Fil^m_Hodge = 0). (4) (Smooth case, Corollary 5.2.11) If R is p-completely flat over A/I and R/pR is a filtered colimit of smooth (A/I)/p-algebras, in particular if R is p-completely smooth, then φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is Nygaard-complete; if R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d then moreover Fil^n_N = I^{⊗(n−d)} ⊗ Fil^d_N for n ≥ d. (5) (Perfect base) For a perfect prism (A, I) and a derived p-complete simplicial A/I-algebra S: Δ_{S/A} is Nygaard-complete for the filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration iff dR^∧_{S/(A/I)} is Hodge-complete. In particular Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S for S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X) (PR.3/nygaard-incomplete-example). (6) (Exhaustiveness) The Nygaard filtration is exhaustive in the trivial sense Fil^0_N = Δ; the non-trivial exhaustiveness statement is PR.3/nygaard-frobenius-colimit.
hypotheses: Completeness always refers to the Nygaard filtration; all objects are already derived (p, I)-complete.
In (3), (4) the filtration is the relative one on the Frobenius twist; in (2), (5) the base prism is perfect and the filtration is on Δ itself.
Hodge-completeness of derived de Rham cohomology is a property owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; for p-completely smooth R the Hodge filtration is the finite stupid filtration.
BL22 Remark 5.8.4 prints Fil^n ≃ I^{n−d} Fil^{n−d}; the correct right-hand side is I^{n−d} ⊗ Fil^d (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E36); (4) states the relative form.
proofSteps: (1): the Milnor sequence for the tower Fil^i_N B: 0 → lim Fil^i → B → lim B/Fil^i → lim^1 Fil^i → 0.

(2): φ is bijective, so Fil^i_N = φ^{-1}(d^i A) = (e^i) (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp); A_inf(S) is classically (p, d)-complete, e^p ≡ d modulo p, so it is derived e-complete and e-adically separated, hence e-adically complete.

(3): PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4) gives A/I ⊗^L_A lim_m Fil^m_N ≅ lim_m Fil^m_Hodge; lim_m Fil^m_N is derived I-complete, so it vanishes iff its reduction does. (4): for such R the Hodge filtration of dR^∧ is the stupid filtration of the p-completed de Rham complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2), which is complete; the last assertion is PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4); for smooth R completeness also follows from PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (3).
(5): for a perfect prism φ_A^* is an equivalence carrying Fil^•_N Δ_{S/A} to Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{S/A} (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration); apply (3).
acceptance: (Z_p, (p)), S = F_p: Δ = Z_p, Fil^i = (p^i), complete.
R = A/I⟨T⟩: complete, with Fil^n_N = I^{n−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N for n ≥ 1.
S = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X): dR^∧_{S/F_p} is the divided power algebra with its divided power filtration, which is not complete; correspondingly Δ_S ≠ Δ̂_S.
The statement of BS22 Theorem 13.1 involves Δ̂_S and not Δ_S for exactly this reason.

nodes.title: Prismatic cohomology as the completed colimit of the Nygaard pieces
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and R an animated commutative A/I-algebra. The maps v : I ⊗^L_A Fil^m_N → Fil^{m+1}_N of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration give a diagram φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−1} ⊗ Fil^1_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{−2} ⊗ Fil^2_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → ⋯, and the maps I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m(φ) : I^{−m} ⊗ Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} are compatible with it. (1) The induced map from the (p, I)-completed colimit of this diagram to Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism: the relative Frobenius exhibits Δ_{R/A} as the completed union of the twisted Nygaard pieces. (2) If the p-completion of R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d, the diagram is constant from m = d on and Fil^m(φ) : Fil^m_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} → I^{⊗ m} ⊗_A Δ_{R/A} is an isomorphism for every m ≥ d. (3) Consequently for X smooth over A/I of dimension ≤ d and i ≥ d, RΓ(X_qsyn, Fil^i_N Δ^{(1)}_{−/A}) ≅ RΓ_Δ(X/A) ⊗_A I^{⊗ i}.
hypotheses: (A, I) bounded prism; R animated A/I-algebra; I^{−m} is the dual of I^{⊗ m}.
The colimit is formed in the (p, I)-complete derived category of A.
BS22 states (3) for the Nygaard-completed sheaf; by PR.3/nygaard-completeness (4) completion changes nothing for smooth X.
proofSteps: Both sides of (1) commute with filtered (indeed sifted) colimits in R, so R may be taken a polynomial algebra in d variables.

By PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison (4) the diagram is constant for m ≥ d. It remains to see that Fil^d(φ) : Fil^d_N → I^d ⊗ Δ is an isomorphism; by derived Nakayama and the same result it suffices that gr^d(φ) : gr^d_N → Δ̄{d} is one.

By PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces, gr^d(φ) is the inclusion Fil_d^conj Δ̄{d} → Δ̄{d}, an isomorphism because gr_n^conj Δ̄ ≅ (∧^n L)[−n]^∧{−n} vanishes for n > d and the conjugate filtration is exhaustive (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison).
(3): apply (2) on affines and glue (BS22, the paragraph after Proposition 15.7).
acceptance: R = A/I (d = 0): Fil^m_N = I^m and I^{−m} ⊗ I^m = A = Δ for all m.
Perfect prism and S perfectoid: e^{−m}(e^m) = A_inf(S).
After inverting I the relative Frobenius φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}[1/I] → Δ_{R/A}[1/I] is an isomorphism for smooth R, in agreement with PR.3/image-of-frobenius.

nodes.title: A quasiregular semiperfectoid ring whose prism is not Nygaard-complete
nodes.statement: Let S_0 = F_p[X^{1/p^∞}]/(X), a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, with perfect base prism (Z_p, (p)). (1) Δ_{S_0} = Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧, the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) in Z_p[Y^{1/p^∞}], with δ(Y^{1/p^n}) = 0 and X^{1/p^n} ↦ Y^{1/p^{n−1}}; it is the p-completion of ⊕_{i ∈ N[1/p]} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!. (2) Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the p-completion of ⊕_i p^{max(n−⌊i⌋, 0)} Z_p · Y^i/⌊i⌋!; equivalently it is generated by the elements p^a · Y^b/b! · Y^ε with a + b ≥ n, b ∈ N, 0 ≤ ε < 1. (3) ∩_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} = 0, and Δ̂_{S_0} is the set of families (a_i)_{i ∈ N[1/p]} of p-adic integers, written Σ a_i Y^i/⌊i⌋!, such that for every n only finitely many i with ⌊i⌋ < n have a_i ∉ p^{n−⌊i⌋}Z_p; Δ_{S_0} is the subset of families with a_i → 0 p-adically. (4) The element exp(Y) = Σ_{m ≥ 0} Y^m/m! lies in Δ̂_{S_0} and not in Δ_{S_0}. Hence c : Δ_{S_0} → Δ̂_{S_0} is injective and not surjective, and lim^1_n Fil^n_N Δ_{S_0} ≠ 0. (5) The same holds for the key case S = (Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}, X^{1/p^∞}]/X)^∧ of PR.3/nygaard-key-case, with Σ_m Y^m/[m]_q! ∈ Δ̂_S ∖ Δ_S. By contrast Δ_S = Δ̂_S for S perfectoid.
hypotheses: S_0 is the reduction of the key case along Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p; the description (1), (2) is that of PR.3/nygaard-key-case at q = 1.

Bhatt–Lurie state the example for k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x) in the coordinates of A_crys, which differ from the present ones by the Frobenius twist of Anschütz–Le Bras Remark 3.4.3 (x corresponds to Y); the filtration is the ideal generated by p^a x^b/b! with a + b ≥ m.
The example concerns the prism of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring as defined in PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp; no absolute prismatic cohomology is used.
proofSteps: (1): Δ_{S_0} is the prismatic envelope Z_p⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩{Y^p/p}^∧ (PR.2/qrsp-prism), which is the p-completed divided power envelope of (Y) by PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (BS22 Corollary 2.39) since Y^p = φ(Y); its basis is the standard one (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0).

(2): S → S_0 is relatively perfect over the map of perfectoid rings Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ → F_p, so by PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (3) the Nygaard filtration is the base change of that of PR.3/nygaard-key-case (e) along q ↦ 1, where [p]_{q^{1/p}} ↦ p and [n]_q! ↦ n!. It agrees with BL22 Proposition 5.3.6.
(3): Fil^n_N is graded and its degree i part is p^{max(n−⌊i⌋,0)}Z_p, with zero intersection over n; Δ/Fil^n = ⊕_{⌊i⌋<n} Z/p^{n−⌊i⌋}, and the limit over n is the stated set of families.

(4): for exp(Y) the family is a_m = 1 for m ∈ N and 0 otherwise; for each n only the indices m < n are non-zero modulo Fil^n, and a_m does not tend to 0. (5): the same argument with [p]_{q^{1/p}}-adic separatedness of A; the perfectoid case is PR.3/nygaard-completeness (2).
acceptance: Acceptance example of the stage: a case where Δ and its Nygaard completion visibly differ.
gr^n_N Δ_{S_0} is the F_p-span of the classes of p^{n−⌊i⌋} Y^i/⌊i⌋! for ⌊i⌋ ≤ n, a free S_0-module of rank n + 1, matching Fil_n^conj of the divided power algebra.
The partial sums Σ_{m<n} Y^m/m! are a Cauchy sequence for the Nygaard topology with no limit in Δ_{S_0}.

nodes.title: The Nygaard filtration in coordinates (de Rham and q-de Rham models)
nodes.statement: Let (A, (d)) be a perfect prism, d′ = φ_A(d), and R a p-completely smooth A/d-algebra. Let M^• be a cochain complex of A-modules in degrees ≥ 0 whose terms are d-torsion-free, d′-torsion-free and d-adically complete, with a φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M of complexes, and an isomorphism M^• ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in D(A) carrying φ_M to the Frobenius. Assume (a) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ d′^n M^n for all n, and (b) for all n the map M^n/dM^n → H^n(M^•/d′M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, is bijective. Then the subcomplexes N^iM^• = d^{max(i − •, 0)} M^• (in degree n: d^{max(i−n,0)}M^n), with φ_M : N^iM^• → d′^iM^•, represent the relative Nygaard filtration and its filtered Frobenius: there is a unique isomorphism N^•M^• ≅ Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} in DF(A) compatible with the maps to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}. If moreover φ_M/d′^n : M^n/d → M^n/d′ is injective for all n, then N^iM^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ d′^i M^n}. Instances. (i) (BMS2 Proposition 8.7) A = W(k) with k a perfect field, d = d′ = p, R smooth over k, Ã a p-completely smooth lift of R with a Frobenius lift, M^• the p-completed de Rham complex of Ã over W(k): the Nygaard filtration of crystalline cohomology is p^{max(i − •, 0)} Ω^•_{Ã/W(k)}. (ii) (BMS2 Remark 9.11) A = A_inf(O_C), d = ξ, d′ = ξ̃ = [p]_q with q = [ε], R with a framing, M^• the framed q-de Rham complex q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf} with φ(T_j) = T_j^p: the Nygaard filtration is ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} q-Ω^•_{R̃/A_inf}.
hypotheses: (A, (d)) is a perfect prism; under Δ_{R/A} = (φ_A)_* φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} the ideal I^i Δ corresponds to d′^i M, which is why d′ appears in (a) and d in the conclusion.
Hypothesis (b) is the Cartier isomorphism in the model M: in (i) it is the inverse Cartier isomorphism (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.3), in (ii) its q-analogue.

In instance (ii) the identification of the framed q-de Rham complex with φ_A^*Δ_{R/A_inf} (through AΩ) and hypothesis (b) are supplied by PR.6, which applies this node; the present stage proves the criterion and instance (i).
BMS2 Remark 9.11 prints q = [ε] − 1; the q-de Rham complex of BMS1 Definition 9.5 is taken with q = [ε], so that q − 1 = μ (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E37).
BMS2 prove (i) through the de Rham–Witt complex; the plan derives it from the Lη_I factorisation, which needs no de Rham–Witt theory.
proofSteps: N^iM^• is a subcomplex and φ_M(N^iM^n) ⊂ d′^{max(i−n,0)+n}M^n ⊂ d′^iM^n by (a), so φ_M is a filtered map from N^•M^• to the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A} refining the relative Frobenius.

gr^i N is ⊕_{n ≤ i} (M^n/d)[−n] with zero differential, so N^• is Beilinson connective; it is complete because each M^n is d-adically complete and d-torsion-free. On H^n of gr^i (n ≤ i) the map to gr^i of the I-adic filtration is x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/d′^n, bijective by (b).

By the criterion for connective covers (BL22, the remark characterising Beilinson connective covers; BMS2 Theorem 5.4 (2)), N^• is the Beilinson connective cover of the I-adic filtration of Δ_{R/A}; so is Fil^•_N φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} by PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation (3). Connective covers are unique.

(i): M ≅ RΓ_crys(R/W(k)) ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} compatibly with Frobenius (CrystallineCohomology:CR.2, PR.1/crystalline-comparison); φ̃ is divisible by p^n on n-forms, and (b) is the Cartier isomorphism. (ii): φ(d_q log T_j) = ξ̃ d_q log T_j gives (a).
acceptance: R = k[T], Ã = W(k)⟨T⟩, φ̃(T) = T^p: Fil^i_N is p^iW(k)⟨T⟩ → p^{i−1}W(k)⟨T⟩dT for i ≥ 1; modulo p · Fil^{i−1}_N this is Ω^{≥ i}, as in PR.3/nygaard-hodge-comparison.
i = 1: Fil^1_N = (pÃ → Ω^1 → ⋯), the kernel of Ω^•_{Ã} → R.
Routed item PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/098 is instance (ii); its q-de Rham input is PR.6's.
The filtration depends on the Frobenius lift only up to filtered quasi-isomorphism.

nodes.title: The prismatic half of the comparison with BMS2 (BS22 Lemma 13.2 and Theorem 13.1)
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with prism (Δ_S, (d)). (1) (BS22 Lemma 13.2 (1)) δ(Fil^i_N Δ_S) ⊂ Fil^{pi}_N Δ_S + (d, p)^{i−1} Δ_S for all i ≥ 1. (2) (Lemma 13.2 (2)) The completion of Δ_S for the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S agrees with its completion for the ideals Fil^i_N Δ_S + (d, p)^j Δ_S; this follows because every gr^i_N Δ_S is classically (d, p)-adically complete. (3) Hence the δ-structure of Δ_S extends uniquely to a continuous δ-structure on the Nygaard completion Δ̂_S, functorially in S; its Frobenius is the Frobenius c ∘ φ̂ of PR.3/nygaard-completion, it maps Fil^i_N Δ̂_S into d^i Δ̂_S, and (Δ̂_S, φ, Fil^•_N) satisfies Δ̂_S/Fil^1_N ≅ S and gr^i_N Δ̂_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} via φ/d^i. (4) (Recognition in the key case) Let R = Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧ with prism (A, ([p]_q)) and S = R⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X). Let D be a derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, (p, [p]_q)-completely flat A-algebra with an endomorphism φ_D over φ_A and an A-algebra map A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩ → D commuting with the Frobenius lifts (φ(Y^{1/p^n}) = Y^{1/p^{n−1}}), such that the image of Y^p lies in [p]_q D. Then there is a unique map Δ_S → D of A⟨Y^{1/p^∞}⟩-algebras commuting with φ, and it is an isomorphism if and only if it is one after derived reduction modulo (p, [p]_q). Export. These statements, with PR.3/nygaard-key-case, PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid, PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces and PR.3/nygaard-completion, are the prismatic input of BS22 Theorem 13.1: the identification of (Δ̂_S, φ, Fil^•_N) with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p), its cyclotomic Frobenius and the Nygaard filtration of BMS2, and likewise BS22 Proposition 15.7 for π_0 TP(S/S[u]; Z_p) and the Nygaard completion of Δ^{(1)}_{S/𝔖}. Those identifications are proved in RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6, which imports this node; they are not asserted here.
hypotheses: S is quasiregular semiperfectoid; d is the image of a generator of ker θ for a perfectoid ring mapping to S.

The node contains no statement about topological Hochschild homology and has no trace-theoretic prerequisite. In the proof of BS22 Theorem 13.1 the inputs from BMS2 (the non-completed theory of Construction 7.12 with its Nygaard filtration, the Hodge–Tate comparison from the Segal conjecture, Corollary 9.12, and the characteristic p comparison, Theorem 8.17) belong to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6; the steps planned here are the lemma, the extension of the δ-structure, and the construction of the comparison map from the q-divided power structure.

The interface entry for this node described it as the identification with π_0 TC^-(S; Z_p); the stage edge PR.3 → RT.6 makes RT.6 the owner of that identification, and the node is sharpened accordingly.
In (1) the case i = 1 is empty of content: (d, p)^0 Δ_S = Δ_S.
proofSteps: (1): choose a surjection S′ = R⟨X_a^{1/p^∞}, Y_b^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X_a) → S inducing a surjection on cotangent complexes, hence on Δ and on every Fil^i_N (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces); reduce to S′, absorb the Y_b into R, pass to finitely many X_a by filtered colimits and to one variable by the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula, PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid (5)), using that the claim is stable under products: for x ∈ Fil^j_N, y ∈ Fil^k_N the formula δ(xy) = x^pδ(y) + y^pδ(x) + pδ(x)δ(y) and φ = x^p + pδ(x) give δ(xy) ∈ Fil^{p(j+k)}_N + (d, p)^{j+k−1}.

In one variable (PR.3/nygaard-key-case) the filtration is generated multiplicatively by [p]_{q^{1/p}} ∈ Fil^1_N, where the claim is empty, and by Y^i/[i]_q! ∈ Fil^i_N, where δ of the element is homogeneous of degree pi and every homogeneous element of degree pi lies in Fil^{pi}_N.

(2): gr^i_N Δ_S ≅ Fil_i Δ̄_S{i} semilinearly (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces), and Fil_i Δ̄_S is derived p-complete and p-completely flat over S, hence classically p-adically complete; φ(d) is a unit multiple of p modulo d. (3): by (1), δ is continuous for the topology of (2), so it extends to the completion (the extension of a δ-structure to a completion by PR.3/delta-nygaard-continuity); the remaining assertions are PR.3/nygaard-completion.

(4): BS22 Lemma 12.5 (PR.3/nygaard-key-case (b)) applied to D and x = Y gives Y^n/[n]_q! ∈ D, and the basis of PR.3/nygaard-key-case (d) gives the map, unique because D is [n]_q-torsion-free; both sides are derived (p, [p]_q)-complete, so derived Nakayama applies.

For a general perfectoid base first apply André’s root cover of PR.3/nygaard-regular-semiperfectoid to reach the cyclotomic key case. Check the inclusion of Nygaard ideals on the explicit q-divided-power generators there and descend the inclusion along the completely faithfully flat map; the one-variable calculation by itself is only cyclotomic.
acceptance: S perfectoid: Δ̂_S = A_inf(S) with its δ-structure; (1) reads δ(e^i A) ⊂ e^{pi}A + (d, p)^{i−1}A.
Key case: δ(Y^i/[i]_q!) is homogeneous of degree pi.
(4) with D = Δ_S gives the identity; with D the non-completed ring of BMS2 it gives the comparison map of the proof of Theorem 13.1.

nodes.title: Derived Frobenius fixed points of a φ-module
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring (Λ = F_p, Z/p^n or Z_p in this stage), B a commutative Λ-algebra and σ a Λ-linear ring endomorphism of B (the Frobenius when B is an F_p-algebra; φ_A when B = A/p^n for a prism (A, (d))). The ∞-category D(B[F]) has as objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M ∈ D(B) and φ_M : M → σ_*M a map in D(B), that is, a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M; it is the lax equaliser of the identity and σ_* on D(B), and a morphism is a map f : M → N with a chosen homotopy φ_N f ≃ σ_*(f) φ_M. The derived Frobenius fixed points are M^{φ=1} := fib(φ_M − 1 : M → M) ∈ D(Λ), the fibre being formed after restriction of scalars to Λ. For t ∈ B such that σ(t) becomes a unit of B[1/t] (for example σ(t) = t^p, or σ(t) ≡ t^p modulo a nilpotent ideal), φ_M extends uniquely to a σ-semilinear endomorphism of M[1/t] = M ⊗^L_B B[1/t], and (M[1/t])^{φ=1} denotes its fixed points. For a Z_p-linear φ-module M one writes (M/p^n)^{φ=1} for the fixed points of M ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n. For every i there is a short exact sequence 0 → coker(φ_M − 1 on H^{i−1}(M)) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ_M − 1 on H^i(M)) → 0; in particular H^0(M^{φ=1}) is in general not the group of φ-fixed vectors of H^0(M), and H^1(M^{φ=1}) can be non-zero for M concentrated in degree 0.
hypotheses: Λ lies in the σ-fixed subring of B, so that φ_M − 1 is Λ-linear; it is not B-linear.
The fibre is taken in D(Λ) (or D(Z)); M^{φ=1} carries no B-module structure.
For (M[1/t])^{φ=1} the image of σ(t) in B[1/t] is a unit; this holds for B = A/p^n, t = d, since φ(d) ≡ d^p mod p.
As a model in the pinned library a φ-module is a cochain complex of Λ-modules with an endomorphism, and the fibre is the shifted mapping cone of φ − 1.
proofSteps: Define D(B[F]) as in the statement of Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.2 and the functor (M, φ_M) ↦ fib(φ_M − 1) to D(Λ); in the library model the fibre is the mapping cone of φ − 1 shifted by −1, an object of the derived category through the localisation functor.
The long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle M^{φ=1} → M → M gives the short exact sequences 0 → coker(φ − 1 | H^{i−1}) → H^i(M^{φ=1}) → ker(φ − 1 | H^i) → 0.

Extension to M[1/t]: σ extends uniquely to B[1/t] because σ(t) is a unit there, and φ_M ⊗ σ is the required endomorphism of M ⊗^L_B B[1/t]; for σ(t) = t^p this is the colimit of φ_M along M → M → … with transition maps t.

Exactness: (−)^{φ=1} is a finite limit, hence commutes with all limits, with shifts and with ⊗^L_Λ Λ' for Λ → Λ' of finite Tor-dimension data used here (Z_p → Z/p^n, Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}); it commutes with filtered colimits in D(B), and Lemma 9.2 treats completed colimits.
acceptance: For M = F_p in degree 0 with φ = id: H^0(M^{φ=1}) = F_p and H^1(M^{φ=1}) = F_p.
For M an algebraic closure of F_p with its Frobenius: M^{φ=1} = F_p in degree 0 (Artin–Schreier equations are solvable).
For M = F_p[x] with its Frobenius: H^1(M^{φ=1}) = coker(F − 1) ≠ 0, the group H^1_ét(A^1_{F_p}, F_p).
If φ_M is topologically nilpotent for a complete filtration of M then M^{φ=1} = 0.

nodes.title: Frobenius fixed points commute with completed colimits
nodes.statement: Let B be an F_p-algebra with an element t ∈ B, with its Frobenius σ, and let D_comp(B[F]) ⊂ D(B[F]) be the full subcategory of pairs (M, φ_M) with M derived t-complete. Then the functors D_comp(B[F]) → D(F_p), M ↦ M^{φ=1} and M ↦ (M[1/t])^{φ=1}, commute with colimits. Explicitly, for a diagram (M_i, φ_i) in D_comp(B[F]) with colimit colim M_i in D(B) and derived t-completion (colim M_i)^∧ (the colimit in D_comp(B[F])), the maps colim (M_i)^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧)^{φ=1} and colim (M_i[1/t])^{φ=1} → ((colim M_i)^∧[1/t])^{φ=1} are isomorphisms. The proof shows N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} for every N ∈ D_comp(B[F]).
hypotheses: B is an F_p-algebra and φ_M is semilinear over the Frobenius of B, so φ(t) = t^p.
t is an arbitrary element; derived t-completeness is required of every M_i and the target colimit is the completed one.
The colimits are indexed by arbitrary small diagrams.
proofSteps: The fibre F of colim M_i → (colim M_i)^∧ is uniquely t-divisible, so F ≃ F[1/t] and it suffices to prove F^{φ=1} = 0, that is, the statement for M ↦ M^{φ=1} (Bhatt–Scholze, proof of Lemma 9.2).

For N ∈ D(B[F]) the quotient N/t carries an induced φ because φ(t) = t^p ∈ tB. If N is derived t-complete, the fibre of N → N/t is complete for the t-adic filtration and φ is topologically nilpotent on it since φ(t) = t^p ∈ t^2 B; hence its fixed points vanish and N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1}.

Both functors in D_comp(B[F]) → D(B[F]) → D(F_p), N ↦ N/t ↦ (N/t)^{φ=1}, commute with all colimits (reduction modulo t kills the difference between a colimit and its completion; fixed points are a finite limit in a stable category).
acceptance: For B = F_p[t] and the completed direct sum of copies of F_p[[t]] indexed by a set J: the fixed points are the direct sum over J of F_p ⊕ F_p[−1].
For a derived p-complete simplicial algebra S over a perfectoid ring: (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1} ≃ (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p)^{φ=1}, the step used in Theorem 9.1.
Without derived t-completeness of the terms the statement N^{φ=1} ≃ (N/t)^{φ=1} fails: N = B[1/t] has N/t = 0.

nodes.title: The étale comparison for perfectoid rings (Artin–Schreier–Witt and tilting)
nodes.statement: Let S be a perfectoid ring, (A_inf(S), (d)) its perfect prism and S^♭ its tilt; write d also for the image of d in S^♭ = A_inf(S)/p. For every perfect prism (A, (d)) with a map A/d → S one has Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), so Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n = W_n(S^♭[1/d]). For n ≥ 1: (1) (Artin–Schreier–Witt) RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n) ≃ fib(F − 1 : W_n(S^♭[1/d]) → W_n(S^♭[1/d])) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}; (2) (tilting) there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(S^♭[1/d]), Z/p^n). Hence RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}, naturally in the perfectoid ring S.
hypotheses: S is a perfectoid ring in the sense of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (integral perfectoid; p-torsion and characteristic p are allowed).
If p = 0 in S both sides vanish: S[1/p] = 0 and d maps to 0 in S^♭.
Étale cohomology is that of the schemes Spec(S[1/p]) and Spec(S^♭[1/d]), not of adic spectra; the adic spectra enter only through Huber's comparison.
proofSteps: Δ_{S/A} is discrete and equal to the initial prism A_inf(S) of S (PR.2/qrsp-prism applied to the perfectoid ring S, and PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); reducing modulo p^n and inverting d gives W_n(S^♭)[1/[d]] = W_n(S^♭[1/d]) because S^♭ is perfect.

Artin–Schreier–Witt: on the étale site of an F_p-scheme the sequence 0 → Z/p^n → W_n(O) → W_n(O) → 0 with second map F − 1 is exact and W_n(O) has no higher cohomology on affines (requested from SF.2); this gives (1) (Bhatt–Scholze, proof of Theorem 9.1, first approach).

Tilting: RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p])) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spa(S[1/p], S)) and the same for (S^♭[1/d], S^♭) by Huber's comparison [Huber, Étale cohomology of rigid analytic varieties and adic spaces, Corollary 3.2.2] (H1:henselian), and the two adic spaces have equivalent étale sites by the tilting equivalence [Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 1.11] (PerfectoidSpaces:P3).
Naturality in S of all three identifications gives a natural isomorphism on the category of perfectoid rings, as needed to finish the proof of Theorem 9.1 arc-locally.

For the perfect characteristic-p coefficient ring T=S^♭[1/d], define Frobenius on W_n(T) by the quotient W(T)/p^n≃W_n(T); equivalently it is the coordinatewise map induced by Frobenius of T. No non-existent truncated-Frobenius declaration is imported from Mathlib.
acceptance: S = O_C, C complete algebraically closed: both sides are Z/p^n in degree 0 (W_n(C^♭)^{F=1} = Z/p^n and F − 1 is surjective).
S a perfect F_p-algebra: both sides are 0.
S = Z_p^cycl (the p-completion of Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]): H^1 of the right-hand side is coker(F − 1) on W_n of the tilt of the cyclotomic field, the group Hom_cont(Gal, Z/p^n).

nodes.title: The étale comparison theorem for arbitrary p-adic formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring, (A, (d)) the perfect prism with A/d = R, and X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R. Let Δ_{X/A} ∈ D(X_ét, A) be the derived prismatic cohomology of X relative to A (PR.2; the étale sheafification of S ↦ Δ_{S/A} on affine opens Spf S), with its Frobenius. Let X_η := X ×_{Spf R} Spa(R[1/p], R) be the adic generic fibre and μ : X_{η,ét} → X_ét the nearby-cycles map. Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} in D(X_ét, Z/p^n). In particular, for X = Spf S affine, RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. The fixed points are the derived ones of PR.4/frobenius-fixed-points. The identification is natural in X and in (R, A), and for X = Spf S with S perfectoid it is the isomorphism of PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt.
hypotheses: R is perfectoid and (A, (d)) is its perfect prism; a generator d of the prism ideal is fixed (it exists, the prism being perfect).

X is any p-adic formal scheme over Spf R: no smoothness, no finite-type, flatness or regularity hypothesis, and no restriction on singularities; this corrects the stage text, which restricted the comparison to smooth formal schemes (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/6).
Δ_{X/A} is the derived (animated) prismatic cohomology of PR.2, not the cohomology of the prismatic site of a singular X.
(−)[1/d] and /p^n are applied before taking fixed points; no completion is applied after inverting d.
proofSteps: Let F(S) = RΓ(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^n) and G(S) = (Δ_{S/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} on affine formal schemes over Spf R. F is an arc_p-sheaf [Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology, Corollary 6.17] and is arc_p-locally concentrated in degree 0 (products of p-complete rank-one valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field, BS22 Remark 8.9), so F is the arc_p-sheafification of H^0(F); lifting clopen decompositions through arc_p-equivalences gives H^0(F) → H^0_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n) and hence F → RΓ_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n).

G(S) → (Δ_{S/A,perf}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} is an isomorphism: reduce to n = 1, where Δ_{S/A,perf}/p is the d-completed colimit of Δ_{S/A}/p along φ_S and each φ_S induces an equivalence on ((−)[1/d])^{φ=1}; apply PR.4/fixed-points-completed-colimits.

G is an arc-sheaf because S ↦ S_perfd is (BS22 Corollary 8.11), and an arc_p-sheaf because G(S × S') = G(S) when pS' = 0: Δ_{S'/A,perf} = W(S'_perf) (BS22 Example 8.3) and (d) = (p) there, so W(S'_perf)/p^n[1/d] = 0.

The map Z/p^n → G extends uniquely to RΓ_{arc_p}(−, Z/p^n) → G; composing gives F → G, a map of arc_p-sheaves. It is an isomorphism arc-locally, where S may be taken perfectoid and the claim is PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt (alternatively on products of absolutely integrally closed valuation rings of rank ≤ 1).

Globalise: the étale sheafification of S ↦ RΓ(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^n) on X_ét is Rμ_* Z/p^n by Huber's comparison between Spec(S[1/p]) and Spa(S[1/p], S) (H1:henselian), and that of G is (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}.
acceptance: X = Spf O_C: both sides are Z/p^n.

X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ (formal torus): after a choice of ε, H^1 of both sides is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers (Kummer theory; C⟨T^{±1}⟩ is a principal ideal domain); it contains the class of T, of order p^n, and is not finitely generated, since units 1 + aT with |a| < 1 close to 1 are not p-th powers.
A singular input, S = O_C⟨x, y⟩/(xy): the statement holds with the derived Δ_{S/A}; no smoothness is used.
X of characteristic p: both sides vanish.
For S perfectoid the map is the Artin–Schreier–Witt/tilting isomorphism.

nodes.title: Coefficient compatibility and passage to Z_p in the étale comparison
nodes.statement: In the situation of PR.4/etale-comparison write c_n : Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1}. (1) For n ≥ 1 the square formed by c_n, c_{n−1}, the map Rμ_* Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^{n−1} induced by reduction and the map of fixed points induced by Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^{n−1} commutes; likewise for the maps induced by multiplication p : Z/p^{n−1} → Z/p^n, and c_n ⊗^L_{Z/p^n} Z/p^{n−1} = c_{n−1}. (2) The c_n are maps of commutative algebra objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n). (3) Passing to derived limits, Rμ_* Z_p := R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ ((Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}, where (−)^∧_p is derived p-completion; for X = Spf S, R lim_n RΓ_ét(Spec(S[1/p]), Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_{S/A}[1/d])^∧_p)^{φ=1}. The limit is the derived limit of complexes; its cohomology sits in Milnor sequences with lim and lim^1 of the groups H^i(−, Z/p^n).
hypotheses: Same hypotheses as PR.4/etale-comparison: R perfectoid, X an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme over R.

Z_p-coefficients on the generic fibre mean the derived limit of the Z/p^n-cohomology (equivalently pro-étale cohomology of the constant sheaf lim Z/p^n); they are not étale cohomology of a constant sheaf Z_p.
The p-completion in (3) is applied after inverting d; (Δ_{X/A}[1/d])^∧_p is in general not Δ_{X/A}[1/d].
proofSteps: The comparison F_n → G_n of Theorem 9.1 is the unique map of arc_p-sheaves of Z/p^n-modules extending the unit Z/p^n → G_n; functoriality of this characterisation in the coefficient ring gives the commutative squares of (1) (the source states the identification as canonical for each n; the squares follow from the uniqueness in its proof).

Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n := Δ_{X/A}[1/d] ⊗^L_Z Z/p^n, so reduction of coefficients is base change and fixed points, a finite limit, commute with it; multiplicativity (2) holds because both sides are sheaves of commutative algebras and the comparison is the unit-preserving map of such (BS22 Theorem 1.8(4) states it for commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n)).

(3): R lim_n (M/p^n)^{φ=1} = (R lim_n M/p^n)^{φ=1} = (M^∧_p)^{φ=1} for M = Δ_{X/A}[1/d], since fibres commute with limits and R lim_n M ⊗^L Z/p^n is the derived p-completion (DD.1); Rμ_* commutes with R lim.
The identification of R lim_n Rμ_* Z/p^n with pro-étale nearby cycles of the sheaf lim Z/p^n uses repleteness of the pro-étale topos (E2).
acceptance: X = Spf O_C: Z_p ≃ (W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, and the square for n → n − 1 is reduction Z/p^n → Z/p^{n−1}.
Finite level: for the formal torus the Kummer class of T at level n maps to the Kummer class of T at level n − 1 on both sides.
For S = Z_p^cycl the lim^1 term vanishes and H^1 = Hom_cont(Gal, Z_p).

nodes.title: The variant of the étale comparison without inverting p or d
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and X a p-adic formal scheme over R. Then for all n ≥ 0 there is a canonical identification Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}/p^n)^{φ=1} of objects of D(X_ét, Z/p^n), where Z/p^n is the constant étale sheaf on X. For X = Spf S affine: RΓ_ét(Spf S, Z/p^n) = RΓ_ét(Spec(S/p), Z/p^n) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) ≃ (Δ_{S/A}/p^n)^{φ=1}, and R lim_n gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ (Δ_{S/A})^{φ=1} = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_{S/A} → Δ_{S/A}). The map Δ_{X/A}/p^n → Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n induces on fixed points the adjunction map Z/p^n → Rμ_* Z/p^n of PR.4/etale-comparison.
hypotheses: Same generality as Theorem 9.1: X arbitrary over a perfectoid ring R.
No element is inverted; the right-hand side is in general not concentrated in degree 0 on global sections, since H^1_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) can be non-zero.
The source leaves the proof to the reader (the remark is quoted in the register as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E17 for a wording slip: read 'a p-adic formal R-scheme'); the proof route below supplies it.
proofSteps: For a p-complete R-algebra S the absolute prismatic complex of S agrees with the relative one, Δ_S ≃ Δ_{S/A}, compatibly with Frobenius (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 4.4.12; PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison for the perfect prism A).

Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 8.1.9 (the weight-0 case of PR.4/syntomic-low-weights) gives RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_syn(Spf S, Z_p) = fib(φ − 1 : Δ_S → Δ_S); its proof reduces modulo p by derived descent to animated F_p-algebras, then by sifted colimits to polynomial F_p-algebras, where F_p ⊗^L Δ is de Rham cohomology and φ − 1 is an automorphism of the Hodge-filtration piece Fil^1 because Frobenius vanishes on differential forms of positive degree.

Reduce modulo p^n; Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change for the henselian pair (S, pS) identifies RΓ_ét(Spec S, Z/p^n) with RΓ_ét(Spec S/p, Z/p^n), the étale cohomology of Spf S; sheafify on X_ét.

Compatibility with Theorem 9.1: both comparison maps are unit-preserving maps of étale sheaves of commutative algebras, and the square with Δ/p^n → Δ[1/d]/p^n commutes by the uniqueness used in Theorem 9.1 (checked arc_p-locally on O_C, as in Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 8.3.7).
acceptance: S = O_C: Z/p^n ≃ (A_inf/p^n)^{φ=1} = W_n(O_C^♭)^{F=1}, and F − 1 is surjective on W_n(O_C^♭).
S = Z_p^cycl: H^1 of both sides is H^1_ét(Spec F_p, Z/p^n) = Z/p^n, since the residue field of S is F_p.
S an F_p-algebra over a perfect ring R: Δ_{S/A}/p is derived de Rham cohomology up to Frobenius twist and the statement is the Artin–Schreier sequence.

nodes.title: The étale comparison for smooth formal schemes (Theorem 1.8(4))
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism and X a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth p-adic formal scheme over A/I, with generic fibre X_η over Q_p as a (pre-)adic space and RΓ_Δ(X/A) = RΓ((X/A)_Δ, O_Δ) the cohomology of the prismatic site (PR.1). Then for every n ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) ≅ (RΓ_Δ(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} of commutative algebras in D(Z/p^n). It is the corollary of PR.4/etale-comparison obtained by taking RΓ(X_ét, −) and using that for smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with site cohomology.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism, so I = (d) is principal and A/I is perfectoid; perfectness is part of the hypothesis of Theorem 1.8(4).
X is smooth over A/I; smoothness is needed only to identify the derived Δ_{X/A} with the site-theoretic RΓ_Δ(X/A), not for the comparison itself.
X is qcqs for the global statement, so that inverting d and reducing modulo p^n commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).
proofSteps: Apply RΓ(X_ét, −) to Rμ_* Z/p^n ≃ (Δ_{X/A}[1/d]/p^n)^{φ=1} (PR.4/etale-comparison): the left side is RΓ_ét(X_η, Z/p^n) by definition of μ.

For smooth X the derived prismatic cohomology agrees with the cohomology of the prismatic site (PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site), so RΓ(X_ét, Δ_{X/A}) = RΓ_Δ(X/A); fixed points, /p^n and (for qcqs X) [1/d] commute with RΓ(X_ét, −).
Multiplicativity is PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients (2).
acceptance: X = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ over (A_inf, ker θ): H^1_ét(X_η, μ_{p^n}) is the group of units of C⟨T^{±1}⟩ modulo p^n-th powers, and the class of T corresponds to a φ-fixed class in H^1 of RΓ_Δ(X/A_inf)/p^n[1/d].
X proper smooth over O_C: with PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness, RΓ_ét(X_C, Z/p^n) is the fixed points of φ on a perfect complex over A_inf/p^n[1/d] = W_n(C^♭).
The statement for singular X is PR.4/etale-comparison, not this node.

nodes.title: Étale cohomological dimension of the generic fibre of a perfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring corresponding to a perfect prism (A, I). The F_p-étale cohomological dimension of the scheme X = Spec(R[1/p]) is ≤ 1: for every étale sheaf F of F_p-modules on X one has H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 1.
hypotheses: X is the spectrum, not the adic spectrum, of R[1/p]; the statement is false for general sheaves on the adic spectrum.
F is an arbitrary étale F_p-sheaf on the scheme X (a filtered colimit of Zariski-constructible sheaves).
The bound concerns F_p-coefficients (hence p-power torsion sheaves by dévissage); nothing is claimed for ℓ ≠ p.
proofSteps: Reduce to F = j_! L with j : U → X the inclusion of a quasi-compact open of a constructible closed subset and L an F_p-local system of constant rank; by the method of the trace [Stacks, Tag 03SH] pass to a finite étale cover V → U of degree prime to p on which L is a successive extension of constant sheaves F_p.

Lift V → U to a finitely presented finite map Spec(S) → Spec(R), put Y = Spec(S[1/p]) and let J ⊂ S be a finitely generated ideal cutting out the complement of V; dévissage reduces to RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) ∈ D^{≤1}.

By the étale comparison (PR.4/etale-comparison) for Spec(S) and Spec(S/J), RΓ(Y, j_! F_p) is (−/p[1/I])^{φ=1} applied to the fibre of Δ_{S/A,perf} → Δ_{(S/J)/A,perf}; fixed points raise the cohomological amplitude by at most one, so it suffices that this fibre is connective, which can be checked after base change to A/I, that is, for S_perfd → (S/J)_perfd.

Both S_perfd and (S/J)_perfd are discrete perfectoid rings because R → S is integral (BS22 Theorem 10.11), (S/J)_perfd ≃ (S_perfd/J S_perfd)_perfd by the universal property (PR.2/connective-perfectoidization-perfectoid), and S_perfd/J → (S_perfd/J)_perfd is surjective by BS22 Theorem 7.4 (PerfectoidQuotients:Q4).
acceptance: R = O_C: X = Spec C has cohomological dimension 0 ≤ 1.

R = Z_p^cycl: X is the spectrum of the completed cyclotomic field, whose absolute Galois group has p-cohomological dimension ≤ 1; H^1_ét(X, F_p) = Hom_cont(Gal, F_p) is non-zero, so the bound 1 is attained.
R a perfect F_p-algebra: X is empty and the statement is vacuous.

nodes.title: Syntomic complexes Z_p(n) on quasisyntomic rings
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasisyntomic ring (p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion and L_{S/Z_p} of p-complete Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]) and n an integer. Let Δ̂_S{n} be the Nygaard-completed prismatic cohomology of S with its n-th Breuil–Kisin twist, with Nygaard filtration N^{≥•}Δ̂_S{n}, obtained by quasisyntomic descent from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (PR.3). Let can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} be the canonical map and φ_n : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} the divided Frobenius; when S is an algebra over a perfectoid ring with perfect prism (A, (d)) and the twist is trivialised, φ_n is the restriction of φ/d^n to N^{≥n}Δ̂_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ̂_S}. The n-th syntomic complex is Z_p(n)(S) := fib(φ_n − can : N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n}) ∈ D(Z_p), a derived p-complete complex, and Z/p^r(n)(S) := Z_p(n)(S) ⊗^L_Z Z/p^r. The functor S ↦ Z_p(n)(S) is a sheaf of complexes on the quasisyntomic site. For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} and Δ̂_S{n} are discrete, Z_p(n)(S) is the two-term complex N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} → Δ̂_S{n} in degrees 0 and 1, H^0 = {x ∈ N^{≥n}Δ̂_S{n} : φ_n(x) = x} and H^1 = coker(φ_n − can). For a perfectoid ring R with perfect prism (A, I), choose a generator e of A{1} and let d be the generator of I with φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (for a Z_p^cycl-algebra: d = [p]_q with e = e_A; in characteristic p: d = p). Then Z_p(n)(R) ≃ (φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A) with differential φ/d^n − 1. Another choice e' = ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v) and the complexes are identified by multiplication by v^n. For a generator d' = ud not of this form the two-term complex is in general not quasi-isomorphic to Z_p(n)(R) (R = Z_p^cycl, d' = u[p]_q with u ∈ Z_p^×, u^n ≢ 1 mod p: H^0 = 0 instead of Z_p).
hypotheses: S is quasisyntomic; the construction is functorial for all maps of quasisyntomic rings and satisfies quasisyntomic descent.

The complex is defined by the formula of BMS2 §7.4 and Theorem 1.12(5) as a fibre of prismatic data; it is not defined as a graded piece of TC (that identification belongs to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6). The first display of BMS2 §7.4 prints gr^n TC for gr^i TC, registered as PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E5.
Sign convention: BMS2 writes hofib(φ − can), Bhatt–Scholze write fib(1 − φ_n); the two fibres are canonically isomorphic.
The divided Frobenius is a map between different objects (source N^{≥n}, target the whole twisted complex), so Z_p(n) is not an instance of fixed points of an endomorphism for n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: On quasiregular semiperfectoid S: Δ_S is the initial prism (PR.2/qrsp-prism), N^{≥n}Δ_S = {x : φ(x) ∈ d^n Δ_S} (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp), the completion Δ̂_S and its filtration are PR.3/nygaard-completion, the twist is PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist and φ_n is PR.3/divided-frobenius; define the two-term complex.

Unfold to all quasisyntomic rings by quasisyntomic descent (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent, PR.3/nygaard-filtration; the quasisyntomic site and its basis of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings are DD.5): each of N^{≥n}Δ̂{n}, Δ̂{n} is a sheaf, and a fibre of sheaves is a sheaf.

Perfectoid case: for R perfectoid Δ̂_R = A_inf(R) = A is Nygaard complete with N^{≥n}A = φ^{−1}(d)^n A, giving formula (9.3) of Bhatt–Scholze; the generator d is the one determined by a generator e of A{1} through φ_{A{1}}(e) = d^{−1}e (PR.3/divided-frobenius (b)); replacing e by ve replaces d by d·v/φ(v), and multiplication by v^n identifies the two complexes.
p-completeness: both terms are derived p-complete, hence so is the fibre; Z/p^r(n) is the derived reduction.
acceptance: For R perfectoid with perfect prism (A, (d)): Z_p(n)(R) is the two-term complex φ^{−1}(d)^n A → A, x ↦ φ(x)/d^n − x.
Z_p(0)(F_p) = fib(0 : Z_p → Z_p) has H^0 = Z_p and H^1 = Z_p.
Z_p(n)(S) = 0 for n < 0 and Z_p(1) is the Tate module of G_m locally (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).
For S a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra: H^0(Z_p(n)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=p^n} (PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p).

nodes.title: Syntomic cohomology of animated rings and bounded p-adic formal schemes
nodes.statement: For an animated commutative ring R and an integer n let Δ_R{n} be the absolute prismatic complex with Breuil–Kisin twist and Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} its absolute Nygaard filtration (PR.5), with ι : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the canonical map and φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} the Frobenius. Define RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) := fib(φ{n} − ι) in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p). Then: (a) R → R^∧_p induces an isomorphism on RΓ_syn(Spf −, Z_p(n)); (b) the map to the Nygaard-completed version fib(φ̂{n} − ι̂ : Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ̂_R{n}) is an isomorphism (Proposition 7.4.6); so for R quasisyntomic RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = Z_p(n)(R) of PR.4/syntomic-complex; (c) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) satisfies p-complete fpqc descent (7.4.7); (d) it commutes with sifted colimits, hence is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras (7.4.8); (e) RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → Tot RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}), Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 (7.4.10) and RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) ≃ lim_m RΓ_syn(Spf(R ⊗^L Z/p^m), Z_p(n)) (7.4.11). For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛, RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) := lim over maps Spec(A) → 𝔛 of RΓ_syn(Spf A, Z_p(n)); it agrees with the affine definition on Spf R, satisfies étale descent, and sits in the fibre sequence RΓ_syn(𝔛, Z_p(n)) → Fil^n_N RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ(𝔛){n} with second map φ{n} − ι.
hypotheses: R is any animated commutative ring; p-completeness is not assumed, and is harmless by (a).

The construction uses the absolute prismatic cohomology and absolute Nygaard filtration of PR.5 and the twists of PR.3; PR.4 owns only the fibre (ownership fixed by red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28).
𝔛 is a bounded p-adic formal scheme: locally Spf R with R p-complete with bounded p^∞-torsion.
n is any integer; the complex vanishes for n < 0 (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).
proofSteps: Definition and (a): Bhatt–Lurie Construction 7.4.1 and Warning 7.4.2; absolute prismatic complexes and the Nygaard filtration are invariant under p-completion (PR.5).

(b): the Frobenius factors as Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^n_N Δ̂_R{n} → Δ_R{n} (BL Remark 5.7.10), and the 3 × 3 diagram of BL Proposition 7.4.6 has pullback squares in the upper left and lower right, so the two fibres agree; on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings the absolute filtration is {x : φ(x) ∈ Δ^{[n]}} (BL Corollary 5.6.3) and Theorem 5.6.2 identifies it with the Nygaard filtration over a perfect prism, giving agreement with PR.4/syntomic-complex.

(c), (d): descent and sifted colimits for the Nygaard-completed filtered complexes (BL Remark 5.8.6); for (d) reduce modulo p, where for m > n the Frobenius maps F_p ⊗ Δ_R^{[m]}{n} into Δ_R^{[pm−n]}{n} ⊂ Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n}, so φ{n} − 1 is an isomorphism on a deep enough step of a complete filtration and F(R) is the fibre of a map between quotients that commute with sifted colimits (BL Proposition 7.4.8).
(e) from the corresponding statements for Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} (BL Proposition 5.5.24, Corollary 5.5.25).
Globalisation: BL Variant 7.4.12, using (e) for agreement on affines and (c) for étale descent.
acceptance: For R quasiregular semiperfectoid the complex is the two-term complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex.
For R a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra it is Fil^n_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R), x ↦ φ(x)/p^n − x (BL Example 7.4.4).
RΓ_syn(Spf Z[1/p], Z_p(n)) = 0, since the p-completion of Z[1/p] is 0.
For 𝔛 = Spf R the limit definition returns RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)).

nodes.title: The prismatic logarithm
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism with Breuil–Kisin twist A{1} (PR.3) and (1 + I)_{rk=1} := {u ∈ 1 + I : δ(u) = 0} the group of rank-one units congruent to 1 modulo I. If (A, I) is transversal, A{1} = lim_r I_r/I_r^2 with I_r = I φ^*(I) ⋯ (φ^{r−1})^*(I) and transition maps division by p, and for u ∈ (1 + I)_{rk=1} the element log_Δ(u) ∈ A{1} is the unique element with image u^{p^r} − 1 in I_{r+1}/I_{r+1}^2 for all r ≥ 0. For a general prism log_Δ : (1 + I)_{rk=1} → A{1} is the unique function compatible with every map of prisms (B, J) → (A, I) from a transversal prism. It is a group homomorphism, natural in the prism, satisfies φ_{A{1}}(log_Δ(u)) = log_Δ(u), and log_Δ(u) ≡ (u − 1 mod I^2) under A{1}/IA{1} ≅ I/I^2. For Ā = A/I the Tate module T_p(Ā^×) = lim (μ_{p^k}(Ā), x ↦ x^p) maps to (1 + I)_{rk=1} by ρ_0 (lift x ∈ Ā^{♭×} uniquely to A^{♭×} and apply ♯), and the composite log_Δ : T_p(Ā^×) → A{1} is also called the prismatic logarithm. For the q-de Rham prism (Z_p[[q − 1]], ([p]_q)) there is a unique generator e_A of A{1} with (q − 1) e_A = log_Δ(q^p). For a crystalline prism (A, (p)) and u with φ(u) = u^p, u^p ≡ 1 mod p: log_Δ(u^p) = log(u) e_A with log(u) = Σ_{n>0} (−1)^{n−1}(u − 1)^n/n.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a prism; for the Tate-module form A/I is its reduction. Transversal means A/I is p-torsion-free (so (p, I) is regular locally).
Rank one means δ(u) = 0, equivalently φ(u) = u^p when A is p-torsion-free.
The construction is algebraic; no K-theory or cyclotomic trace enters (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5 describes the earlier trace-theoretic construction of the comparison for Z_p(1), which this replaces).
Ownership: the twist A{1} is PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist; the logarithm is planned here because its consumers are the Tate twists of this stage.
proofSteps: Transversal case (BL Proposition 2.3.1, Construction 2.3.2): u^{p^r} ≡ 1 mod I_{r+1} because u^{p^r} = φ^s(u^{p^{r−s}}), and division by p carries the class of u^{p^r} − 1 to that of u^{p^{r−1}} − 1, since x^p − 1 ≡ p(x − 1) mod I_r^2 for x = u^{p^{r−1}}; additivity because (u^{p^r} − 1)(v^{p^r} − 1) ∈ I_{r+1}^2 (Proposition 2.3.3).

General prisms (BL Propositions 2.5.10, 2.5.16, Remark 2.5.17): every prism receives a map from a transversal prism through which given rank-one units lift (Lemmas 2.5.13, 2.5.15), and A{1} is the limit of the twists of transversal prisms over A (Proposition 2.5.1); define log_Δ by compatibility and deduce additivity, functoriality, Frobenius invariance (2.5.18) and the normalisation modulo I (2.5.19).

Tate modules (BL Notation 2.7.1, Propositions 2.7.2, 2.7.3, Construction 2.7.4): A^{♭×} → (A/I)^{♭×} is an isomorphism because the groups I^n/I^{n+1} are p-complete, and ♯ of an element of A^♭ has rank one.

Examples: q-de Rham prism (BL Proposition 2.6.1: [p^{r+1}]_q ≡ p [p^r]_q mod I_r^2 and (q − 1)[p^r]_q = q^{p^r} − 1) and crystalline prisms (BL Corollary 2.6.12), proved directly: for a crystalline prism I_r = (p^r), A{1} = lim (p^r)/(p^{2r}) with e_A the class of p^r, and u − 1 has divided powers because φ(u) = u^p ≡ 1 mod p; hence u^{p^m} = exp(p^m log u) ≡ 1 + p^m log(u) modulo p^{2m}, the terms p^{km}(log u)^k/k! for k ≥ 2 being divisible by p^{2m}; so the class of (u^p)^{p^r} − 1 in (p^{r+1})/(p^{2r+2}) is log(u)·p^{r+1}, that is log_Δ(u^p) = log(u)e_A. This avoids the q-logarithm of Anschütz–Le Bras.
acceptance: q-de Rham prism: log_Δ(q^p) = (q − 1) e_A with e_A a generator of A{1}.
Perfected q-de Rham prism: for ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) ∈ T_p((A/I)^×), ρ_0(ε) = q^p and log_Δ(ε) = (q − 1) e_A.
log_Δ(1) = 0 and log_Δ(uv) = log_Δ(u) + log_Δ(v).
log_Δ is not defined on units of rank ≠ 1: for u ∈ 1 + I with δ(u) ≠ 0 the classes u^{p^r} − 1 need not lie in I_{r+1}.

nodes.title: Syntomic complexes in weights n < 0, n = 0 and n = 1
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) For n > 0, RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(−n)) = 0. (2) There is a canonical map of commutative algebra objects α_R : RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p), characterised by functoriality in R, and it is an isomorphism when R is p-complete; here RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = lim_k RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z/p^k). If moreover R is a p-complete ring with x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, then RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the ring of continuous Z_p-valued functions on Spec R. (3) There is a canonical map c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), functorial in R and given, for R quasiregular semiperfectoid, in degree 0 by T_p(R^×) → T_p(Δ̄_R^×) → H^0_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)), the second map being the prismatic logarithm; for R p-complete the induced map RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(1)) from the p-completion is an isomorphism. (4) Consequently, for a quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1], and the natural map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Z_p(1)(R), where Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] and (−)^∧ is derived p-completion, is an isomorphism on H^i for i ≤ 1 and injective on H^2; it is an isomorphism if and only if (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0, which holds for perfectoid R and fails for R = F_p(t) (H^2 of the target is T_p Br(R) ≠ 0). This corrects Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6, which asserts the isomorphism for every quasisyntomic ring; Z_p(1) is, locally for the quasisyntomic topology, the sheaf R ↦ T_p(R^×) = lim_n μ_{p^n}(R) in degree 0; and for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R the sequence 0 → T_p(R^×) → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 (maps log[·] and φ/p − 1) is exact.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring in (1); p-complete in the isomorphism statements of (2) and (3); quasisyntomic in (4).
Étale cohomology with Z_p-coefficients is the derived inverse limit of Z/p^k-cohomology; G_m-cohomology is étale (for (4), flat cohomology gives the same τ^{≤1}).

These statements replace BMS2 Propositions 7.16 and 7.17, whose proofs use K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow; the proofs planned here are Bhatt–Lurie's and use no K-theory, TC or trace (requirement of the BMS2 route).
In (2) the comparison is with étale cohomology of Spec R (equivalently of Spec R/p), not of the generic fibre Spec R[1/p].
proofSteps: (1) (BL Corollary 7.4.9): by sifted colimits and descent reduce to R quasiregular semiperfectoid, where with a generator e of A{−n}, φ{−n}(e) = λe with λ ∈ I^n, the complex is A → A, x ↦ x − λφ(x), whose differential has the convergent inverse x ↦ x + λφ(x) + λφ(λ)φ^2(x) + ⋯.

(2) (BL Proposition 8.1.8, Theorem 8.1.9, Corollary 8.1.10): α_R exists by the universal property of RΓ_ét(Spec −, Z_p) among étale sheaves of algebras; by derived descent modulo p (7.4.10 and Gabber's affine proper base change) reduce to animated F_p-algebras, by sifted colimits to polynomial F_p-algebras, where F_p ⊗ Δ_R ≃ dR_{R/F_p} and φ − 1 is an automorphism of Fil^1_Hodge = (Ω^{≥1}, d) since Frobenius vanishes on it; the remaining map is the Artin–Schreier isomorphism.

(3) (BL Theorem 7.1.1, Proposition 7.5.2, Theorem 7.5.6): construct c_1^syn on quasiregular semiperfectoid rings from PR.4/prismatic-logarithm (its image is φ{1}-fixed and lies in Fil^1_N) and extend by descent and Kan extension; to prove the isomorphism reduce modulo p by derived descent to animated F_p-algebras, then to quasisyntomic F_p-algebras, where it is the crystalline first Chern class isomorphism (BL Theorem 7.3.5), proved from the logarithm sequence 0 → (1 + J)^× → Fil^1_N A_crys(R) → A_crys(R) → 0 for quasiregular semiperfect R; surjectivity of φ/p − 1 there is PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective with i = 1.

(4) (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 9.6): Pic(−) is a quasisyntomic sheaf locally concentrated in degree −1 (rings without non-trivial line bundles form a basis), units are p-divisible locally, so the sheaf of complexes associated with R ↦ Pic(R)^∧[−2] is locally T_p(R^×), which is Z_p(1) by (3); the presheaf R ↦ Pic(R)^∧[−2] is itself not a sheaf of complexes, and the comparison map has cofibre (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧[−1] ∈ D^{≥2}. For perfectoid R this cofibre vanishes because Z_p(1)(R) ∈ D^{[0,1]} (PR.4/syntomic-complex). The exact sequence is BL Example 7.4.5.
acceptance: Z_p(0)(O_C) = Z_p in degree 0; Z_p(0)(F_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec F_p, Z_p) has H^1 = Z_p.
Z_p(1)(O_C) = T_p(O_C^×) = Z_p(1) in degree 0, since O_C^× is p-divisible and Pic(O_C) = 0.
Z_p(1)(Z_p) has H^1 = (Z_p^×)^∧ = 1 + pZ_p for p odd and H^0 = T_p(Z_p^×) = 0.
Z_p(−1)(R) = 0 for every R.

nodes.title: The divided Frobenius contracts deep Nygaard levels modulo p
nodes.statement: Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 and A a p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebra; fix i ≥ 0. For every integer m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), both φ_i and the canonical map preserve N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p functorially in A, and φ_i − 1 : N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p → N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p is an equivalence; more precisely φ_i maps N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p into N^{≥m+1}Δ̂_A{i}/p. Consequently Z/p(i)(A) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) → (Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p)), and, for quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebras S, Z_p(i)(S) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : Fil^i_N Δ_S → Δ_S) computed without Nygaard completion and without twists.
hypotheses: C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0; over O_C the Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised.
A is p-torsion-free and quasisyntomic over O_C; by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion the endomorphism φ_i of N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p and the equivalence extend to every quasisyntomic O_C-algebra.
m ≥ (pi + 1)/(p − 1), which is the condition p(m − i) ≥ m + 1.
proofSteps: By quasisyntomic descent assume A quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free; then all N^kΔ̂_A/p are discrete, so N^{≥k}Δ̂_A/p is discrete and ξ-torsion-free, and φ_i is induced by ξ̃^{−i}φ on Δ̂_A[1/ξ̃], ξ̃ = φ(ξ) (BMS2 proof of Lemma 7.22).
φ_i(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A) ⊂ ξ̃^{m−i}Δ̂_A for m ≥ i; modulo p, ξ̃ ≡ ξ^p, so φ_i(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A/p) ⊂ ξ^{p(m−i)}Δ̂_A/p ⊂ N^{≥p(m−i)}Δ̂_A/p because ξ^kΔ̂_A ⊂ N^{≥k}Δ̂_A.
For p(m − i) ≥ m + 1 this gives φ_i(N^{≥m}/p) ⊂ N^{≥m+1}/p: φ_i is topologically nilpotent for the complete Nygaard filtration, so φ_i − 1 is an automorphism.

The consequences follow by comparing the fibres of φ_i − 1 on N^{≥i} → Δ̂ and on the quotients by N^{≥m}; for the uncompleted form use that the divided Frobenius of the completion factors through Δ_S (PR.3/nygaard-completion (b)): the cofibres of Fil^i_N Δ_S → N^{≥i}Δ̂_S and of Δ_S → Δ̂_S agree, φ_i induces 0 between them and the canonical map the identity, so the two fibres of φ_i − 1 agree (Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 7.4.6); this holds for every quasiregular semiperfectoid ring.
acceptance: i = 0: every m ≥ 1 works when p ≥ 2, and φ maps N^{≥m}/p into N^{≥pm}/p.
A = O_C, i = 1: N^{≥m}A_inf/p = ξ^m O_C^♭ and φ_1(ξ^m x) = ξ^{p(m−1)} x^p, which lies in ξ^{m+1}O_C^♭ exactly when p(m − 1) ≥ m + 1.

nodes.title: Z/p^r(i) commutes with filtered colimits
nodes.statement: For all i ≥ 0 and r ≥ 1 the sheaf Z/p^r(i) = Z_p(i)/p^r commutes with filtered colimits in the category QSyn of quasisyntomic rings: for a filtered diagram (A_j) of quasisyntomic rings whose p-completed colimit A is quasisyntomic, colim_j Z/p^r(i)(A_j) → Z/p^r(i)(A) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Colimits of rings are p-completed colimits; the statement is about the reduction modulo p^r, not about Z_p(i) itself.
The proof planned is the direct proof of BMS2 through Lemma 7.22; the first printed proof, through K-theory and the theorem of Clausen–Mathew–Morrow, is not used (no trace input may enter PR.4).
i ≥ 0; for i < 0 both sides vanish.
proofSteps: Induct on r to reduce to r = 1, using the fibre sequences Z/p^{r−1}(i) → Z/p^r(i) → Z/p(i).
Fix C = Q_p^cycl completed; by quasisyntomic descent along A → A ⊗̂ O_C and its Čech nerve (functorial quasisyntomic covers) assume the A_j are O_C-algebras.

For p-torsion-free quasisyntomic O_C-algebras, PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction lets one compute Z/p(i)(A) modulo N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p for m large, and (N^{≥i}Δ̂_A{i}/p)/(N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p) is a finite extension of Nygaard graded pieces, which commute with filtered colimits (they are built from wedge powers of the cotangent complex, PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces).

For arbitrary quasisyntomic O_C-algebras define φ_i on N^{≥m}Δ̂_A{i}/p by left Kan extension and Nygaard completion; φ_i − 1 is still an equivalence and the same argument applies (BMS2, direct proof of Proposition 7.21). The statement for all animated rings is BL Proposition 7.4.8.
acceptance: O_C = colim of the rings of integers of finite extensions, p-completed: Z/p^r(i)(O_C) is the colimit of the complexes of the p-completed finite levels.
A filtered colimit of perfectoid rings: Z/p^r(i) of the p-completed colimit is the colimit, as used in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4.
The statement fails for Z_p(i) without reduction: Z_p(0) of a filtered colimit is p-complete, the colimit of Z_p(0) need not be.

nodes.title: p-adic Tate twists of perfectoid rings and étale cohomology of the generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let R be a perfectoid ring. For every integer n ≥ 1 there is a canonical identification Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), where the right-hand side is the derived limit over k of RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}). For n = 0 there are canonical identifications Z_p(0)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec((R/p)_perf), Z_p). The identifications are multiplicative in n, natural in R, and for n = 1 the map is the Kummer map T_p-completion of units: on a p-complete, p-torsion-free rank-one valuation ring V with algebraically closed fraction field C it is T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)). Moreover, as presheaves on perfectoid rings both sides are, p-completely arc-locally, concentrated in degree 0 and p-torsion-free, and the multiplication Z_p(1)^{⊗̂n} → Z_p(n) exhibits the target as the p-complete arc-sheafification of the source.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary perfectoid ring; for n ≥ 1 both sides vanish on rings of characteristic p.
For n ≥ 1 the comparison is with the generic fibre Spec R[1/p]; for n = 0 with Spec R, equivalently with the special fibre. The two cases are different statements.

The comparison map for n = 1 is constructed from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights), not from the cyclotomic trace; with this input the proof is purely algebraic (Bhatt–Scholze Remark 9.5).
Two slips in the printed proof are in the register as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E18: (∗_b) concerns (G_1/p)^{⊗n} → G_n/p, and 'stacks' reads 'stalks'.
proofSteps: n = 0: PR.4/etale-comparison-without-inverting-d and R lim give Z_p(0)(R) = fib(φ − 1 on A_inf(R)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p); Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change passes to R/p and then to its perfection.

Over Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebras, with q = [ε], d = [p]_q, μ = q − 1: multiplication by μ^{−n} gives α'_n : F_n(R)/p = (d^{n/p}R^♭ → R^♭, φ/d^n − 1) → G_n(R)/p = (R^♭[1/d] → R^♭[1/d], φ − 1), where G_n/p is identified by PR.4/perfectoid-artin-schreier-witt; α'_n is the colimit of maps homotopic to isomorphisms induced by φ, hence a quasi-isomorphism, and is multiplicative in n.

(∗): F_n and G_n are p-complete arc-sheaves on perfectoid rings (arc-descent, BS22 §8.2 and Bhatt–Mathew), arc-locally discrete and p-torsion-free, and F_1^{⊗̂n} → F_n, G_1^{⊗̂n} → G_n are arc-sheafifications: checked for G_n/p on products of p-complete valuation rings with algebraically closed fraction field, using that G_n(−)/p turns p-completed filtered colimits into filtered colimits (Fujiwara–Gabber) and that stalks are absolutely integrally closed valuation rings.

Construct α_1 : F_1 → G_1 from Z_p(1) = lim μ_{p^n} and Kummer theory; it is an isomorphism because, arc-locally on V as in the statement, T_p(V^×) → T_p(C^×) is an isomorphism (C^×/V^× is uniquely p-divisible) and T_p(C^×) → H^0(Spec C, Z_p(1)) is an isomorphism (H^1(Spec C, G_m) = 0). By (∗), α_1 induces a multiplicative system of isomorphisms α_n.
acceptance: R = O_C: Z_p(n)(O_C) ≃ Z_p(n) in degree 0, a free Z_p-module of rank one, for every n ≥ 0.
R perfect of characteristic p and n ≥ 1: Z_p(n)(R) = 0; for n = 0, Z_p(0)(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) = W(R)^{F=1} derived.
R = Z_p^cycl: H^1(Z_p(n)(R)) = H^1(Gal of the completed cyclotomic field, Z_p(n)), non-zero.
Finite level: Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = μ_{p^k}^{⊗n}(C), and the maps for k → k − 1 are the reduction maps.

nodes.title: Picard groups of perfectoid rings are uniquely p-divisible
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid ring R the groups Pic(R) and Pic(R[1/p]) are uniquely p-divisible. Moreover the canonical map Pic(R)^∧[−2] → Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] of p-completed Picard groupoids is an isomorphism, compatible with Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights), Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) (PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid) and the Kummer map Pic(R[1/p])^∧[−2] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)).
hypotheses: R is any perfectoid ring.
Pic(R) = (τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))[1] denotes the Picard groupoid as an object of D(Z); Pic(R) with roman type is its H^0, the Picard group.
Cohomology of G_m is computed in the flat topology (equivalently étale).
proofSteps: Pic(R) ≅ Pic(A_inf(R)) ≅ Pic(R^♭) by deformation theory along the (p, d)-adically complete ring A_inf(R), and the Picard group of a perfect ring is uniquely p-divisible (Frobenius is an automorphism inducing multiplication by p).

In the square with a : Pic(R)^∧[−2] ≃ Z_p(1)(R) (valid for perfectoid R: Z_p(1)(R) = RΓ(Spec R, G_m)^∧[−1] is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1, so (τ^{≥2}RΓ(Spec R, G_m))^∧ = 0), c : Z_p(1)(R) ≃ RΓ(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)), b the canonical map and d the Kummer map, commutativity is checked by p-complete arc-descent on R = O_C; d[1] is the p-completion of τ^{≤1}RΓ(Spec R[1/p], G_m) → RΓ(Spec R[1/p], G_m), hence injective on cohomology, so b and d are isomorphisms.
Reduce b modulo p: H^0 gives Pic(R[1/p])/p ≅ Pic(R)/p = 0, and H^{−1} with the Bockstein sequences gives a surjection Pic(R)[p] → Pic(R[1/p])[p], whose source is 0.
acceptance: R = O_C: Pic(O_C) = 0 and Pic(C) = 0.
R perfect of characteristic p: R[1/p] = 0 and Pic(R) is uniquely p-divisible because Frobenius acts as an automorphism and as multiplication by p.
Consequence used in Theorem 14.1: H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^×.

nodes.title: Z_p(n) is discrete and p-torsion-free
nodes.statement: For each n ≥ 0 the sheaf of complexes Z_p(n) on the quasisyntomic site is discrete and p-torsion-free: for every quasisyntomic ring S, H^0(Z_p(n)(−)) is a sheaf of p-torsion-free abelian groups, and every class in H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) vanishes on some quasisyntomic cover S → S' (so the quasisyntomic sheafification of H^1(Z_p(n)(−)) is 0, and H^i(Z_p(n)(−)) = 0 locally for i ≠ 0). Hence Z_p(n)(S) = RΓ(S_qsyn, H^0(Z_p(n))) is the cohomology of a sheaf of p-torsion-free groups. Two lemmas of the proof: (Lemma 14.4) for a perfectoid Z_p[ζ_{p^∞}]^∧-algebra R, R' = R⟨X_1^{1/p^∞}, …, X_r^{1/p^∞}⟩ and S = R'/(X_1, …, X_r), the map Z_p(n)(R') → Z_p(n)(S) is surjective on H^1; (Lemma 14.5) for a perfectoid ring R and a surjection S' → S of quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras such that the p-completion of L_{S'/R} → L_{S/R} is surjective on H^{−1}, the map Δ_{S'} → Δ_S is surjective.
hypotheses: The statement is local: discreteness means vanishing of H^1 after quasisyntomic sheafification; Z_p(n)(S) itself can have H^1 ≠ 0 (already Z_p(0)(F_p)).
n ≥ 0; for n < 0 the sheaf is 0.

This is Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2. Its K-theoretic consequences, Corollaries 14.2 and 14.3 of Bhatt–Scholze (evenness of K(−; Z_p) locally and for regular quotients), need K(−; Z_p) ≃ τ_{≥0}TC(−; Z_p) on henselian pairs and belong to the proposed roadmap RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs; they are not planned here.
In the printed proof 'C/Q' reads 'C/Q_p complete and algebraically closed' (register PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E30).
proofSteps: p-torsion-freeness of H^0: for S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Δ_S is a d-torsion-free δ-ring; if x ∈ H^0 has px = 0 then φ(x) = 0, so d^n x = d^n φ_n(x) = φ(x) = 0 and x = 0 (BMS2 Remark 7.20; by PR.3/nygaard-completion (b) a class of H^0 is the image of an element of Fil^n_N Δ_S, so the argument takes place in the δ-ring Δ_S). It remains to prove (∗)_S: every α ∈ H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) dies on a quasisyntomic cover, for S quasiregular semiperfectoid over O_C, where Z_p(n)(S) = fib(1 − φ_n : Fil^n_N Δ_S → Δ_S) (PR.4/divided-frobenius-contraction).

Perfectoid S = R: for n = 0 use PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid and Artin–Schreier covers; for n > 0 reduce to n = 1 by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid, where H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) is H^0 of the derived p-completion of R^× (PR.4/picard-perfectoid-uniquely-divisible), and André's lemma (PerfectoidQuotients:Q3) gives a cover R → R' with (R')^× p-divisible.

S_0 = R⟨x_i^{1/p^∞}⟩/(x_i): Lemma 14.4 reduces (∗)_{S_0} to the perfectoid ring R⟨x_i^{1/p^∞}⟩. Proof of 14.4: with A = A_inf(R), D = Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(R'){X_i^p/[p]_q}^∧ has a completed N[1/p]^r-grading with basis X^i/[⌊i⌋]_q!, Fil^n_N D is described termwise by powers of [p]_{q^{1/p}}, φ_n − 1 is surjective on the part of total integral degree ≥ n + 1 (φ_n is contracting there), φ_n divides degrees by p on the rest, and in degrees with all i_j < 1 the map A_inf(R') → D is bijective.

General S = R'/I: by André's lemma assume generators x_t of I have compatible p-power roots, map S' = (R'[x_t^{1/p^∞}]/(x_t))^∧ onto S; the map on p-completed cotangent complexes is surjective on H^{−1}, so Δ_{S'} → Δ_S and then H^1(Z_p(n)(S')) → H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) are surjective (Lemma 14.5, from the Hodge–Tate comparison PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison); filter the index set by finite subsets to reduce to S_0.
acceptance: n = 0: Z_p(0) is the constant sheaf lim Z/p^r, and H^1(Z_p(0)(F_p)) = Z_p dies on the cover F_p → algebraic closure.
n = 1: Z_p(1) = T_p G_m, and a class in H^1(Z_p(1)(R)) = (R^×)^∧ dies after adjoining p-power roots of units.
S = O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩/(X): H^1(Z_p(n)(S)) is a quotient of H^1(Z_p(n)(O_C⟨X^{1/p^∞}⟩)) by Lemma 14.4.
In characteristic p the statement is PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p.

nodes.title: Connectivity, rigidity and left Kan extension of syntomic complexes
nodes.statement: Let i ≥ 0. (1) The functor R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(i)) on animated rings commutes with sifted colimits and is left Kan extended from finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras; on quasisyntomic rings Z_p(i) is left Kan extended from finitely generated p-complete polynomial Z_p-algebras. (2) For every quasisyntomic ring R, Z_p(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i+1}(Z_p). (3) (Rigidity) For a henselian pair (R, I) with R and R/I p-complete, fib(Z_p(i)(R) → Z_p(i)(R/I)) ∈ D^{≤ i}(Z_p). (4) For a p-complete ring R, H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) ≅ coker(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_{R/p} → Ω^i_{R/p}/dΩ^{i−1}_{R/p}); it vanishes when R is w-strictly local, in particular strictly henselian local. (5) Consequently, for every scheme X the étale sheaf of complexes Z/p^n(i)_X obtained by restricting syntomic cohomology (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes) to the small étale site lies in D^{[0, i]}(X_ét, Z/p^n), and Z/p^n(i)(R) ∈ D^{≤ i} for R strictly henselian local.
hypotheses: Statements (2)–(4) are Theorems 5.1, 5.2 and Corollary 5.43 of Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, as used by Bhatt–Mathew (routed item PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-23/009).
In (3) both R and R/I are p-complete and (R, I) is henselian.

The printed proofs of (2)–(4) describe Nygaard graded pieces as gr^n THH and use THH of graded rings; no trace-theoretic object may enter PR.4, so the plan replaces each such description by its prismatic counterpart and records the remaining step as a gap.

(5) uses that the generic-fibre part of Z/p^n(i)_X is μ_{p^n}^{⊗i} in degree 0 and that stalks at characteristic-p points are computed on strictly henselian local rings by PR.4/syntomic-filtered-colimits.
proofSteps: (1): BL Proposition 7.4.8 (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes (d)); AMMN Theorem 5.1(2).

(2): the cofibre of N^{≥i+1}Δ_R{i} → N^{≥i}Δ_R{i} is N^iΔ_R{i} ∈ D^{≤ i} (BL Proposition 5.5.19, from the fibre sequence for Nygaard graded pieces of Remark 5.5.8; PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration); modulo p, can and φ_i on N^{≥i+1}Δ_R{i}/p respect the I-adic filtrations and φ_i is zero on graded pieces, so by the connectivity lemma fib(can − φ_i) ∈ D^{≤ i+1} (AMMN Lemma 5.34, Proposition 5.35), first for p-complete polynomial algebras and then by (1).

(3): continuity Z_p(i)(R) ≃ lim_s Z_p(i)(R/I^s) for noetherian F-finite I-adically complete R, Néron–Popescu and left Kan extension reduce to trivial square-zero extensions A ⊕ N of p-completed polynomial algebras, where the internal grading by the weight of N and 'Frobenius multiplies the grading by p' give pro-nilpotence (AMMN Propositions 5.36, 5.38, 5.41; Bhatt–Mathew Remark 3.8 for the gradings in prismatic terms).

(4): by (3) reduce to F_p-algebras and then to ind-smooth ones, where F_p(i)(R) ≃ fib(1 − C^{−1} : Ω^i_R → Ω^i_R/dΩ^{i−1}_R)[−i] by PR.4/log-de-rham-witt-comparison reduced modulo p and the sequence 0 → Ω^i_log → Ω^i → Ω^i/dΩ^{i−1} → 0.
(5): combine (2), (4), the fibre square of PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-schemes and Bhatt–Mathew §1.2.
acceptance: i = 0: Z/p^n(0)_X = Z/p^n in degree 0.
i = 1: Z/p^n(1)_X = fib(p^n : G_m → G_m) on X_ét, in degrees [0, 1].
R strictly henselian local: H^{i+1}(F_p(i)(R)) = 0.

nodes.title: Logarithmic forms as fixed points of the divided Frobenius on the de Rham–Witt complex
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and X a smooth k-scheme, with de Rham–Witt complex WΩ^•_X and Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X ⊂ WΩ^•_X, the subcomplex p^{i−1}VW(O_X) → p^{i−2}VWΩ^1_X → ⋯ → VWΩ^{i−1}_X → WΩ^i_X → WΩ^{i+1}_X → ⋯, on which the Frobenius φ is uniquely divisible by p^i; write φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X. Let W_rΩ^i_{X,log} ⊂ W_rΩ^i_X be the image of dlog[·] : G_m^{⊗i} → W_rΩ^i_X and WΩ^i_{X,log} = lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}, as pro-étale sheaves. Then for every i ≥ 0 the sequence of complexes of pro-étale sheaves 0 → WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] → N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X → 0, with second map φ_i − 1, is exact in each degree, and WΩ^i_{X,log} = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_{X,log}.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field of characteristic p and X is smooth over k.
Exactness is degreewise and holds for sheaves on the pro-étale site of X; surjectivity of F − 1 in degree i holds only locally.
The objects N^{≥i}WΩ and WΩ_log are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.4; this node is the statement about φ_i − 1 that the syntomic comparison needs (link CR.4 → PR.4).
In the printed proof the boundary case reads 'i = n − 1'; it is n = i − 1 (register PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E7).
proofSteps: Degrees n > i: φ_i − 1 = p^{n−i}F − 1 on WΩ^n_A, an isomorphism because p^{n−i}F is p-adically contracting and WΩ^n_A is p-adically complete.

Degrees n < i: N^{≥i}WΩ^n_A = p^{i−1−n}V WΩ^n_A and (φ_i − 1) ∘ p^{i−1−n}V = 1 − p^{i−1−n}V on WΩ^n_A (using FV = p and φ = p^n F), an isomorphism by p-adic completeness, and by V-adic completeness in the boundary case n = i − 1.

Degree n = i: φ_i − 1 = F − 1 on WΩ^i_X; the sequence of pro-sheaves 0 → {W_nΩ^i_{X,log}} → {W_nΩ^i_X} → {W_nΩ^i_X} → 0 with F − 1 is exact on X_ét [Illusie, Complexe de de Rham–Witt et cohomologie cristalline, Théorème I.5.7.2]; passing to the inverse limit gives exactness on the pro-étale site and WΩ^i_log = R lim_r W_rΩ^i_log.
acceptance: i = 0: 0 → Z_p → W(O_X) → W(O_X) → 0 with F − 1, the Artin–Schreier–Witt sequence on the pro-étale site.
i = 1, X = G_m: dlog[T] ∈ WΩ^1 is fixed by F, since F(dlog[T]) = dlog[T].
X = Spec k, i ≥ 1: N^{≥i}W(k) = p^{i−1}VW(k) = p^iW(k) and (φ_i − 1)(p^i x) = F(x) − p^i x is bijective onto W(k), so WΩ^i_{k,log} = 0 and the cokernel vanishes.

nodes.title: Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 on the Nygaard pieces of Â_crys
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, A_crys(S) the p-completed divided power envelope of W(S^♭) → S, with Frobenius φ, Nygaard filtration N^{≥i}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^i A_crys(S)}, Nygaard completion Â_crys(S) and divided Frobenius φ_i = φ/p^i : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S). (1) For every i > 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → Â_crys(S) is surjective. (2) For every i ≥ 0 the map φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}Â_crys(−) → Â_crys(−) is surjective as a map of sheaves on the site of quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras with the quasisyntomic topology.
hypotheses: S is quasiregular semiperfect: Frobenius is surjective on S and L_{S/F_p} is a flat S-module placed in degree −1.
In (1) i > 0 is necessary: for i = 0 and S = F_p the map φ − 1 on Z_p is zero.

The inputs on A_crys(S) are BMS2 Theorem 8.14 (p-torsion-freeness; φ_i mod p identifies N^iA_crys(S) with Fil_i^conj(A_crys(S)/p); the image of N^{≥i} modulo p is the divided power filtration Fil^i_pd, the Hodge filtration of derived de Rham cohomology), owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4.
proofSteps: (1): by p-completeness it suffices to prove surjectivity modulo p. On N^{≥i+1}Â_crys(S), φ_i is divisible by p, so φ_i − 1 is minus the canonical map and its image modulo p contains the image Fil^{i+1}_pd of N^{≥i+1} (Theorem 8.14(4)).
On pN^{≥i−1}Â_crys(S), φ_i − 1 agrees modulo p with φ_{i−1}, whose image modulo p is Fil^conj_{i−1}(Â_crys(S)/p) (Theorem 8.14(2)).

For j ≥ 1, Fil^conj_{j−1} + Fil^{pj}_pd = Â_crys(S)/p, since Fil^conj_{j−1} is generated by divided power monomials of total degree < pj and Fil^{pj}_pd by those of degree ≥ pj; with j = i and pi ≥ i + 1 this gives (1).

(2): for i = 0, part (1)'s argument shows the image of φ − 1 modulo p contains Fil^1_pd, and Â_crys(S) → S composed with φ − 1 is surjective on a tower of Artin–Schreier covers, which is a quasisyntomic cover; conclude by p-adic completeness.
acceptance: S perfect, i ≥ 1: A_crys(S) = W(S), N^{≥i} = p^iW(S), φ_i − 1 = (F − p^i)/p^i, surjective because F is bijective and p^iF^{−1} is contracting.
S = F_p, i = 0: φ − 1 = 0 on Z_p is not surjective, but becomes surjective on W of an algebraic closure.
S = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), i = 1: the class of the divided power γ_p(x) is hit, since it lies in Fil^p_pd.
