nodes.title: Syntomic complexes of quasiregular semiperfect rings
nodes.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra. There is a φ-equivariant isomorphism Δ_S ≅ A_crys(S) identifying the Nygaard filtration of Δ_S with N^{≥•}A_crys(S) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^• A_crys(S)}, and Z_p(i)(S) is represented by the two-term complex N^{≥i}A_crys(S) → A_crys(S), x ↦ φ(x)/p^i − x (equivalently by its Nygaard-completed version). For i > 0 the complex Z_p(i)(S) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals the p-torsion-free group A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i}. For i = 0, H^0(Z_p(0)(S)) = A_crys(S)^{φ=1} is p-torsion-free and H^1(Z_p(0)(S)) = coker(φ − 1) vanishes after sheafification on quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebras. In particular Conjecture 7.18 of BMS2 holds in characteristic p. By quasisyntomic descent, for every quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a fibre sequence RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i)) → Fil^i_N RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) with second map φ/p^i − 1, and after inverting p, RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(i))[1/p] ≃ fib(φ − p^i on RΓ_crys(X/Z_p)[1/p]).
hypotheses: S is a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra; X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme.

Δ̂_S and its Nygaard filtration are identified with Â_crys(S) through the prismatic crystalline comparison and the Nygaard theory of PR.1–PR.3 (Bhatt–Lurie Example 7.4.4; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2), not through BMS2 Theorem 8.17, which is a statement about TC^− owned by RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6.

The printed Proposition 8.20 asserts concentration in degree 0 for all i ≥ 0 and every S; for i = 0 this holds only after sheafification (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E41: Z_p(0)(F_p) has H^1 = Z_p). The statement above is the corrected one.
The exact sequence 0 → π_{2i}TC → π_{2i}TC^− → π_{2i}TP → 0 of the same passage belongs to RefinedTraceMethods:RT.6.
The filtration on crystalline cohomology is the Nygaard filtration, not the Hodge filtration; after inverting p it becomes trivial.
proofSteps: Identify (Δ_S, φ, Fil_N) with (A_crys(S), φ, N^{≥•}): Δ_S, the initial prism of S, is a crystalline prism, and the crystalline comparison identifies it φ-equivariantly with the p-completed divided power envelope A_crys(S) of W(S^♭) → S (PR.2/qrsp-char-p-acrys (2), PR.2/qrsp-prism, CR.0; Anschütz–Le Bras Lemma 3.4.2); both Nygaard filtrations are defined by divisibility of φ by powers of the generator p (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

Surjectivity of φ_i − 1 for i > 0 on the completed complex is PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective (1); p-torsion-freeness of N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) follows from that of A_crys(S) (BMS2 Theorem 8.14(1), DD.4) and the definition of the Nygaard filtration.

The map α from ker(φ_i − 1) on N^{≥i}A_crys(S) to the kernel on the completion is an isomorphism: the Frobenius of A_crys(S) factors through the Nygaard completion, which gives β : N^{≥i}Â_crys(S) → A_crys(S) with β ∘ α = φ_i and α ∘ β = φ_i; so α(x) = 0 and φ_i(x) = x give x = β(α(x)) = 0, and for y in the completed kernel x = β(y) maps to y and satisfies φ(x) = p^i x. The uncompleted kernel is A_crys(S)^{φ=p^i} by definition of the filtration.

i = 0: PR.4/acrys-divided-frobenius-surjective (2). Globalisation: quasisyntomic descent for crystalline cohomology and its Nygaard filtration (BL Theorem 4.6.1, Notation 5.3.2, Proposition 5.3.6) and PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes; Fil^i_N ⊗ Q is everything since p^i lies in Fil^i_N.
acceptance: S perfect: Z_p(i)(S) = W(S)^{F=p^i} = 0 for i > 0, and Z_p(0)(S) = fib(F − 1 on W(S)).
S = O_C/p: H^0(Z_p(i)(S)) = A_crys^{φ=p^i} contains t^i for t = log[ε], since φ(t) = pt; after inverting p these are the graded pieces of the ring of the Fargues–Fontaine curve.
S = F_p, i = 0: H^1 = Z_p ≠ 0, the counterexample to the uncorrected statement.
i = 1: A_crys(S)^{φ=p} ≅ T_p(S^×) via x ↦ log[x] (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights).

nodes.title: Syntomic complexes of smooth algebras in characteristic p are logarithmic de Rham–Witt sheaves
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, A a smooth k-algebra and X = Spec A. Let λ : qSyn_A^op → X_proét be the natural map from the (opposite of the) quasisyntomic site of A to the pro-étale site of X. Then for all i ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] of sheaves of complexes on X_proét. Reducing modulo p^r: Rλ_* Z/p^r(i) ≃ W_rΩ^i_{X,log}[−i] on X_ét.
hypotheses: k is a perfect field of characteristic p and A is smooth over k (Theorem 1.15(1) of BMS2 and Corollary 8.21).
The statement is on the pro-étale site of X because the coefficients are p-adic; WΩ^i_log is the inverse limit sheaf.

The source deduces it from the description of gr^i TC^− and gr^i TP; the plan uses instead the identification of Rλ_* of the Nygaard-filtered prismatic sheaves with the Nygaard-filtered de Rham–Witt complex, which needs no trace-theoretic input.
proofSteps: Rλ_* of S ↦ (Δ_S, Fil^•_N, φ) on qSyn_A is the étale-local Nygaard-filtered absolute prismatic complex of A, which is (WΩ^•_X, N^{≥•}WΩ^•_X, φ): crystalline comparison (PR.1/crystalline-comparison, BL Theorem 4.6.1), the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham–Witt complex (CR.4), and the match of filtrations for regular F_p-algebras (BL Proposition 5.3.8; equivalently BMS2 Theorem 8.14(3) with quasisyntomic descent, DD.4).
N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X is complete for the Nygaard filtration, so the Nygaard completion changes nothing and Rλ_* Z_p(i) ≃ fib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}WΩ^•_X → WΩ^•_X) as pro-étale sheaves of complexes.
PR.4/log-forms-divided-frobenius identifies this fibre with WΩ^i_{X,log}[−i].

Use the finite-level logarithmic kernel sequence requested from CR.4 to identify WΩ^i_log/p^r with W_rΩ^i_log. Surjectivity of restriction alone supplies only the surjection; the kernel sequence proves injectivity.
The finite-level identification is applied after étale sheafification; it is compatible with the restriction operators and the Nygaard-filtered comparison.
acceptance: i = 0: Rλ_* Z_p(0) = Z_p, the constant pro-étale sheaf lim Z/p^r.
i = 1: Rλ_* Z_p(1) = WΩ^1_log[−1], matching the classical fact that the pushforward of μ_{p^n} from the flat site is W_nΩ^1_log[−1].
A = k: Z_p(i)(k) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
A = k[T^{±1}], i = 1: dlog[T] is a non-zero section of WΩ^1_log.

nodes.title: Syntomic complexes of smooth formal schemes over O_C vanish above degree i
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C) with ξ a generator of ker θ, ξ̃ = φ(ξ), and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C. On 𝔛_ét the syntomic sheaf Z/p^n(i) = Z_p(i)/p^n is identified with hofib(φ_i − 1 : N^{≥i}AΩ_𝔛{i} → AΩ_𝔛{i})/p^n, where AΩ_𝔛 is the A_inf-cohomology sheaf with its Nygaard filtration. Then this complex is concentrated in degrees ≤ i, and the natural map τ^{≤i} hofib(τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n) → hofib(N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i})/p^n (both fibres of φ_i − 1) is an equivalence of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét. In coordinates: for 𝔛 = Spf A with a framing O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ → A (the p-completion of an étale map) and the induced deformation Ã over A_inf, AΩ_A = q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, N^{≥i}AΩ_A = ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^•_{Ã/A_inf}, φ(d_q log T_a) = ξ̃ d_q log T_a and φ_i = ξ̃^{−i}φ.
hypotheses: C is algebraically closed and complete (the hypothesis of Theorem 1.15(2); Section 10 itself uses the notation μ, ξ of Section 9 and does not restate it).
𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C; the framing exists étale-locally.

The identification of Z/p^n(i) on 𝔛_ét with the AΩ-fibre uses AΩ ≃ φ^*Δ (PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison) and the match of the Nygaard filtration with the Lη_ξ filtration (PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation); the printed text cites BMS2 Theorem 9.6 and Remark 9.11, obtained there through TC, which the plan does not use.
proofSteps: Restrict Z_p(i) to 𝔛_ét (BMS2 Remark 10.4: a quasisyntomic sheaf gives an étale sheaf on 𝔛) and identify N^{≥i}Δ̂{i} → Δ̂{i} with N^{≥i}AΩ{i} → AΩ{i}: PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison, PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration, PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation, and PR.5/absolute-relative-comparison for the perfect prism A_inf.

Reduce to n = 1 and to a framed affine; write the complex as ξ̃^{−i}φ − 1 : ξ^{max(i−•,0)} q-Ω^• → q-Ω^• on the basis d_q log T_{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ d_q log T_{a_j}, on which φ acts by ξ̃^j (PR.6/q-de-rham-comparison and AI.4 for the coordinate description).

Degree j > i: the map is ξ̃^{j−i}φ − 1 on Ã/p, an automorphism with inverse −Σ_{r≥0} ξ̃_r^{j−i}φ^r, ξ̃_r = ξ̃φ(ξ̃)⋯φ^{r−1}(ξ̃). Degree j = i: the map is φ − 1 on Ã/p, étale-locally surjective by Artin–Schreier covers, the étale sites of 𝔛, Spf Ã/p and Spec A/p being equivalent.
Hence the fibre has no cohomology above degree i and is unchanged by truncating source and target at degree i.
acceptance: i = 0: the complex is fib(φ − 1 on Ã/p^n) étale-locally, namely Z/p^n in degree 0.
𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i) = Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0 for all i.
𝔛 the formal torus of dimension 1 and i = 0: the degree-1 term contributes nothing, since ξ̃φ − 1 is invertible on Ã/p.
The basis elements d_q log T_{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ d_q log T_{a_i} of degree i are fixed by φ_i.

nodes.title: The condition (As) for Rν_* A_inf,X modulo p^n
nodes.statement: Setting: A is a p-power-torsion ring in a topos with an automorphism φ, and μ, ξ ∈ A are non-zero-divisors with μ = ξ φ^{−1}(μ); put ξ_r = ξ φ^{−1}(ξ) ⋯ φ^{1−r}(ξ), so μ = ξ_r φ^{−r}(μ). Let C ∈ D^{≥0}(A) with H^0(C) μ-torsion-free and a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism φ : C ≃ C. Condition (As): 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : C/μ^j C → C/μ^j C is a quasi-isomorphism for all i ≥ j ≥ 0. Claim: for a smooth formal scheme 𝔛 over Spf O_C with generic fibre X and ν : X_proét → 𝔛_ét, (As) holds for A = A_inf/p^n and C = Rν_* A_inf,X/p^n. More precisely 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} is an automorphism of the pro-étale sheaf A_inf,X/(p^n, μ^j) for i ≥ j ≥ 0, and 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} : A_inf,X/p^n → A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i).
hypotheses: C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity, μ = [ε] − 1, ξ = μ/φ^{−1}(μ) (the standing notation of BMS2 Section 9).
i ≥ j ≥ 0 in (As); for j = 0 the condition is empty.
In the printed remark 'g − μ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' reads 'g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g)' (register PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-19/E10); the node uses the corrected computation.
proofSteps: Reduce to n = 1 by dévissage, where A_inf,X/(p, μ^j) = Ô_X^{♭+}/μ^j.

Injectivity: if f ∈ Ô_X^{♭+} and f − ξ^i φ^{−1}(f) ∈ μ^j Ô_X^{♭+}, then g = f/μ^j satisfies g − ξ^{i−j}φ^{−1}(g) ∈ Ô_X^{♭+} because ξ^i φ^{−1}(μ)^j = ξ^{i−j}μ^j; with h = φ^{−1}(g) this says h^p − ξ^{i−j}h ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}, so h is integral over Ô_X^{♭+}, which is integrally closed in Ô_X^♭; hence g ∈ Ô_X^{♭+}.

Surjectivity on Ô_X^{♭+}: by integral closedness it reduces to surjectivity of 1 − ξ^i φ^{−1} on Ô_X^♭, i.e. to solving h^p − ξ^i h = f pro-étale locally; ξ is a unit of Ô_X^♭, so this is an Artin–Schreier-type finite étale equation, solvable pro-étale locally by the tilting equivalence (PerfectoidSpaces:P3).
Kernel on A_inf,X/p^n: μ^i is fixed by ξ^i φ^{−1} since ξ φ^{−1}(μ) = μ, and the kernel of 1 − φ^{−1} on A_inf,X/p^n[1/μ] = W_n(Ô_X^♭) is Z/p^n.
acceptance: i = j = 0: empty; i = j = 1: 1 − ξφ^{−1} is bijective on Ô_X^{♭+}/μ.
X = Spa(C, O_C): 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} is surjective on O_C^♭ with kernel F_p · μ^i modulo p.
The kernel Z/p^n · μ^i is identified with Z/p^n(i) by ε^{⊗i} ↦ μ^i for the chosen ε (over C every Tate twist is trivialised by ε); the identification is canonical only after twisting A_inf by {i}.

nodes.title: Fixed points of ξ^i φ^{−1} are unchanged under Lη_μ in degrees ≤ i
nodes.statement: In the abstract setting of PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition assume (As). Write T_ℓ=1−ξ^ℓφ^(−1). BMS2 Lemma 10.7, for i≥0 and j≥1, makes three assertions. On the quotient H^i(C)/μ^jH^i(C), the operator T_(ℓ+j) is injective at ℓ=0 and invertible at positive ℓ. On the μ^j-torsion subgroup of H^i(C), T_ℓ is onto at ℓ=0 and invertible at positive ℓ. On the quotient H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ], T_ℓ is invertible for every ℓ≥0. (Lemma 10.8) Define ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C as the composite τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C ≃ τ^{≤i}Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C → τ^{≤i}Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} C = τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C (first map φ^{−1}, second map multiplication by ξ^i). Then the canonical map ι : τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C → C commutes with 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} and induces a quasi-isomorphism τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}Lη_μ C) → τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on C).
hypotheses: A is p-power torsion, so p is nilpotent on C and 1 − p·(anything) is an automorphism of C.
(As) holds; H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free; φ : C ≃ C is a φ-semilinear quasi-isomorphism.
The décalage functor Lη and the identities H^j(Lη_μ C) ≅ H^j(C)/H^j(C)[μ] and Lη_ξ Lη_{φ^{−1}(μ)} = Lη_μ are owned by AInfCohomology:AI.1.
proofSteps: (1), (2): the fibre sequence C → C → C/μ^jC (first map μ^j) is compatible with 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1}, 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1}, 1 − ξ^{ℓ+j}φ^{−1}; so is the Bockstein sequence 0 → H^i(C)/μ^j → H^i(C/μ^j) → H^{i+1}(C)[μ^j] → 0, whose middle operator is an automorphism by (As). This gives injectivity on the left and surjectivity on the right.

For ℓ > 0 it remains to prove injectivity of 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} on H^{i+1}(C)[μ^j]; induct on j through 0 → H[μ] → H[μ^j] → H[μ^{j−1}] to j = 1, where ξ^ℓφ^{−1} is the restriction of pξ^{ℓ−1}φ^{−1} because ξ ≡ p modulo φ^{−1}(μ), and 1 − pξ^{ℓ−1}φ^{−1} is an automorphism.
(3): multiplication by μ embeds H^i(C)[μ^j]/H^i(C)[μ] into H^i(C)[μ^{j−1}] compatibly with 1 − ξ^ℓφ^{−1} and 1 − ξ^{ℓ+1}φ^{−1}; injectivity from (2) on the right, surjectivity from (2) on the left.

For Lemma 10.8, AI.1 identifies the kernel of H^j(ι) with H^j(C)[μ^j]/H^j(C)[μ] and its cokernel with H^j(C)/μ^jH^j(C), for 0<j≤i. On the kernel the induced operator is T_(i−j); on the cokernel it is T_i. Lemma 10.7 makes the kernel operator invertible for all j≤i, and makes the cokernel operator invertible for j<i and injective for j=i. In degree zero ι is an isomorphism. The long exact sequences of the two homotopy fibres now give the asserted comparison through degree i, including the boundary injectivity needed at degree i.
acceptance: j = 0 in Lemma 10.8: H^0(Lη_μ C) = H^0(C) because H^0(C) is μ-torsion-free.
i = 0: both truncated fibres are the kernel of 1 − φ^{−1} on H^0(C).
For C = Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n the lemma compares fixed points on τ^{≤i}AΩ/p^n and on Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n.

nodes.title: Syntomic complexes as truncated p-adic nearby cycles
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p and 𝔛 a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_C with generic fibre X; let ψ : X_ét → 𝔛_ét be the map of sites. Then for all i ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1 there is a natural equivalence Z/p^n(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) of sheaves of complexes on 𝔛_ét, compatible in n; on the left Z/p^n(i) is the syntomic sheaf Z_p(i)/p^n restricted to 𝔛_ét, on the right the usual Tate twist on X. Passing to the inverse limit over n gives Z_p(i) ≃ τ^{≤i} Rψ_* Z_p(i) on the pro-étale site of 𝔛. Consequently the nearby cycle sheaves R^iψ_* Z/p^n are flat over Z/p^n.
hypotheses: C is algebraically closed and complete over Q_p (BMS2 Theorem 1.15(2)); 𝔛 is smooth over Spf O_C. No properness is assumed.
The comparison is with the truncation τ^{≤i}, not with all of Rψ_*: Z/p^n(i) → Rψ_* Z/p^n(i) is an isomorphism exactly when R^jψ_* Z/p^n = 0 for j > i.
X is a rigid space, Rψ_* is the nearby-cycles functor of the formal scheme (owner ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology); no theory of nearby cycles beyond the definition is used.
The AΩ input is PrismaticCohomology:PR.6/ainf-omega-comparison; no TC enters.
proofSteps: By PR.4/syntomic-truncation-ainf, Z/p^n(i) = τ^{≤i} hofib(φ_i − 1 : τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ{i}/p^n → τ^{≤i}AΩ{i}/p^n).

φ_i identifies τ^{≤i}N^{≥i}AΩ with τ^{≤i}AΩ (the Nygaard filtration is the Lη_ξ-filtration, PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation), turning the fibre into τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on τ^{≤i}AΩ/p^n), with AΩ = Lη_μ Rν_*A_inf,X (AI.3).
By PR.4/leta-frobenius-fixed-points and PR.4/ainf-artin-schreier-condition this equals τ^{≤i} hofib(1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on Rν_*A_inf,X/p^n).

On X_proét the map 1 − ξ^iφ^{−1} on A_inf,X/p^n is surjective with kernel Z/p^n · μ^i ≅ Z/p^n(i), so the fibre is τ^{≤i}Rν_*Z/p^n(i) = τ^{≤i}Rψ_*Z/p^n(i). All identifications are compatible with reduction n → n − 1; flatness of R^iψ_*Z/p^n follows from compatibility in n (BMS2 Remark 10.3).
acceptance: 𝔛 = Spf O_C: Z/p^n(i)(O_C) ≃ Z/p^n(i)(C) in degree 0, agreeing with PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid.
𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ and i = 1: H^1 of both sides contains the Kummer class of T, which is non-zero in R^1ψ_*μ_{p^n}.
i = 0: Z/p^n ≃ τ^{≤0}Rψ_*Z/p^n = ψ_*Z/p^n.
Compatibility in n: the squares with Z/p^n(i) → Z/p^{n−1}(i) commute.

nodes.title: The étale comparison morphism for syntomic cohomology
nodes.statement: (1) For every p-complete animated commutative ring R there is a canonical map of graded commutative ring objects of D(Z), ⊕_n γ{n} : ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → ⊕_{n∈Z} RΓ_ét(Spec(R[1/p]), Z_p(n)), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in R and by γ{1} ∘ c_1^syn ≃ c_1^ét, where c_1^ét : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(1)) is the étale first Chern class. (2) γ{0} is the composite of α_R^{−1} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) with restriction to Spec R[1/p]. (3) For a perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebra R with Ext^i_{Z_p^cyc}(F_p, R) = 0 for all i and x ↦ x^p − x surjective on R/pR, the map H^0_ét(Spf R, Z_p)[log_Δ(ε)] → ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is an isomorphism of graded rings; in particular each RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is concentrated in degree 0. This applies to O_C for C algebraically closed and spherically complete of mixed characteristic. (4) For a derived p-complete animated Z[ζ_(p^∞)]-algebra R, the class ε of the compatible roots of unity lies in H^0_syn(Spf R,Z_p(1)); inverting it in the graded syntomic algebra gives the graded generic étale algebra after p-completion. In weight zero this is the p-completed colimit along multiplication by ε of the nonnegative syntomic weights. The statement for arbitrary animated R is in syntomic-cohomology-schemes, after that object is constructed.
hypotheses: R is a p-complete animated ring in (1), (2); a perfectoid algebra over Z_p^cyc, the p-completion of Z[q^{1/p^∞}]/([p]_q), in (3); an animated Z[ζ_{p^∞}]-algebra in (4).

γ{n} is in general not an isomorphism, and no range of degrees in which it is one is asserted here: the isomorphism statements are (4) after inverting ε, PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid for perfectoid rings and PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison for smooth formal schemes over O_C. Bhatt–Lurie Section 8 proves no range of degrees in which γ{n} is an isomorphism.
(4) is a reformulation of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.1 over the perfectoid base Z_p^cyc and depends on it.
In the Bhatt–Lurie text the remark after Theorem 8.1.9 cites the wrong theorem and Remark 8.5.4 misprints a target (source issues PrismaticCohomology/E43, E44).
proofSteps: Let 𝒞 be the perfectoid rings admitting a map from Z_p^cyc satisfying the two conditions of (3); 𝒞 contains products of O_{C_i} with C_i algebraically closed and spherically complete, hence is a basis for the arc_p-topology, and R ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is right Kan extended from 𝒞 [Bhatt–Mathew, Corollary 6.17]. So γ and the homotopy with c_1 need only be built on 𝒞.

(3): for perfectoid Z_p^cyc-algebras multiplication by log_Δ(ε) : Z_p(n − 1) → Z_p(n) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 2 (its cofibre is 1 − φ^{−1} on (q − 1)^{−n}A/(q − 1)^{1−n}A, where φ^{−1} is divisible by p^{n−1}), and for n = 1 under the Ext-vanishing condition (BL Lemma 8.3.2); with PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (weights ≤ 0) this gives the polynomial ring.

(1), (2): on 𝒞 both graded rings are discrete in degree 0 after truncation, and there is a unique graded ring map extending restriction in weight 0 and sending log_Δ(ε) to the Kummer class ρ(ε); it sends log_Δ(u) to ρ(u) for all u ∈ T_p(R^×), checked pointwise on Spec R[1/p] by reduction to O_C, where T_p(O_C^×) is free on ε; hence independence of choices and functoriality (BL proofs of Theorem 8.3.1 and Proposition 8.3.7).

(4): reduce to R p-complete over Z_p^cyc = A/I with (A, I) the perfected q-de Rham prism; colim_n Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → colim_n Δ_R{n} along log_Δ(q^p) is an isomorphism after p-completion (BL Proposition 8.5.3), so colim_n RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) = fib(φ − 1 on A[1/(q − 1)] ⊗̂ Δ_R) = (Δ_{R/A}[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, which is RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p) by PR.4/etale-comparison and PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients; the composite with the map from (1) is the identity, checked arc_p-locally.
acceptance: R = O_C with C algebraically closed and spherically complete: ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)] and γ sends log_Δ(ε) to the generator ρ(ε) of Z_p(1)(C); γ{n} is an isomorphism for n ≥ 0 and 0 → Z_p(n)(C) for n < 0.
R = Z_p, n = 1: γ{1} on H^1 is the inclusion of the p-completion of Z_p^× into that of Q_p^×, with cokernel Z_p; not an isomorphism.
R an F_p-algebra: the target vanishes, and (4) says that ε acts nilpotently up to p-completion: colim along ε of RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) is 0.
n = 0: γ{0} is restriction RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p).

nodes.title: Syntomic cohomology of schemes
nodes.statement: For an animated commutative ring R with p-completion R̂ and an integer n, RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) is the pullback in D̂(Z_p) of RΓ_syn(Spf R̂, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p], Z_p(n)) ← RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)), the first map being γ{n} of PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison; the projection to RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is again called the étale comparison morphism γ{n}. Properties: (a) if R is p-complete then RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) = RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (b) if p is invertible in R then γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p(n)); (c) with j : Spec R[1/p] → Spec R there is a fibre sequence RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)); (d) R ↦ RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(n)) satisfies fpqc descent, hence extends to schemes, formal schemes and algebraic stacks X by RΓ_syn(X, Z_p(n)) = lim over Spec R → X; (e) it is left Kan extended from smooth Z-algebras and commutes with filtered colimits; it does not commute with sifted colimits; (f) RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(0)) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) canonically; (g) c_1^syn : RΓ_ét(Spec R, G_m)[−1] → RΓ_syn(Spec R, Z_p(1)) exhibits the target as the p-completion of the source. For a scheme X, Z/p^k(n)_X ∈ D(X_ét, Z/p^k) denotes the restriction of RΓ_syn(−, Z_p(n))/p^k to the small étale site. (h) For every animated Z[ζ_(p^∞)]-algebra R, inverting the compatible-root class ε in ⊕_nRΓ_syn(Spec R,Z_p(n)) and p-completing gives ⊕_nRΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p],Z_p(n)), naturally as graded algebras (BL Theorem 8.5.1).
hypotheses: R is any animated commutative ring; the étale site and étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] depend only on π_0(R).
The pullback is formed in the p-complete derived ∞-category; all four corners are p-complete.
Étale cohomology of Spec R[1/p] with twisted coefficients, j_!, Gabber's affine proper base change and formal glueing for étale cohomology are imported (SF.2 and the arc-descent gap).
In the printed proof of Proposition 8.4.10 the last colimit is indexed by ℰ where ℰ' is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E45).
proofSteps: Definition and (a), (b): BL Construction 8.4.1 and Remark 8.4.2; for (a) the right vertical map of the square is an isomorphism, for (b) both lower corners vanish.

(c): formal glueing gives a pullback square for RΓ_ét(−, j_!Z_p(n)) along R → R̂ [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 6.4], and RΓ_ét(Spec R̂, j_!Z_p(n)) = 0 by Gabber's affine proper base change; so RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) is the fibre of RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p]) → RΓ_ét(Spec R̂[1/p]) (BL Remark 8.4.4).

(d): the first term of (c) satisfies arc-descent [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 5.4] and the third p-complete fpqc descent (PR.4/syntomic-cohomology-formal-schemes); (e): the third term commutes with sifted colimits, and F(R) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, j_!Z_p(n)) commutes with filtered colimits and is invariant under henselian surjections (Gabber), which gives left Kan extension from smooth Z-algebras by a cofinality argument (BL Proposition 8.4.10, Corollary 8.4.11, Warning 8.4.12).

(f), (g): arithmetic fracture squares for RΓ_ét(−, Z_p) and RΓ_ét(−, G_m)^∧ [Bhatt–Mathew, Theorem 5.13; Česnavičius–Scholze] reduce to the p-complete case (PR.4/syntomic-low-weights) and the case p invertible (BL Propositions 8.4.13, 8.4.14).

nodes.title: Syntomic cohomology is not étale cohomology of the generic fibre in all degrees
nodes.statement: The étale comparison morphism γ{n} : RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p(n)) → RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) is not an isomorphism in general, and the φ = 1 statement of PR.4/etale-comparison does not extend to the divided-Frobenius fibres Z_p(n). Instances: (1) R = Z_p, n = 1: H^1 of the source is the p-completion of Z_p^× and H^1 of the target the p-completion of Q_p^×; γ{1} is injective on H^1 with cokernel Z_p, generated by the Kummer class of p. (2) R an F_p-algebra: the target is 0 for every n, while RΓ_syn(Spf R, Z_p) = RΓ_ét(Spec R, Z_p) ≠ 0 for R ≠ 0, and for R = O_C/p the group H^0(Z_p(n)(R)) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is non-zero for all n ≥ 0. (3) For 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_C the sheaf Z/p^k(n) on 𝔛_ét is the truncation τ^{≤n}Rψ_*Z/p^k(n), so Z/p^k(n) → Rψ_*Z/p^k(n) is an isomorphism if and only if R^jψ_*Z/p^k = 0 for all j > n. (4) For a p-torsion-free F-smooth scheme X (for example regular and flat over Z) with j : X[1/p] → X, Bhatt–Mathew prove that Z/p^k(n)_X → τ^{≤n}Rj_*μ_{p^k}^{⊗n} is an isomorphism on cohomology sheaves in degrees < n and injective in degree n with image generated by symbols from O_X^×; instance (1) is the case X = Spec Z_p, n = 1. What does hold for all p-complete R is the isomorphism after inverting ε and p-completing (PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison (4)) and, for the fixed points of φ itself, PR.4/etale-comparison.
hypotheses: The warning concerns the syntomic complexes Z_p(n), built from the Nygaard filtration and the divided Frobenius; it does not concern the φ = 1 statement of Theorem 9.1, which holds for every p-adic formal scheme over a perfectoid ring.
(4) is quoted from Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8 as the general shape of the discrepancy; its proof (F-smoothness, Bloch–Kato) is outside this stage and is not a prerequisite of any node.
In (1) p is odd for the explicit description 1 + pZ_p of the completed units; the statement about the cokernel holds for all p.
proofSteps: (1): by PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (3), RΓ_syn(Spf Z_p, Z_p(1)) = RΓ_ét(Spec Z_p, G_m)^∧[−1] = (Z_p^×)^∧[−1], and RΓ_ét(Spec Q_p, Z_p(1)) has H^1 = lim Q_p^×/(Q_p^×)^{p^k} by Kummer theory; γ{1} is induced by Z_p^× ⊂ Q_p^× by the characterisation of PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison, and Q_p^×/Z_p^× = Z.
(2): R[1/p] = 0; PR.4/syntomic-low-weights (2) and PR.4/syntomic-complex-char-p give the non-vanishing; t = log[ε] ∈ A_crys(O_C/p) satisfies φ(t) = pt.
(3) is a reformulation of PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison. (4) is the statement of Bhatt–Mathew Theorem 1.8.
acceptance: The cokernel of γ{1} on H^1 for R = Z_p is Z_p, not 0.
For R = F_p: RΓ_syn(Spf F_p, Z_p) has H^0 = H^1 = Z_p while Spec F_p[1/p] is empty.
For R = O_C: γ{n} is an isomorphism for every n ≥ 0, so the discrepancy is invisible on the basis of the arc_p-topology.
A statement 'Z_p(n)(R) ≃ RΓ_ét(Spec R[1/p], Z_p(n)) for every quasisyntomic R' is false by (1).

nodes.title: Acceptance examples: O_C, the formal torus, finite levels and the maps n → n − 1
nodes.statement: Let C be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p, A_inf = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε^{1/p}] with ε a compatible system of primitive p-power roots of unity, d = [p]_q a generator of ker(A_inf → O_C) and μ = q − 1, so φ(μ) = dμ. (1) For every n ≥ 0, Z_p(n)(O_C) is concentrated in degree 0 and equals Z_p · μ^n ⊂ φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf, the kernel of φ/d^n − 1; it is identified with H^0(Spec C, Z_p(n)) = T_p(C^×)^{⊗n}. (2) At finite level Z/p^k(n)(O_C) = Z/p^k · μ^n = μ_{p^k}(C)^{⊗n}, and the maps induced by k → k − 1 are the reduction maps, compatible with those of étale cohomology; likewise in PR.4/etale-comparison the isomorphisms Z/p^k ≃ (A_inf[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1} = W_k(C^♭)^{F=1} commute with reduction. (3) For the formal torus 𝔛 = Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ with S = O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩: RΓ_ét(Spec S[1/p], Z/p^k) ≃ (Δ_{S/A_inf}[1/d]/p^k)^{φ=1}, and on 𝔛_ét, Z/p^k(0) = Z/p^k and Z/p^k(1) ≃ τ^{≤1}Rψ_*μ_{p^k}, whose H^1 contains the Kummer class of T, a non-zero section of R^1ψ_*μ_{p^k}. (4) For C spherically complete, ⊕_n RΓ_syn(Spf O_C, Z_p(n)) = Z_p[log_Δ(ε)].
hypotheses: C is complete and algebraically closed; in (4) also spherically complete.
The normalisation q = [ε^{1/p}] makes [p]_q a generator of the kernel of θ, as in the proof of Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 9.4.
These are instances of earlier nodes, collected as the acceptance tests the stage names; nothing new is proved.
proofSteps: (1): Z_p(n)(O_C) = fib(φ/d^n − 1 : φ^{−1}(d)^n A_inf → A_inf) (PR.4/syntomic-complex); μ^n lies in the kernel because φ(μ^n) = d^nμ^n; by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid the complex is RΓ(Spec C, Z_p(n)), free of rank one in degree 0, and multiplication by μ^{−n} is the comparison used in that proof.
(2): reduce (1) modulo p^k; compatibility in k is PR.4/etale-comparison-coefficients and the compatibility in n of PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison.

(3): PR.4/etale-comparison for S and PR.4/nearby-cycles-comparison for 𝔛; T has no p-th root in the strict henselisations of 𝔛 at points of the special fibre after inverting p, these local rings being normal, so its Kummer class is non-zero.
(4): PR.4/syntomic-etale-comparison (3).
acceptance: φ(μ) = dμ, hence φ(μ^n)/d^n = μ^n.
Z/p^k(n)(O_C) → Z/p^{k−1}(n)(O_C) is surjective with kernel p^{k−1}Z/p^k · μ^n.
The Kummer class of T in H^1_ét(Spec C⟨T^{±1}⟩, μ_{p^k}) has order p^k.
Z_p(n)(O_C) ≠ 0 for every n ≥ 0, whereas Z_p(n)(O_C/p) = A_crys^{φ=p^n} is much larger: reduction modulo p changes syntomic cohomology.

nodes.title: The absolute prismatic site of a p-adic formal scheme
nodes.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. The absolute prismatic site X_Δ is the opposite of the category whose objects are triples (A, I, u), with (A, I) a bounded prism and u : Spf(A/I) → X a morphism of p-adic formal schemes (A/I carries the p-adic topology), and whose morphisms (A, I, u) → (B, J, v) are the maps of prisms f : (A, I) → (B, J) with u ∘ Spf(f mod I) = v. The flat topology on X_Δ is generated by the finite families {(A, I, u) → (A_s, I_s, u_s)}_s of maps of prisms over X for which A → ∏_s A_s is (p, I)-completely faithfully flat. The structure sheaf is O_Δ(A, I, u) = A, with its δ-structure and Frobenius φ; the prism-ideal sheaf (the ideal sheaf of the Hodge–Tate divisor) is I_Δ(A, I, u) = I ⊂ A; the reduced structure sheaf is Ō_Δ(A, I, u) = A/I = O_Δ/I_Δ. For all integers m, n the presheaf (A, I, u) ↦ I^m ⊗_A A{n} is a sheaf with values in the p-complete derived ∞-category D̂(Z_p), and RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(X){n} denotes the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u). Comparison with relative sites: if X lies over Spf(A/I) for a bounded prism (A, I), the relative site (X/A)_Δ is the category of objects (B, J, v) of X_Δ together with a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) such that v lies over Spf(B/J) → Spf(A/I); the forgetful functor (X/A)_Δ → X_Δ carries covers to covers and O_Δ, I_Δ, Ō_Δ to the relative sheaves. If (A, I) is a perfect prism this functor is an equivalence (X/A)_Δ ≃ X_Δ.
hypotheses: X is a p-adic formal scheme; Bhatt–Lurie assume in addition that X is bounded (locally Spf of a p-complete ring with bounded p-power torsion) wherever the site computes cohomology.

Every prism in the site is bounded; the convention is that of Bhatt–Scholze (the site is the opposite category), while Bhatt–Lurie write (X)_Δ for the category of triples itself and put the topology on its opposite.

Register entry PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E5: for a semiperfectoid ring the category having an initial object consists of all prisms, not only bounded ones; the absolute site here always uses bounded prisms.
Complete flatness and the complete derived category are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
proofSteps: Category: triples (A, I, u) with the maps of prisms of PR.0/prism-category compatible with the structure maps; composition and identities are those of prisms (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Definition 2.3; Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 4.4.27).

Topology and sheaves: covers are tested on underlying prisms, so O_Δ and Ō_Δ are sheaves with vanishing higher Čech cohomology by PR.1/prismatic-structure-sheaf (Bhatt–Scholze, Corollary 3.12); I_Δ = I is a sheaf because I ⊗_A B = IB for a map of prisms (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal); I^m{n} is a sheaf by completely faithfully flat descent for invertible modules and the base-change compatibility of the twists A{n} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.4.28).

Relative comparison: unwind Bhatt–Lurie Definition 4.1.1 against Definition 4.4.27; for a perfect prism every ring map A/I → B/J lifts uniquely to a map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) (the lemma inside Bhatt–Scholze Remark 4.7), which gives the equivalence.
Repleteness of the topos Shv(X_Δ), so that derived limits behave well: Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Remark 2.4, with the replete topoi of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2.
acceptance: For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R the site (Spf R)_Δ has a final object, the prism (Δ_R, I) of PR.2/qrsp-prism (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Example 2.5; Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.4.29).

For X = Spf(O_K), K a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic with perfect residue field, the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E(u))) and the A_inf-prism of O_C are objects of X_Δ that cover the final object (Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Example 2.6).
For an F_p-algebra R every object (A, I, u) of (Spf R)_Δ is crystalline: I = (p).

nodes.title: Generalized Cartier divisors and the stack Cart
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring. A generalized Cartier divisor of Spec R is a pair (I, α) with I an invertible R-module and α : I → R an R-linear map. Cart(R) is the groupoid whose objects are these pairs and whose morphisms (I, α) → (I′, α′) are the R-linear isomorphisms ρ : I → I′ with α = α′ ∘ ρ. A ring map f : R → S induces the pullback functor Cart(R) → Cart(S), (I, α) ↦ (S ⊗_R I, S ⊗ α). The pair is a Cartier divisor exactly when α is injective; the Cartier divisors form a full subgroupoid with only identity automorphisms. The functor R ↦ Cart(R) is a stack for the fpqc topology, equivalent to the quotient stack [A^1/G_m]: the divisor of an element f ∈ R is (R, f·), and (R, f·) ≅ (R, g·) exactly when g = u f for a unit u.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring; for a scheme X the definition is the same with an invertible O_X-module.
Injectivity of α is not preserved by pullback: this is the reason for the generalized notion.
proofSteps: Definition and groupoid structure: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.1.1, with invertible modules as in Mathlib (Module.Invertible).
Cartier divisors as the objects with α injective, and full faithfulness of D ↦ (O(−D), ι): Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.2. Pullback: Remark 3.1.3.

Stack property and the identification with [A^1/G_m]: effective fpqc descent for modules and for module maps (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1), and Zariski-local triviality of invertible modules, which makes A^1 → Cart, f ↦ (R, f·), a G_m-torsor over Cart (quotient stacks of LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1).
acceptance: The element 0 gives the generalized Cartier divisor (R, 0) with automorphism group R^×: the point of [A^1/G_m] with stabiliser G_m.
The divisor (Z, p·) is a Cartier divisor of Spec Z whose pullback to Spec F_p is (F_p, 0), which is not a Cartier divisor.

nodes.title: Cartier–Witt divisors
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring in which p is nilpotent and let W(R) be its ring of p-typical Witt vectors, with its δ-structure whose Frobenius is the Witt vector Frobenius F. A Cartier–Witt divisor of R is a generalized Cartier divisor (I, α) of Spec W(R) such that (a) the image of I → W(R) → R (α followed by the restriction x ↦ x_0) is a nilpotent ideal of R, and (b) the image of I → W(R) → W(R) (α followed by δ) generates the unit ideal of W(R). WCart(R) is the full subgroupoid of Cart(W(R)) on these objects, and WCart(R) = ∅ when p is not nilpotent in R. In Witt coordinates x = (x_0, x_1, …) one has δ(x)_0 = x_1, and an element of W(R) with invertible x_0 is a unit when p is nilpotent in R; hence (a) and (b) together are equivalent to: every α(y)_0 is nilpotent, and the elements α(y)_1, y ∈ I, generate the unit ideal of R. A divisor is principalized when I = W(R); then α is multiplication by f = α(1), and (W(R), f·) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if f lies in WCart_0(R) = {f ∈ W(R) : f_0 nilpotent, f_1 a unit}, the set of distinguished Witt vectors (equivalently f = Σ V^n[a_n] with a_0 nilpotent and a_1 a unit). For an invertible ideal I ⊂ W(R), the inclusion (I, ι) is a Cartier–Witt divisor if and only if (W(R), I) is a prism and the images of p and I in R are nilpotent.
hypotheses: p is nilpotent in R; by convention there is no Cartier–Witt divisor otherwise.
The δ-structure on W(R) is the canonical one (natural in R, with Frobenius F); when W(R) has p-torsion it is not determined by F alone.
Condition (a) is stated for the ideal image; since I is finitely generated it is equivalent to the nilpotence of each element α(y)_0.
proofSteps: Definition: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.1.4, on the generalized Cartier divisors of the previous node and the Witt vectors of Mathlib (WittVector, with constantCoeff for restriction).

Coordinate form of (b): the identity δ(x)_0 = x_1 holds in the universal case Z[x_0, x_1, …], where W is p-torsion-free and the ghost components give w_0(F x − x^p) = p x_1; it follows for all R by naturality of δ (PR.0/delta-ring-category). The kernel V W(R) of W(R) → R lies in the Jacobson radical when p is nilpotent in R, so an ideal of W(R) is the unit ideal exactly when its image in R is.
Principalized divisors and WCart_0: Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.1 and Remark 3.2.2; the Teichmüller expansion f = Σ V^n[a_n] holds in every ring with a_n = f_n the Witt coordinates.

Relation with prisms: Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.5, using PR.0/prism and PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators (I is locally generated by a distinguished element exactly when δ(I) generates the unit ideal modulo the radical).

Prove the Zariski principalisation here, before using it to construct the Cartier–Witt stack or its quotient presentation (BL Remark 3.1.6). Reduce the invertible W(R)-module to R, choose generators Zariski-locally, and lift them to W(R); the local Nakayama criterion and the Witt completeness prove they generate.
acceptance: p ∈ W(Z/p^n) is a distinguished Witt vector: p = (p, 1 − p^{p−1}, …); it defines the de Rham point.
V(1) ∈ W(R) is a distinguished Witt vector for every R; it defines the point η of the Hodge–Tate divisor.
A Teichmüller element [a] is never distinguished over a nonzero ring (its coordinate x_1 is 0), and a unit of W(R) is never distinguished.

nodes.title: The Cartier–Witt stack WCart
nodes.statement: A ring map f : R → S induces W(f) : W(R) → W(S), and pullback along W(f) carries Cartier–Witt divisors of R to Cartier–Witt divisors of S, giving a functor f^* : WCart(R) → WCart(S), (I, α) ↦ (W(S) ⊗_{W(R)} I, W(S) ⊗ α), with coherent isomorphisms (g f)^* ≅ g^* f^*. The Cartier–Witt stack WCart is the resulting functor from commutative rings to groupoids (empty on rings in which p is not nilpotent, so WCart lives over Spf Z_p). It satisfies descent for the fpqc topology: for a faithfully flat map R → S, WCart(R) is equivalent to the groupoid of descent data in WCart(S) relative to S ⊗_R S and S ⊗_R S ⊗_R S. Restriction along W(R) → R gives a morphism of stacks μ : WCart → Cart = [A^1/G_m], (I, α) ↦ (R ⊗_{W(R)} I, R ⊗ α), which factors through [Â^1/G_m] (the formal completion of A^1 at 0): the image of μ(I, α) is a nil ideal, so μ(I, α) is never a Cartier divisor unless R = 0. WCart is not a formal scheme: its points have nontrivial automorphisms.
hypotheses: Rings are ordinary commutative rings; WCart(R) is empty unless p is nilpotent in R.

Corrected direction (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E53): the functor induced by f : R → S goes from WCart(R) to WCart(S); Bhatt–Lurie Remark 3.1.7 prints the opposite direction, and Warning 3.1.8 uses the correct one.

The fpqc descent is asserted in the source without proof (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E55); W(R) → W(S) is in general not flat for a flat map R → S, so the proof below does not use flat descent along it.
proofSteps: Pullback: W(f) is a δ-map with W(f)(x)_i = f(x_i) (Mathlib WittVector.map), so conditions (a) and (b) in coordinate form are preserved; the pseudofunctor structure is that of Cart applied to W (previous nodes).

Descent for morphisms: Zariski-locally on R two divisors are principalized (next node), and isomorphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) are the units u of W(R) with g = u f; S ↦ W(S)^× and S ↦ W(S) are representable by affine schemes, hence fpqc sheaves.

Descent for objects: write the groupoid of invertible W(R)-modules as the limit over n of the groupoids for W_n(R); the kernel of W_{n+1}(R)^× → W_n(R)^× has a finite filtration (by powers of p) whose graded pieces are quasi-coherent on flat R-algebras, so its Čech H^1 and H^2 for a faithfully flat cover vanish (Amitsur exactness, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1); induction on n starting from fpqc descent for invertible R-modules gives effectivity, and the map α descends as a morphism.
The morphism μ and its factorisation through the formal affine line: Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.1.6. Stack formalism (2-category of fpqc stacks, morphisms of stacks): LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1.
acceptance: WCart(F_p) contains the point (W(F_p), p·) = (Z_p, p·) and every point of WCart(F_p) is isomorphic to it; its automorphism group is trivial, while over F_p[ε]/(ε²) the point (W, V(1)·) has the non-trivial automorphism 1 + [ε].
The pullback of (W(Z/p²), p·) along Z/p² → F_p is (W(F_p), p·).
μ carries the point (W(R), V(1)·) to (R, 0), the generalized Cartier divisor with automorphism group R^×.

nodes.title: Presentation of WCart as the quotient [WCart_0 / W^×]
nodes.statement: Let WCart_0 be the functor R ↦ WCart_0(R) of distinguished Witt vectors; it is represented by the affine formal scheme Spf(A^0), A^0 the (p, a_0)-adic completion of Z[a_0, a_1^{±1}, a_2, a_3, …]. Let W^× be the affine group scheme R ↦ W(R)^×; it acts on WCart_0 by multiplication. The morphism WCart_0 → WCart, f ↦ (W(R), f·), exhibits WCart as the quotient stack [WCart_0 / W^×], the quotient being formed in the 2-category of stacks for the Zariski topology on Spec R. Explicitly: (i) every Cartier–Witt divisor of R is, Zariski-locally on Spec R, isomorphic to a principalized one; (ii) for f, g ∈ WCart_0(R) the isomorphisms (W(R), f·) → (W(R), g·) are the units u ∈ W(R)^× with g = u f, so WCart_0 ×_{WCart} WCart_0 ≅ WCart_0 × W^×. Since WCart is an fpqc stack, the same morphism exhibits it as the fpqc quotient, and Spf(A^0) → WCart is a surjection for the Zariski topology whose (n+1)-fold fibre power is Spf(A^0) × (W^×)^n.
hypotheses: The quotient is formed for the Zariski topology, as in the source; its agreement with the fpqc quotient uses the fpqc descent of the previous node.
W^× is a flat affine group scheme over Z that is not of finite type; WCart_0 is a formal scheme, a functor on rings in which p is nilpotent.

Carriers imported: quotient stacks and their universal property from LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1, effective descent from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1; what those stages do not state is recorded in the requests.
proofSteps: By the description of morphisms between principalized divisors (cartier-witt-divisor), the map WCart_0 → WCart is W^×-equivariant and induces a fully faithful map from the prestack quotient; it remains to show Zariski-local essential surjectivity (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.2.3 and Remark 3.2.2).

(I, α) is in the essential image if and only if I ≅ W(R). Since p is nilpotent in R the kernel of W(R) → R lies in the Jacobson radical and W(R) is complete along it, so an invertible W(R)-module I is trivial if and only if R ⊗_{W(R)} I is trivial.
R ⊗_{W(R)} I is an invertible R-module, hence trivial on a Zariski cover Spec R[1/g_i]; pulling (I, α) back to R[1/g_i] gives principalized divisors.
Representability of WCart_0 by Spf(A^0): a Witt vector is its sequence of coordinates, f_0 nilpotent and f_1 invertible (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.1).
acceptance: Over a local ring R in which p is nilpotent every Cartier–Witt divisor is principalized, and WCart(R) is the action groupoid of W(R)^× on WCart_0(R).
The fibre product WCart_0 ×_{WCart} WCart_0 is the formal scheme WCart_0 × W^×, with the two projections f and u f.
Two distinguished generators of the same divisor differ by a unique Witt unit; the corresponding points are isomorphic in the quotient groupoid, with automorphisms exactly their stabilizers.

nodes.title: Transversal prisms and coproducts of prisms
nodes.statement: For the prism charts used in Cartier–Witt geometry, import the transversal approximations, coproducts and residue-field lifts of PR.3/transversal-approximation. Their maps to Cartier–Witt divisors are compatible with the canonical cocones and with change of base. The coproduct of two chart points corresponds to the common refinement of their prism charts; this node supplies chart compatibility, rather than a second construction of transversal coproducts.
hypotheses: Prisms are those of PR.0/prism (δ-ring, invertible ideal, derived (p, I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)A).
(2) needs (A, I) transversal and (B, J) bounded; existence of coproducts without these hypotheses requires animated prisms and is not claimed.
Flat and faithfully flat maps of prisms are defined by p-complete (faithful) flatness of A/I → B/J (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1).
proofSteps: Use the δ-ring and transversal-coproduct results owned by PR.3/transversal-approximation.
Apply the functorial Cartier–Witt divisor construction to their prism maps and verify the cocone equalities on the underlying Witt modules.
For a residue-field lift, use the cofree Witt universal property of PR.0/delta-ring-category; its reduction gives the same chart point.
acceptance: The identity chart maps to the identity Cartier–Witt point.
Two transversal charts mapping to one prism give isomorphic Cartier–Witt points on their PR.3-owned common refinement.

nodes.title: The point ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart of a prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and f : A → R a ring map. f lifts uniquely to a δ-map f̃ : A → W(R). Put f̃^*(I) = W(R) ⊗_A I and let α : f̃^*(I) → W(R) be induced by the inclusion I ⊂ A. The pair (f̃^*(I), α) is a generalized Cartier divisor of W(R), and it is a Cartier–Witt divisor of R exactly when the image of I + (p) in R consists of nilpotent elements. This defines a morphism of stacks ρ_A : Spf(A) → WCart, where Spf(A) is the formal scheme of the (p, I)-adic topology, functorial in the prism: for a map of prisms h : (A, I) → (B, J) there is a canonical isomorphism ρ_B ≅ ρ_A ∘ Spf(h). Composing with μ gives the Cartier divisor I ⊂ A pulled back along f. Special cases: (i) the de Rham point ρ_dR = ρ_{Z_p} : Spf(Z_p) → WCart of the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)), which is R ↦ (W(R), p·); more generally ρ_A(f) ≅ (W(R), p·) for a crystalline prism; (ii) the universal oriented prism (A^0, I^0): A^0 = Z[a_0, a_1^{±1}, a_2, …]^∧_{(p, a_0)} with the δ-structure induced by the Witt vector Frobenius on WCart_0 = Spf(A^0) and I^0 = (a_0); it is a transversal prism, maps of prisms (A^0, I^0) → (B, J) correspond bijectively to generators of J via h ↦ h(a_0), and ρ_{A^0} is the atlas WCart_0 → WCart.
hypotheses: (A, I) is any prism; boundedness is needed only where D(Spf A) is identified with complete complexes.
The δ-lift f̃ exists because W is right adjoint to the forgetful functor from δ-rings (PR.0/delta-ring-category).
The condition for a Cartier–Witt divisor is that f is continuous for the (p, I)-adic topology on A and the discrete topology on R.
proofSteps: δ-lift: the adjunction δ-rings ⇄ rings with right adjoint W gives f̃ with f̃(a)_0 = f(a) (PR.0/delta-ring-category).

Conditions (a) and (b): the image of f̃^*(I) in R is f(I)R; and p ∈ I + φ(I)A (PR.0/prism) with δ-compatibility of f̃ shows that δ(f̃(I)) generates the unit ideal of W(R) once f(I) and f(p) are nilpotent (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.2.4).
Functoriality: for a map of prisms h, J = IB (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal) gives W(R) ⊗_B J ≅ W(R) ⊗_A I compatibly with the maps to W(R).

The prism (A^0, I^0): the Witt vector Frobenius preserves WCart_0 and lifts Frobenius modulo p, and A^0 is p-torsion-free, so it defines a δ-structure; φ(a_0) = a_0^p + p a_1, so δ(a_0) = a_1 is invertible and a_0 is distinguished; the universal property is Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.2.7, and the identification with the atlas is Example 3.2.5.
acceptance: For the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)) and R = Z/p^n the point is (W(Z/p^n), p·).
For an oriented prism (A, (d)) the point ρ_A(f) is the principalized divisor (W(R), f̃(d)·).
μ(ρ_A(f)) is the generalized Cartier divisor (R ⊗_A I → R) of Spec R.

nodes.title: Fibre products of prisms over WCart and flatness of ρ_A
nodes.statement: (1) Let (A, I) be a bounded prism and (B, J) a transversal prism, with coproduct (C, K) in the category of prisms. Then the square formed by Spf(C) → Spf(A), Spf(C) → Spf(B), ρ_A and ρ_B is a pullback square of stacks: Spf(A) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(C). (2) For every prism (B, J) the morphism ρ_B : Spf(B) → WCart is affine: for every ring R and every Cartier–Witt divisor of R, Spf(B) ×_{WCart} Spec(R) is an affine R-scheme. (3) A bounded prism (B, J) is transversal if and only if ρ_B is flat; if (B, J) is transversal and B ≠ 0 then ρ_B is faithfully flat. In particular for the universal oriented prism the (n+1)-fold fibre power of Spf(A^0) over WCart is Spf(A^n), where (A^n, I^n) is the coproduct of n+1 copies of (A^0, I^0); (A^•, I^•) is a cosimplicial transversal prism, the Čech nerve of the atlas.
hypotheses: (1): (A, I) bounded and (B, J) transversal; the roles are not symmetric in the source and the coproduct exists by transversal-prism-coproducts.
(3): (B, J) bounded.

Corrected misprints of the proof (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E56): the fibre product computed there is Spf(A^0) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(B) × W^×, and the bijection is with the invertible elements of the test prism.
proofSteps: Reduce (1) Zariski-locally to I = (d_A), J = (d_B); factor through the universal oriented prism (A^0, I^0) → (A, I), a_0 ↦ d_A; the left square Spf(C) = Spf(A) ×_{Spf(A^0)} Spf(C^0) is a pullback because (B, J) → (C^0, K^0) is flat (transversal-prism-coproducts).

For the right square use the quotient presentation: Spf(A^0) ×_{WCart} Spf(B) ≅ Spf(B) × W^× = Spf(B′) with B′ the (p, J)-completion of the free δ-B-algebra on a unit u; maps of prisms (A^0, I^0) → (B″, JB″) over (B, J) correspond to units of B″ by h ↦ h(a_0)/d_B, so (B′, JB′) is the coproduct (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.2.8).
(2): replace (B, J) by a transversal prism mapping to it, localise on Spec R so that the divisor is principalized, and apply (1) with (A^0, I^0) (Corollary 3.2.9).

(3): by the quotient presentation flatness of ρ_B is flatness of Spf(B) ×_{WCart} Spf(A^0) = Spf(C) over Spf(A^0); use (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) faithfully flat over each factor when the other is transversal and nonzero, and descent of transversality (Corollary 3.2.10).
acceptance: Spf(Z_p) ×_{WCart} Spf(A) = Spf(A{p/I}^∧) for a transversal prism (A, I): the universal crystalline prism over (A, I).
ρ_dR : Spf(Z_p) → WCart is affine and not flat (the crystalline prism is not transversal); the atlas ρ_{A^0} and the q-de Rham point are faithfully flat.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent and perfect complexes on WCart
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R let D(R) be the derived ∞-category of R-modules, a symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category, functorial in R by derived base change. D(WCart) is the limit of the categories D(R) over the category of points of WCart, whose objects are pairs (R, (I, α)) with (I, α) a Cartier–Witt divisor of R and whose morphisms are ring maps with an isomorphism of pulled-back divisors. Its objects are the quasi-coherent complexes on WCart: such an E assigns to every Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R a complex E_α ∈ D(R), compatibly with base change. Perf(WCart) ⊂ D(WCart) is the full subcategory of the E with every E_α perfect; these are the dualizable objects. The structure sheaf O_WCart is the unit object, (R, α) ↦ R. The Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf I ∈ D(WCart) is (R, (I, α)) ↦ R ⊗_{W(R)} I, an invertible object with a morphism I → O_WCart induced by α; I^m denotes its m-th tensor power for m ∈ Z. For a bounded prism (A, I) pullback along ρ_A is a symmetric monoidal exact functor ρ_A^* : D(WCart) → D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A), where D̂(A) ⊂ D(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete complexes; ρ_A^* O_WCart = A and ρ_A^* I = I. Since ρ_A is affine, ρ_A^* has a right adjoint ρ_{A*} : D̂(A) → D(WCart) satisfying base change and the projection formula. The functor D(Z) → D(WCart), M ↦ M ⊗ O_WCart, has a right adjoint RΓ(WCart, −) : D(WCart) → D(Z), the global sections functor; it takes values in D̂(Z_p).
hypotheses: The limit is a limit of ∞-categories; it is not the limit of the triangulated homotopy categories.
D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A) uses that the prism (A, I) is bounded.
WCart is a stack over Spf Z_p, so every R in the index category has p nilpotent.
In the suggested Lean section these categories and functors are a structure of carriers; Mathlib has no derived category of a stack.
proofSteps: Definition as a limit: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.3.1, an instance of the functor X ↦ D(X) on stacks of LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1, with the stable ∞-categories and limits of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:abstract and E0.
Unit and Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf: Bhatt–Lurie, Examples 3.3.3 and 3.3.4; invertibility of I is objectwise invertibility of R ⊗_{W(R)} I.

Pullback to a bounded prism and the identification D(Spf A) ≃ D̂(A): the paragraph before Proposition 3.3.5, with derived completion from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; pushforward along the affine morphism ρ_A (wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms) with base change and projection formula from LP1.

Global sections: the right adjoint exists because M ↦ M ⊗ O_WCart preserves colimits between presentable categories; its values are p-complete because p is nilpotent on every point (Bhatt–Lurie, Corollary 3.3.11).
acceptance: ρ_A^* O_WCart ≅ A and ρ_A^* I ≅ I in D̂(A) for every bounded prism (A, I).
I is not isomorphic to O_WCart: its restriction to the Hodge–Tate divisor has Sen operator 1.
For the de Rham point, ρ_dR^* E ∈ D̂(Z_p) is the de Rham specialisation E_dR of Bhatt–Lurie Notation 5.4.4.

nodes.title: Quasi-coherent complexes on WCart are prismatic crystals
nodes.statement: The pullback functors ρ_A^* induce an equivalence of symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories D(WCart) → lim_{(A, I)} D̂(A), the limit being indexed by the category of all bounded prisms with transition functors M ↦ B ⊗̂^L_A M (derived (p, J)-completed base change). The limit is unchanged if the index category is enlarged to all prisms or restricted to transversal prisms. Equivalently, with (A^•, I^•) the cosimplicial prism of coproducts of the universal oriented prism, pullback along ρ_{A^•} gives an equivalence D(WCart) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•). Passing to dualizable objects, Perf(WCart) ≃ lim_{(A, I)} Perf(A). Hence D(WCart) is the ∞-category of crystals of (p, I_Δ)-complete complexes on the absolute prismatic site ((Spf Z_p)_Δ, O_Δ), and Perf(WCart) is the category of perfect complexes on it. Consequences: (1) the Breuil–Kisin twists (A, I) ↦ A{n} define invertible objects O_WCart{n} ∈ D(WCart) with ρ_A^* O_WCart{n} = A{n}, and E{n} denotes E ⊗ O_WCart{n}; (2) under D(WCart) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•) the global sections functor is M^• ↦ Tot(M^•) ∈ D̂(Z_p).
hypotheses: The index category is that of bounded prisms; boundedness identifies D̂(A) with D(Spf A) (Bhatt–Lurie, Warning 3.3.6).
D̂(A) is the full subcategory of derived (p, I)-complete objects of D(A) (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1).
The equivalence is one of ∞-categories; the Lean section records only the joint conservativity of the functors ρ_A^*.
proofSteps: Tot description (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 3.3.10): Spf(A^0) → WCart is a Zariski surjection (wcart-quotient-presentation) whose Čech nerve is Spf(A^•) (wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms); cohomological descent for the Zariski topology gives D(WCart) ≃ Tot D(Spf A^•) ≃ Tot D̂(A^•), each A^n being transversal, hence bounded.

Reduce the limit over bounded prisms to the prisms with principal ideal by (p, I)-completely faithfully flat descent for D̂ (DD.1), using that every prism is Zariski-locally oriented (PR.0/local-distinguished-prism-generators).
The functor Δ → {oriented bounded prisms}, [n] ↦ A^n, is cofinal: every oriented prism receives a map from (A^0, I^0), and the A^n are the coproducts (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Proposition 3.3.5).

Enlarging or restricting the index category: the category of transversal prisms over a given prism is sifted (transversal-prism-coproducts; Warning 3.3.6). Perfect complexes: dualizable objects of a limit of symmetric monoidal categories are the families of dualizable objects, and a (p, I)-complete dualizable object of D̂(A) is a perfect complex; on the site side this is Bhatt–Scholze F-crystals, Proposition 2.7.
Twists: the functoriality A{n} ⊗_A B ≅ B{n} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist makes (A, I) ↦ A{n} an object of the limit (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 3.3.8); global sections: Corollary 3.3.11.
acceptance: A morphism of D(WCart) is an isomorphism as soon as its pullback to every bounded prism is; it suffices to test on one nonzero transversal prism, for example the q-de Rham prism.
The rule (A, I) ↦ Δ_{(A/I ⊗^L R)/A} with its base-change isomorphisms defines an object of D(WCart): the prismatic cohomology sheaf.
The rule (A, I) ↦ A/I is ι_* O_{WCart^HT}, and (A, I) ↦ I is the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf.

nodes.title: The group scheme G_m^♯ and the Frobenius kernel of W^×
nodes.statement: Let O(G_m) = Z[t^{±1}]. O(G_m^♯) is the subring of Q[t^{±1}] generated by t^{−1} and the divided powers (t−1)^n/n!, n ≥ 0; it is the divided power envelope of the ideal (t−1) ⊂ Z[t^{±1}]. G_m^♯ = Spec O(G_m^♯), with β : G_m^♯ → G_m induced by the inclusion; β is an isomorphism over Q and there is a unique group structure on G_m^♯ making β a homomorphism (the comultiplication t ↦ t ⊗ t preserves O(G_m^♯)). For a torsion-free ring R, β(R) is injective with image the units u such that n! divides (u−1)^n for all n; in particular G_m^♯(Z_p) = 1 + pZ_p. Let W^×[F] be the kernel of the Witt vector Frobenius F : W^× → W^×, an affine group scheme over Z. Then: (1) F : W → W and F : W^× → W^× are faithfully flat, so W^×[F] is flat over Z; (2) the map W^×[F] → G_m, u ↦ u_0, lifts uniquely to an isomorphism of group schemes W^×[F] × Spec Z_(p) ≅ G_m^♯ × Spec Z_(p). Variant: with G_a^♯ = Spec Z[x^n/n! : n ≥ 1] and W[F] = ker(F : W → W), the map W[F] → G_a lifts uniquely to an isomorphism W[F] × Spec Z_(p) ≅ G_a^♯ × Spec Z_(p).
hypotheses: The isomorphism (2) holds after localisation at p, not over Z: W^×[F] becomes G_m over Z[1/p], while G_m^♯ becomes G_m only over Q, having divided powers at every prime ℓ.
G_m^♯(R) → R^× is neither injective nor surjective for general R; G_m^♯(F_p) is trivial.
proofSteps: Divided power envelope and group structure: Bhatt–Lurie, Notation 3.4.9 and Remark 3.4.10, with the envelopes of CrystallineCohomology:CR.0; the comultiplication formula c((t−1)^n/n!) = Σ_{a+b=n} t^a (t−1)^b/b! ⊗ (t−1)^a/a!.

Faithful flatness of F on W = Spec Z[a_0, a_1, …]: the ring is torsion-free; after inverting p, ghost coordinates give a polynomial ring on which F shifts the variables; modulo p, F is a_i ↦ a_i^p (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.4.7, Corollary 3.4.8).

Let S = O(W^×[F])_(p), flat over Z_(p), with the δ-structure of the Witt Frobenius and φ(t) = 1; then t − 1 is killed by φ and has divided powers in S (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), giving ν : O(G_m^♯)_(p) → S.

ν is an isomorphism over Q (ghost components split W^× over Z[1/p]) and a homomorphism of group schemes by flatness; modulo p it carries the F_p-basis of monomials (t−1)^{e_0} α(t−1)^{e_1} ⋯ with α(x) = −x^p/p, 0 ≤ e_i < p, to the basis a^{e_0} δ(a)^{e_1} ⋯ of S/p = F_p[a, δ(a), …]/(a^p, δ(a)^p, …) (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 3.4.11). The additive variant is Variant 3.4.12.
acceptance: G_m^♯(Z_p) = 1 + pZ_p for every prime p, including p = 2.
Over a Q-algebra R, G_m^♯(R) = R^×.
In the language of δ-rings: the free δ-Z_(p)-algebra on an invertible element x with φ(x) = 1 is O(G_m^♯)_(p).

nodes.title: The Hodge–Tate divisor WCart^HT and its identification with BG_m^♯
nodes.statement: WCart^HT(R) is the full subgroupoid of WCart(R) of the Cartier–Witt divisors (I, α) for which I → W(R) → R is zero, that is, α factors through V W(R). R ↦ WCart^HT(R) is a closed substack of WCart, the Hodge–Tate divisor; it is the fibre of μ : WCart → [Â^1/G_m] over BG_m = [0/G_m], which gives μ^HT : WCart^HT → BG_m, and it is the effective Cartier divisor cut out by I → O_WCart. For a prism (A, I) the morphism ρ_A carries Spf(A/I) into WCart^HT, giving ρ_A^HT : Spf(A/I) → WCart^HT, and Spf(A/I) = Spf(A) ×_{WCart} WCart^HT. The point η : Spf(Z_p) → WCart^HT is R ↦ (W(R), V(1)·). Its automorphism group is Aut(η)(R) = {u ∈ W(R)^× : u V(1) = V(1)} = W^×[F](R), because u V(1) = V(F(u)) and V is injective. Theorem: η is faithfully flat and extends to an isomorphism of stacks Spf(Z_p) × BG_m^♯ ≅ WCart^HT, where BG_m^♯ is the classifying stack of G_m^♯ for the fpqc topology; under it μ^HT is induced by β : G_m^♯ → G_m. Consequence: for every ring R and Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R, the group Aut(I, α) is commutative and annihilated by a power of p.
hypotheses: R ranges over rings with p nilpotent; η is a point over Spf Z_p.
The classifying stack is formed for the fpqc topology; the isomorphism uses that WCart^HT is an fpqc stack (cartier-witt-stack).
η is not an isomorphism onto WCart^HT and the Hodge–Tate divisor is not a formal scheme.
proofSteps: Closed substack, fibre description and the pullback square for a prism: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.4.1, Remark 3.4.2 and the diagram after Example 3.4.3; the image of ρ_A(f) in R is f(I)R.

Aut(η): the identity V(x) y = V(x F(y)) (Mathlib verschiebung_mul_frobenius) gives u V(1) = V(F(u)); with injectivity of V this identifies Aut(η) with W^×[F], which is G_m^♯ over Spf Z_p by divided-power-multiplicative-group (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.4.4, Remark 3.4.5).

fpqc-local surjectivity of η: by the quotient presentation assume I = W(R), α(1) = V(u); u is a unit because its coordinate u_0 = α(1)_1 is; F : W^× → W^× is faithfully flat, so after a faithfully flat extension u = F(u′) and V(u) = u′ V(1) (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Theorem 3.4.13).

A faithfully flat surjection from Spf Z_p with automorphism group G_m^♯ identifies the stack with the classifying stack (torsors and classifying stacks: LanglandsParameterStacks:LP1, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1). Remark 3.4.14 identifies μ^HT.

Automorphisms (Corollary 3.4.16): filter by powers of the nilpotent ideal J = (p, image of I); the kernels of the restriction maps are R/J-modules, and modulo J the group is G_m^♯(R/J), killed by p because G_m^♯ ⊗ F_p is killed by Frobenius.
acceptance: Over an F_p-algebra p = V(1) in W(R), so the de Rham point and η agree there; over Z/p² the divisor (W, p·) is not in the Hodge–Tate divisor.

For a perfectoid ring Ā = A/I the perfect prism gives a point ρ_A^HT : Spf(Ā) → WCart^HT, a G_m^♯-torsor over Spf(Ā) whose trivialisations are the A-linear maps ξ : I → W(Ā) with V(1)·ξ = ψ|_I, ψ : A → W(Ā) the δ-lift of the quotient map (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 3.4.15).
μ^HT ∘ η : Spf(Z_p) → BG_m is the trivial torsor and Aut(η) → G_m is β.

nodes.title: Complexes on the Hodge–Tate divisor and the Sen operator
nodes.statement: D(WCart^HT) is the limit of D(R) over the points Spec R → WCart^HT; equivalently D(WCart^HT) ≃ lim_{(A, I)} D̂(A/I) over bounded prisms (D̂(A/I) the p-complete derived category), or the totalization of D̂(A^•/I^•). ι^* : D(WCart) → D(WCart^HT) is restriction and ι_* its right adjoint; O_{WCart^HT}{n} = ι^* O_WCart{n} ≅ ι^* I^n. For E ∈ D(WCart^HT) the fibre at η is E_η = η^* E ∈ D̂(Z_p). Sen operator: let R be an algebra over the dual numbers Z[ε]/(ε²). The Teichmüller element [ε] ∈ W(R) satisfies F([ε]) = [ε^p] = 0, so (1 + [ε]) V(y) = V(y) for all y, and multiplication by 1 + [ε] is an automorphism of every Cartier–Witt divisor (I, α) of R lying in WCart^HT. This is functorial and defines an automorphism γ of the projection π : WCart^HT × Spec Z[ε]/(ε²) → WCart^HT. For E ∈ D(WCart^HT), γ acts on π^* E by a map E → Z[ε]/(ε²) ⊗ E which is the identity modulo ε, hence of the form id + ε Θ_E. The endomorphism Θ_E : E → E, natural in E, is the Sen operator; it induces Θ_E on E_η. Properties: (Leibniz) Θ_{E ⊗ E′} = Θ_E ⊗ id + id ⊗ Θ_{E′}; Θ = 0 on O_{WCart^HT}; Θ is the identity on ι^* I; Θ is multiplication by n on O_{WCart^HT}{n}; on η_* O_{Spf Z_p}, whose fibre at η is the p-completed coordinate ring of G_m^♯, Θ is the differential operator t ∂/∂t.
hypotheses: p ≥ 2 is used in ε^p = 0.
Θ_E is an endomorphism in the ∞-category D(WCart^HT), natural in E; on the fibre it makes E_η an object of D(Z[Θ]).
The sign convention is that of the source: Θ = +n on O{n}; on gr_n of the conjugate filtration of Hodge–Tate cohomology Θ = −n.
proofSteps: Categories and functors: Bhatt–Lurie, Definition 3.5.1, Example 3.5.2 and Remark 3.5.3, by the same descent argument as prismatic-crystals-on-wcart applied to the prisms (A^n, I^n) modulo I^n.

The automorphism: V(x) y = V(x F(y)) and F([ε]) = [ε^p] give [ε] V(y) = V(F([ε]) y) = 0 (Mathlib verschiebung_mul_frobenius and the multiplicativity of Teichmüller representatives); functoriality in R and in (I, α) gives γ (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.5.4).

Leibniz rule and vanishing on the unit: γ acts on a tensor product diagonally (Remark 3.5.5). On ι^* I: the restriction W(R) → R carries 1 + [ε] to 1 + ε, so Θ = 1; the twists follow from O{n}|_HT ≅ I^n|_HT (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist: A{1}/I ≅ I/I²) and Leibniz (Example 3.5.6).
Regular representation: under Aut(η) ≅ G_m^♯ the automorphism γ at η is the point 1 + ε, so f((1 + ε)t) = f(t) + ε Θ(f) (Example 3.5.9).
acceptance: Θ = 0 on the unit object, Θ = 1 on the restriction of the Hodge–Tate ideal sheaf, Θ = n on O{n}.
For a quasi-coherent complex F on WCart, the Sen operator of ι^* F^* F on its fibre at η is canonically trivial (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 3.6.8).
For the p-complete diffracted Hodge complex η^* of the Hodge–Tate cohomology sheaf of R, Θ acts by −n on the n-th graded piece of the conjugate filtration.

nodes.title: Classification of complexes on WCart^HT by the Sen operator
nodes.statement: The functor D(WCart^HT) → D(Z[Θ]), E ↦ (E_η, Θ_E), is fully faithful, and its essential image consists of the objects M ∈ D(Z[Θ]) such that (a) M is p-complete and (b) the action of Θ^p − Θ on the cohomology H^*(F_p ⊗^L M) is locally nilpotent. Moreover: (1) the unit map O_{WCart^HT} → (η_* O_{Spf Z_p})^{Θ=0} is an isomorphism; (2) for every E ∈ D(WCart^HT) there is a canonical fibre sequence RΓ(WCart^HT, E) → E_η → E_η with second map Θ_E; (3) H^n(WCart^HT, O) is Z_p for n = 0, 1 and zero otherwise, and RΓ(WCart^HT, O{n}) ≅ (Z_p/n)[−1] for n ≠ 0; (4) RΓ(WCart^HT, −) : D(WCart^HT) → D̂(Z_p) commutes with colimits; (5) E ≅ O_{WCart^HT}{n} if and only if E_η ≅ Z_p and Θ_E is multiplication by n; (6) D(WCart^HT) is generated under shifts and colimits by the twists O_{WCart^HT}{n}, n ≥ 0, and D(WCart) is generated under shifts and colimits by the invertible sheaves I^n, n ∈ Z.
hypotheses: D(Z[Θ]) is the derived category of modules over the polynomial ring Z[Θ]; no completeness is imposed on the target beyond (a) and (b).
Colimits in D(WCart^HT) and D̂(Z_p) are p-completed colimits.
The statement holds for every prime p, including p = 2.
proofSteps: (1): η is faithfully flat, so it suffices to check after η^*, where it is the exactness of 0 → Z_p → Ô(G_m^♯) → Ô(G_m^♯) → 0 with second map t ∂/∂t; on series Σ c_n (t−1)^n/n! with c_n → 0 the operator is (c_n) ↦ (c_{n+1} + n c_n), surjective with kernel the constants (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.5.10).
(2)–(4): tensor (1) with E and use the projection formula for η to get E → η_* E_η → η_* E_η, then take global sections (Proposition 3.5.11, Example 3.5.12, Corollary 3.5.13).

(5), (6): twist to n = 0 and lift an isomorphism Z_p ≅ E_η through (2) (Corollary 3.5.14); filter the regular representation Ô(G_m^♯) by the subcomodules V_{≤n} spanned by (t−1)^m/m!, m ≤ n, with graded pieces O{n} because t ∂/∂t ≡ n on V_{≤n}/V_{≤n−1} (Proposition 3.5.15); for D(WCart) use the fibre sequences I^{1−n}E → I^{−n}E → ι_* ι^*(I^{−n}E) (Corollary 3.5.16).

Full faithfulness: by (6) reduce to E = O{n}, then to n = 0, which is (2). Essential image: (b) holds on the generators because n^p ≡ n mod p; conversely a nonzero M satisfying (a), (b) receives a nonzero map from some Z_p[Θ]/(Θ − n)[m], since Θ^p − Θ = ∏_{0≤n<p}(Θ − n) modulo p (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Theorem 3.5.8).
acceptance: The pair (Z_p, Θ = n) corresponds to O_{WCart^HT}{n}; the pair (Z_p, Θ = 1/2) for odd p satisfies (b) (Θ^p − Θ acts by 2^{−p} − 2^{−1} ≡ 0 mod p) and gives an invertible sheaf that is not a twist.
The pair (Z_p[Θ]^∧_p, Θ) does not satisfy (b) and is not in the image.
H^1(WCart^HT, O) = Z_p is generated by the class of the logarithm G_m^♯ → G_a.

nodes.title: The Frobenius endomorphism of WCart
nodes.statement: For a ring R, pullback along F:W(R)→W(R) sends generalized Cartier divisors to generalized Cartier divisors and preserves the Cartier–Witt conditions; these functors are natural in R and define the Frobenius morphism F : WCart → WCart. On principalized divisors it is (W(R), f·) ↦ (W(R), F(f)·); on the atlas Spf(A^0) and on its Čech nerve Spf(A^•) it is induced by the Frobenius lifts φ_{A^n}. For an F_p-algebra R, F on WCart(R) is WCart(φ_R): F lifts the absolute Frobenius of WCart × Spec F_p. For a prism (A, I) there is a canonical isomorphism ρ_A ∘ Spf(φ_A) ≅ F ∘ ρ_A. Pullback gives a symmetric monoidal functor F^* : D(WCart) → D(WCart) with F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} ⊗ O_WCart{n}, and a natural map RΓ(WCart, E) → RΓ(WCart, F^* E). F does not preserve the Hodge–Tate divisor: the square with sides WCart^HT ⊂ WCart, F, WCart^HT → Spf(Z_p) and ρ_dR commutes up to a unique isomorphism, so F contracts WCart^HT to the de Rham point; concretely F^*(I, α) ≅ (W(R), p·) for (I, α) ∈ WCart^HT(R). The closed substack F^{−1}WCart^HT meets WCart^HT in WCart^HT × Spec F_p.
hypotheses: F is an endomorphism of the stack over Spf Z_p; it is not an isomorphism and F^* is not an equivalence.
The isomorphism F^* O{n} ≅ I^{−n} O{n} is the Frobenius of the twist from PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist: φ^* A{1} ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ A{1}.
proofSteps: F is an endomorphism of the δ-ring W(R), natural in R (PR.0/delta-ring-category); in coordinates F(x)_0 = x_0^p + p x_1 and F(x)_1 ≡ x_1^p modulo (p, x_0), so the coordinate form of the Cartier–Witt conditions is preserved (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 3.6.1).
Characteristic p: F = W(φ_R) (Mathlib frobenius_eq_map_frobenius), Remark 3.6.2; compatibility with ρ_A: the δ-lift f̃ satisfies f̃ ∘ φ_A = F ∘ f̃ (Remark 3.6.3).
Twists: Remark 3.6.5, from the crystal description of O{n} (prismatic-crystals-on-wcart).

Contraction of the Hodge–Tate divisor: for α = V ∘ β with β F-semilinear, the linearisation γ : F^* I → W(R) of β is an isomorphism by condition (b), and F^* α = F V γ = p γ, so (F^* I, F^* α) ≅ (W(R), p·); uniqueness because ρ_dR has no nontrivial automorphisms, p being a nonzerodivisor in W(Z_p) (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 3.6.6). The intersection statement is Remark 3.6.14.
acceptance: F(V(1)) = p: the image of η under F is the de Rham point.
F^* O_WCart ≅ O_WCart and F^* O_WCart{1} ≅ I^{−1} ⊗ O_WCart{1}.
Over the dual numbers F(1 + [ε]) = 1: the non-trivial automorphism of η defining the Sen operator dies under F.

nodes.title: The Frobenius pullback square for global sections on WCart
nodes.statement: Let E be a quasi-coherent complex on the Cartier–Witt stack WCart. The commutative square of stacks formed by WCart^HT ⊂ WCart, F : WCart → WCart, WCart^HT → Spf(Z_p) and ρ_dR induces a pullback square in D̂(Z_p): RΓ(WCart, E) is the fibre product of RΓ(WCart, F^* E) and RΓ(Spf Z_p, ρ_dR^* E) over RΓ(WCart^HT, (F^* E)|_{WCart^HT}). Moreover (F^* E)_η ≅ ρ_dR^* E with trivial Sen operator, so RΓ(WCart^HT, (F^* E)|_{WCart^HT}) ≅ ρ_dR^* E ⊕ ρ_dR^* E[−1] and there is a fibre sequence RΓ(WCart, E) → RΓ(WCart, F^* E) → ρ_dR^* E[−1]. Consequently the functor (F^*, ρ_dR^*) : D(WCart) → D(WCart) ×_{D(WCart^HT)} D(Spf Z_p) is fully faithful; it is not an equivalence.
hypotheses: E is a quasi-coherent complex on WCart; Bhatt–Lurie Theorem 3.6.7 prints "on the Cartier–Witt stack WCart^HT", a misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E52): the square involves RΓ(WCart, E), F^* E and ρ_dR^* E.
The square is a pullback in the p-complete derived category D̂(Z_p).
No hypothesis on p.
proofSteps: Reduction to the Hodge–Tate divisor: E is the limit of the E/I^n E, so by induction it suffices to treat E = ι_* G with G ∈ D(WCart^HT) (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Theorem 3.6.7).

Transversality (Remark 3.6.20): the squares relating WCart^HT, F^{−1}WCart^HT and WCart^HT × Spec F_p are pushouts of animated rings on the Čech nerve, because I^n ⊂ A^n stays injective after base change along φ_{A^n} for the transversal prisms A^n (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 2.2.1); this identifies the square for ι_* G with one on F^{−1}WCart^HT.

The square on F^{−1}WCart^HT (Lemma 3.6.19): by colimit-preservation of global sections and generation by twists (sen-operator-classification) reduce to G = O{n}; the cases are settled by Lemmas 3.6.15–3.6.17 and Proposition 3.6.18, which says that F^* : H^1(WCart^HT, O) → H^1(F^{−1}WCart^HT, O) is the inclusion pZ_p ⊂ Z_p.

Fibre sequence: Proposition 3.6.6 gives (F^* E)_η ≅ ρ_dR^* E with trivial Sen operator and the fibre sequence of sen-operator-classification splits (Remark 3.6.8). Full faithfulness: reduce to Hom(I^n, −) by generation of D(WCart) by the I^n and twist (Corollary 3.6.9); failure of essential surjectivity is Warning 3.6.11.
acceptance: For E = O_WCart: a fibre sequence RΓ(WCart, O) → RΓ(WCart, O) → Z_p[−1] whose first map is the Frobenius.
For E the prismatic cohomology sheaf of R twisted by n: the pullback square of Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.4.14 with corner the p-completed derived de Rham complex.

nodes.title: Relative prismatic complexes of animated rings and the relative prismatic site
nodes.statement: Fix a bounded prism (A, I) with Ā = A/I. For an animated Ā-algebra R let Δ_{R/A} ∈ D̂(A) be the derived prismatic complex (the sifted-colimit-preserving extension from finitely generated polynomial Ā-algebras, where it is the limit of B over (R/A)_Δ); no p-completeness of R is required and Δ_{R/A} ≅ Δ_{R̂/A}. For a scheme, formal scheme or algebraic stack X over Ā put RΓ_Δ(X/A) = lim_{Spec R → X} Δ_{R/A} in D̂(A). (1) X ↦ RΓ_Δ(X/A) satisfies étale descent; for an Ā-algebra R with bounded p-power torsion Δ_{R/A} ≅ RΓ_Δ(Spf R̂ / A); for every animated Ā-algebra R, Δ_{R/A} ≅ Tot Δ_{(F_p^{⊗•+1} ⊗^L R)/A} and Δ_{R/A} ≅ lim_n Δ_{(Z/p^n ⊗^L R)/A}. (2) For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over Ā let RΓ^site_Δ(𝔛/A) be the limit of B over the relative prismatic site (𝔛/A)_Δ. There is a comparison map ξ_𝔛 : RΓ_Δ(𝔛/A) → RΓ^site_Δ(𝔛/A), functorial in 𝔛 and equal to the tautological identification for the formal spectra of p-completed finitely generated polynomial algebras. If every affine open Spf(R) ⊂ 𝔛 satisfies (∗): R has bounded p-power torsion and R/pR ⊗^L_R L_{R/Ā} has Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0] over R/pR, then ξ_𝔛 is an isomorphism in D̂(A). (3) If R satisfies (∗⁺): R has bounded p-power torsion and R/pR ⊗^L_R L_{R/Ā} is a flat R/pR-module placed in cohomological degree −1, then Δ_{R/A} is concentrated in degree 0, Δ̄_{R/A} is p-completely flat over R, and (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is an initial object of (R/A)_Δ. (4) If (A, I) is transversal and (B, J) is a perfect prism, then R = Ā ⊗^L B̄ satisfies (∗⁺) and (Δ_{R/A}, IΔ_{R/A}) is the coproduct (A, I) ⊔ (B, J).
hypotheses: (A, I) is a bounded prism, fixed; 𝔛 is a bounded p-adic formal scheme over A/I.

Condition (∗) holds when R̂ is p-completely smooth over Ā; it is the Tor-amplitude condition of p-quasisyntomic algebras, taken relative to Ā. It is not automatic, and ξ_𝔛 is not claimed to be an isomorphism without it.
The relative prismatic site is a large category; the limit defining RΓ^site is taken in a larger universe (Bhatt–Lurie, Warning 4.3.2).

Use the BS22 bounded relative site of PR.1. Under condition (∗), its limit agrees with the BL22 relative-site limit allowing unbounded objects: the (∗⁺) initial objects are bounded and descent reduces to these. Fibre products of Ā-schemes over Spec A and over Spec Ā coincide, so no base-of-fibre-product erratum is asserted.
proofSteps: (1): étale descent from the derived Hodge–Tate comparison and p-completely formally étale base change of Δ̄ (PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison; Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 4.1.13, Corollaries 4.1.14 and 4.1.15); derived descent along F_p^{⊗•+1}: reduce by base change (PR.1/prismatic-base-change) and the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula) to the universal oriented prism, where the unit map is refined by a faithfully flat map because F : W^× → W^× is faithfully flat (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 4.2.8, Corollary 4.2.9, Proposition 4.2.5).

(2), construction of ξ: both sides satisfy étale descent, so reduce to affines; the left side is left Kan extended from p-completed polynomial algebras, where the two agree by definition (Proposition 4.3.4).

(3) and the isomorphism in the semiperfect case: under (∗⁺) the conjugate filtration shows discreteness (Variant 4.1.19); the composite Δ_{R/A} → Δ^site_{R/A} → Δ_{R/A} is an idempotent of δ-rings (PR.2/derived-agrees-with-site), an isomorphism for quotients of Ā and for algebras generated modulo p by elements with compatible p-power roots, by reduction to Ā[Y^{1/p^∞}]/(Y − f) (Lemmas 4.3.10, 4.3.11).

(2), general case: both Δ_{−/A} and Δ^site_{−/A} satisfy p-quasisyntomic descent on rings satisfying (∗) (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent, with flat descent of the cotangent complex from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5); choose a p-quasisyntomic cover R → R⁰ in which every element has a p-th root (Lemmas 4.3.12, 4.3.13; proof of Theorem 4.3.6). (4) is Example 4.3.15, using that maps out of a perfect prism are determined on quotients.
acceptance: For 𝔛 smooth over Spf(Ā) the complex RΓ_Δ(𝔛/A) agrees with the site-theoretic definition of PR.1/relative-prismatic-cohomology.
For a transversal prism (A, I), Δ_{(Ā/p)/A} is A{p/I}^∧, the universal crystalline prism over (A, I) (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.3.16).
Affine polynomial test: for R = Ā[x_1, …, x_d], ξ is the identity of the limit over (R/A)_Δ.
