nodes.title: The prismatic cohomology sheaf on WCart and absolute prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring. For a bounded prism (A, I) with Ā = A/I, the relative prismatic complex Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ∈ D̂(A) is compatible with base change: for a map of bounded prisms (A, I) → (B, IB) there is a canonical isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ≅ Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B}. By prismatic-crystals-on-wcart this family is an object H_Δ(R) of D(WCart), the prismatic cohomology sheaf of R, with ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} for every bounded prism (B, J). R ↦ H_Δ(R) is a functor from animated rings to commutative algebra objects of D(WCart) which commutes with sifted colimits and satisfies étale descent. For integers m, n the absolute prismatic complexes are Δ_R^{[m]}{n} = RΓ(WCart, I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n}) ∈ D̂(Z_p); Δ_R{n} = Δ_R^{[0]}{n} and Δ_R = Δ_R{0} is the absolute prismatic complex of R, an E_∞-algebra over Z_p. Concretely Δ_R is the totalization of Δ_{(Ā^• ⊗^L R)/A^•} for the cosimplicial prism (A^•, I^•). For a scheme, formal scheme or algebraic stack X, RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} is the limit of Δ_R^{[m]}{n} over the category of points Spec R → X (R an ordinary ring), RΓ_Δ(X) = RΓ_Δ^{[0]}(X){0} is the absolute prismatic complex of X and H^*_Δ(X) its cohomology; RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spec R){n} = Δ_R^{[m]}{n}. For a bounded p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 that is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, (A, I) ↦ RΓ_Δ(Spf(A/I) × 𝔛 / A) on transversal prisms defines H_Δ(𝔛) ∈ D(WCart), characterised by étale descent and agreement with H_Δ(R) for 𝔛 = Spf R with R p-complete of bounded p-power torsion, and RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} ≅ RΓ(WCart, I^m ⊗ H_Δ(𝔛){n}). If 𝔛 is smooth and proper over Spf Z_p then H_Δ(𝔛) is a perfect complex on WCart.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; no completeness or boundedness is assumed (Δ_R^{[m]}{n} depends only on the p-completion of R).
The sheaf H_Δ(𝔛) of a formal scheme is defined for 𝔛 bounded, quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the complex RΓ_Δ(X) is defined for every X by the limit over points.
Corrected misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E54): the limit defining RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} is over the absolute complexes Δ_R^{[m]}{n}; Bhatt–Lurie Construction 4.4.19 prints a relative symbol.
The twists {n} are the Breuil–Kisin twists of PR.3, imported; they are not constructed here (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28).
proofSteps: Crystal data: the base-change isomorphism of derived prismatic cohomology (PR.1/prismatic-base-change for the derived complexes of PR.2/derived-prismatic-cohomology; Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.1.5) gives an object of lim D̂(A), hence of D(WCart) (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.4.1). Sifted colimits and the algebra structure are inherited from the relative complexes (Remarks 4.4.2, 4.1.8); étale descent from relative-site-comparison (1).

Absolute complexes: tensor with I^m and O_WCart{n} (quasi-coherent-complexes-on-wcart, prismatic-crystals-on-wcart) and apply global sections; the totalization formula is Corollary 3.3.11 (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.4.10, Remark 4.4.11).

Globalisation: right Kan extension along the category of points (Construction 4.4.19, with left Kan extension along a full inclusion and its dual from EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3); for a bounded qcqs formal scheme the finite limit over an affine hypercover commutes with completed base change along maps of transversal prisms, giving H_Δ(𝔛) (Variant 4.4.6, the Example after Construction 4.4.19).
Perfectness in the smooth proper case: PR.1/proper-smooth-perfectness over each prism (Remark 4.4.7).
acceptance: H_Δ(Z) = O_WCart and Δ_Z = RΓ(WCart, O_WCart); H_Δ of the zero ring is zero.
For a perfectoid ring Ā = A/I: H_Δ(Ā) = ρ_{A*} A and Δ_Ā ≅ A; in particular Δ_{F_p} ≅ Z_p.
Affine polynomial test: ρ_A^* H_Δ(Z[x_1, …, x_d]) = Δ_{Ā[x_1, …, x_d]/A}, computed by the Čech–Alexander complex of PR.1.

nodes.title: Absolute versus relative prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (B, J) be a bounded prism with B̄ = B/J and let R be an animated commutative ring. (1) By construction ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} in D̂(B), compatibly with maps of bounded prisms. If R is an animated B̄-algebra, the multiplication B̄ ⊗^L R → R induces ξ : H_Δ(R) → ρ_{B*} Δ_{R/B} in D(WCart) and, on global sections, comparison maps Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → J^m ⊗ Δ_{R/B}{n} for all integers m, n; for X over B̄ these give RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} → J^m{n} ⊗^L_B RΓ_Δ(X/B). (2) If (B, J) is a perfect prism, ξ is an isomorphism H_Δ(R) ≅ ρ_{B*} Δ_{R/B}; hence Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ J^m Δ_{R/B}{n} for all m, n, RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} ≅ J^m{n} ⊗^L_B RΓ_Δ(X/B) for X over B̄, and H_Δ(𝔛) ≅ ρ_{B*} RΓ_Δ(𝔛/B) for a bounded qcqs p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over B̄. (3) For a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring R: Δ_R is concentrated in degree 0, (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) is a prism, equal to the initial prism of R, and H_Δ(R) is the pushforward of the structure sheaf along Spf(Δ_R) → WCart. For a prism that is not perfect the maps in (1) are not isomorphisms in general: the pullback ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) is the relative complex of B̄ ⊗^L R, not of R.
hypotheses: (1) holds for every bounded prism; the isomorphisms of (2) require the prism to be perfect.
R is an animated algebra over B̄ = B/J in (2); no finiteness or completeness hypothesis.
The comparison is not an isomorphism for every bounded prism: for a bounded prism only the identity ρ_B^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{(B̄ ⊗^L R)/B} holds.
proofSteps: Fix a nonzero transversal prism (A, I) (the q-de Rham prism); ρ_A is faithfully flat (wcart-fibre-products-of-prisms), so it suffices to prove that ρ_A^*(ξ) is an isomorphism.
With (C, K) = (A, I) ⊔ (B, J) and Spf(C) = Spf(A) ×_{WCart} Spf(B), base change for ρ_{B*} identifies ρ_A^*(ξ) with the composite Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} → Δ_{(C̄ ⊗^L R)/C} → Δ_{(C̄ ⊗^L_{B̄} R)/C}.

This composite is the base change of Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L B̄)/A} → Δ_{C̄/C} = C along Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L B̄)/A} → Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}: the squares are pushouts of commutative algebras by base change (PR.1/prismatic-base-change) and the Künneth formula (PR.2/kunneth-formula).

Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L B̄)/A} ≅ C by relative-site-comparison (4) (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.3.15, Proposition 4.4.8). (2) follows by tensoring with I^m{n}, the projection formula and global sections (Proposition 4.4.12); (3) is Example 4.4.13 with PR.2/qrsp-prism.
acceptance: For a perfect field k and a k-scheme X: RΓ_Δ(X) ≅ RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)).
For O_C and a formal scheme 𝔛 over O_C: RΓ_Δ(𝔛) ≅ RΓ_Δ(𝔛/A_inf), with the prism of PR.0/ainf-prism.
For the Breuil–Kisin prism (W(k)[[u]], (E)) and R = O_K the comparison map Δ_{O_K} → Δ_{O_K/W(k)[[u]]} = W(k)[[u]] is not claimed to be an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Descent and continuity properties of absolute prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix integers m, n. (1) The functor R ↦ Δ_R^{[m]}{n} from animated commutative rings to D̂(Z_p) satisfies descent for the étale topology, and X ↦ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} satisfies étale descent. (2) Derived descent: for every animated ring R, with R^• = R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}, the map Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Tot Δ_{R^•}^{[m]}{n} is an isomorphism; each R^k is an animated F_p-algebra. (3) Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ lim_k Δ^{[m]}_{(Z/p^k) ⊗^L R}{n}. (4) Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ Δ_{R̂}^{[m]}{n} for the derived p-completion R̂ of R. (5) If X is a scheme whose structure sheaf has bounded p-power torsion and 𝔛 = Spf(Z_p) × X is its p-adic formal scheme, then RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(X){n} ≅ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n}; for a ring R with bounded p-power torsion, Δ_R^{[m]}{n} ≅ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spf R̂){n}. (6) On the category of p-quasisyntomic p-adic formal schemes the functor 𝔛 ↦ RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} satisfies descent for the p-quasisyntomic topology. The functor R ↦ Δ_R does not commute with filtered colimits as a functor to D̂(Z_p).
hypotheses: (1)–(4) hold for all animated commutative rings.

(5) requires bounded p-power torsion; (6) is stated on p-quasisyntomic formal schemes: affine opens Spf R with R p-complete, of bounded p-power torsion, and L_{R/Z_p} ⊗^L R/p of Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0].
Descent is for D̂(Z_p)-valued functors: limits are p-completed derived limits.
proofSteps: (1): étale descent of R ↦ H_Δ(R) in D(WCart) follows from that of the relative complexes (relative-site-comparison (1)); tensoring with the invertible sheaf I^m{n} and taking global sections preserves limits (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 4.4.3, Proposition 4.4.14, Remark 4.4.22).

(2): H_Δ(R) ≅ Tot H_Δ(R^•) by the relative statement over every prism (relative-site-comparison (1), which rests on faithful flatness of F on W^×), then global sections (Remark 4.4.4, Proposition 4.4.15).

(3), (4), (5): by (2) reduce to algebras over F_p ⊗^L Z, where the towers {Z/p^k ⊗^L R} and {R/p^k} are pro-constant or pro-isomorphic; combine with étale descent and the description of a formal scheme as the colimit of its reductions (Corollaries 4.4.17, 4.4.18, Proposition 4.4.25, Corollary 4.4.26).

(6): étale descent reduces to affines; for a p-quasisyntomic cover R → R⁰ with Čech nerve R^•, H_Δ(R) ≅ Tot H_Δ(R^•) by the relative quasisyntomic descent of relative-site-comparison applied over each transversal prism; tensor with I^m{n} and take global sections (Proposition 4.4.32).
acceptance: Δ_R = 0 when p is invertible in R; Δ_{Z[1/N]} ≅ Δ_Z for N prime to p.
Δ_R ≅ Tot of the derived crystalline cohomology of the animated F_p-algebras R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗k+1}.
Quasisyntomic test: for R p-quasisyntomic with a quasiregular semiperfectoid cover R → S, Δ_R is the totalization of the cosimplicial ring Δ_{S^•}.

nodes.title: Absolute prismatic cohomology as cohomology of the absolute prismatic site
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For integers m, n let RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n} be the limit of I^m{n} over the category of triples (A, I, u) of the absolute prismatic site, formed in D̂(Z_p); it is RΓ(𝔛_Δ, I_Δ^m{n}). For every object (A, I, u), restriction along u gives RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} → RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(Spf A/I){n} ≅ Δ_Ā^{[m]}{n} → I^m{n} ⊗^L_A Δ_{Ā/A} = I^m{n}, and in the limit a comparison map ξ : RΓ_Δ^{[m]}(𝔛){n} → RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n}. Theorem: if for every affine open Spf(R) ⊂ 𝔛 the ring R is p-quasisyntomic, then ξ is an isomorphism in D̂(Z_p) for all m, n. In particular RΓ_Δ(𝔛) ≅ RΓ(𝔛_Δ, O_Δ) compatibly with the E_∞-algebra structures. Supplements: 𝔛 ↦ RΓ^{site,[m]}_Δ(𝔛){n} satisfies p-quasisyntomic descent on all bounded p-adic formal schemes; for R quasiregular semiperfectoid the category of triples has the initial object (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) (a final object of the site) and both sides are I^m{n} of it.
hypotheses: 𝔛 is bounded and every affine open is the formal spectrum of a p-quasisyntomic ring; quasi-compactness is not needed.
Without the quasisyntomic hypothesis ξ is still defined, and it is not claimed to be an isomorphism: the animated theory and the underived site cohomology of a general formal scheme differ.
Smooth formal schemes over Spf Z_p, Spf W(k) or Spf O_K satisfy the hypothesis.
proofSteps: Quasiregular semiperfectoid case: by absolute-relative-comparison (3) and PR.2/qrsp-prism the site (Spf R)_Δ has the initial object (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}), so the limit is evaluation there (Bhatt–Lurie, Example 4.4.29).

The site-theoretic side is a p-quasisyntomic sheaf: for a cover 𝔛_0 → 𝔛 the totalization over the Čech nerve is the limit over the triples whose structure map factors through 𝔛_0, a covering sieve for the flat topology by the lifting of quasisyntomic covers to flat covers of prisms in PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 7.11; Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 4.4.31).
The stack-theoretic side is a p-quasisyntomic sheaf on p-quasisyntomic formal schemes by absolute-prismatic-descent (6).
Quasiregular semiperfectoid rings form a basis of the p-quasisyntomic topology (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5), so the two sheaves agree (proof of Theorem 4.4.30).
acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf(O_K): RΓ_Δ(Spf O_K) is the cohomology of the structure sheaf of (Spf O_K)_Δ, computed by the Čech nerve of the Breuil–Kisin prism.
For R = Z_p[x_1, …, x_d]^∧ the absolute prismatic complex is the limit of A over all bounded prisms (A, I) with a map R → A/I.
For 𝔛 = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid both sides are Δ_R.

nodes.title: Absolute Hodge–Tate cohomology and the diffracted Hodge complex
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring. The Hodge–Tate cohomology sheaf H_Δ̄(R) ∈ D(WCart^HT) is the object given on bounded prisms by (A, I) ↦ Δ̄_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} ∈ D̂(Ā); it equals ι^* H_Δ(R). It carries the conjugate filtration Fil_n^conj H_Δ̄(R), given by (A, I) ↦ Fil_n^conj Δ̄_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}: an exhaustive increasing filtration with Fil_0^conj = R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} and graded pieces gr_n^conj H_Δ̄(R) ≅ LΩ^n_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}{−n}[−n]. The absolute Hodge–Tate complexes are Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, H_Δ̄(R){n}) ∈ D̂(R), with Δ̄_R = Δ̄_R{0}, and Fil_m^conj Δ̄_R{n} = RΓ(WCart^HT, Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){n}), whose colimit over m is Δ̄_R{n}. For all m, n there is a fibre sequence I^{m+1} ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} → I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} → ι_*(H_Δ̄(R){m+n}) in D(WCart), and on global sections Δ_R^{[m+1]}{n} → Δ_R^{[m]}{n} → Δ̄_R{m+n}. Thus Δ_R^{[•]}{n} is a filtered object of D̂(Z_p) with gr^m = Δ̄_R{m+n}; it is filtration-complete, and R ↦ Δ_R^{[•]}{n}, as a functor to filtration-complete p-complete filtered complexes, commutes with sifted colimits, as do R ↦ Fil_m^conj Δ̄_R{n} and R ↦ Δ̄_R{n}. The p-complete diffracted Hodge complex is Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* H_Δ̄(R) ∈ D̂(R), with conjugate filtration Fil_n^conj Ω̂^DHod_R = η^* Fil_n^conj H_Δ̄(R), graded pieces LΩ̂^n_R[−n], and Sen operator Θ acting by −n on gr_n^conj; Fil_n^conj Ω̂^DHod_R lies in D^{≤n}. For every n there is a canonical isomorphism Δ̄_R{n} ≅ fib(Θ + n : Ω̂^DHod_R → Ω̂^DHod_R), and likewise for each step of the conjugate filtration. If (A, I) is a perfect prism and R an animated Ā-algebra, then Δ̄_R{n} ≅ Δ̄_{R/A}{n}.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; LΩ^n_R is the n-th derived exterior power of the cotangent complex of R over Z, and LΩ̂^n_R its p-completion (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0).
Corrected misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E58): the graded pieces of the diffracted Hodge complex are LΩ̂^n_R[−n]; the display in Bhatt–Lurie Construction 4.7.1 omits the shift.
Δ̄_R is not the reduction of Δ_R modulo an ideal; it is the first graded piece of the filtration Δ_R^{[•]}.
The Hodge-completed and derived de Rham theories are owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology and are not constructed here.
proofSteps: Sheaf and conjugate filtration: the relative conjugate filtration of PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison is compatible with base change, so it defines filtered objects of D(WCart^HT) ≃ lim D̂(A/I) (sen-operator; Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.5.1, Remarks 4.5.2–4.5.4); the graded pieces use A{1}/I ≅ I/I² (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist).

Global sections commute with the colimit over the conjugate filtration because RΓ(WCart^HT, −) preserves colimits (sen-operator-classification (4)); this also gives the sifted-colimit statements (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.5.5, Propositions 4.5.8 and 4.5.10).

Fibre sequence: tensor I → O_WCart → ι_* O_{WCart^HT} with I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R){n} and use ι^* I^m ≅ O_{WCart^HT}{m} (Remark 4.5.7); completeness of Δ_R^{[•]}{n}: the limit of I^m ⊗ H_Δ(R) vanishes because every ρ_A^* of it is I-adically complete.

Diffracted Hodge complex and the fibre formula: apply the fibre sequence of sen-operator-classification (2) to H_Δ̄(R){n}, whose Sen operator on the fibre is Θ + n (Bhatt–Lurie, Construction 4.7.1, Notation 4.7.2, Remarks 4.7.3 and 4.7.5). Perfect prism: Example 4.5.6, from absolute-relative-comparison.
acceptance: Δ̄_Z = RΓ(WCart^HT, O) = Z_p ⊕ Z_p[−1], and Δ̄_Z{n} ≅ (Z_p/n)[−1] for n ≠ 0.
For a perfectoid ring R the complex Ω̂^DHod_R is the coordinate ring of the G_m^♯-torsor of the Hodge–Tate point of R, concentrated in degree 0.
For R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian the conjugate filtration of Ω̂^DHod_R is its Postnikov filtration.

nodes.title: Absolute prismatic cohomology in characteristic p is crystalline cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme. There is a canonical isomorphism γ : RΓ_Δ(X) ≅ RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) of commutative algebra objects of D̂(Z_p), characterised up to homotopy by functoriality in X and by the commutativity of the square whose top row is RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_Δ(X) (γ^{−1} followed by the Frobenius φ), whose left side is the crystalline augmentation ε_crys : RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ(X, O_X), whose bottom row is RΓ(X, O_X) ≅ Fil_0^conj RΓ_Δ̄(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ̄(X), and whose right side is the reduction RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_Δ̄(X). Supplements: (1) for a perfect field k and a quasisyntomic k-scheme X, RΓ_Δ(X) = RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)) and the identification with RΓ_crys(X/W(k)) is Frobenius-semilinear: RΓ_crys(X/W(k)) ≅ F^* RΓ_Δ(X/W(k)) in D(W(k)); for a perfect F_p-algebra R, under Δ_R = W(R) = A_crys(R), γ^{−1} is W(φ_R^{−1}). (2) On animated F_p-algebras R ↦ Δ_R commutes with sifted colimits and agrees with RΓ_crys(−/Z_p) on polynomial algebras: Δ_R is derived crystalline cohomology. (3) For an arbitrary F_p-scheme X there is a natural map RΓ_Δ(X) → RΓ_crys(X/Z_p), which need not be an isomorphism. (4) X ↦ RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) satisfies p-quasisyntomic descent on quasisyntomic F_p-schemes, and A_crys(R) is p-torsion-free for a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra R. Here φ means the relative Frobenius over (Z_p,(p)) transported through Δ_X≃Δ_(X/Z_p); this construction uses only the relative Frobenius constructed in PR.1.
hypotheses: X is a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme: Zariski-locally the spectrum of a p-quasisyntomic F_p-algebra; no quasi-compactness or smoothness is assumed.
RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) is the crystalline cochain complex relative to (Z_p, (p)) of CrystallineCohomology:CR.2.
The isomorphism is not linear over W(k): the Frobenius twist is the φ_A-twist of PR.1/crystalline-comparison.
proofSteps: Quasiregular semiperfect R: Δ_R is a p-torsion-free ring with Δ_R^{[1]} = (p) (absolute-relative-comparison (3)); the composite Δ_R → Δ_R → Δ̄_R (φ, then reduction) has image R = Fil_0^conj (PR.3/nygaard-graded-pieces) and kernel J = {x : φ(x) ∈ pΔ_R}, which has divided powers; the universal property of A_crys(R) (CrystallineCohomology:CR.0) gives β_R : A_crys(R) → Δ_R (Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 4.6.8).
Globalise β to β_X : RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) → RΓ_Δ(X) for quasisyntomic X by quasisyntomic descent of RΓ_Δ and RΓ_Δ̄ (absolute-prismatic-descent (6); Corollary 4.6.10).

β_R is an isomorphism for R quasiregular semiperfect: modulo p, β̄_R carries γ_{pn}(x) into Fil_n^conj with leading term λ(n) γ_n(x̄), λ(n) ∈ F_p^×, by an eigenvalue computation on k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x); with the surjection Γ^*_R(I/I²) → gr^conj(A_crys(R)/p) and the Hodge–Tate comparison this shows gr(β̄_R) is an isomorphism (Lemmas 4.6.11, 4.6.13; conjugate filtration of A_crys from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.4).

General X: Zariski-locally X = Spec R; choose a polynomial algebra P ↠ R, let P⁰ be its perfection and R^• = P^• ⊗_P R, whose terms are quasiregular semiperfect; both sides descend along R → R^• (crystalline descent to semiperfect rings from DD.4; absolute-prismatic-descent (6)) (proof of Theorem 4.6.1). The supplements are Warning 4.6.2, Example 4.6.9, Remarks 4.6.5 and 4.6.6, Corollaries 4.6.7 and 4.6.15.
acceptance: For a smooth F_p-scheme the isomorphism is the case A = Z_p of PR.1/crystalline-comparison.
For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R), the p-completed divided power envelope of (x) in W(F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]).
For R perfect, Δ_R = W(R) and the comparison is the inverse Witt vector Frobenius.

nodes.title: The absolute de Rham comparison and the de Rham point
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring, R̄ = F_p ⊗^L R, and let dR̂_R be the p-complete derived de Rham complex of R (over Z) with its Hodge filtration. (1) There is a canonical isomorphism α_R : ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) ≅ dR̂_R in D̂(Z_p), functorial in R and characterised by the requirement that α_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} is the isomorphism (F^* H_Δ(R))|_{WCart^HT} ≅ dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT} obtained from the relative de Rham comparison Ā ⊗^L_A F^* Δ_{R′/A} ≅ dR̂_{R′/Ā} over all bounded prisms and from F ∘ ι ≅ ρ_dR ∘ (WCart^HT → Spf Z_p). (2) Consequently Δ_{R̄} ≅ dR̂_R as commutative algebra objects of D̂(Z_p), functorially in R. (3) The de Rham comparison map γ^dR{n} : Δ_R{n} → dR̂_R is the restriction to the de Rham point composed with α_R, using the trivialisation of ρ_dR^* O_WCart{n} by the generator e^n of Z_p{n}; the prismatic augmentation ε_Δ : Δ_R → R̂ is γ^dR followed by dR̂_R → gr^0_Hodge = R̂. (4) For every n the square with corners Δ_R{n}, dR̂_R, RΓ(WCart, F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) and dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O) is a pullback square, and there is a fibre sequence Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → dR̂_R[−1]. (5) For a p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 flat over Spf Z_p with regular Noetherian special fibre X, RΓ_crys(X/Z_p) ≅ RΓ_dR(𝔛) (Berthelot).
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; dR̂_R is the p-completed derived de Rham complex, not Hodge-completed, owned by DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2.
Corrected misprint (new source issue to be registered): in Bhatt–Lurie Corollary 5.4.14 the source of γ^dR{n} is Δ_R{n}.
(5) needs flatness over Z_p and a regular Noetherian special fibre, for example 𝔛 smooth over Spf W(k).
proofSteps: ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) = Δ_{R̄/Z_p} by construction, and Δ_{R̄/Z_p} ≅ Δ_{R̄} because (Z_p, (p)) is perfect (absolute-relative-comparison; Bhatt–Lurie, Example 5.4.5).

The isomorphism on the Hodge–Tate divisor: F^* H_Δ(R) pulls back to F^* Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A}, whose reduction modulo I is the derived de Rham complex by PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general in its animated form (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 5.2.5), compatibly in the prism; combine with wcart-frobenius (Construction 5.4.7, Remark 5.4.6).

Descent of the isomorphism to the de Rham point: the composite ρ_dR^* H_Δ(R) → dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O) = dR̂_R ⊕ dR̂_R[−1] has second component functorially null: the source is left Kan extended from p-torsion-free p-quasisyntomic rings, the target is right Kan extended from quasiregular semiperfectoid rings (quasisyntomic descent of dR̂ from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5), and for such rings both are concentrated in degree 0 (Proposition 5.4.8).

(4): apply frobenius-pullback-square to E = H_Δ(R){n} and insert (1) (Corollary 5.4.14, Remark 5.4.15). (5): combine (2) with absolute-crystalline-comparison and the comparison of derived and classical de Rham complexes of DD.2 (the Remark after Theorem 5.4.2).

nodes.title: The absolute Nygaard filtration
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring and n an integer. (a) For a bounded prism (A, I) the relative Nygaard filtration Fil^m_N F^* Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} is compatible with completed base change in the prism, so it defines a decreasing filtered object Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) of D(WCart) with Fil^0_N = F^* H_Δ(R). (b) There is a fibre sequence of filtered objects I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N F^* H_Δ(R) → Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) → ι_*(Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}). (c) Put Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n}) = Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) ⊗ F^* O_WCart{n}; since F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} O_WCart{n} is canonically trivial on WCart^HT, (b) gives a map RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O). (d) The absolute Nygaard filtration Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is the fibre product, in the filtered derived category of p-complete complexes, of RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) and Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R over Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗̂ RΓ(WCart^HT, O). Then Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} = Δ_R{n}, Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} is an isomorphism for m ≤ 0, and the projection Fil^•(γ^dR{n}) : Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R is the filtered de Rham specialisation. (e) There is a fibre sequence of filtered complexes Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, Fil^•_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_R[−1]. (f) ⊕_n Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is a graded commutative algebra in filtered complexes; Fil^•_N Δ_R is a filtered E_∞-algebra and each Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} a module over it. (g) Graded pieces: gr^m_N Δ_R{n} = cofib(Fil^{m+1}_N → Fil^m_N) sits in a fibre sequence gr^m_N Δ_R{n} → Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod_R → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R whose second map is Θ + m; there is a unique class e^n ∈ H^0(gr^0_N Δ_R{n}) with image 1 in H^0(gr^0_Hodge dR̂_R), and multiplication by e^n is an isomorphism gr^m_N Δ_R ≅ gr^m_N Δ_R{n}. (h) For a scheme, formal scheme or stack X, Fil^m_N RΓ_Δ(X){n} is the limit of Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} over the points Spec R → X. (i) The Nygaard-completed complexes are Fil^m_N Δ̂_R{n} = lim_k Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}/Fil^{m+k}_N Δ_R{n}, with Δ̂_R{n} = Fil^0_N Δ̂_R{n}; Δ_R{n} is Nygaard-complete when lim_m Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} = 0.
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring; the filtration is decreasing, indexed by all integers and constant in degrees ≤ 0.

The relative Nygaard filtration and its base-change compatibility are imported from PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; the Breuil–Kisin twists from PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/28).
The Hodge filtration is that of the p-complete derived de Rham complex of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.2; no Hodge completion is used in (a)–(h).
Corrected misprint (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E54): in (h) the limit is over the absolute complexes Fil^m_N Δ_R{n}.
Syntomic complexes built from this filtration are owned by PR.4 and are not defined here.
proofSteps: (a): the base-change isomorphism B ⊗̂^L_A Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} ≅ Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{(B ⊗^L_A R′)/B} of the relative filtration (Bhatt–Lurie, Remark 5.1.10) and prismatic-crystals-on-wcart give the filtered sheaf (Notation 5.5.1).

(b): globalise the fibre sequence I ⊗ Fil^{•−1}_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} → Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} → Fil^•_Hodge dR̂_{R′/Ā} (Bhatt–Lurie, Corollary 5.2.8, part of PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration with PR.3/de-rham-comparison-general) over all bounded prisms; in filtration degree 0 it is the isomorphism of absolute-de-rham-comparison (Remark 5.5.2).
(c), (d), (e): twist using wcart-frobenius, take global sections, and form the pullback; in degree 0 the pullback is Δ_R{n} by absolute-de-rham-comparison (4) (Construction 5.5.3, Remark 5.5.6).

(f), (g): multiplicativity of the relative filtration (Remark 5.5.7); graded pieces from gr^m_N F^* H_Δ(R) ≅ ι_* Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){m} and the fibre sequence of sen-operator-classification, where the Sen operator of the twist by {m} is Θ + m (Remark 5.5.8, Corollary 5.5.14, Remark 5.5.15).
(h), (i): Notation 5.5.23 and Definition 5.8.5; for quasiregular semiperfectoid and quasisyntomic rings the completion agrees with PR.3/nygaard-completion by absolute-nygaard-perfect-prism.
acceptance: Fil^0_N Δ_R{n} = Δ_R{n} and Δ_R/Fil^1_N Δ_R ≅ R̂ through the prismatic augmentation.
For R = F_p: Fil^m_N Δ_{F_p} = p^m Z_p and gr^m_N Δ_{F_p} = F_p in degree 0.
For R = Z: gr^1_N Δ_Z = 0, so the Nygaard filtration is not the p-adic filtration.

nodes.title: Graded pieces, de Rham specialisation, descent and completeness of the absolute Nygaard filtration
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring and m, n integers. (1) For every m ≥ 0 the map Δ_R{n}/Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → dR̂_R/Fil^m_Hodge dR̂_R induced by the filtered de Rham specialisation is an isogeny: its fibre is annihilated by a power of p. For 0 ≤ m < p it is an isomorphism. In particular gr^m_N Δ_R ≅ LΩ̂^m_R[−m] for m < p, and Fil^1_N Δ_R → Δ_R → R̂ is a fibre sequence, the second map being the prismatic augmentation. (2) gr^m_N Δ_R{n} has cohomology in degrees ≤ m: the filtered complex Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} is connective for the Beilinson t-structure. (3) R ↦ gr^m_N Δ_R{n} commutes with sifted colimits and satisfies descent for the p-completely faithfully flat topology. R ↦ Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} satisfies étale descent on animated rings, p-quasisyntomic descent on p-quasisyntomic rings, derived descent Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} ≅ Tot Fil^m_N Δ_{R ⊗^L F_p^{⊗•+1}}{n}, and Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} ≅ lim_k Fil^m_N Δ_{(Z/p^k) ⊗^L R}{n} ≅ Fil^m_N Δ_{R̂}{n}; it does not commute with sifted colimits (already for m = 0). (4) If R is a p-torsion-free ring with R/pR regular Noetherian, then Δ_R{n} is Nygaard-complete for every n. For R = k[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x), k a perfect field of characteristic p, Δ_R is not Nygaard-complete.
hypotheses: (1)–(3) hold for every animated commutative ring; (4) requires R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian.
The isomorphism range in (1) is m < p; for m ≥ p only an isogeny is claimed.
The Beilinson t-structure on filtered complexes and filtration-completeness are those of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1.
proofSteps: (1): the fibre of gr^m of the de Rham specialisation is (Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R)^{Θ=−m}; on gr_i^conj, i < m, the operator Θ + m is multiplication by m − i, nonzero, and a unit of Z_p when m < p; induct on m (Bhatt–Lurie, Proposition 5.5.12, Example 5.5.13, the Corollary after Warning 5.5.17).
(2): the fibre sequence for gr^m_N of absolute-nygaard-filtration (g) and Fil_i^conj Ω̂^DHod_R ∈ D^{≤i} (Proposition 5.5.19).

(3): the same fibre sequence reduces to flat descent and sifted-colimit preservation of Fil_d^conj Ω̂^DHod_R, that is of the completed derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.0 and DD.5); the statements for Fil^m follow by induction on m from absolute-prismatic-descent (Remark 5.5.10, Propositions 5.5.20 and 5.5.24, Corollaries 5.5.21, 5.5.22, 5.5.25 and 5.5.26).

(4): F^* H_Δ(R) is complete for its Nygaard filtration, checked on the Čech nerve A^• by the relative completeness for p-completely flat algebras with p-completely flat cotangent complex (PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration; Bhatt–Lurie, Lemma 5.8.3); the derived de Rham complex of R is Hodge-complete because it is the completed de Rham complex with its stupid filtration (DD.2); conclude with the fibre sequence (e) (Proposition 5.8.2). The counterexample is Example 5.8.1: the series exp(x) defines an element of the completion not in A_crys(R).
acceptance: For R = Z_p[x]^∧: gr^1_N Δ_R ≅ Ω̂^1_R[−1], for every prime p.
For R = W(k), k a perfect field: the Nygaard filtration of Δ_R is complete, gr^0_N Δ_R = W(k) and gr^m_N Δ_R ≅ (W(k)/m)[−1] for m ≥ 1.
Quasisyntomic test: the filtration of a p-quasisyntomic ring is the totalization of the filtrations of a quasiregular semiperfectoid Čech nerve.

nodes.title: The absolute Nygaard filtration over a perfect prism, for quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and in characteristic p
nodes.statement: (1) Let (A, I) be a perfect prism, R an animated Ā-algebra and n an integer. Let Fil^•_N F^*(Δ_{R/A}{n}) be the relative Nygaard filtration of F^* Δ_{R/A} tensored with F^*(A{n}) ≅ I^{−n} A{n}. The comparison map Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Fil^•_N F^*(Δ_{R/A}{n}), obtained by restricting to the point ρ_A and composing with Δ_{(Ā ⊗^L R)/A} → Δ_{R/A}, is an isomorphism of filtered complexes. (2) Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring, so that (Δ_R, Δ_R^{[1]}) is a prism. For all integers m, n the map Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} identifies Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} with the subgroup {x ∈ Δ_R{n} : φ(x) ∈ Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}}; in particular Fil^m_N Δ_R{n} and gr^m_N Δ_R{n} are concentrated in degree 0, and for n = 0 the filtration is {x : φ(x) ∈ I^m Δ_R}, the Nygaard filtration of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp. For a p-quasisyntomic ring R the absolute Nygaard filtration is the totalization of this filtration over a quasiregular semiperfectoid Čech nerve, so it agrees with PR.3/nygaard-filtration. (3) Crystalline case, (A, I) = (Z_p, (p)) and R an F_p-algebra, where F^* is the identity: the comparison γ : Δ_{R/Z_p} → RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) carries the prismatic augmentation to the crystalline augmentation, so Fil^1_N corresponds to fib(ε_crys) when R is quasisyntomic, and the Frobenius divided by p is defined on it. For R quasiregular semiperfect, with I = ker(R^♭ → R): Fil^n_N A_crys(R) = {x : φ(x) ∈ p^n A_crys(R)} is the ideal generated by the elements p^{m_0} γ_{m_1}([x_1]) ⋯ γ_{m_k}([x_k]) with x_i ∈ I and m_0 + ⋯ + m_k ≥ n. For R a regular Noetherian F_p-algebra, γ extends to an isomorphism of filtered complexes Fil^•_N Δ_{R/Z_p} ≅ N^• WΩ_R with the Nygaard filtration of the de Rham–Witt complex.
hypotheses: (1) requires (A, I) perfect; for a bounded prism only the comparison map is defined.
(2): R quasiregular semiperfectoid; the index of the ideal filtration is m − n (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E51 concerns the same index in Bhatt–Lurie §5.7).
(3): R an F_p-algebra; quasisyntomic, quasiregular semiperfect or regular Noetherian as stated in each assertion.
The relative Nygaard filtration and the filtrations of quasiregular semiperfectoid and quasisyntomic rings are owned by PR.3; this node only compares with them.
proofSteps: Reduce (1) to graded pieces by induction on m, the case m = 0 being absolute-relative-comparison and bijectivity of φ_A; both gr^m_N Δ_R{n} and Fil_m^conj Δ̄_{R/A}{m} commute with sifted colimits and satisfy p-completely faithfully flat descent (absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces (3); PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison), so it suffices to treat quasiregular semiperfectoid Ā-algebras admitting a map from Z_p^cyc, a basis of the quasisyntomic topology (Bhatt–Lurie, proof of Theorem 5.6.2).

For such R the relative filtration is {y : φ(y) ∈ I^m Δ_{R/A}} (PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp), so (1) for R is equivalent to (2) for R, a statement independent of the prism; hence it suffices to prove (1) for the perfection of the q-de Rham prism, with quotient Z_p^cyc (Remark 5.6.7, Proposition 5.6.8).

Over Z_p^cyc reduce by sifted colimits to polynomial algebras and by induction on the number of variables to R = Z_p^cyc, where the claim is that (Θ + m, ξ) : Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod ⊕ Z_p^cyc is an isomorphism of free modules of rank m + 1, an explicit computation with the prism (Z_p[[p̃]], (p̃)) and the q-de Rham prism of PR.0 (Lemma 5.6.14).
(2): Corollary 5.6.3 and Corollary 5.6.4; the quasisyntomic statement by descent (absolute-nygaard-graded-pieces (3); Remark 5.6.5).

(3): Proposition 5.3.1 (compatibility of augmentations, by reduction to quasiregular semiperfect rings), Proposition 5.3.6 (induction on n using gr^n_N ≅ Fil_n^conj and the divided power description of gr^conj(A_crys/p)), Proposition 5.3.8 (comparison with the de Rham–Witt complex of CrystallineCohomology:CR.4, essentially Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze Theorem 8.17).
Use perfect-prism-sen-calculation for the kernel/cokernel computation in BL Proposition 5.6.8, then descend from the cyclotomic chart; the all-prime proof is not Theorem 3.8.3.
acceptance: For a perfectoid ring Ā = A/I: Fil^m_N Δ_Ā = φ^{−1}(I^m) ⊂ A and gr^m_N Δ_Ā is an invertible Ā-module.
For R = F_p[x^{1/p^∞}]/(x): Fil^m_N Δ_R is the ideal of A_crys(R) generated by p^a x^b/b! with a + b ≥ m.
For a smooth algebra R over a perfect field k the filtration is the classical Nygaard filtration of WΩ_R.

nodes.title: The Frobenius on absolute prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let R be an animated commutative ring. (a) Relative Frobenius: the maps Fil^•(φ) : Fil^•_N F^* Δ_{R′/A} → I^• Δ_{R′/A} of the relative theory, for R′ = Ā ⊗^L R over all bounded prisms, define a morphism of filtered objects Fil^•(Φ) : Fil^•_N F^* H_Δ(R) → I^• ⊗ H_Δ(R) of D(WCart); in degree 0 it is Φ : F^* H_Δ(R) → H_Δ(R), and gr^m(Φ) factors through an isomorphism gr^m_N F^* H_Δ(R) ≅ ι_* Fil_m^conj H_Δ̄(R){m}. Φ exhibits H_Δ(R) as the colimit of F^* H_Δ(R) → I^{−1} Fil^1_N F^* H_Δ(R) → I^{−2} Fil^2_N F^* H_Δ(R) → ⋯, with successive quotients ι_*(Fil^n_Hodge dR̂_R ⊗ O_{WCart^HT}{−n}). (b) Twisting by F^* O_WCart{n} ≅ I^{−n} O_WCart{n} gives Φ{n} : Fil^n_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n}) → H_Δ(R){n}, and the Frobenius φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} is the composite of Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → RΓ(WCart, Fil^n_N F^*(H_Δ(R){n})) with RΓ(WCart, Φ{n}). For n = 0 this is the Frobenius endomorphism φ : Δ_R → Δ_R, equal to the pullback RΓ(WCart, H_Δ(R)) → RΓ(WCart, F^* H_Δ(R)) along F followed by RΓ(WCart, Φ). (c) φ{n} refines to a map of filtered complexes Fil^•(φ{n}) : Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R^{[•−n]}{n}, whose graded piece gr^m_N Δ_R{n} → Δ̄_R{m} is the natural map fib(Θ + m : Fil_m^conj Ω̂^DHod_R → Fil_{m−1}^conj Ω̂^DHod_R) → fib(Θ + m on Ω̂^DHod_R). (d) If R is a p-torsion-free ring with R/pR regular Noetherian, Fil^•(φ{n}) exhibits Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} as the connective cover of Δ_R^{[•−n]}{n} for the Beilinson t-structure. (e) If R is p-completely smooth of relative dimension ≤ d over W(k), k a perfect field, then φ{n} : Fil^n_N Δ_R{n} → Δ_R{n} is an isomorphism for n > d; for R = W(k) there is a fibre sequence Δ_{W(k)} → Δ_{W(k)} → W(k)[−1] with first map φ. (f) The augmentation identity ε_Δ followed by R̂→Δ̄_R equals the absolute Frobenius followed by Δ_R→Δ̄_R; compare the de Rham-point map with the Hodge–Tate restriction after φ is constructed. (g) The filtered map factors uniquely through Nygaard completion. Thus φ̂{n}:Fil^n_NΔ̂_R{n}→Δ̂_R{n} is defined. The functor R↦Fil^•_NΔ̂_R{n}, valued in filtration-complete complexes, preserves sifted colimits; on finitely generated polynomial Z-algebras it is the Beilinson connective cover of Δ_R^[•−n]{n} (BL Remark 5.7.10).
hypotheses: R is an arbitrary animated commutative ring in (a)–(c); (d) requires R p-torsion-free with R/pR regular Noetherian; (e) requires p-complete smoothness over W(k).

Corrected index (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E51): the target of Fil^m(φ{n}) is Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}; Bhatt–Lurie Remark 5.7.8, Proposition 5.7.9 and Remark 5.7.10 print the index • + n, which contradicts Notation 5.7.5, Corollary 5.6.3 and the stated graded piece Δ̄_R{m}.

proofSteps: (a): the relative filtered Frobenius and its graded pieces are PR.3/relative-nygaard-filtration and PR.3/divided-frobenius in the animated form of Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 5.1.1; compatibility with base change in the prism globalises them to D(WCart) (Construction 5.7.1, Remarks 5.7.2 and 5.7.3).
(b): tensor with the twist isomorphism of wcart-frobenius and take global sections; compose with the first projection of the pullback square defining Fil^•_N Δ_R{n} (Notation 5.7.5).

(c): the same construction in every filtration degree gives a target I^{m−n} ⊗ H_Δ(R){n}, with global sections Δ_R^{[m−n]}{n}; the graded pieces are computed by the fibre sequences of absolute-nygaard-filtration (g) and absolute-hodge-tate-cohomology (Remark 5.7.8).

(e): Examples 5.7.4, 5.7.6 and 5.7.7, from the vanishing of Fil^n_Hodge for n > d.

nodes.title: The q-analogue [p]_q and the operation γ
nodes.statement: Let A = Z_p[[q−1]] with the δ-structure δ(q) = 0, so φ(q) = q^p, and let [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1) = 1 + q + … + q^{p−1} ∈ A, the value at q of the p-th cyclotomic polynomial; (A, ([p]_q)) is the q-de Rham prism of PR.0. For a δ-A-algebra D put N(D) := φ^{-1}([p]_q D) = {x ∈ D : φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D}; it is an ideal of D. If D is [p]_q-torsion-free, the operation γ : N(D) → D is γ(x) := φ(x)/[p]_q − δ(x). The following facts are fixed with the definition. (i) φ(q−1) = q^p − 1 = (q−1)·[p]_q, so q − 1 ∈ N(D). (ii) [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q−1). (iii) A/[p]_q ≅ Z_p[ζ_p] with ζ_p a primitive p-th root of 1, and in this ring (q−1)^{p−1} and p differ by a unit; hence derived (p,[p]_q)-completion and derived (p, q−1)-completion agree on every complex of A-modules. (iv) δ([p]_q) ≡ 1 modulo [p]_q A. (v) For x, y ∈ N(D): γ(x+y) = γ(x) + γ(y) + ((x+y)^p − x^p − y^p)/p, where the last term is the integral polynomial Σ_{0<i<p} (binom(p,i)/p) x^i y^{p−i}. (vi) For x ∈ N(D) and f ∈ D: γ(fx) = φ(f)γ(x) − x^p δ(f). (vii) Hence for every ideal I ⊂ D the subset {x ∈ I : φ(x) ∈ [p]_q D and γ(x) ∈ I} is an ideal of D, and the two conditions φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D, γ(I) ⊂ I may be checked on a generating set of I. (viii) If q = 1 in D then [p]_q = p and γ(x) = x^p/p. Convention: γ is the divided [p]_q-th power without the unit factor ∏_{j=1}^{p−1} [j]_q; the source keeps this normalisation and so does this node.
hypotheses: p is a prime; A = Z_p[[q−1]] with δ(q) = 0.
D is a δ-A-algebra; γ is defined only when D is [p]_q-torsion-free, and only on N(D).
The general q-integers [n]_q, the q-derivative and their identities are owned by QWittVectors:QW.6; this node uses only [p]_q, which PR.0 owns as the generator of the q-de Rham prism.
Fact (iii) corrects the printed sentence 'derived (p,[p]_q)-completion coincides with derived (p,[p]_q)-completion' to '(p, q−1)-completion'; the misprint is registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27.
Fact (iv) is not printed in the source; it is the analogue for [p]_q of the computation δ(ξ) ≡ 1 mod ξ in Example 16.9 (2) and is used in smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals.
proofSteps: [p]_q and the prism (A, ([p]_q)) come from PR.0's q-de Rham prism. Facts (i) and (ii) are the identities Φ_p(q)·(q−1) = q^p − 1 and Φ_p(1) = p for the p-th cyclotomic polynomial, which Mathlib has (cyclotomic_prime, cyclotomic_prime_mul_X_sub_one, eval_one_cyclotomic_prime).
N(D) is the preimage of the ideal [p]_q D under the ring homomorphism φ of the δ-ring D, so it is an ideal; γ is well defined because [p]_q is a nonzerodivisor on D (Notation 16.1).

Facts (v) and (vi) (Remark 16.6): expand φ(x+y) = φ(x) + φ(y) and φ(fx) = φ(f)φ(x), and use the δ-ring formulas for δ(x+y) and δ(fx) from PR.0; for (vi), φ(f)(γ(x)+δ(x)) − f^pδ(x) − x^pδ(f) − pδ(f)δ(x) = φ(f)γ(x) − x^pδ(f).
Fact (vii): by (v) the correction term is a multiple of xy and by (vi) γ(fx) ∈ I when γ(x) ∈ I and x ∈ I, so the subset is closed under sums and multiples (Remark 16.6).

Fact (iv): pδ([p]_q) = φ([p]_q) − [p]_q^p, and φ([p]_q) = Σ_{i<p} q^{pi} ≡ p modulo [p]_q because q^p ≡ 1 modulo [p]_q; p is a nonzerodivisor in A/[p]_q ≅ Z_p[ζ_p], so δ([p]_q) − 1 ∈ [p]_q A. Fact (viii) is the definition with [p]_q = p: pγ(x) = φ(x) − pδ(x) = x^p.
acceptance: γ(q−1) = (q−1) − δ(q−1) in every [p]_q-torsion-free δ-A-algebra (the computation of Corollary 16.8).
For D = Z_p with q = 1: γ(p) = p^{p−1}, since δ(p) = 1 − p^{p−1}.
In A itself N(A) = (q−1)A: φ(f) ∈ [p]_q A exactly when f(1) = 0.

nodes.title: q-PD pairs
nodes.statement: A q-PD pair is a δ-pair (D, I) (a δ-ring D with an ideal I ⊂ D) with a map of δ-pairs (A, (q−1)) → (D, I), A = Z_p[[q−1]] with δ(q) = 0 (so D is a δ-A-algebra and q − 1 ∈ I), such that D and I are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and the following three conditions hold. (1) φ(I) ⊂ [p]_q D (so γ is defined on I) and γ(I) ⊂ I. (2) Require [p]_q to be regular in D and require bounded p-power torsion in D/([p]_q). Together with the δ-A-algebra structure, these conditions make (D, ([p]_q)) a bounded prism receiving the base prism (A, ([p]_q)). (3) The ring D/(q−1) is p-torsion-free and has finite (p,[p]_q)-complete Tor-amplitude over D; equivalently finite p-complete Tor-amplitude, because [p]_q ≡ p mod (q−1). The map D → D/I is called a q-PD thickening and I a q-PD ideal. Being a q-PD pair is a property of a δ-pair over (A, (q−1)), not extra structure. Morphisms of q-PD pairs are maps of δ-pairs over (A, (q−1)): δ-ring maps D → D′ sending q to q and I into I′. A δ-PD pair is a q-PD pair with q − 1 = 0 in D; δ-PD pairs form a full subcategory. Two sufficient cases for (2) and (3) are a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D completely flat over A, or a p-complete, p-torsion-free D in which q=1. By (2) and PR.0's Lemma 3.7, D is classically (p,[p]_q)-adically complete.
hypotheses: The source's phrase 'derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-pair (D, I)' is read as: both D and I are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete. Remark 16.3 (a) and the proof of Corollary 16.8 confirm that completeness of the ideal is part of the definition.
Condition (3) is a technical condition; condition (2) could be weakened to D being [p]_q-torsion-free. The source works with bounded prisms and so does this node.
The conditions γ(I) ⊂ I, q − 1 ∈ I and the p-torsion-freeness of D/(q−1) are part of Definition 16.2 and are easily overlooked.
Derived completeness, complete flatness and complete Tor-amplitude are DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1's notions.
proofSteps: State the data (D, I, the δ-A-algebra structure) and the conditions; by (1) and (2) the operation γ of q-divided-power-operation is defined on I.
Classical completeness: (D, ([p]_q)) is a bounded prism by (2), so D is classically (p,[p]_q)-complete by PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness (BS22 Lemma 3.7).

The two standard sources of (2) and (3) (text after Definition 16.2): if D is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A then D/[p]_q is p-completely flat over Z_p[ζ_p] and D/(q−1) = D ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is p-completely flat over Z_p with Tor-amplitude in [−1, 0]; if q = 1 in D and D is p-torsion-free then [p]_q = p and D/(q−1) = D.
Morphisms compose and the identity is a morphism, so q-PD pairs form a category; δ-PD pairs are the full subcategory on the pairs with q = 1.
acceptance: (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) is a q-PD pair, and it is initial (smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals).
(A_inf, (ξ)) with ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q) is a q-PD pair (ainf-q-pd-pair).
(Z_p, (p)) with q = 1 is a δ-PD pair; (Z_p[[q−1]], (p, q−1)) is not a q-PD pair, since φ(p) = p ∉ [p]_q Z_p[[q−1]].

nodes.title: δ-PD pairs and reduction modulo q − 1
nodes.statement: (a) (Remark 16.3.) Let D be a δ-ring, regarded as an A-algebra through q ↦ 1, and I ⊂ D an ideal. Then (D, I) is a δ-PD pair if and only if (i) D is p-torsion-free and both D and I are p-adically complete, and (ii) I admits divided powers: x^n/n! ∈ I for every x ∈ I and n > 0. (b) (Remark 16.4.) If (D, I) is a q-PD pair then (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)) is a δ-PD pair, and (D, I) ↦ (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)) is left adjoint to the inclusion of δ-PD pairs into q-PD pairs. (c) (Example 16.9 (3).) For a p-torsion-free p-complete δ-ring D with a p-complete ideal I, (D, I) is a δ-PD pair exactly when every x ∈ I has all its divided powers x^n/n! in I. In particular a δ-PD pair is a p-adically complete PD pair in the sense of CrystallineCohomology:CR.0 whose ring is p-torsion-free and carries a δ-structure.
hypotheses: In (a) the source prints 'I ⊂ A'; the ideal lies in D (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
In (c) the source prints 'admits all divided powers in D'; the divided powers must lie in I, as Remark 16.3 (b) says (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
The divided powers are unique because D is p-torsion-free: γ_n(x) = x^n/n!.
proofSteps: (⇐ of (a)) With q = 1 one has [p]_q = p and γ(x) = x^p/p, which lies in I by (ii); D is p-torsion-free and p-complete, so (D, (p)) is a bounded prism, and D/(q−1) = D gives (3).

(⇒ of (a)) Completeness and torsion-freeness in (i) are conditions (2), (3) and the completeness in the definition. For (ii): condition (1) gives x^p/p ∈ I; as (p−1)! is a unit, x^p/p! ∈ I; for n < p, x^n/n! is a unit multiple of x^n; the general case follows by induction from γ_{kp}(x) = u·γ_k(γ_p(x)) with u a p-adic unit (the composition rule of divided powers, Mathlib's DividedPowers.dpow_comp and CR.0).

(b) Conditions (2), (3) make D/(q−1) p-torsion-free and p-complete; the image of I satisfies x^p/p ∈ Ī by (1) reduced modulo q−1, and it is p-complete as the image of a derived complete module; apply (a). Adjunction: a map of q-PD pairs to a δ-PD pair kills q − 1, so it factors uniquely through the reduction.
(c) is (a) for the given D.

(A_inf, (ξ)) reduces to (A_inf/(q−1), (ξ)), so ξ has divided powers in A_inf/(q−1).
For D the p-completed PD polynomial algebra on t over Z_p with δ(t) = 0, the ideal tD is not a q-PD ideal although every element of tD has all divided powers in D: t^p/p ∉ tD.

nodes.title: Homological properties of q-PD pairs
nodes.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair. (1) D is derived f-complete for every f ∈ I. (2) The functor M ↦ M ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) of (p,[p]_q)-completed base change along D → D/(q−1) is conservative on derived (p,[p]_q)-complete complexes. (3) This functor commutes with totalisations of cosimplicial derived (p,[p]_q)-complete complexes in D^{≥0}. (4) Let I_0 ⊂ D be an ideal containing q − 1 such that (D, I_0) satisfies conditions (1)–(3) of q-pd-pair, with D derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and I_0 not assumed derived complete, and let I′ ⊂ D be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal generated by I_0, that is, the image of I_0^∧ → D. Completing this ideal therefore gives a q-PD pair (D,I′). (5) This property also survives scalar extension: take a δ-A-map D→D′ which is completely flat for (p,[p]_q), assume D′ is derived complete for that ideal, and complete the ideal generated by the image of I. The resulting pair on D′ satisfies the q-PD conditions.
hypotheses: (3): the source prints 'cosimplicial (p,[p]_q)-complexes'; the complexes are derived (p,[p]_q)-complete (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).

(4): the source states it for a q-PD pair (D, I); since the ideal of a q-PD pair is already derived complete that statement is empty, and the proof of (5) and of Theorem 16.17 apply (4) to an ideal that is not known to be complete. The node states the form that the printed proof of (4) proves (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E63).
Completed base change, conservativity (derived Nakayama) and Tor-amplitude are DD.1's.
proofSteps: (1) For f ∈ I, φ(f) = f^p + pδ(f) ∈ [p]_q D, so f^p ∈ (p, [p]_q); derived (p,[p]_q)-completeness gives derived f^p-completeness, hence derived f-completeness.

(2) It suffices that base change to D/(q−1, p) is conservative. If M ⊗^L_D D/(q−1, p) = 0 then M ⊗^L_D Kos(D; [p]_q, q−1) = 0, because this Koszul complex has at most two nonzero cohomology groups, each a D/(q−1, p)-module; then M = 0 by derived Nakayama (DD.1).

(3) Condition (3) of q-pd-pair gives finite complete Tor-amplitude of D → D/(q−1); a completed base change of finite complete Tor-amplitude commutes with totalisations in D^{≥0} (BS22 Lemma 4.22, a statement of DD.1).

(4) φ^{-1}([p]_q D) is derived complete, so φ(I′) ⊂ [p]_q D. As q − 1 ∈ I_0, I′ is the preimage of its image in D/(q−1), and that image is the p-complete ideal generated by the image of I_0 (derived completion preserves surjections). This reduces γ(I′) ⊂ I′ to q = 1, where it is the p-adic continuity of divided powers in a p-torsion-free ring (delta-pd-pairs).

(5) Condition (1) for (D′, I′): the generators of I·D′ satisfy it by fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation, then apply (4) to I_0 = I·D′. Condition (2): PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness (BS22 Lemma 3.7). Condition (3): the p-completed base change of D → D′ along D → D/(q−1) is p-completely flat with p-torsion-free source, so it is discrete and p-torsion-free and equals D′/(q−1); D′ → D′/(q−1) is the completed base change of D → D/(q−1), so it has finite p-complete Tor-amplitude.
acceptance: For (D, I) = (A_inf, (ξ)): A_inf is derived ξ-complete, and a derived (p, ξ)-complete complex M with M ⊗^L A_inf/(q−1) = 0 is zero.
For D = Z_p[[q−1]] → D′ = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T⟩ (completed polynomial ring, δ(T) = 0): (D′, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair.
(2) fails without completeness: for D = Z_p[[q−1]], M = D[1/(q−1)] has zero base change and is not zero.

nodes.title: Higher q-divided powers and the smallest and largest q-PD ideals
nodes.statement: (a) (Existence of higher q-divided powers, Lemma 16.7.) Let D be a δ-A-algebra and let f, z ∈ D satisfy [p]_q·z = φ(f). Then φ(z − δ(f)) ∈ [p]_q D. In particular, if D is [p]_q-torsion-free, the ideal N(D) = φ^{-1}([p]_q D) is stable under γ: if γ(x) is defined then so is γ(γ(x)). (b) (Corollary 16.8.) Let D be a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete δ-A-algebra satisfying conditions (2) and (3) of q-pd-pair. Then (q−1)D is the smallest q-PD ideal of D and N(D) is the largest q-PD ideal of D. (c) (Example 16.9 (1).) The pair (A, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair and is the initial object of the category of q-PD pairs; more generally (D, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair for every derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-A-algebra D.
hypotheses: (a) is stated for every δ-A-algebra, with no torsion-freeness, flatness or completeness. The source states it for [p]_q-torsion-free D and proves it by reduction to a universal case whose flatness is taken from Proposition 3.13; that proposition concerns the completed envelope, so the printed argument covers derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D, which is all the source uses (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E61). The proof steps give a direct argument.
(b): the source prints 'A-algebra'; a δ-A-algebra is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
A q-PD ideal of D is an ideal I such that (D, I) is a q-PD pair.
proofSteps: (a), direct argument: apply δ to [p]_q·z = φ(f) and use δ∘φ = φ∘δ and the product formula for δ: φ(δ(f)) = δ(z)·φ([p]_q) + z^p·δ([p]_q). With φ([p]_q) = [p]_q^p + pδ([p]_q) this gives φ(z) − φ(δ(f)) = (1 − δ([p]_q))·φ(z) − δ(z)·[p]_q^p, which lies in [p]_q D by fact (iv) of q-divided-power-operation.

(a), the source's route: in the universal case A{f, φ(f)/[p]_q}, flat over A by PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes (Proposition 3.13), φ([p]_q) = p is a nonzerodivisor modulo [p]_q, and φ²(f) = φ(f)^p + pφ(δ(f)) ≡ pφ(δ(f)) modulo [p]_q.

(b), smallest: (q−1)D is derived complete as the image of multiplication by q − 1 on D. φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q, and γ(q−1) = (q−1) − δ(q−1); pδ(q−1) = (q^p − 1) − (q−1)^p = (q−1)([p]_q − (q−1)^{p−1}) and D/(q−1) is p-torsion-free, so δ(q−1) ∈ (q−1). Fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation extends this to the ideal. Every q-PD ideal contains q − 1 by definition.
(b), largest: N(D) is the limit of D →φ φ_*D ← φ_*D (multiplication by [p]_q), hence derived complete; it is stable under γ by (a); every q-PD ideal lies in N(D) by condition (1).
(c) A satisfies (2) and (3), so (b) applies; it is initial because a q-PD pair is by definition a δ-pair over (A, (q−1)). The same argument applies to completely flat D.
acceptance: In A = Z_p[[q−1]] one has N(A) = (q−1)A, so (q−1) is the only q-PD ideal of A.
In Z_p with q = 1: the smallest q-PD ideal is 0 and the largest is N(Z_p) = pZ_p.
In A_inf: N(A_inf) = φ^{-1}(φ(ξ)A_inf) = (ξ), so (q−1) is the smallest and (ξ) the largest q-PD ideal of A_inf.

nodes.title: The q-PD pair (A_inf, (ξ))
nodes.statement: (a) (Example 16.9 (2).) Let A_∞ be the (p,[p]_q)-completed perfection of A = Z_p[[q−1]] (PR.0's perfection of the q-de Rham prism) and ξ := φ^{-1}([p]_q) ∈ A_∞. Then (A_∞, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair. (b) (Notation 17.1.) Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, with a compatible system (ζ_{p^n})_n of primitive p-power roots of 1, ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ and A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = W(O_C^♭). Then q := [ε] has δ(q) = 0, so A_inf is a perfect δ-A-algebra; it is (p, q−1)-completely flat over A, hence flat over A; the element ξ := φ^{-1}([p]_q) = 1 + [ε^{1/p}] + … + [ε^{(p−1)/p}] generates the kernel of Fontaine's map θ : A_inf → O_C; and (A_inf, (ξ)) is a q-PD pair whose q-PD thickening is θ : A_inf → A_inf/(ξ) ≅ O_C. Moreover [p]_q = φ(ξ) =: ξ̃ generates the kernel of θ̃ := θ∘φ^{-1}, the prism (A_inf, ([p]_q)) is the image of the perfect prism (A_inf, (ξ)) under the automorphism φ, and q − 1 = (q^{1/p} − 1)·ξ.
hypotheses: C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of 1; the system (ζ_{p^n}) is fixed. The ideals (q−1) and (ξ) do not depend on the choice.
A_inf, θ and the element [ε] are owned by PerfectoidQuotients:Q0:integral-algebra; the perfect prism (A_inf, ker θ) by PR.0.
proofSteps: Conditions (2) and (3): A_∞ and A_inf are (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over A (A_∞ is a completed colimit along the flat Frobenius of A; for A_inf, (p, q−1) is a regular sequence and A_inf/(p, q−1) = O_C^♭/(ε−1) is flat over F_p), so the remark after Definition 16.2 applies; flatness over the noetherian ring A follows from complete flatness and derived completeness (the implication quoted in Notation 17.1; DD.1).

Condition (1) on the generator: φ(ξ) = [p]_q, so γ(ξ) = 1 − δ(ξ), and one needs δ(ξ) ≡ 1 modulo ξ. As p is a nonzerodivisor modulo ξ it suffices that φ(ξ) ≡ p modulo ξ; and φ(ξ) = [p]_q ≡ p modulo (q−1), while ξ divides q − 1 because q − 1 = φ^{-1}((q−1)[p]_q) = (q^{1/p} − 1)·ξ.
By fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation the conditions hold on the ideal (ξ), which is derived complete (principal, generated by a nonzerodivisor of a derived complete ring) and contains q − 1.

(b): q = [ε] is a Teichmüller element, so δ(q) = 0 (PR.0, Q0:integral-algebra); θ(ξ) = 1 + ζ_p + … + ζ_p^{p−1} = 0 and ξ is distinguished, so it generates ker θ (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). The statements about ξ̃ and θ̃ follow by applying φ.
acceptance: The reduction (A_inf/(q−1), (ξ)) is a δ-PD pair: ξ has divided powers in A_inf/(q−1).
(A_inf, (q−1)) is also a q-PD pair, with A_inf/(q−1) a p-torsion-free lift of O_C modulo the divided power ideal (ξ); q-pd-thickening-invariance compares the two.

nodes.title: q-PD envelopes
nodes.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair, P a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete, (p,[p]_q)-completely flat δ-D-algebra and x_1, …, x_r ∈ P a sequence that is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D; let J = (I, x_1, …, x_r) ⊂ P. (1) The derived (p,[p]_q)-complete simplicial δ-P-algebra E := P{φ(x_1)/[p]_q, …, φ(x_r)/[p]_q}^∧ obtained by freely adjoining the elements φ(x_i)/[p]_q has complete flatness over D for the ideal (p,[p]_q). Its higher homotopy groups vanish and multiplication by [p]_q on its underlying ring is injective. (2) Let K ⊂ E be the minimal derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal containing the image of J and stable under γ. Then P/J → E/K is an isomorphism, (E, K) is a q-PD pair, and (P, J) → (E, K) is the universal map of δ-pairs from (P, J) to a q-PD pair: every map of δ-pairs (P, J) → (E′, K′) to a q-PD pair factors uniquely through (E, K). One writes D_{J,q}(P) := E and calls (D_{J,q}(P), K) the q-PD envelope of (P, J); it depends only on the ideal J, not on the generators. (3) Extension used by the Čech–Alexander construction: the same statements hold when J is, Zariski locally on Spf(P), generated by I and a sequence as above, and when (P, J) is a filtered colimit (completed) of such pairs.
hypotheses: (D, I) is a q-PD pair; P is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; the sequence is (p,[p]_q)-completely regular relative to D (DD.1's notion, BS22 Definition 2.42).
The source does not state that P is derived complete. Without it E/K is the derived p-completion of P/J, so the isomorphism P/J ≅ E/K needs it (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
Part (3) is not stated in Lemma 16.10, but Construction 16.13 and Remark 16.16 apply the lemma to such ideals (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E64).
Free adjunction of elements to simplicial δ-rings is PR.0's animated-delta-rings.
proofSteps: Let Ẽ be the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete simplicial commutative δ-P-algebra freely adjoining φ(x_i)/[p]_q. Complete flatness of Ẽ over D may be checked after derived base change along D → D/(q−1) (q-pd-homological-properties); there [p]_q = p and the claim is BS22 Corollary 2.44 with Lemma 2.43 (PR.0), the sequence φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p being p-completely regular relative to D/(q−1). So Ẽ is discrete, equal to E, and [p]_q-torsion-free (PR.0, Lemma 3.7).

The map E → P/J: E/(q−1) is the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) along (x_1, …, x_r) (PR.0's pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope), which maps to P/(q−1, x_1, …, x_r) → P/J. Let K′ be the kernel of E → P/J; it is the preimage of the kernel K̄′ of E/(q−1) → P/J, and K̄′ has divided powers.

(E, K′) is a q-PD pair: put K″ = K′ ∩ φ^{-1}([p]_q E). γ(K″) ⊂ K″, because γ(f) ∈ φ^{-1}([p]_q E) by smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals (a), and γ(f) reduces to f^p/p ∈ K̄′. K″ is the preimage of its image in E/(q−1), since x + (q−1)y ∈ K″ for x ∈ K″. It contains (I, x_1, …, x_r). By BS22 Lemma 16.11 (CR.0: the ideal of a PD envelope is the smallest ideal containing the generators and stable under f ↦ f^p/p) one gets K″ = K′ = K.

Universality: for a map of δ-pairs g : (P, J) → (E′, K′) to a q-PD pair, g(φ(x_i)) ∈ [p]_q E′; as E′ is [p]_q-torsion-free and derived complete, g extends uniquely to a δ-map E → E′; the preimage of K′ is a derived complete γ-stable ideal containing J, so it contains K.

(3): Zariski gluing by the flat-localisation property of envelopes (PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes (3)) together with q-pd-homological-properties (5); filtered colimits by the universal property, the envelope being the completed colimit of the envelopes.
acceptance: For P = Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩ with δ(X) = 0 and J = (q−1, X): the envelope contains z with [p]_q·z = X^p, γ(X) = z ∈ K, and its reduction modulo q − 1 is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra Z_p⟨X⟩ with X^p/p.
For P = A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ and J = (ξ): φ(ξ)/[p]_q = 1, so D_{J,q}(P) = P.
Universal property applied to the q-PD pair (A_inf(S), (ξ)) of a p-torsion-free perfectoid O_C-algebra S gives the coordinate map of ainf-omega-comparison-map.

nodes.title: q-PD envelopes: base change, PD envelopes and prismatic envelopes
nodes.statement: In the situation of q-pd-envelope: (a) (Lemma 16.10 (3).) The functor (P, J) ↦ (D_{J,q}(P), K) commutes with (p,[p]_q)-completed derived base change along maps (D, I) → (D′, I′) of q-PD pairs: D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂^L_D D′ ≅ D_{J′,q}(P′) for P′ = P ⊗̂^L_D D′ and J′ = (I′, x_1, …, x_r). (b) In particular D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) = D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) is the p-completed PD envelope of the ideal J/(q−1) ⊂ P/(q−1), relative to the PD pair (D/(q−1), I·D/(q−1)), and K/(q−1) is its PD ideal. (c) (Lemma 16.11.) Let B be a p-torsion-free Z_p-algebra and I ⊂ B an ideal generated by a sequence that is regular modulo p; let (D_I(B), J) be the PD envelope of (B, I). Then J is the smallest ideal of D_I(B) that contains I·D_I(B) and is stable under f ↦ f^p/p. (d) (Relation to prismatic envelopes.) D_{J,q}(P) is the prismatic envelope of PR.0, over the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)), of the δ-pair (P, ([p]_q, φ(x_1), …, φ(x_r))); when q = 1 in D this is the identification of P{φ(x_i)/p}^∧ with the p-completed PD envelope of (x_1, …, x_r) (BS22 Corollary 2.39).
hypotheses: (b): the source prints 'is the pd-envelope'; the p-completed PD envelope is meant, as in its proof and in Remark 16.16 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
(c): the source says 'an ideal I that is regular modulo p'; the node reads it as generated by a sequence regular modulo p.
(d) is not printed as a statement; it is the content of the first step of the proof of Lemma 16.10 and of the reference to Proposition 3.13 in the proof of Lemma 16.7.
PD envelopes and their ideals are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.0.
proofSteps: (a) E is the free derived complete δ-P-algebra on the elements φ(x_i)/[p]_q, and complete regularity relative to the base is stable under base change, so the construction commutes with completed base change; K′ is identified by the universal property.

(b) Take D′ = D/(q−1) with the δ-PD pair of delta-pd-pairs (b). Then [p]_q = p and P̄{φ(x_i)/p}^∧ is the p-completed PD envelope by PR.0's pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope (BS22 Lemma 2.38, Corollary 2.39), with its PD structure compatible with that of I·D/(q−1) (CR.0).

(c) The regularity hypothesis makes D_I(B) p-torsion-free; the description of J is the standard generation of the PD ideal by divided powers of generators, in which γ_n for general n is a unit multiple of iterates of γ_p and ordinary powers (CR.0; the source cites the Stacks project, Tag 07GS).

(d) Modulo (p, [p]_q) one has φ(x_i) ≡ x_i^p, and (x_1^p, …, x_r^p) is completely regular relative to D when (x_1, …, x_r) is (the remark after BS22 Lemma 2.43); apply PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes to the ideal ([p]_q, φ(x_1), …, φ(x_r)).
acceptance: For D = Z_p[[q−1]], P = D⟨X⟩, J = (q−1, X): D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) is the p-completed PD polynomial algebra on X over Z_p.
For D with q = 1: D_{J,q}(P) is the p-completed PD envelope D_J(P)^∧ and K its PD ideal.
Base change of the envelope of (Z_p[[q−1]]⟨x⟩, (q−1, x)) along the map of q-PD pairs (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)) → (A_inf, (ξ)) is the envelope of (A_inf⟨x⟩, (ξ, x)).

nodes.title: The q-crystalline site and q-crystalline cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. Write (R/D)_{q-crys} for the site whose underlying category reverses the arrows between relative q-PD thickenings of R: its objects are q-PD pairs (E, J) over (D, I) together with a D/I-algebra map R → E/J, and its morphisms are maps of q-PD pairs over (D, I) compatible with the maps from R. The category carries the indiscrete topology, so every presheaf is a sheaf. The structure presheaf O_{q-crys} sends (E, J) to E; it takes values in δ-D-algebras. The q-crystalline cohomology of R relative to D is qΩ_{R/D} := RΓ((R/D)_{q-crys}, O_{q-crys}), the derived limit of the rings E over all q-PD thickenings; it is a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete commutative algebra object of D(D), equipped with the φ_D-semilinear endomorphism φ_{R/D} induced by the Frobenius lifts of the δ-rings E. It is functorial in R and in the base pair (D, I).
hypotheses: (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I: derived p-complete with R ⊗^L_{D/I} (D/I)/p smooth over (D/I)/p.
The source prints 'valued in δ-B-algebras'; δ-D-algebras is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
The objects only carry a map R → E/J; it need not be an isomorphism.
The category is not small; the cohomology is computed by a weakly initial object and its Čech nerve (q-crystalline-cech-alexander), which is how the derived limit is given a meaning.
proofSteps: Objects, morphisms and the topology are as stated; with the indiscrete topology the cohomology of a presheaf is its derived limit over the opposite category.
O_{q-crys} is a presheaf of δ-D-algebras, so its derived global sections are a commutative algebra object of D(D) with an endomorphism induced by the Frobenii φ_E, semilinear over φ_D.
Completeness: each E is derived (p,[p]_q)-complete and derived complete objects are closed under limits (DD.1).
Functoriality: a map R → R′ over D/I induces (R′/D)_{q-crys} → (R/D)_{q-crys} by composing structure maps; a map of q-PD pairs (D, I) → (D′, I′) acts by restriction of the base.
acceptance: For R = D/I the pair (D, I) is the initial q-PD thickening, so qΩ_{(D/I)/D} = D with φ_{R/D} = φ_D.
For D with q = 1 the site consists of p-complete PD thickenings carrying δ-structures and qΩ_{R/D} is crystalline cohomology (q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison).

nodes.title: Čech–Alexander complexes for q-crystalline cohomology
nodes.statement: Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. Present R as a quotient of a polynomial D-algebra completed for (p,[p]_q); denote this presentation by P→R and its kernel by J_0. Apply the free δ-D-algebra construction to P and then derive its completion, obtaining F. In F put J=(J_0F)^∧. Let P^• and F^• be the (completed) Čech nerves of D → P and D → F; F^• is the free derived complete δ-D-algebra on P^•. Let J_0^• ⊂ P^• be the kernel of P^• → P → R and J^• = (J_0^•F^•)^∧. Then: (1) R ≅ P^•/J_0^• → F^•/J^• is the derived p-completed Čech nerve of R → F/J. (2) The q-PD envelopes D_{J^•,q}(F^•) → F^•/J^•, with kernels K^•, form a cosimplicial object (D_{J^•,q}(F^•), K^•) of (R/D)_{q-crys}, which is the Čech nerve of its 0-th term D_{J,q}(F). (3) D_{J,q}(F) is weakly initial: every q-PD thickening of R receives a map from it. (4) Hence qΩ_{R/D} ≃ lim_Δ D_{J^•,q}(F^•), the totalisation of a cosimplicial δ-D-algebra whose terms are (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D; the Frobenius φ_{R/D} is induced by the Frobenii of the terms. (5) (Small variant, Remark 16.16.) For a (p,[p]_q)-completely smooth (or ind-smooth) δ-D-algebra P with a D-algebra surjection P → R, for instance a (p, I)-completely smooth lift of R with a δ-structure, let P^• be the completed Čech nerve of D → P and J^• = ker(P^• → R); then lim_Δ D_{J^•,q}(P^•) ≃ qΩ_{R/D} as well.
hypotheses: For the augmentation P^n→R, work Zariski locally on Spec(P): its kernel is obtained from I together with a filtered colimit of ideals defined by D-relative completely regular sequences. Part (3) of q-pd-envelope consequently provides the termwise envelopes.
The choice of P → R may be made functorial in R (the polynomial algebra on the set R), giving a strictly functorial complex.
In (5) the weak initiality is replaced by the comparison with crystalline cohomology.
proofSteps: (1): push out P^• → F^• along P^• → P and then along P → R.

(2): the construction carrying a surjection (P → R) to the thickening D_{J,q}(F) takes tensor products of the input to coproducts in the site (universal properties of the free δ-algebra and of the q-PD envelope), so the cosimplicial object is a Čech nerve; this is the argument of BS22 Constructions 4.17–4.18 (PR.1's cech-alexander-complex).

(3): given a thickening (E, J_E), lift R → E/J_E to a D-algebra map P → E (P is a completed polynomial algebra and E is derived complete), extend uniquely to a δ-map F → E, note that J maps into J_E, and apply the universal property of q-pd-envelope.
(4): Čech theory for a weakly final object of a presheaf topos (the argument of the Stacks project, Tag 07JM, as used in PR.1; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2).

(5): run the proof of q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison with D_{J^•,q}(P^•): modulo q − 1 it is the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope, which computes crystalline cohomology because D_{J^0}(P^0) is weakly initial among PD thickenings (CR.2); then use conservativity of reduction modulo q − 1 (q-pd-homological-properties (2), (3)).
acceptance: For R = D/I and P = D the cosimplicial ring is constant with value D.
For D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R = Z_p⟨T⟩ and P = D⟨T⟩ (small variant): the term of degree 1 is D⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧.
Two choices of presentation give canonically isomorphic objects of D(D).

nodes.title: q-crystalline and crystalline cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. There is a canonical identification qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))) of commutative algebra objects of D(D/(q−1)), where the right side is the crystalline cohomology of Spf(R) relative to the p-adic PD thickening D/(q−1) → D/I, whose ideal I·D/(q−1) has divided powers by delta-pd-pairs. Consequences (Remark 16.15 (1)): a map of derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D-complexes is an isomorphism if and only if its completed base change to D/(q−1) is; hence R ↦ qΩ_{R/D} is a sheaf for the Zariski topology on p-completely smooth D/I-algebras, and defines a Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of commutative algebras on every smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I, whose reduction modulo q − 1 is the pushforward of the crystalline structure sheaf.
hypotheses: (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I.
The source prints 'q Ω_D' in the proof; qΩ_{R/D} is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
Crystalline cohomology over a p-adic PD base and its computation by PD envelopes are owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2 and CR.0.
The ringed q-crystalline site of a non-affine formal scheme (Remark 16.15 (2)) is not developed in the source and is not used.
proofSteps: Compute qΩ_{R/D} by the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) of q-crystalline-cech-alexander.
The completed base change − ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) commutes with the totalisation (q-pd-homological-properties (3)), so the left side is computed by the cosimplicial ring D_{J^•,q}(F^•) ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1).
By q-pd-envelope-base-change (b) this is the cosimplicial p-completed PD envelope of J^•/(q−1) ⊂ F^•/(q−1), a Čech–Alexander complex computing RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))) (CR.2).
Sheaf property: D is derived (q−1)-complete (q-pd-homological-properties (1)), so derived Nakayama reduces isomorphy to D/(q−1); combine with Zariski descent for crystalline cohomology (CR.2).
acceptance: D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R p-completely smooth over Z_p: qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D Z_p ≃ RΓ_crys(R/Z_p), the p-completed de Rham complex of R; so qΩ_{R/D} is a q-deformation of de Rham cohomology.
D with q = 1: the statement is the identity, qΩ_{R/D} = RΓ_crys(R/D).
D = A_inf, I = (ξ): qΩ_{R/A_inf} ⊗̂^L A_inf/(q−1) ≃ RΓ_crys(R/(A_inf/(q−1))).

nodes.title: Invariance under q-PD thickenings of the base
nodes.statement: Let (D, J) → (D, I) be a morphism of q-PD pairs that is the identity on the underlying δ-ring, so J ⊂ I are two q-PD ideals of D (for example J = (q−1)). Assume R is p-completely smooth over D/I and choose a p-completely smooth lift R̃ over D/J. Base change along D/J→D/I identifies R̃ with R; the resulting comparison qΩ_{R̃/D}≃qΩ_{R/D} is canonical, the first taken relative to (D, J) and the second relative to (D, I). It is induced by the functor (R̃/D)_{q-crys} → (R/D)_{q-crys} sending a thickening (E, K) with R̃ → E/K to (E, K_I), where K_I is the derived (p,[p]_q)-complete ideal of E generated by K and I·E, with the induced map R = R̃ ⊗̂_{D/J} D/I → E/K_I; this functor does not change the underlying δ-D-algebra.
hypotheses: Both (D, J) and (D, I) are q-PD pairs on the same δ-ring; R̃ ⊗̂_{D/J} D/I ≅ R.
The printed proof writes 'E → E/K ≃ R̃' for an object of the site; objects only carry a map R̃ → E/K, and the functor is defined on all of them as stated here (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
The identification is compatible with Frobenius and multiplication, since it is induced by a functor of sites that is the identity on structure rings.
proofSteps: (E, K + I·E) satisfies condition (1) of q-pd-pair: it holds on K and on the image of I, hence on the ideal they generate by fact (vii) of q-divided-power-operation; the derived complete ideal K_I it generates is then a q-PD ideal by q-pd-homological-properties (4).
The functor is the identity on the rings E, so it induces a map qΩ_{R̃/D} → qΩ_{R/D} of commutative algebras compatible with Frobenius.

Take a presentation P → R̃ and compose with R̃ → R. By inspection of the proof of q-pd-envelope the q-PD envelopes of the two kernels in F^• are the same rings, since the envelope ring only adjoins φ(x_i)/[p]_q for the regular sequence and does not depend on the base ideal; so the Čech–Alexander complex computing qΩ_{R̃/D} also computes qΩ_{R/D}.
acceptance: D = A_inf, J = (q−1) ⊂ I = (ξ): for R̃ p-completely smooth over A_inf/(q−1) lifting R over O_C, qΩ_{R̃/A_inf} ≃ qΩ_{R/A_inf}.
For q = 1 this is the invariance of crystalline cohomology under enlarging the PD ideal of the base.
For J = I and R̃ = R the identification is the identity.

nodes.title: q-crystalline and prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{D/I, φ_D} D/([p]_q) be the p-completed base change of R along the map D/I → D/([p]_q) induced by φ_D (it exists because φ_D(I) ⊂ [p]_q D); it is a p-completely smooth D/([p]_q)-algebra. Let Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} be the prismatic cohomology of R^{(1)} relative to the bounded prism (D, ([p]_q)). Then there is a canonical isomorphism α : Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}. The map α is induced by the functor (R/D)_{q-crys} → (R^{(1)}/D)_Δ sending (E, J) to the prism (E, ([p]_q)) with the map R^{(1)} → E/([p]_q) obtained by linearising R → E/J → E/([p]_q), the second map being induced by φ_E. By construction α is a map of commutative algebra objects of D(D), compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms and natural in R and in (D, I).
hypotheses: (D, I) is a q-PD pair; R is p-completely smooth over D/I.
The Frobenius twist R^{(1)} is part of the statement: R itself is not an algebra over D/([p]_q) unless q = 1.
The printed proof writes 'E → E/J ≅ R'; objects carry only a map R → E/J, which suffices (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).

The printed proof identifies the source and the target of α modulo q − 1 with crystalline cohomology and does not say that the reduction of α is that identification; step 5 supplies this (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E66).
The reduction to I = (q−1) uses a lift of R to a p-completely smooth D/(q−1)-algebra, which the source uses implicitly.
proofSteps: Construction of α: for (E, J) in the site, φ_E(J) ⊂ [p]_q E, so φ_E induces a φ_D-linear map R → E/J → E/([p]_q), hence a D-linear map R^{(1)} → E/([p]_q) and an object of the prismatic site of R^{(1)} over (D, ([p]_q)); evaluating the prismatic structure sheaf gives α.

Reduction to I = (q−1): lift R to a p-completely smooth D/(q−1)-algebra R̃ (the kernel of D/(q−1) → D/I consists of elements f with f^p ∈ p·D/(q−1), so smooth algebras lift; DD.1) and apply q-pd-thickening-invariance; R̃^{(1)} = R^{(1)} because φ_D factors through D/I.
It suffices to prove that α is an isomorphism after (p,[p]_q)-completed base change to D/(q−1) (q-pd-homological-properties (2)).

D → D/(q−1) is a map of bounded prisms (D, ([p]_q)) → (D/(q−1), (p)); by PR.1's prismatic-base-change, Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) ≃ Δ_{R̄^{(1)}/(D/(q−1))} = φ^*Δ_{R̄/(D/(q−1))} with R̄ = R/p; by PR.1's crystalline-comparison this is RΓ_crys(R̄/(D/(q−1))) = RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))), which is qΩ_{R/D} ⊗̂^L_D D/(q−1) by q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison.

The reduction of α is this composite: both α and the comparison map of PR.1's crystalline-comparison (general case of BS22 Theorem 5.2) are induced by sending a (q-)PD thickening E, whose ideal is carried by φ into the prism ideal, to the prism E; the equality is checked on the Čech–Alexander complexes of q-crystalline-cech-alexander and their reductions.
acceptance: D = Z_p[[q−1]], I = (q−1), R p-completely smooth over Z_p: R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p] and Δ_{R^{(1)}/D} ≃ qΩ_{R/D}.
D = A_inf, I = (ξ): R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A_inf, φ} A_inf and Δ_{R^{(1)}/A_inf} = φ^*Δ_{R/A_inf}, the prismatic cohomology relative to (A_inf, (ξ)) pulled back along φ.
q = 1: the statement is the crystalline comparison of PR.1 for the PD ideal I.
R = D/I: both sides are D and α is the identity.
