nodes.title: Framed D-algebras and framed q-PD data
nodes.statement: Fix a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]] and a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra R. A framed D-algebra is a pair (P, S) of a derived (p,[p]_q)-complete D-algebra P and a set S with elements X_s ∈ P (s ∈ S) such that the framing □ : D[X_s : s ∈ S]^∧ → P is (p,[p]_q)-completely ind-étale; then P is (p,[p]_q)-completely ind-smooth over D. This is the (p, q−1)-complete case, over the base ring D with its element q, of the framed algebras of QWittVectors:QW.6, and the following are imported from QW.6, not constructed here: the pairwise commuting D-algebra automorphisms γ_s of P, determined by γ_s(X_s) = qX_s, γ_s(X_t) = X_t for t ≠ s and γ_s ≡ id modulo (q−1)X_s; the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s}(f) = (γ_s(f) − f)/((q−1)X_s); the twisted Leibniz rule; the framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D}, the Koszul complex of the ∇_{q,s}; and its reduction modulo q − 1 to the de Rham complex. PR.6 adds: (i) the unique δ-D-algebra structures on D[S]^∧ and on P with δ(X_s) = 0 for all s, compatible along □, for which every γ_s is a δ-D-algebra automorphism; (ii) P is flat over A, so (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on P; (iii) retain a chosen framing (P,S) and a D-algebra presentation P→R. Writing J for its kernel, these data constitute the framed q-PD datum. A morphism of framed q-PD data (P, S, J) → (P′, S′, J′) is a D-algebra map P → P′ together with an injective map S → S′, s ↦ s′, such that X_s ↦ X_{s′}, carrying J into J′.
hypotheses: D is flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]]: the standing assumption of BS22 §16.3.

The source writes 'p-completely ind-smooth' and 'p-completely ind-étale'. The unique extension of γ_s uses that (q−1)X_s is topologically nilpotent, which holds for the (p, q−1)-adic topology and fails for the p-adic one; the conditions are therefore (p,[p]_q)-complete ones, as the source itself writes in Remark 16.16 and at the end of Construction 16.20 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E65).

Ownership (RT-AREA-etale/28): framed algebras, γ_s, ∇_{q,s}, the twisted Leibniz rule, the framed q-de Rham Koszul complex and its reduction modulo q − 1 belong to QWittVectors:QW.6 in the general form over an I-completely étale framing, I = (q−1) or (p, q−1). This node imports the (p, q−1)-complete case and adds only (i)–(iii).

A morphism of framed q-PD data is injective on coordinates (the map S → S′ with X_s ↦ X_{s′} is injective); it need not be étale. Without injectivity the map does not commute with the q-derivatives: for D⟨X_0,X_1⟩ → D⟨X⟩, ∇_q(X_0X_1) ↦ 2X dX but ∇_q(X²) = (1+q)X dX.
proofSteps: Import from QW.6 the framed algebra (P, S) with its automorphisms and q-derivatives, for the base ring D, the element q and the ideal (p, q−1): the automorphism of D[S]^∧ scaling X_s by q is congruent to the identity modulo the topologically nilpotent element (q−1)X_s, so it extends uniquely along the completely ind-étale framing (Construction 16.19).

(i) D[S] has the δ-D-algebra structure with δ(X_s) = 0, that is φ(X_s) = X_s^p; it extends uniquely to the completion and along the completely ind-étale map □ (BS22 Lemma 2.18; equivalently, P being p-torsion-free, the framed Frobenius lift of QW.6 gives a δ-structure by PR.0's torsionfree-frobenius-equivalence). γ_s is a δ-map on D[S]^∧ because δ(qX_s) = 0, and on P by uniqueness of the extension.
(ii) P is (p,[p]_q)-completely flat over D and derived complete, D is flat over the noetherian ring A, so P is flat over A (DD.1); hence q − 1 and X_s are nonzerodivisors on P.
(iii) The kernel J of P → R is, locally on Spf(P), generated by I and a filtered colimit of completely regular sequences relative to D, so q-pd-envelope (3) applies to (P, J).
acceptance: One polynomial coordinate: P = D⟨X⟩, S = {X}: γ(X^n) = q^n X^n and ∇_q(X^n) = [n]_q X^{n−1}.
A torus: P = D⟨X^{±1}⟩ with γ(X^n) = q^n X^n for n ∈ Z and logarithmic q-derivative (γ − 1)/(q−1).
Two framings: on D⟨T⟩ the coordinates T and T + 1 give automorphisms with γ^{T}(T) = qT and γ^{T+1}(T) = qT + (q−1).
S = ∅ and P = D: the framed q-PD datum (D, ∅, I) of R = D/I.

nodes.title: Extension of the automorphisms γ_s to the q-PD envelope
nodes.statement: Let (P, S, J) be a framed q-PD datum (so D is flat over A). For each s ∈ S the automorphism γ_s of P extends uniquely to an automorphism of the q-PD envelope D_{J,q}(P) that is congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s. The extensions are δ-D-algebra automorphisms and commute pairwise; (q−1)X_s is a nonzerodivisor on D_{J,q}(P), so the q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} := (γ_s − 1)/((q−1)X_s) are defined on D_{J,q}(P) and commute; and they lift the derivations ∂/∂X_s of the p-completed PD envelope D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) of P/(q−1) → R.
hypotheses: (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum over a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A.
This lemma and the resulting q-derivatives on D_{J,q}(P) are kept by PR.6 (RT-AREA-etale/28); the q-derivatives on P itself are QW.6's.
The source prints 'as in Construction 16.10'; Lemma 16.10 is meant (registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E27).
proofSteps: It suffices to extend γ_s to an endomorphism of D_{J,q}(P) congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s; such an endomorphism of a derived complete ring is an automorphism.

Consider P → P → D_{J,q}(P), the first map being γ_s. All rings are A-flat, so by the universal property of the envelope as a free δ-algebra (q-pd-envelope) it suffices that φ(γ_s(f)) ∈ [p]_q·D_{J,q}(P) for f ∈ J. Write γ_s(f) = f + (q−1)X_s·g with g ∈ P; then φ(γ_s(f)) = φ(f) + [p]_q·(q−1)·X_s^p·φ(g), using φ(q−1) = (q−1)[p]_q and δ(X_s) = 0.

The same formula shows that the extension is congruent to the identity modulo (q−1)X_s. Uniqueness and commutation: D_{J,q}(P) is topologically generated as a δ-P-algebra by the elements φ(f)/[p]_q, f ∈ J, and is [p]_q-torsion-free.

Lifting ∂/∂X_s: identify D_{J,q}(P)/(q−1) with the p-completed PD envelope (q-pd-envelope-base-change (b)) and reduce to the statement on P/(q−1), which is QW.6's reduction modulo q − 1, by torsion-freeness and density.
acceptance: For J = (q−1)P the envelope is P and the extension is γ_s itself.

nodes.title: The q-de Rham complex of a framed q-PD datum
nodes.statement: Let (P, S, J) be a framed q-PD datum over a q-PD pair (D, I) with D flat over A. Its q-de Rham complex is the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms ∇_{q,s} (s ∈ S) of the q-PD envelope: qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} := (D_{J,q}(P) → D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂_P Ω^1_{P/D} → D_{J,q}(P) ⊗̂_P Ω^2_{P/D} → …), where Ω^1_{P/D} is the completed direct sum of the P·dX_s and ∇_q(f) = Σ_s ∇_{q,s}(f) dX_s; it is a cochain complex of D-modules, and an instance of the Koszul complex of commuting q-derivations of QWittVectors:QW.6, applied to the ring D_{J,q}(P) with the elements X_s and the automorphisms of gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope. Properties. (a) If J = I·P with I = (q−1), then D_{J,q}(P) = P and the complex is the framed q-de Rham complex qΩ^{*,□}_{P/D} of QW.6. (b) Functoriality: a morphism of framed q-PD data (P, S, J) → (P′, S′, J′), which by definition is injective on coordinates, induces a morphism of complexes qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}; a D-algebra map identifying two coordinates (for instance a codegeneracy of the Čech nerve) does not. (c) Reduction: the complex modulo q − 1 is the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of J/(q−1) ⊂ P/(q−1). (d) Frobenius: ∇_{q,s}∘φ = [p]_q·X_s^{p−1}·φ∘∇_{q,s}, so the maps f·dX_{s_1}⋯dX_{s_i} ↦ φ(f)·∏_j([p]_q X_{s_j}^{p−1})·dX_{s_1}⋯dX_{s_i} form a φ_D-semilinear endomorphism of the complex. (e) Toric form: if the X_s are units of P the complex is isomorphic to the Koszul complex of the logarithmic q-derivatives X_s∇_{q,s} = (γ_s − 1)/(q−1), which is η_{(q−1)} applied to the Koszul complex of the endomorphisms γ_s − 1 (the décalage of AInfCohomology:AI.1 on (q−1)-torsion-free complexes).
hypotheses: (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum; D is flat over A.
For infinite S the complex is the completed filtered colimit over finite subsets of S.
(b): the source prints the last sentence of Construction 16.20 with the framing A[{X_s}] → P; the framing D[{X_s}] → P is meant (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E62).
(d) is not printed in §16; it follows from φ∘γ_s = γ_s∘φ and φ((q−1)X_s) = [p]_q(q−1)X_s^p, and is what the Frobenius compatibility in Theorem 17.2 uses.
The Koszul complex of commuting endomorphisms and the identification in (e) are AI.1's (BMS1 Definition 7.1, Lemma 7.9); the Koszul complex of q-derivations is QW.6's.
proofSteps: Extend the γ_s to D_{J,q}(P) and form the commuting q-derivatives ∇_{q,s} (gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope); take their Koszul complex (QW.6, AI.1).

(b): let α : D_{J,q}(P) → D_{J′,q}(P′) be induced by P → P′ and the universal property. For t ∈ S′ outside the image of S one has γ_t∘α = α: the identity holds on the étale coordinates X_s, hence on P by complete étaleness of the framing, and on the envelope because it is [p]_q-torsion-free and generated over P by the elements φ(f)/[p]_q. So α commutes with the q-derivatives indexed by S and is killed by the others.
(c): q-pd-envelope-base-change (b) and the last statement of gamma-extension-to-q-pd-envelope.

(d): apply φ to (q−1)X_s∇_{q,s}(f) = γ_s(f) − f and cancel the nonzerodivisor (q−1)X_s. (e): X_s is a unit, so the Koszul complexes of ∇_{q,s} and X_s∇_{q,s} are isomorphic; then use η_f Kos(g_i) ≅ Kos(g_i/f) for f dividing all g_i (AI.1).
acceptance: One polynomial coordinate: P = D⟨X⟩, J = (q−1)P with I = (q−1): the complex is D⟨X⟩ → D⟨X⟩dX, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^{n−1}dX; for D = Z_p[[q−1]] its H^0 is D and its H^1 is the completed direct sum of the D/[n]_q·X^{n−1}dX, n ≥ 1.
A torus: P = D⟨X^{±1}⟩: the complex is D⟨X^{±1}⟩ → D⟨X^{±1}⟩ dlog X, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^n dlog X, with [n]_q = (q^n − 1)/(q − 1) for n ∈ Z.
S = ∅: the complex is D in degree 0.

nodes.title: q-de Rham and q-crystalline comparison
nodes.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A = Z_p[[q−1]], R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra and (P, S, J) a framed q-PD datum with P/J ≅ R. Then there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism qΩ_{R/D} ≃ qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}: the q-de Rham complex of the framed q-PD datum computes q-crystalline cohomology. The identification is natural for morphisms of framed q-PD data injective on coordinate sets lying over maps R → R′, and it carries the Frobenius φ_{R/D} to the Frobenius of framed-q-de-rham-complex (d).
hypotheses: (D, I) is a q-PD pair with D flat over A; (P, S, J) is a framed q-PD datum for R.

The source states the quasi-isomorphism; naturality in the framed datum and the compatibility with Frobenius are visible in its proof (the bicomplex is functorial and carries the Frobenius) and are used in Theorem 17.2.
For q = 1 this is the comparison of crystalline cohomology with the de Rham complex of a PD envelope, owned by CrystallineCohomology:CR.2.
proofSteps: Let P^• be the completed Čech nerve of D → P; the coordinates S define coordinates S^n on P^n by coproducts, and J^n = ker(P^n → P → R) gives framed q-PD data (P^n, S^n, J^n). The coface maps are morphisms of framed q-PD data (injective on coordinates); the codegeneracies are not and do not commute with ∇_q. Apply framed-q-de-rham-complex to get complexes M^{n,*} = qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J^n,q}(P^n)} with maps of complexes for the cofaces; each row M^{•,i} = D_{J^•,q}(P^•) ⊗̂ Ω^i_{P^•/D} is a cosimplicial D-module. Form the double complex with horizontal differential the alternating sum of the cofaces. In a semi-cosimplicial module whose cofaces are all isomorphisms the cofaces of each level coincide, which is what step 4 uses.
Rows: for i > 0 the cosimplicial D-module M^{•,i} is homotopy equivalent to 0 as a cosimplicial module, by the standard argument for the crystalline case (Stacks project, Tag 07JP; CR.2).

Columns: every face map P^i → P^j induces a quasi-isomorphism M^{i,*} → M^{j,*}: modulo q − 1 this is the PD Poincaré lemma (framed-q-de-rham-complex (c); CR.2), and the terms are derived (q−1)-complete and (q−1)-torsion-free, so derived Nakayama gives the claim.

Therefore the complex attached to the cosimplicial module M^{•,0} is quasi-isomorphic to the column M^{0,*}. The former is the small Čech–Alexander complex of q-crystalline-cech-alexander (5) and computes qΩ_{R/D}; the latter is qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D}.

Naturality and Frobenius: the bicomplex is functorial in the framed datum by framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) and carries the Frobenius of (d), which on row 0 is the Frobenius of the δ-rings D_{J^•,q}(P^•).
acceptance: One polynomial coordinate: qΩ_{Z_p⟨X⟩/Z_p[[q−1]]} is computed by Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩ → Z_p[[q−1]]⟨X⟩dX, X^n ↦ [n]_q X^{n−1}dX.
A torus over A_inf: qΩ_{O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩/A_inf} is computed by A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A_inf⟨x^{±1}⟩ dlog x, x^n ↦ [n]_q x^n dlog x.
Modulo q − 1 the quasi-isomorphism reduces to the statement that the de Rham complex of the p-completed PD envelope of P/(q−1) → R computes RΓ_crys(R/(D/(q−1))).

nodes.title: Change of framing and the cocycle identity
nodes.statement: Let (D, I) be a q-PD pair with D flat over A and R a p-completely smooth D/I-algebra. Let (P, S, J) and (P′, S′, J′) be two framed q-PD data for R; the case P = P′ with two coordinate systems is included. Put P″ = P ⊗̂_D P′ (derived (p,[p]_q)-completed), S″ = S ⊔ S′ and J″ = ker(P″ → R). Then (P″, S″, J″) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and the two morphisms of framed q-PD data induce quasi-isomorphisms qΩ^{*,□}_{D_{J,q}(P)/D} → qΩ^{*,□″}_{D_{J″,q}(P″)/D} ← qΩ^{*,□′}_{D_{J′,q}(P′)/D}. The resulting isomorphism c_{□,□′} in D(D) equals the composite of the identifications of q-de-rham-comparison with qΩ_{R/D}. Consequently c_{□,□} = id and c_{□′,□″}∘c_{□,□′} = c_{□,□″} for three framed data (the cocycle identity); the isomorphisms are compatible with Frobenius and with maps R → R′ covered by morphisms of framed data; the framed q-de Rham complex is independent of the framing up to canonical isomorphism in D(D); and on a smooth p-adic formal scheme 𝔛 over D/I the complexes of framed affine charts descend to the Zariski sheaf qΩ_{𝔛/D} of q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison.
hypotheses: Both data are framed q-PD data for the same R over the same q-PD pair, D flat over A.
The complexes of two framings are different complexes; only their images in D(D), with Frobenius and multiplication, are identified.

The statement is what the source calls independence 'up to canonical quasi-isomorphism' of the framing; it is deduced from Construction 16.20 and the proof of Theorem 16.22, where the same argument is applied to the face maps of the Čech nerve.
proofSteps: (P″, S″) is a framed D-algebra: the framing is the completed tensor product of the two framings; J″ is the kernel of the surjection P″ → R.
The maps P → P″ ← P′ are morphisms of framed q-PD data, so framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) gives the two maps of complexes.

They are quasi-isomorphisms: modulo q − 1 they are the comparison maps between the PD de Rham complexes of two embeddings of R and of their product, quasi-isomorphisms by the independence of the embedding in CR.2; the terms are derived (q−1)-complete and (q−1)-torsion-free, so derived Nakayama applies. This is the column argument of the proof of Theorem 16.22.

Agreement with q-de-rham-comparison: the bicomplex of that proof is functorial in the framed datum, so the two maps commute with the identifications with qΩ_{R/D}. The cocycle identity and c_{□,□} = id follow formally.
Descent: qΩ_{−/D} is a Zariski sheaf (q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison) and the identifications are natural for localisation.
acceptance: Two framings: R = Z_p⟨T⟩ over Z_p[[q−1]] with coordinates T and T + 1. The complexes differ, ∇^{T+1}(T²) − ∇^{T}(T²) = q − 1, and are identified through the datum on Z_p[[q−1]]⟨T_0, T_1⟩{φ(T_1 − T_0)/[p]_q}^∧ with coordinates T_0 and T_1 + 1.
Three framings T, T + 1, T + 2 of Z_p⟨T⟩: the three isomorphisms satisfy the cocycle identity.
Equal framings give the identity.

nodes.title: The framed q-de Rham complex of a smooth Z_p-algebra and prismatic cohomology
nodes.statement: Let A = Z_p[[q−1]] with the q-de Rham prism (A, ([p]_q)), and let R be a p-completely smooth Z_p-algebra with a p-completely étale framing □ : Z_p⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ → R. Let P be the (p, q−1)-completely étale A⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩-algebra lifting R (so P/(q−1) = R), framed by T_1, …, T_d, and let qΩ_R^□ := qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} be its (p, q−1)-completed framed q-de Rham complex (QWittVectors:QW.6). Let R^{(1)} := R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p], the p-completed base change of R along Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p]. Then there are canonical isomorphisms in D(A), compatible with Frobenius, qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = RΓ_Δ(Spf(R^{(1)})/A). Consequently qΩ_R^□ is independent of the framing □ up to canonical quasi-isomorphism, is functorial in R as an object of D(A), and qΩ_R^□ ⊗^L_A A/(q−1) is the p-completed de Rham complex of R over Z_p. Scope: this is a statement for one prime p over the (p, q−1)-complete base Z_p[[q−1]]; it does not produce a theory over Z[[q−1]] or over the Habiro ring. The gluing over all primes is owned by HabiroCohomologyFoundations HQ.1–HQ.2.
hypotheses: R is p-completely smooth over Z_p with a p-completely étale framing; the prism is (Z_p[[q−1]], ([p]_q)), not (Z_p[[q−1]], (q−1)).
The base change to Z_p[ζ_p] is part of the statement: prismatic cohomology is taken of R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂ Z_p[ζ_p], not of R.
The framed complex qΩ_R^□ itself is QW.6's object; this node proves its comparison.
proofSteps: (A, (q−1)) is a q-PD pair (smallest-largest-q-pd-ideals (c)) and A is flat over itself. (P, {T_i}, (q−1)P) is a framed q-PD datum for R, and D_{J,q}(P) = P because (P, (q−1)P) is already a q-PD pair, P being completely flat over A; so its q-de Rham complex is qΩ^{*,□}_{P/A} (framed-q-de-rham-complex (a)).
q-de-rham-comparison gives qΩ_R^□ ≃ qΩ_{R/A}.
q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison with I = (q−1) gives qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A}; here φ_A induces Z_p = A/(q−1) → A/([p]_q) = Z_p[ζ_p], the structure map, so R^{(1)} = R ⊗̂_{Z_p} Z_p[ζ_p].

Independence of □ and functoriality: change-of-framing. Reduction modulo q − 1: q-crystalline-crystalline-comparison and the identification of RΓ_crys(R/Z_p) with the de Rham complex of the smooth lift (CR.2).
acceptance: One polynomial coordinate: R = Z_p⟨T⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T⟩ → A⟨T⟩dT), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^{n−1}dT. Modulo [p]_q the coefficient [n]_ζ is a unit for p ∤ n and 0 for p | n, so H^0 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩ and H^1 = Z_p[ζ_p]⟨T^p⟩·T^{p−1}dT, which are R^{(1)} and Ω^1_{R^{(1)}/Z_p[ζ_p]} through T ↦ T^p, as the Hodge–Tate comparison for Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} predicts.
A torus: R = Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩: qΩ_R^□ = (A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩ dlog T), T^n ↦ [n]_q T^n dlog T.
Two framings T and T + 1 of Z_p⟨T⟩ give canonically isomorphic objects of D(A).

nodes.title: The all-coordinates comparison map from q-crystalline cohomology to AΩ
nodes.statement: Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C) with q = [ε] and ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)) of ainf-q-pd-pair. Let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra that is very small: R/p is generated over O_C/p by units, and R is small, that is, there are units x_1, …, x_n of R defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. Put S = R^× and let C_S be the filtered poset of finite subsets Σ ⊂ S such that A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ → R, x_s ↦ s, is surjective. For Σ ∈ C_S let P_Σ = A[x_s^{±1} : s ∈ Σ]^∧ be the formal torus over A, with δ(x_s) = 0 and the automorphisms γ_s scaling x_s by q, and J_Σ = ker(P_Σ → R); (P_Σ, Σ, J_Σ) is a framed q-PD datum. (1) The q-side. qΩ_{R/A} is computed by the complex colim_{Σ ∈ C_S} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}_{s∈Σ}), which is functorial in the very small algebra R. (2) The AΩ-side. Let Δ_Σ = ∏_{s∈Σ} Z_p(1) and let R_{Σ,∞} be the p-completed integral closure of R in the pro-étale Δ_Σ-torsor over R[1/p] obtained by extracting all p-power roots of the x_s; R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid, and σ_s denotes the automorphism of A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) induced by the s-th basis vector of Δ_Σ. Then AΩ_R is computed by colim_{Σ ∈ C_S} η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}_{s∈Σ}), and already by each term whose Σ contains units x_1, …, x_n defining a formally étale map O_C⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_n^{±1}⟩ → R. (3) The map. For each Σ ∈ C_S there is a unique map of δ-A-algebras μ_0 : D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) extending the δ-map P_Σ → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}), x_s ↦ [(s, s^{1/p}, s^{1/p²}, …)]; it intertwines γ_s with σ_s and is compatible with enlarging Σ. It induces maps Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {∇_{q,s}}) ≅ η_{q−1} Kos_c(D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ); {γ_s − 1}) → η_{q−1} Kos_c(A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}); {σ_s − 1}), and in the colimit over Σ the comparison map μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R. It is a map of E_1-A-algebras (represented by differential graded algebras), natural in the very small algebra R and compatible with the Frobenius endomorphisms. For a general p-completely smooth O_C-algebra, and for smooth formal O_C-schemes, μ is obtained by gluing, the very small affine opens being a basis. Naturality in R is asserted for maps injective on the chosen coordinate sets; an arbitrary map identifying two units requires a different family-indexed construction.
hypotheses: C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}; R is p-completely smooth over O_C and very small.
The colimit in (2) is over C_S; the printed index set is a misprint registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E28.

AΩ_R, the perfectoid rings R_{Σ,∞}, the identification of continuous cohomology of Δ_Σ with a Koszul complex and the statement that the complexes in (2) compute AΩ_R are owned by AInfCohomology AI.3 and AI.4 (BMS1 Lemma 7.3, Theorem 9.4 (iii), and the all-coordinates construction).
Kos_c denotes the completed Koszul complex: for the q-derivatives it is the complex of framed-q-de-rham-complex.

The source asserts that R_{Σ,∞} is perfectoid for every Σ in C_S by a general reference, and notes that the subset of those Σ containing a framing is cofinal and suffices; for these the perfectoidness follows from almost purity (AI.3, AI.4). The plan uses this cofinal subset.
The map is constructed without any choice of coordinates: all finite generating sets of units are used at once.
proofSteps: (1): q-de-rham-comparison for each Σ, the functoriality of framed-q-de-rham-complex (b) in Σ, and a filtered colimit.

(2): import from AI.3 and AI.4. Each Σ containing a framing gives a complex computing AΩ_R by BMS1 Theorem 9.4 (iii) and the enlargement criterion quoted in the source; the continuous cohomology of Δ_Σ is the Koszul complex by BMS1 Lemma 7.3 (AI.1).

(3), the map μ_0: let P_Σ → P_{Σ,∞} be the (p, ξ)-completed perfection (PR.0's prism-perfection). It is a perfect, completely flat δ-A-algebra, so P_{Σ,∞}/ξ is perfectoid, obtained from P_Σ/ξ by extracting p-power roots of the x_s, and P_{Σ,∞} ≅ A_inf(P_{Σ,∞}/ξ) (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings). Composing with A_inf of the map to R_{Σ,∞} gives a δ-map P_Σ → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) lying over R → R_{Σ,∞}. Since A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) → R_{Σ,∞} is a q-PD thickening (q-pd-homological-properties (5) applied to A → A_inf(R_{Σ,∞})), the universal property of q-pd-envelope extends it uniquely to μ_0.
Equivariance: σ_s∘μ_0 and μ_0∘γ_s are both the extension, by the universal property, of maps out of P_Σ that agree; so they coincide.

The Koszul map: the x_s are units, so the Koszul complex of the ∇_{q,s} is η_{q−1} of the Koszul complex of the γ_s − 1 (framed-q-de-rham-complex (e)); η_{q−1} is functorial for μ_0 on (q−1)-torsion-free complexes (AI.1). Multiplicativity: both Koszul complexes are differential graded algebras and μ_0 is a ring map (BMS1 Lemmas 7.5 and 6.13; AI.1). Frobenius: μ_0 is a δ-map.
acceptance: A torus: R = O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩, Σ = {x}: J_Σ = (ξ), D_{J_Σ,q}(P_Σ) = P_Σ = A⟨x^{±1}⟩, A_inf(R_{Σ,∞}) = A⟨x^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and μ_0 is the inclusion; μ_R is the injective quasi-isomorphism of BMS1 Lemma 9.6.
R = O_C, Σ = ∅: both complexes are A in degree 0 and μ_R is the identity.
Enlarging Σ by a unit that is a product of the given ones changes neither side up to the canonical quasi-isomorphisms.

nodes.title: A criterion for comparison maps to be isomorphisms
nodes.statement: (a) Work over a commutative A, choose a regular element d, and assume R is smooth over A/d. Take commutative derived A-algebras E,F, complete for d, whose reductions are coconnective and have strictly graded commutative cohomology rings. Choose structure maps η_E:R→H^0(E/d), η_F:R→H^0(F/d). Require that the maps (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR) → (H^*(E/d), β_d) and (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR) → (H^*(F/d), β_d), induced by the universal property of the de Rham complex, are isomorphisms; here β_d is the Bockstein differential. Then every commutative A-algebra map α : E → F that intertwines η_E with η_F is an isomorphism. (b) The same holds if (A, (d)) is a bounded prism, R is p-completely smooth over A/d (with the p-completed de Rham complex), and E and F are derived (p, d)-complete. (c) In both cases it suffices that α is a map in D(A) for which H^*(α/d) is a homomorphism of graded rings; in particular the criterion applies to maps of E_1-algebras.
hypotheses: d is a nonzerodivisor; E, F are derived d-complete (resp. (p, d)-complete); E/d, F/d coconnective with strictly graded commutative cohomology rings.
(c) is what the printed proof uses, and it is the form in which the proof of Theorem 17.2 applies the lemma, the comparison map being a priori a map of E_1-algebras (Remark 17.3).
The Bockstein differential and the map from the de Rham complex are those of PR.1's hodge-tate-comparison-map and AI.1.
proofSteps: α is an isomorphism if and only if α/d : E/d → F/d is, by derived d-completeness (resp. (p, d)-completeness) and derived Nakayama (DD.1); so it suffices that H^*(α/d) is an isomorphism.

H^*(α/d) is a map of graded A/d-algebras that commutes with the Bockstein differentials (naturality of β_d), so it is a map of commutative differential graded algebras (H^*(E/d), β_d) → (H^*(F/d), β_d).

It intertwines η_E with η_F, so by the universal property of the de Rham complex it forms a commutative triangle with the two maps from (Ω^*_{R/(A/d)}, d_dR); these are isomorphisms, hence so is H^*(α/d).
acceptance: E = F = Δ_{R/A} over a bounded oriented prism, with η the Hodge–Tate structure map: every η-compatible endomorphism is an automorphism.
The identity of E satisfies the hypothesis and the conclusion.
The unit map A → Δ_{R/A} for R ≠ A/d is not an isomorphism: A does not satisfy the de Rham hypothesis for R.

nodes.title: Comparison with AΩ
nodes.statement: Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε], ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q), and let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra. Let AΩ_R be the complex of Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze (AInfCohomology:AI.3). Then the comparison map μ_R : qΩ_{R/A} → AΩ_R of ainf-omega-comparison-map is an isomorphism, and AΩ_R ≃ qΩ_{R/A} ≃ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}. Here qΩ_{R/A} is taken relative to the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)); R^{(1)} = R ⊗_{A, φ} A is the Frobenius twist, an algebra over A/([p]_q); Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} is prismatic cohomology relative to the prism (A, ([p]_q)); and Δ_{R/A} is prismatic cohomology relative to the perfect prism (A, (ξ)) = (A_inf, ker θ). All these maps are isomorphisms of E_∞-A-algebras compatible with the Frobenius, natural in R. The Frobenius pullback is essential: φ_A is an automorphism of A, so φ_A^* only twists the A-module structure, but AΩ_R is not isomorphic to Δ_{R/A} in D(A) in general. (Remark 17.3.) The construction gives an isomorphism of E_1-A-algebras, natural in R and compatible with Frobenius; it is upgraded to an isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras by left Kan extension to quasiregular semiperfectoid R-algebras, where it is an isomorphism of associative rings between discrete commutative rings, and then quasisyntomic descent.
hypotheses: C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, with a fixed compatible system of p-power roots of 1; the introduction of the source states the result for C algebraically closed, §17 and BMS1 §§8–9 in this generality.
R is a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra; AΩ_R is the value on Spf(R) of the complex AΩ of AI.3.
The check that μ_R intertwines the two Hodge–Tate structure maps is left to the reader in the source (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E67); step 3 carries it out by reduction to the torus.
The Hodge–Tate specialisation of AΩ used in step 2 carries the Frobenius twist that BMS1 Theorem 9.2 leaves implicit: R is an A_inf-algebra through θ̃ there.
proofSteps: Second isomorphism: q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison for the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)). The Frobenius φ_A is an isomorphism of prisms (A, (ξ)) → (A, ([p]_q)) carrying R to R^{(1)}, so Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} by PR.1's prismatic-base-change.

μ_R is an isomorphism by hodge-tate-comparison-criterion (b), (c) with d = [p]_q: on the q-side, the Hodge–Tate comparison for Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} (PR.1) gives η_{qΩ} : R^{(1)} → H^0(qΩ_{R/A}/[p]_q) inducing (Ω^*_{R^{(1)}/(A/[p]_q)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(qΩ_{R/A}/[p]_q), β); on the AΩ-side, AΩ_R/[p]_q ≃ Ω̃_{R^{(1)}} (BMS1 Theorem 9.2) and the Hodge–Tate comparison for Ω̃ (BMS1 Theorem 8.3) give η_{AΩ} with the same property (AI.4).

μ_R intertwines η_{qΩ} with η_{AΩ}: both are ring maps out of R^{(1)}, natural in R, so for very small R it suffices to compare them on the images of the units s ∈ R^×, which topologically generate; each unit is the image of x under a map O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩ → R, so by naturality the check reduces to the torus, where μ is the inclusion A⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A⟨x^{±1/p^∞}⟩ and both maps are computed: on the q-side the coordinate of R^{(1)} goes to the class of φ(x) = x^p by the construction of q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison; on the AΩ-side the class of x^p reduces along θ̃ to x, since θ̃([x^♭]^p) = θ([x^♭]) = x.
Frobenius: μ_0 is a map of δ-rings, and both Frobenius endomorphisms are induced by the Frobenius lifts on the Koszul complexes (ainf-omega-comparison-map; AI.3 for AΩ).

E_∞ upgrade (Remark 17.3): left Kan extend both functors from p-completely smooth R-algebras to quasiregular semiperfectoid ones (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3, PR.2's derived-prismatic-cohomology). There the prismatic side is a discrete commutative ring (PR.2's qrsp-prism), so the E_1-isomorphism is an isomorphism of associative rings between discrete commutative rings, hence of commutative rings and of E_∞-rings. Quasisyntomic descent (PR.2's quasisyntomic-descent, DD.5) returns the isomorphism of E_∞-A-algebras on smooth algebras.
acceptance: R = O_C: all three objects are A_inf.
A torus R = O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩: AΩ_R is computed by A⟨x^{±1}⟩ → A⟨x^{±1}⟩, x^n ↦ [n]_q x^n, so H^1(AΩ_R) is the completed direct sum of the A/[n]_q for n ∈ Z, and the same complex computes φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}.

The twist cannot be dropped: for the torus, H^0(Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/ξ) = R while H^0(AΩ_R ⊗^L_A A/ξ) = O_C (closed functions for the de Rham differential), so there is no isomorphism AΩ_R ≅ Δ_{R/A} in D(A).

nodes.title: The θ and θ̃ specialisations under the AΩ comparison
nodes.statement: In the setting of ainf-omega-comparison let θ : A → O_C be Fontaine's map, with kernel (ξ), and θ̃ := θ∘φ_A^{-1} : A → O_C, with kernel (ξ̃), ξ̃ = φ(ξ) = [p]_q; so θ̃∘φ_A = θ. Under AΩ_R ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}: (a) (Hodge–Tate corner.) AΩ_R ⊗^L_{A,θ̃} O_C ≃ (φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ⊗^L_{A,θ̃} O_C = Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_{A,θ} O_C = Δ̄_{R/A}, the Hodge–Tate cohomology of R relative to (A, (ξ)). The left side is the complex Ω̃_R of BMS1 (AInfCohomology:AI.4). The resulting isomorphism Ω̃_R ≃ Δ̄_{R/A} of commutative O_C-algebras is compatible with the maps from R to H^0 and identifies the two Hodge–Tate isomorphisms of commutative differential graded algebras (Ω^*_{R^{(1)}/(A/[p]_q)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(AΩ_R/[p]_q), β_{[p]_q}) and (Ω^*_{R^{(1)}/(A/[p]_q)}, d_dR) ≅ (H^*(Δ̄_{R^{(1)}/A}), β_{[p]_q}). (b) (de Rham corner.) AΩ_R ⊗^L_{A,θ} O_C ≃ (φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}) ⊗^L_{A,θ} O_C ≃ Ω^*_{R/O_C}, the p-completed de Rham complex, the last isomorphism being the de Rham comparison of PR.3 for the prism (A, (ξ)). (c) The two corners are different: for R = O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩, H^0 of (a) is R and H^0 of (b) is O_C. An identification of AΩ_R with Δ_{R/A} without the Frobenius twist would exchange the Hodge–Tate and de Rham specialisations.
hypotheses: Setting and notation of ainf-omega-comparison; O_C is an A-algebra in two ways, through θ and through θ̃.

(b) is the identification obtained by transporting PR.3's de Rham comparison through the isomorphism of ainf-omega-comparison. Its agreement with the de Rham specialisation of AΩ constructed in AI.4 is not asserted here; it belongs to AInfCohomology:AI.7, which proves agreement of comparison maps with comparison-uniqueness.
Breuil–Kisin twists are trivialised by the generator [p]_q, as in the proof of Theorem 17.2.
proofSteps: (a): base change of the isomorphisms of ainf-omega-comparison along θ̃, and θ̃∘φ_A = θ. The identification of the left side with Ω̃_R is BMS1 Theorem 9.2 (i) (AI.4), in which R is an A-algebra through θ̃.

Compatibility with the maps from R and with the Hodge–Tate isomorphisms: step 3 of ainf-omega-comparison shows that μ_R intertwines η_{qΩ} and η_{AΩ}; both Hodge–Tate isomorphisms are induced from these maps by the universal property of the de Rham complex (PR.1's hodge-tate-comparison; BMS1 Theorem 8.3 with its Bockstein statement, AI.4).
(b): base change along θ and PR.3's de-rham-comparison-general (BS22 Corollary 15.4) for (A, (ξ)): φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ⊗^L_A A/ξ ≅ Ω^*_{R/O_C}.
(c): for the torus, H^0(Δ̄_{R/A}) = R by the Hodge–Tate comparison, and the closed functions of the p-completed de Rham complex of O_C⟨x^{±1}⟩ over O_C are the constants.
acceptance: The square of ring maps θ̃∘φ_A = θ commutes on Teichmüller elements: θ̃([x^p]) = θ([x]).
R = O_C: both corners are O_C.
Torus: the Hodge–Tate corner has H^1 free of rank 1 over R, the de Rham corner has H^1 = completed direct sum of O_C/n·x^n dlog x.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of comparison isomorphisms
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a perfect prism with perfectoid ring R = A/I. Let Sm_R be the category of p-completely smooth R-algebras and C_{Sm_R} the ∞-category of pairs (G, η) where G : Sm_R → D_{(p,I)-comp}(A) is a symmetric monoidal functor and η : id → G ⊗^L_A R is a natural transformation of symmetric monoidal functors Sm_R → D_{p-comp}(R). Prismatic cohomology with the Hodge–Tate structure maps η_S : S → Δ̄_{S/A} is an object Δ_{−/A} of C_{Sm_R}. (Theorem 18.2.) Δ_{−/A} has no nontrivial endomorphisms in C_{Sm_R}: End(Δ_{−/A}) = {1}. No compatibility with the Frobenius is imposed. (Lemma 18.3.) Let rsPerfd_R be the category of R-algebras that are quotients of p-completely flat perfectoid R-algebras by sequences that are p-completely regular relative to R. Suppose that for every S in rsPerfd_R an A-algebra endomorphism ε_S of Δ_{S/A} is given such that ε_S is functorial in S and compatible with the identity of S under η_S : S → Δ̄_{S/A}. Then ε_S = id for all S. (Use for comparison maps.) If an object (G, η_G) of C_{Sm_R} is isomorphic to Δ_{−/A}, the isomorphism is unique and every morphism between the two objects is that isomorphism or its inverse. In particular the isomorphisms of q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison over a q-PD pair whose prism (D, ([p]_q)) is perfect, such as (A_inf, (ξ)), the isomorphism AΩ ≃ φ_A^*Δ_{−/A_inf} of ainf-omega-comparison, and the comparison of PR.3 with the Nygaard complexes of topological Hochschild homology (BS22 Theorem 13.1) are the unique ones compatible with the Hodge–Tate structure maps; they do not depend on coordinates or presentations and are compatible with one another.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a perfect prism, R = A/I the corresponding perfectoid ring.

The theorem is about endomorphisms in the category of pairs (G, η) with the Hodge–Tate structure map, and it imposes no Frobenius compatibility; it is not a statement about automorphisms of a functor to E_∞-A-algebras with φ.

Misprints of the printed proof are registered as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-22/E29 and PrismaticCohomology/E68: the sequence f_1, …, f_r lies in R′, the ring presented is A_inf(R′){g_i/d}^∧, the completeness is (p, d)-adic, and Joyal's identity reads φ^{n+1}(x) = x^{p^{n+1}} + pδ_1(x)^{p^n} + … + p^nδ_n(x)^p + p^{n+1}δ_{n+1}(x).
For the AΩ comparison the perfect prism is (A_inf, ([p]_q)) with A_inf/[p]_q ≅ O_C through θ̃, and R ↦ R^{(1)} identifies the two categories of smooth algebras.
proofSteps: Reduction: every S in Sm_R has a quasisyntomic Čech cover S → S^• with all S^i in rsPerfd_R (DD.5). Derived prismatic cohomology with its Hodge–Tate map defines an object on rsPerfd_R (PR.2's derived-prismatic-cohomology), and by descent (PR.2's quasisyntomic-descent) it suffices to show that this object has no nontrivial endomorphisms. Its values are discrete (PR.2's qrsp-prism), which reduces the theorem to Lemma 18.3.

Perfectoid S: Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(S), so ε_S is an A-algebra endomorphism of A_inf(S); it preserves I·A_inf(S), and it is a δ-map because every endomorphism of a perfect p-complete δ-ring is (PR.0's perfect-delta-rings). So it is an endomorphism of the perfect prism (A_inf(S), I·A_inf(S)) inducing the identity on S, hence the identity (PR.0's perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings).

General S = R′/(f_1, …, f_r): Δ_{S/A} = A_inf(R′){g_1/d, …, g_r/d}^∧ for a distinguished generator d of I and lifts g_i of f_i (PR.2's qrsp-prism, PR.0's regular-prismatic-envelopes). Let K be the kernel of ε_S − id. It is a subring; it is an A_inf(R′)-submodule containing the image of A_inf(R′), because ε_{R′} = id by step 2 and functoriality; and it is saturated for multiplication by p and by every φ^n(d), because the envelope is (p, d)-completely flat over A, so these elements are nonzerodivisors (PR.0's bounded-prism-complete-flatness).

K is derived (p, d)-complete, so it suffices that K contains the elements δ_n(g_i/d) for Joyal's operations δ_n, which topologically generate (PR.0's free-delta-ring). Induction on n: g_i/d ∈ K by d-saturation; φ^{n+1}(g_i/d) ∈ K because φ^{n+1}(d)·φ^{n+1}(g_i/d) = φ^{n+1}(g_i) ∈ K; Joyal's identity expresses p^{n+1}δ_{n+1}(g_i/d) through φ^{n+1}(g_i/d) and powers of the δ_j(g_i/d), j ≤ n, and K is p-saturated.
Use for comparison maps: two morphisms a, b between Δ_{−/A} and G with a an isomorphism differ by the endomorphism a^{-1}b of Δ_{−/A}, which is the identity.

nodes.title: The Nygaard filtration in q-de Rham coordinates
nodes.statement: Let C be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing μ_{p^∞}, A = A_inf(O_C), q = [ε], ξ = φ^{-1}([p]_q) and ξ̃ = [p]_q, as in ainf-q-pd-pair. Let R be a p-completely smooth O_C-algebra with a framing □ : O_C⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ → R that is the p-adic completion of an étale map, and let R̃ be the (p, ξ)-completely étale A⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩-algebra lifting R, with the automorphisms γ_i lifting T_i ↦ qT_i (identity on the other coordinates) and the Frobenius lift φ with φ(T_i) = T_i^p. Let M^• = qΩ^•_{R̃/A} be the framed q-de Rham complex in toric form: the Koszul complex of the commuting endomorphisms ∂_q/∂_q log T_i = (γ_i − 1)/(q − 1) of R̃, with basis the forms d_q log T_{j_1} ⋯ d_q log T_{j_n} in degree n, and with the φ_A-semilinear endomorphism φ_M given on degree n by f·ω ↦ ξ̃^n·φ(f)·ω for a basis form ω. Then: (1) M^• ≅ qΩ_{R/A} ≅ φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} ≅ AΩ_R in D(A), compatibly with the Frobenius endomorphisms. (2) φ_M(M^n) ⊂ ξ̃^n M^n for every n, and the map M^n/ξM^n → H^n(M^•/ξ̃M^•), x ↦ class of φ_M(x)/ξ̃^n, is bijective. (3) The relative Nygaard filtration of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} (PR.3) is represented by the subcomplexes N^{≥i}M^• = ξ^{max(i − •, 0)} M^•, that is ξ^i R̃ → ξ^{i−1} R̃^{⊕d} → ⋯ → ξ M^{i−1} → M^i → M^{i+1} → ⋯, with filtered Frobenius φ_M : N^{≥i}M^• → ξ̃^i M^•; moreover N^{≥i}M^n = {x ∈ M^n : φ_M(x) ∈ ξ̃^i M^n}. (4) Under (1) the map AΩ_R → Lη_ξ φ_*AΩ_R = φ_*Lη_ξ̃ AΩ_R of BMS2 is represented by φ_M : M^• → φ_*η_ξ̃ M^• ⊂ φ_*M^•.
hypotheses: C is a perfectoid field of characteristic 0 containing all p-power roots of unity; R is p-completely smooth over O_C with a framing as stated (a small algebra in the sense of BMS1).
The prism is (A, (ξ)) = (A_inf, ker θ); Δ_{R/A} is taken relative to it, and φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} is prismatic cohomology of the Frobenius twist relative to (A, ([p]_q)), as in ainf-omega-comparison.
BMS2 Remark 9.11 prints q = [ε] − 1; the q-de Rham complex of BMS1 Definition 9.5 has q = [ε], so that q − 1 = μ (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E37).
The statement depends on the framing only through the model M^•; the filtration on φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} does not depend on it (change-of-framing).
proofSteps: (1): (R̃, {T_i}, ξR̃) is a framed q-PD datum over the q-PD pair (A, (ξ)) of ainf-q-pd-pair whose q-PD envelope is R̃ itself; by q-de-rham-comparison its framed q-de Rham complex computes qΩ_{R/A}, by q-crystalline-prismatic-comparison qΩ_{R/A} ≅ Δ_{R^{(1)}/A} = φ_A^*Δ_{R/A}, and by ainf-omega-comparison this is AΩ_R; all three isomorphisms are compatible with Frobenius.

(2), divisibility: φγ_i = γ_iφ (γ_i is a δ-A-algebra automorphism) and φ(q − 1) = q^p − 1 = [p]_q·(q − 1) give ((γ_i − 1)/(q − 1))∘φ = [p]_q·(γ_i − 1)φ/(q^p − 1) = [p]_q·φ∘((γ_i − 1)/(q − 1)), that is (∂_q/∂_q log T_i)∘φ = [p]_q·φ∘(∂_q/∂_q log T_i), which is framed-q-de-rham-complex (d) in toric form (e); hence φ_M is a map of complexes and multiplies degree-n basis forms by ξ̃^n.

(2), bijectivity: for the torus R̃ = A⟨T^{±1}⟩ the complex is the completed direct sum over a ∈ Z^d of Koszul complexes on which ∂_q/∂_q log T_i acts by [a_i]_q; modulo ξ̃ = [p]_q the element [a]_q is a unit when p ∤ a and is 0 when p | a, so H^n(M^•/ξ̃) is the completed sum of the lines (A/ξ̃)·T^{pa}·ω, and x ↦ φ_M(x)/ξ̃^n sends T^a·ω to T^{pa}·ω over the isomorphism φ : A/ξ ≅ A/ξ̃. For a general framed R both sides are obtained from the torus by the (p, ξ)-completely étale base change R̃ ⊗̂_{A⟨T^{±1}⟩, φ} A⟨T^{±1}⟩ ≅ R̃; on the right this is étale localisation of Hodge–Tate cohomology (PR.1/etale-localization) transported through (1).

(3): apply PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates with d = ξ, d′ = ξ̃ and the model M^•: its terms are finite free over R̃, which is (p, ξ)-completely flat over A, hence ξ- and ξ̃-torsion-free and ξ-adically complete; hypotheses (a) and (b) of that node are (2). The description by divisibility holds because φ : R̃/ξ → R̃/ξ̃ is injective (R̃ is the base change of R̃ along the Frobenius of the torus, which is finite free).
(4): by PR.3/leta-frobenius-factorisation the Frobenius of φ_A^*Δ_{R/A} factors through Lη of Δ_{R/A}; in the model this is the inclusion of φ_M(M^•) in η_ξ̃ M^•, as BMS2 Remark 9.11 states.
acceptance: One coordinate, R = O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩: N^{≥1}M^• is ξ·A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → A⟨T^{±1}⟩·d_q log T, and N^{≥i}M^• is ξ^i·A⟨T^{±1}⟩ → ξ^{i−1}·A⟨T^{±1}⟩·d_q log T for i ≥ 1.
Graded pieces: gr^i of N^{≥•}M^• is, in degree n ≤ i, (ξ^{i−n}M^n/ξ^{i−n+1}M^n) ≅ Ω^n_{R/O_C}, with zero differential, matching gr^i_N ≅ τ^{≤i}Δ̄_{R/A}{i} of PR.3/relative-nygaard-graded-pieces.

After base change along A_inf → W(k), k the residue field of O_C (so q ↦ 1 and ξ ↦ p), the filtration becomes p^{max(i − •, 0)} of the de Rham complex of the lift R̃ ⊗̂ W(k), the de Rham instance of PR.3/nygaard-filtration-in-coordinates. Modulo q − 1 alone this is not so: ξ is not p times a unit in A_inf/(q − 1).
The element T^a with p ∤ a is not a cocycle modulo ξ̃ in degree 0: ∂_q/∂_q log T (T^a) = [a]_q T^a with [a]_q a unit modulo ξ̃; so H^0(M^•/ξ̃) is spanned by the T^{pa}.

nodes.title: Prismatic crystals in vector bundles and in perfect complexes
nodes.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. A prismatic crystal in vector bundles on X is an object of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) := lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A): a rule E giving a finite projective A-module E(A) for every bounded prism (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, and for every map of prisms f: (A, I) → (B, J) over X an isomorphism of B-modules c_f: E(A) ⊗_A B ≅ E(B), with c_id = id and c_{g∘f} = c_g ∘ (c_f ⊗_B C) for (A,I) → (B,J) → (C,K). Equivalently the c_f are given by f-semilinear maps E(A) → E(B), functorial in f, each exhibiting E(B) as the base change of E(A). A morphism E → E′ is a family of A-linear maps E(A) → E′(A) commuting with the transition maps. In the same way D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ) := lim D_perf(A) (a limit of ∞-categories, transition functors B ⊗^L_A −), and for the two sheaves of O_Δ-algebras O′ = O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ} (value A[1/p]^∧_I, the I-adic completion of A[1/p]) and O′ = O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p (value A[1/I]^∧_p, the p-adic completion of the ring A[1/I] of functions on Spec A ∖ V(I)) one puts Vect(X_Δ, O′) := lim Vect(O′(A)) and D_perf(X_Δ, O′) := lim D_perf(O′(A)). Structure: the unit O_Δ (A ↦ A); tensor product (E ⊗ E′)(A) = E(A) ⊗_A E′(A) and duals E^∨(A) = Hom_A(E(A), A), making Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) rigid symmetric monoidal; the evaluation functors ev_{(A,I)}: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(A); the pullback g^*: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(Y_Δ, O_Δ) along g: Y → X, (g^*E)(A, I, Spf(A/I) → Y) = E(A, I, Spf(A/I) → Y → X); and base change Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O′), E ↦ (A ↦ E(A) ⊗_A O′(A)).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
X is an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme; no boundedness or quasi-syntomicity is needed for the definition.
In the version read (arXiv v2) the definition is the displayed formula opening §4, the sheaf-theoretic notions are Notation 2.1, and their agreement is Proposition 2.7 (node crystal-descent).

Completions: A[1/p]^∧_I is the classical I-adic completion; it agrees with the derived one because I is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor of A[1/p]. A[1/I]^∧_p is the derived p-completion; it is the classical completion whenever A[1/I] has bounded p^∞-torsion (for instance A p-torsion-free: transversal, perfect and Breuil–Kisin prisms), but not for every bounded prism. For Vect the two give the same category lim_n Vect(A[1/I]/p^n); for D_perf the derived completion is meant.
proofSteps: Define the category of compatible families directly, with transition data given as semilinear maps that are base changes; functoriality of the semilinear maps is the cocycle condition (BS23-FCRYS §4, first display).

Base change of finite projective modules along A → B is finite projective and commutes with ⊗ and duals (Mathlib TensorProduct, Module.Finite, Module.Projective); this gives the unit, tensor product, duals and their compatibility with the transition maps.
Pullback along g: Y → X is restriction of the family along the functor Y_Δ → X_Δ that composes the structure map with g; evaluation is the projection of the limit.
For O′ use that a map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J) has IB = J (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal), so it induces A[1/I]^∧_p → B[1/J]^∧_p and A[1/p]^∧_I → B[1/p]^∧_J.
acceptance: The unit crystal evaluates to A on every prism.
For X = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid, evaluation at Δ_R is an equivalence Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect(Δ_R) (node f-crystals-over-qrsp).
The rule A ↦ A/I is compatible with base change but is not a crystal in vector bundles.

nodes.title: Descent for prismatic crystals
nodes.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. (1) The assignment (A, I) ↦ Vect(A) on X_Δ is a sheaf of categories for the flat topology, and the natural functor lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) to vector bundles on the ringed topos (Shv(X_Δ), O_Δ) (locally of the form P ⊗ O for P finite projective) is an equivalence; the same holds with D_perf in place of Vect. (2) The same two statements hold for O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ} and O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p. (3) Čech form: if (B, J) ∈ X_Δ covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) and (B^•, J^•) is its Čech nerve (the cosimplicial prism of iterated coproducts in the category of prisms over X), then Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ lim(Vect(B^0) ⇉ Vect(B^1) ⇶ Vect(B^2)): a crystal is a finite projective B-module M with an isomorphism p_1^*M ≅ p_2^*M over B^1 satisfying the cocycle condition over B^2; likewise for the two completed sheaves and for D_perf (with the full cosimplicial limit).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
In (3) the Čech nerve exists whenever the iterated coproducts exist in the category of bounded prisms over X; this is checked for the two covers of Spf(O_K) in node breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers.

The input for (2) is the Drinfeld–Mathew theorem (the source's Theorem 2.2, Mathew, Faithfully flat descent of almost perfect complexes in rigid geometry, Theorem 5.8): for a connective E_∞-ring R and a finitely generated ideal I ⊂ π_0 R the functors S ↦ D_perf, D^-_coh, Vect of Spec(S^∧_I) ∖ V(IS) are sheaves for the I-completely flat topology. It is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1.
proofSteps: (1): a (p, I)-completely faithfully flat map of bounded prisms A → B induces faithfully flat maps A/(p, I)^n → B ⊗_A A/(p, I)^n; Vect(A) = lim_n Vect(A/(p,I)^n) since A is classically (p, I)-complete (PR.0/bounded-prism-complete-flatness), and ordinary faithfully flat descent applies at each level (BS23-FCRYS, lines after Theorem 2.2; Anschütz–Le Bras Proposition A.3).

Since the prestack is a sheaf, its global sections over the topos are the limit over the site; this is the equivalence with the sheaf-theoretic category (proof of Proposition 2.7, first paragraph). The same argument gives D_perf.

(2) for D_perf: devissage modulo powers of I_Δ reduces to lim D_perf(A/I[1/p]) ≃ D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ/I_Δ[1/p]), which is Drinfeld–Mathew (1) for the ring A/I and the ideal (p); the case of O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p is the same with the roles of p and I exchanged. For Vect use: over a ring R derived J-complete for a finitely generated ideal J, E ∈ D_perf(R) is a vector bundle if and only if E ⊗^L_R R/J is one.

(3): Čech theory in the topos Shv(X_Δ) for a cover of the final object, applied to the sheaf of categories of (1) and (2); for 1-categories of vector bundles the limit over the cosimplicial diagram is computed by its 2-truncation (BS23-FCRYS Example 2.8).
acceptance: For X = Spf(O_K) and the Breuil–Kisin prism: a crystal is a finite free 𝔖-module with a descent isomorphism over 𝔖^(1) and the cocycle condition over 𝔖^(2).
For a faithfully flat map of bounded prisms A → B the sequence Vect(A) → Vect(B) ⇉ Vect(B ⊗̂_A B) is an equaliser of categories.
The statement for O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p does not follow from flat descent of modules alone: A[1/I]^∧_p → B[1/I]^∧_p is not flat in general, and Drinfeld–Mathew is used.

nodes.title: Crystals on the prismatic site and on the quasi-syntomic site
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme, X_qsyn its quasi-syntomic site and X_qrsp ⊂ X_qsyn the full subcategory of Spf(R) → X with R quasiregular semiperfectoid; Δ_• is the sheaf of rings R ↦ Δ_R on X_qsyn (defined on X_qrsp) and I ⊂ Δ_• its ideal sheaf. (1) lim_{R ∈ X_qrsp} Vect(Δ_R) ≃ Vect(X_qsyn, Δ_•). (2) There is a natural equivalence Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect(X_qsyn, Δ_•), induced by pullback along the map of ringed topoi ν: (Shv(X_Δ), O_Δ) → (Shv(X_qsyn), Δ_•) determined by R ↦ Δ_R. (3) Both statements hold with D_perf in place of Vect, and with (O_Δ[1/p]^∧_{I_Δ}, Δ_•[1/p]^∧_I) or (O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p) in place of (O_Δ, Δ_•). (4) Concretely, for X = Spf(R) affine and R → S a quasi-syntomic cover with S quasiregular semiperfectoid, with p-completed Čech nerve S^•, both sides are lim Vect(Δ_{S^•}).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
X is quasi-syntomic (DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.5). For R in X_qrsp the prism Δ_R is bounded.
The topos Shv(X_qsyn) equals Shv(X_qrsp) (BMS2 Proposition 4.31, Variant 4.35; DD.5).
proofSteps: Reduce to X_qrsp and, by Zariski descent on both sides, to X = Spf(R) affine (proof of Proposition 2.14).

The functor Δ(−): R_qrsp → R_Δ, S ↦ Δ_S, satisfies Hom_{R-alg}(S, A/I) = Hom_{R_Δ}(Δ_S, (A, I)) because Δ_S is the initial prism over S (PR.2/qrsp-prism); hence it commutes with finite non-empty coproducts.
If S ∈ R_qrsp is a quasi-syntomic cover of R then Δ_S covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) (BS22 Proposition 7.11, PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent).

Choose such an S with Čech nerve S^•: Čech theory in R_qsyn gives Vect(R_qsyn, Δ_•) ≃ lim Vect(Δ_{S^•}), and Čech theory in R_Δ (node crystal-descent (3)) identifies the same limit with Vect(R_Δ, O_Δ). Independence of S: the category of such covers has finite non-empty coproducts, so it is sifted; or use ν^*.
(1) is proved as crystal-descent (1)–(2), on the site X_qrsp.
acceptance: For X = Spf(O_K): Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ lim(Vect(A_inf) ⇉ Vect(Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C}) ⇶ Vect(Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C ⊗̂ O_C})), completed tensor products over O_K.
For X = Spf(R) with R quasiregular semiperfectoid both sides are Vect(Δ_R).

nodes.title: F-crystals over a single prism
nodes.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism with Frobenius φ, and let A[1/I] be the ring of functions on Spec A ∖ V(I): the initial A-algebra L with IL = L (it is A[1/d] when I = (d)). The category Vect^φ(A) of F-crystals over (A, I) has objects the pairs (M, φ_M) with M a finite projective A-module and φ_M: (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I] an isomorphism of A[1/I]-modules, where φ^*M = A ⊗_{φ,A} M and N[1/I] = A[1/I] ⊗_A N; equivalently φ_M is a φ-semilinear map M → M[1/I] whose A[1/I]-linearisation is bijective. Morphisms are A-linear maps f: M → M′ with φ_{M′} ∘ φ^*f = f ∘ φ_M after inverting I. (M, φ_M) is effective when φ_M carries φ^*M into M. Tensor product and duals are those of the underlying modules with φ_M ⊗ φ_{M′} and (φ_M^∨)^{-1}; the unit is (A, φ). A map of prisms (A, I) → (B, J) induces the base change Vect^φ(A) → Vect^φ(B), M ↦ M ⊗_A B. For an A-algebra A′ with a compatible Frobenius (such as A[1/I]^∧_p, A[1/p], A⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) the category Vect^φ(A′) is defined in the same way.
hypotheses: (A, I) is a prism (PR.0/prism); boundedness is not needed for the definition.

Objects of Vect^φ(𝔖) for the Breuil–Kisin prism (𝔖, (E(u))) are Breuil–Kisin modules; the effective ones with finite free M are the modules of finite E-height Mod^φ_{/𝔖} of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/kisin-modules. Objects of Vect^φ(A_inf) are the finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules of AInfCohomology:AI.2 (node bkf-modules-comparison).
No bound on the poles or zeros of φ_M along I is part of the data; this is why the notion is adequate only for finite locally free coefficients (node mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails).
proofSteps: Define A[1/I] by its universal property and show it is A[1/d] for an orientation d (Mathlib Localization.Away); in general it is the filtered colimit of the invertible modules I^{-n}.
Record φ_M as a semilinear map M → A[1/I] ⊗_A M that is a base change along A → A → A[1/I] (first map φ); this is equivalent to the isomorphism (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I].
Base change along a map of prisms uses φ_B ∘ f = f ∘ φ_A and IB = J (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal), which give φ_B^*(M ⊗_A B) = (φ_A^*M) ⊗_A B and B[1/J] = A[1/I] ⊗_A B.
acceptance: Over the Breuil–Kisin prism the rank one objects (𝔖, c·E(u)^n·φ), c ∈ W(k)^×, n ∈ Z, are F-crystals, effective exactly for n ≥ 0.
Over a crystalline prism (A, (p)) an F-crystal is a finite projective A-module with an isomorphism φ^*M[1/p] ≅ M[1/p].
The zero map is not a Frobenius structure on a module with M[1/I] ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Prismatic F-crystals on a p-adic formal scheme
nodes.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme. A prismatic F-crystal (of vector bundles) on X is a pair (E, φ_E) with E ∈ Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ) and φ_E: (φ^*E)[1/I_Δ] ≅ E[1/I_Δ] an isomorphism of crystals over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]; that is, an F-crystal structure φ_{E(A)} on each E(A) (node f-crystal-over-prism) such that the transition isomorphisms E(A) ⊗_A B ≅ E(B) are isomorphisms in Vect^φ(B). Morphisms are morphisms of crystals commuting with φ_E. The category is Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) = lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect^φ(A). (E, φ_E) is effective when φ_E carries φ^*E into E. Tensor products make Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) rigid symmetric monoidal with unit (O_Δ, φ); g: Y → X induces g^*: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^φ(Y_Δ, O_Δ). For a sheaf O′ of O_Δ-algebras with a compatible Frobenius, Vect^φ(X_Δ, O′) is defined in the same way, and a prismatic F-crystal of perfect complexes is E ∈ D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ) with φ^*E[1/I_Δ] ≃ E[1/I_Δ]. Example: the Breuil–Kisin twist O_Δ{1} of PR.3 is an invertible prismatic F-crystal on Spf(Z_p), hence by pullback on every bounded X, with φ^*O_Δ{1} ≅ I_Δ^{-1} ⊗ O_Δ{1}; O_Δ{n} = O_Δ{1}^{⊗n} for n ∈ Z.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
X is an arbitrary p-adic formal scheme for the definition; the twist O_Δ{1} is used on bounded X.

Finite locally free F-crystals do not classify torsion or derived Galois representations: the source states that with Z/p^n-coefficients or in the derived category the correct objects should also bound the zeros and poles of φ_E along I_Δ (perfect complexes on Drinfeld's stack Σ″, F-gauges). No statement about F-gauges is planned here.
proofSteps: Add to a crystal (node prismatic-crystal) the Frobenius structures of node f-crystal-over-prism on its values, compatible with the transition maps; φ^*E is the crystal A ↦ φ_A^*E(A), well defined because maps of prisms commute with φ.
The limit description, tensor products, duals and pullback are inherited from prismatic-crystal and f-crystal-over-prism.
The twist: O_Δ{1}(A) = A{1} with the isomorphism φ^*A{1} ≅ I^{-1} ⊗ A{1} of PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist, natural in the prism (BS23-FCRYS Example 4.5).
acceptance: The unit (O_Δ, φ) is effective; O_Δ{−1} is effective and O_Δ{1} is not.
On a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme the notion is that of an F-crystal on the crystalline site (node crystalline-realization).
For X = Spf(R), R quasiregular semiperfectoid, Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) = Vect^φ(Δ_R).

nodes.title: Laurent F-crystals
nodes.statement: Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For a prism (A, I) the Frobenius φ of A induces a Frobenius on the p-adic completion A[1/I]^∧_p, because φ(I) ≡ I^p modulo p. A Laurent F-crystal in vector bundles on X is an object of Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} := lim_{(A,I) ∈ X_Δ} Vect(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}: a crystal E of vector bundles over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with an isomorphism φ_E: φ^*E ≅ E. In perfect complexes: D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} := lim D_perf(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, the ∞-category of pairs (E, φ_E: φ^*E ≃ E). Since I_Δ is invertible in O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p this category is Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p) in the sense of node prismatic-f-crystal. The Z_p-module of Frobenius-fixed sections of E over (A, I) is E(A)^{φ=1} = {x : φ_E(x) = x}.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
X is bounded: locally Spf(R) with R[p^∞] of bounded exponent (the source's Notation 3.1). The definition itself makes sense for every X; boundedness is used to speak of the generic fibre.
If X has characteristic p then every prism of X_Δ has I = (p), A[1/I]^∧_p = 0, and the category is zero (the source's Remark 3.3).
proofSteps: Construct the Frobenius of A[1/I]^∧_p: modulo p^n the element φ(d) of a local generator d of I differs from d^p by a multiple of p, so φ(d) is a unit of A[1/I]/p^n; pass to the limit.
Define the category as a limit, using crystal-descent (2) to identify crystals over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p with compatible families.
The Frobenius structure is recorded as a φ-semilinear endomorphism of each value whose linearisation is bijective, commuting with the transition maps.
acceptance: For X = Spf(O_C) the category is Vect(W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, equivalent to Vect(Z_p) by taking φ-fixed points.
For X of characteristic p the category is zero.

A crystal over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p[1/p] with φ^*E ≅ E is in general not a Laurent F-crystal up to isogeny: over O_C these are all F-isocrystals over C^♭, of which only those of slope 0 arise (the source's Remark 3.9).

nodes.title: Riemann–Hilbert for F_p-local systems and invariance under completed perfection
nodes.statement: (1) Let S be a commutative F_p-algebra. Extension of scalars along F_p → O_{Spec(S),ét} and Frobenius fixed points are mutually inverse equivalences D^b_lisse(Spec(S), F_p) ≃ D_perf(S)^{φ=1}, where D_perf(S)^{φ=1} is the ∞-category of pairs (E, α) with E a perfect complex of S-modules and α: φ^*E ≃ E, and D^b_lisse is the bounded derived category of étale F_p-sheaves with locally constant cohomology sheaves of finite rank; on hearts of vector bundles it is Katz's equivalence between F_p-local systems on Spec(S) and finite projective S-modules M with φ^*M ≅ M. Each cohomology module of such an (E, α) is finite projective. (2) Let R be an F_p-algebra with an element t such that R is derived t-complete, and S = (R_perf)^∧_t the t-completed perfection. Then the base change functors D_perf(R[1/t])^{φ=1} → D_perf(R_perf[1/t])^{φ=1} → D_perf(S[1/t])^{φ=1} are equivalences.
hypotheses: In (1) S is an arbitrary commutative F_p-algebra (no noetherian, normality or reducedness hypothesis).
In (2) R is derived t-complete, hence henselian along t; R_perf = colim_φ R.
Étale sheaves, lisse complexes, the Artin–Schreier sequence and topological invariance of the étale site are requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.
proofSteps: Full faithfulness in (1): by finite étale descent on both sides reduce to endomorphisms of the constant sheaf, i.e. to RΓ(Spec(S)_ét, F_p) ≃ fib(φ − 1: S → S), the Artin–Schreier sequence.

Each H^i(E) is a vector bundle: by descending induction treat the top cohomology H^n(E), which is finitely presented with φ^*H^n ≅ H^n; by noetherian approximation and localisation S is noetherian local, any Fitting ideal J satisfies J = φ(J)S, so J ∈ {0, S} by Krull's intersection theorem.

Essential surjectivity in (1): by the previous step and full faithfulness reduce to a vector bundle (M, α); the functor of α-fixed bases is a finite étale GL_n(F_p)-torsor over Spec(S) (Katz, p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms, Proposition 4.1.1; Kedlaya–Liu, Relative p-adic Hodge theory: foundations, Proposition 3.2.7), which gives the local system.

(2): the first functor is an equivalence by (1) and topological invariance of the étale site (R[1/t] → R_perf[1/t] is a universal homeomorphism). Full faithfulness of the composite is BS22 Lemma 9.2 (φ-fixed points commute with t-completed filtered colimits; PR.4), perfect complexes over R being derived t-complete. Essential surjectivity: by (1) for S[1/t] it suffices that every lisse F_p-sheaf on Spec(S[1/t]) comes from Spec(R[1/t]), which holds because finite étale algebras over R_perf[1/t] and over S[1/t] agree (Gabber–Ramero, Foundations for almost ring theory, Proposition 5.4.54; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).
acceptance: S = F_p: both sides are perfect complexes of F_p-vector spaces.
S = k a separably closed field: every (M, α) is trivial, M ≅ M^{φ=1} ⊗_{F_p} k (Lang).
S = F_p[x]: the rank one module with φ(1) = 1 + x has the Artin–Schreier covering as associated torsor; it is not trivial.
The statement fails for finitely generated modules that are not projective if the isomorphism α is replaced by an arbitrary map.

nodes.title: Laurent F-crystals are Z_p-local systems on the generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme with generic fibre X_η, regarded as a locally spatial diamond. (1) For every bounded prism (A, I) with perfection (B, J), base change is an equivalence D_perf(A[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(B[1/J]^∧_p)^{φ=1}; hence extension of scalars is an equivalence D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(X_Δ, O_{Δ,perf}[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, the right side being the limit over perfect prisms. (2) The right side is equivalent to D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p): the full subcategory of D(X_{η,proét}, Z_p) of locally bounded, derived p-complete objects whose reduction modulo p has locally constant cohomology sheaves with finitely generated stalks. (3) On vector bundles: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), and after inverting p in the Hom groups, Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p. (4) For X = Spf(R) with R perfectoid, Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p = W(R^♭[1/I]) and the equivalence is M ↦ the local system of φ-fixed points on Spa(R[1/p], R). (5) For X = Spf(O_K) as in node crystalline-lattices-theorem: Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_K), finite free Z_p-modules with continuous G_K-action, the representation being the φ-fixed points of the value on A_inf with the action induced by that of G_K on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃).
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
X is bounded. In the source this is Corollary 3.7 (derived) and Corollary 3.8 (vector bundles); item 3.9 of the source is the remark on the two enlargements recorded in the last hypothesis.

The identification (2) uses that X ↦ D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p) is a sheaf of ∞-categories for the quasi-syntomic topology, by v-descent on the diamond X_η; this is requested from DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2 (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/30 (a)).

Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p is in general smaller than the category of pro-étale Q_p-local systems, and Vect(…)^{φ=1} ⊗ Q_p smaller than Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p[1/p])^{φ=1}; no equivalence between the enlargements is claimed (the source's Remark 3.9).
proofSteps: (1): by the definition of both sides as limits it is enough to treat one prism; by devissage along powers of p reduce to coefficients modulo p, where A/p[1/I] → B/p[1/I] is the passage from R = A/p (derived t-complete for a local generator t of I) to the t-completed perfection, and node artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert (2) applies.

(4): for R perfectoid, Δ_R = A_inf(R) (PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings) and A_inf(R)[1/I]^∧_p = W(R^♭[1/I]); modulo p apply artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert (1) to S = R^♭[1/I], then the tilting equivalence of finite étale sites of Spa(R[1/p], R) and its tilt (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-tilting-equivalence) and the algebraisation of finite étale covers of affinoid perfectoid spaces; pass to Z_p-coefficients by devissage and derived p-completeness (the source's Example 3.5).

(2): the limit over perfect prisms in X_Δ is the limit over perfectoid rings R with Spf(R) → X; these give a basis of affinoid perfectoid objects over the diamond X_η, so v-descent for D^{(b)}_lisse (DiamondEtaleCohomology:C2) and (4) identify the limit with D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p).

(3) follows by the same argument on hearts; the second statement by inverting p. (5): X_η = Spa(K, O_K), whose Z_p-local systems are continuous G_K-representations on finite free Z_p-modules; the Čech nerve of Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(K, O_K) is G_K^n × Spa(C, O_C), so descent data are continuous semilinear actions.
acceptance: X = Spf(O_C): the category of Laurent F-crystals is Vect(Z_p) (taking φ-fixed points of modules over W(C^♭)).
X of characteristic p: both sides are zero.
X = the p-completion of P^1 over Z_p: de Jong's Q_p-local system with monodromy SL_2(Q_p) is not in Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) ⊗ Q_p.
Analogue on the special fibre (the source's Remark 3.11): D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ)^{φ=1} ≃ D^b_lisse(X_{p=0}, Z_p).

nodes.title: The étale realisation functor
nodes.statement: For every p-adic formal scheme X the p-completed base change E ↦ E ⊗_{O_Δ} O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, with the induced Frobenius, is a symmetric monoidal functor T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1}: on a prism (A, I) it sends (M, φ_M) to M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p with φ_M ⊗ φ, which is an isomorphism because I is invertible in the target. For X bounded, composing with the equivalence of node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems gives T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), the étale realisation; it preserves ranks, tensor products and duals and commutes with pullback along maps of bounded p-adic formal schemes. For F-crystals of perfect complexes the same formula gives T with values in D^{(b)}_lisse(X_η, Z_p). For X = Spf(O_K), T(E) is the G_K-representation (E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} W(C^♭))^{φ=1}. On twists, T(O_Δ{i}) = Z_p(i) for all i and all bounded X.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.

The functor to Laurent F-crystals exists for every p-adic formal scheme X; the identification of its target with Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) requires X bounded. The source's Construction 4.8 says "for any p-adic formal scheme" for both and refers to Corollary 3.7; the hypothesis and the reference (Corollary 3.8 for vector bundles) are corrected here (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E72).

T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1) is stated in the source's Example 4.9 without proof, with a pointer to the q-logarithm of Anschütz–Le Bras and the prismatic logarithm of Bhatt–Lurie. The plan uses, for perfectoid R, the identification of the φ-fixed elements of Fil^1_N Δ_R{1} with the Tate module T_p(R^×) (BS22 Theorem 9.4 and Remark 9.5, PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid), which is natural in R and therefore Galois-equivariant.
proofSteps: On each prism: base change M ↦ M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p with the Frobenius of node laurent-f-crystal; φ_M becomes an isomorphism φ^*(M ⊗ A[1/I]^∧_p) ≅ M ⊗ A[1/I]^∧_p. Naturality in the prism gives a functor on the limits.
Symmetric monoidality: base change commutes with tensor products of finite projective modules.
Compose with laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (3) for bounded X; compatibility with pullback follows from the naturality of that equivalence in X.

Twists: by pullback from Spf(Z_p) and descent it suffices to treat perfectoid R containing all p-power roots of unity; there T_p(R^×) → Δ_R{1}^{φ=1} → (Δ_R{1}[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1} identifies the local system T(O_Δ{1}) with Z_p(1), by PR.4/tate-twist-perfectoid and naturality in R; tensor powers give all i.
acceptance: T(O_Δ) is the constant local system Z_p; T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1).
For X of characteristic p, T = 0; in particular T is not faithful there.

Over Spf(O_C), T is faithful but not full: Hom(O_Δ{1}, O_Δ) = (μA_inf)^{φ=1} = 0, while the realisations Z_p(1) and Z_p are isomorphic Z_p-modules (there is no Galois action over O_C). In the other direction the inclusion A_inf ⊂ μ^{-1}A_inf = A_inf{1} is a morphism whose realisation is an isomorphism although it is not one.

T commutes with proper smooth pushforward of the structure sheaf (the source's Example 4.9), through the Artin–Schreier sequence on X_{η,proét}; this is the étale comparison PR.4/etale-comparison with coefficients and is recorded as a consistency check, not planned as a node.

nodes.title: The crystalline and de Rham realisations
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme, flat over Z_p, with special fibre X_{p=0}. (1) For a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme Z every prism of Z_Δ is crystalline, I = (p), and crystals of vector bundles on Z_Δ and on the crystalline site Z_crys are identified compatibly with Frobenius; hence Vect^φ(Z_Δ, O_Δ) is the category Vect^φ(Z_crys) of F-crystals on Z_crys (finite locally free crystals E with φ^*E[1/p] ≅ E[1/p]). (2) Pullback along X_{p=0} → X gives the crystalline realisation D_crys: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^φ(X_{p=0,crys}). (3) Forgetting the Frobenius and using that crystals on X_crys and on X_{p=0,crys} agree gives the de Rham realisation D_dR: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_crys); for X formally smooth over a base Y it gives D_{dR,Y} with values in Vect((X/Y)_crys) ≃ vector bundles on X with a topologically quasi-nilpotent flat connection relative to Y. For X = Spf(O_K): the value of D_crys(E) on the prism (W(k), (p)) of Spec(k) is the φ-module E(W(k)); it determines D_crys(E) up to isogeny only (Dwork's trick, node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) = E(W(k))[1/p].
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.
X is quasi-syntomic and Z_p-flat (the source assumes flatness for simplicity). Part (1) needs only that Z is a quasi-syntomic F_p-scheme.
The crystalline site, crystals on it and their description by connections belong to CrystallineCohomology:CR.1 (requested).
proofSteps: (1): by quasi-syntomic descent on both sides (node quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison) reduce to Z = Spec(R) with R quasiregular semiperfect, where Δ_R ≅ A_crys(R) compatibly with φ (crystalline comparison for prismatic cohomology, PR.1/crystalline-comparison extended to quasiregular semiperfect rings, PR.2/qrsp-prism) and both categories are modules over this ring.
I = (p) on Z_Δ: p ∈ I because p = 0 in A/I, and the irreducibility lemma for distinguished elements (PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity) gives I = (p).
(2) is pullback of prismatic F-crystals (node prismatic-f-crystal) along the closed immersion, followed by (1).
(3): X_{p=0} ⊂ X is a pro-PD thickening, so crystals on X_crys and X_{p=0,crys} agree (CrystallineCohomology:CR.1).
acceptance: D_crys(O_Δ) is the unit F-crystal; D_crys preserves ranks and tensor products.
For X = Spf(O_K): D_crys(O_Δ{n}) is W(k) with Frobenius p^{-n}φ.
On Spec(F_p): prismatic F-crystals are finite free Z_p-modules M with an automorphism of M[1/p].

nodes.title: F-crystals over a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring; faithfulness of the étale realisation
nodes.statement: Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring with prism (Δ_R, I) and X = Spf(R). (1) (Δ_R, I) is the final object of X_Δ (the initial prism over R), so evaluation at Δ_R gives equivalences Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) ≃ Vect^φ(Δ_R) and D_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ D_perf(Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p)^{φ=1}, and similarly for every sheaf of node prismatic-crystal. (2) If R is p-torsion-free then (Δ_R, I) is transversal ((p, d) is a regular sequence for a generator d of I), the map Δ_R → Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p is injective, and so is M → M ⊗_{Δ_R} Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p for every finite projective Δ_R-module M. (3) Consequently the étale realisation T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} is faithful when R is p-torsion-free.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; a prism is a bounded prism (A, I) in the sense of PR.0, and X_Δ is the absolute prismatic site of PR.5: the opposite of the category of bounded prisms (A, I) with a map Spf(A/I) → X, with the flat topology. A "map of prisms over X" (A, I) → (B, J) is an arrow of the category of prisms, that is an arrow (B, J) → (A, I) of X_Δ.

The source says "initial object" of X_Δ in Examples 3.5 and 4.10 and "final object" in Example 2.5; with X_Δ the opposite category of prisms (Definition 2.3) the object is final (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E71).
Part (2) assumes R p-torsion-free; for R of characteristic p the target ring is zero.
proofSteps: (1): Δ_R is the initial prism over R (BS22 Proposition 7.10, PR.2/qrsp-prism); a limit over a category with an initial object is the value there.

(2): Δ̄_R is p-torsion-free because it has an exhaustive filtration with graded pieces p-completely flat over the p-torsion-free ring R (Hodge–Tate comparison, PR.2/derived-hodge-tate-comparison); hence (p, d) is regular. The cofibre of Δ_R → Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p is derived p-complete, so by derived Nakayama injectivity follows from injectivity of Δ_R/p → Δ_R/p[1/I], which holds because d is a nonzerodivisor modulo p.
(3): a morphism of F-crystals over Δ_R that vanishes after base change to Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p vanishes, by (2) applied to the internal Hom module.
acceptance: R = O_C: A_inf → W(C^♭) is injective.
R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C and its triple analogue: T is faithful on every term of the Čech nerve of Spf(O_C) → Spf(O_K).
R = O_C/p: Δ_R = A_crys, I = (p), and the étale realisation is zero, so faithfulness fails without p-torsion-freeness.
