nodes.title: The Breuil–Kisin and A_inf prisms as covers of Spf(O_K), and their Čech nerves
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK. (1) Breuil–Kisin prism: for a uniformizer π ∈ O_K with Eisenstein polynomial E(u) ∈ W[u], the prism (𝔖, (E(u))) = (W[[u]], (E(u))) with φ(u) = u^p and 𝔖/E(u) ≅ O_K, u ↦ π, is an object of X_Δ which covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ). For every (B, J) ∈ X_Δ and every lift v ∈ B of the image of π, the prismatic envelope C = B[u]{(u − v)/J}^∧_{(p,J)} is a (p, J)-completely flat δ-B-algebra, E(u)C = JC, and (C, JC) is the coproduct of (𝔖, (E)) and (B, J) in the category of prisms over X. (2) A_inf-prism: (A_inf, ker θ̃) = Δ_{O_C} with O_K → O_C is an object of X_Δ covering the final object, because O_K → O_C is a quasi-syntomic cover. (3) Čech nerves: 𝔖^{(•)}, with 𝔖^{(0)} = 𝔖 and 𝔖^{(1)} = W[[u, v]]{(u − v)/E(u)}^∧_{(p,E(u))}, in which E(v)/E(u) is a unit; each 𝔖^{(i)} is a transversal prism. The Čech nerve of A_inf is Δ_{Y^{•/X}}: its terms are Δ_R for R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} … ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, which are quasiregular semiperfectoid and p-torsion-free. (4) A compatible system π̃ = (π, π^{1/p}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ of p-power roots of π (so θ([π̃]) = π and θ̃([π̃]^p) = π) gives the map of prisms over X (𝔖, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃), u ↦ [π̃]^p, which on W(k) is the Frobenius of the Witt-functorial inclusion W(k) ⊂ A_inf (BMS1 §4; this is the W-algebra structure of A_inf compatible with θ̃, as in the source's Notation 5.1). It is the composite of Kisin's embedding u ↦ [π̃] with the Frobenius of A_inf (missed source issue on Notation 7.1), and G_K acts on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃) of X_Δ. (5) Evaluation: for a crystal E on X_Δ (over any of the sheaves of node prismatic-crystal) one has E(𝔖) ⊗_𝔖 A_inf ≅ E(A_inf), E(A_inf) carries a semilinear G_K-action, and E is equivalent to E(𝔖) with a descent datum over 𝔖^{(1)}, and to E(A_inf) with a descent datum over Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C}, each with the cocycle condition over the third term.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
π is a uniformizer; 𝔖 depends on π, A_inf does not. The δ-W-algebra map 𝔖 → A_inf depends on the choice of π^♭.
The prisms themselves are PR.0/breuil-kisin-prism and PR.0/ainf-prism; this node adds their structure as objects of X_Δ, the covering property and the Čech nerves.
proofSteps: (1), covering: by (4) the Breuil–Kisin prism maps to the A_inf-prism in X_Δ, and the latter covers the final object by (2); hence so does the former (the first argument indicated in the source's Example 2.6 (1)). (1), coproduct: C exists and is (p, J)-completely flat over B by the existence theorem for prismatic envelopes of regular ideals (BS22 Proposition 3.13, PR.0/regular-prismatic-envelopes) applied to B[u] and the ideal (J, u − v). Since u ≡ v modulo JC, E(u) ≡ E(v) ∈ JC; the irreducibility lemma (BS22 Lemma 2.24, PR.0/distinguished-factor-rigidity) gives E(u)C = JC. The two maps O_K → C/JC agree on π, hence are equal, and the universal property of the envelope gives the coproduct property. The source's direct argument for the covering property also needs B → C to be faithfully flat, which it reads off from Proposition 3.13 although that proposition states complete flatness only (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E79); the plan does not use it.

(2): O_K → O_C is a quasi-syntomic cover and O_C is perfectoid; BS22 Proposition 7.11 (PR.2/quasisyntomic-descent) shows Δ_{O_C} covers the final object (compare node quasisyntomic-crystal-comparison).
(3): iterate (1) for 𝔖^{(•)}; transversality follows from complete flatness over 𝔖. For A_inf use that Δ(−) commutes with finite non-empty coproducts on quasiregular semiperfectoid algebras.

(4): W[[u]] → A_inf, u ↦ [π^♭], is a map of δ-rings because δ vanishes on Teichmüller elements; with θ̃([π^♭]) = π the composite 𝔖 → A_inf → O_C is 𝔖 → O_K ⊂ O_C (the source's Notation 7.1). (5) is node crystal-descent (3) for the two covers.
acceptance: K = Q_p(p^{1/p}), π = p^{1/p}: E = u^p − p, and 𝔖 → A_inf carries u − p to a unit multiple of [p]_{q^{1/p}} (the source's Example 7.8).
The Breuil–Kisin prism is not perfect; the A_inf-prism is its image under a map to a perfect prism, not its perfection (the perfection is A_inf of the completion of K(π^{1/p^∞})).

nodes.title: F-crystals over O_C are Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules; the functor of Fargues' theorem
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK and PER. (1) Evaluation at A_inf identifies Vect^φ(Y_Δ, O_Δ) = Vect^φ(A_inf) with the category of finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules of AInfCohomology:AI.2: finite free A_inf-modules M with φ_M: φ^*M[1/ξ̃] ≅ M[1/ξ̃]. (2) For such M the étale realisation is T = (M ⊗_{A_inf} W(C^♭))^{φ=1}, a finite free Z_p-module with M ⊗ W(C^♭) ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} W(C^♭), and this isomorphism restricts to M[1/μ] ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/μ] (BMS1 Lemma 4.26); since μ is invertible at the Hodge–Tate point, M ⊗ B_dR^+ ≅ T ⊗ B_dR^+, and F := φ^*M ⊗_{A_inf} B_dR^+ is a B_dR^+-lattice in T ⊗_{Z_p} B_dR. (3) The functor M ↦ (T, F) from Vect^φ(A_inf) to pairs (T a finite free Z_p-module, F a B_dR^+-lattice in T ⊗ B_dR) is an equivalence (Fargues); PR.7 uses only that it is fully faithful. (4) Vector bundles on Spec(A_inf) ∖ {x_k}, x_k the closed point, extend uniquely to Spec(A_inf).
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).

Period rings, normalised as in the source's Notation 5.1: A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = Δ_{O_C} with q = [ε], μ = q − 1, ξ̃ = [p]_q, θ̃: A_inf → O_C with kernel (ξ̃), and θ = θ̃ ∘ φ; A_crys = A_inf{[p]_q/p} = Δ_{O_C/p}, the p-completed PD envelope of ker θ; B_crys^+ = A_crys[1/p], B_crys = A_crys[1/μ]; B_dR^+ the completion of A_inf[1/p] at ker θ̃, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/[p]_q]; the map φ^*B_crys → B_dR is A_inf-linear for the Frobenius-twisted structure on B_crys. These are the rings of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1 with θ replaced by θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{-1}; the dictionary is part of the request to R06.1.

C is algebraically closed and complete. Fargues' equivalence, BMS1 Lemma 4.26, the elementary proof of full faithfulness (BMS1 Remark 4.29) and the extension statement (Kedlaya; BMS1 Lemma 4.6) are owned by AInfCohomology:AI.2 and requested there; they are not planned again.
AI.2 states Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules with φ_M: M[1/ξ] → M[1/ξ̃] semilinear; the linearised form used here is the same datum.
proofSteps: (1): node f-crystals-over-qrsp (1) for R = O_C, and Δ_{O_C} = A_inf with I = ker θ̃ (PR.0/ainf-prism); finite projective A_inf-modules are free because A_inf is local.

(2): laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (4) for R = O_C gives T and the trivialisation over W(C^♭) = A_inf[1/I]^∧_p; BMS1 Lemma 4.26 (AI.2) descends it to A_inf[1/μ]; θ̃(μ) = ε_p − 1 ≠ 0 gives the statement over B_dR^+.
(3) and (4) are imported from AI.2.

nodes.title: Prismatic F-crystals on O_K give crystalline Galois representations
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK and PER. Let E ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ). (1) There is a canonical G_K-equivariant, Frobenius-compatible isomorphism T(E) ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys ≅ E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys, where E(W(k)) is the value of E on the crystalline prism (W(k), (p)) over Spec(k) ⊂ Spec(O_K/p); hence T(E)[1/p] is a crystalline representation of G_K, of dimension rk(E), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) ≅ E(W(k))[1/p] as φ-modules over K_0. Thus T takes values in Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K), the category of finite free Z_p-modules with continuous G_K-action whose rationalisation is crystalline. (2) Compatibility of lattices: base change of (1) along φ^*B_crys → B_dR gives T(E) ⊗ B_dR ≅ φ^*E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_dR, and the B_dR^+-lattice F′ = φ^*E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_dR^+ equals the lattice F = φ^*E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} B_dR^+ of node bkf-modules-comparison. (3) Under T(E)[1/p] = V, F = D_dR(V) ⊗_K B_dR^+.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).

Period rings, normalised as in the source's Notation 5.1: A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = Δ_{O_C} with q = [ε], μ = q − 1, ξ̃ = [p]_q, θ̃: A_inf → O_C with kernel (ξ̃), and θ = θ̃ ∘ φ; A_crys = A_inf{[p]_q/p} = Δ_{O_C/p}, the p-completed PD envelope of ker θ; B_crys^+ = A_crys[1/p], B_crys = A_crys[1/μ]; B_dR^+ the completion of A_inf[1/p] at ker θ̃, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/[p]_q]; the map φ^*B_crys → B_dR is A_inf-linear for the Frobenius-twisted structure on B_crys. These are the rings of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1 with θ replaced by θ̃ = θ ∘ φ^{-1}; the dictionary is part of the request to R06.1.
Crystalline representations, D_crys and D_dR are those of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2 (period-functors, admissible-representations).
The Frobenius twist: the filtered φ-module attached to E has underlying K_0-space D = E(W(k))[1/p] and filtration on D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K, the convention of the source's Construction 6.5.
proofSteps: Crystal property for A_inf = Δ_{O_C} → A_crys = Δ_{O_C/p}: E(A_inf) ⊗_{A_inf} A_crys ≅ E(A_crys). Invert μ and use M[1/μ] ≅ T ⊗ A_inf[1/μ] (node bkf-modules-comparison (2)): T(E) ⊗ B_crys ≅ E(A_crys)[1/μ].

Dwork's Frobenius trick: O_K/p → k is a nilpotent thickening in characteristic p, so φ^n of O_K/p factors through k for n large; for a crystal E′ on Spec(O_K/p), (φ^n)^*E′ is the pullback of E′|_{Spec(k)} along φ_n: k → O_K/p. Pull back to O_C/p and use the F-crystal structure to remove the Frobenius pullback after inverting p: E(A_crys)[1/μ] ≅ E(W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys.

The composite isomorphism is G_K-equivariant (G_K acts on the objects A_inf, A_crys of the site and trivially on E(W(k))), so dim_{K_0}(T(E)[1/p] ⊗ B_crys)^{G_K} = rk(E) and T(E)[1/p] is crystalline (R06.2).
(2) and (3): unwind the constructions of F and F′; the filtration on D_dR is induced by B_dR^+ ⊂ B_dR.
acceptance: E = O_Δ: T = Z_p, D_crys = K_0 with φ.
E = O_Δ{1}: T = Z_p(1), E(W(k)) = W(k) with p^{-1}φ; this fixes the normalisation of D_crys relative to R06.2.
A ramified character of finite order is de Rham but not crystalline, so by (1) its lattice is not the realisation of a prismatic F-crystal on Spf(O_K).

nodes.title: Full faithfulness of the étale realisation over O_K
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK. The étale realisation T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p)^{φ=1} ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_K) is fully faithful. More precisely: (1) T is faithful over X, over Y = Spf(O_C) and over every term of the Čech nerve Y^{•/X}. (2) For a lattice T_0 in a de Rham representation V of G_K the assignment T_0 ↦ (T_0, D_dR(V) ⊗_K B_dR^+) is compatible, through the functor of Fargues' theorem, with restriction of F-crystals from X to Y and of Laurent F-crystals from X to Y. (3) For M, N ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) and a morphism g: T(M) → T(N) there is a unique f: M → N with T(f) = g.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
The proof uses only the full faithfulness part of Fargues' theorem (node bkf-modules-comparison (3)).

A second proof, through the Breuil–Kisin prism, is in the source's Remark 5.7: descent along 𝔖^{(•)}, full faithfulness in cosimplicial degree 0 by node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism, and faithfulness in every degree because 𝔖^{(i)} → 𝔖^{(i)}[1/I]^∧_p is injective.
proofSteps: (1): node f-crystals-over-qrsp (2)–(3) for the p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid rings O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} … ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C; faithfulness over X follows from that over Y since A_inf covers the final object.
(2): the commutative diagram of the source's Construction 5.5, using node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal (2)–(3) to identify the lattice of M|_Y with D_dR ⊗ B_dR^+.

Fullness over Y: g|_Y is a map of finite free Z_p-modules which is G_K-equivariant, hence respects the lattices D_dR(·) ⊗ B_dR^+; by full faithfulness in Fargues' theorem it comes from a unique f_Y: M|_Y → N|_Y.
Descent: the two pullbacks a, b of f_Y to Y ×_X Y satisfy T(a) = T(b), both being the pullback of g; by (1) over Y ×_X Y, a = b, and node crystal-descent (3) gives f with f|_Y = f_Y.
acceptance: Hom(O_Δ, O_Δ{n}) = 0 for n ≠ 0, matching Hom_{G_K}(Z_p, Z_p(n)) = 0.
End(O_Δ) = Z_p.
The statement fails with O_Δ/p-coefficients (node mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails).

nodes.title: Period sheaves on the quasi-syntomic site of O_K
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK. On X_qrsp (quasiregular semiperfectoid O_K-algebras R, quasi-syntomic over O_K; each Δ_R is a transversal bounded prism with ideal I) define the presheaves of rings: Δ_• (R ↦ Δ_R); A_crys = Δ_•{I/p} (R ↦ Δ_R{I/p} = Δ_{R/p} = A_crys(R)); the rational localisation Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ (R ↦ Δ_R[I/p]^∧_p, equal to Δ_R[x]/(px − d)^∧_p for a generator d of I); Δ_•{φ(I)/p} (R ↦ Δ_R{φ(I)/p}, the φ-pullback of A_crys); Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p; and the de Rham period sheaves B_dR^+ = (Δ_•[1/p])^∧_I, B_dR = B_dR^+[1/I]. They are related by natural maps Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p ← Δ_• → Δ_•{φ(I)/p} → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ → Δ_•{I/p}. The Frobenius of Δ_• carries I to φ(I) and induces φ̃: Δ_•{I/p} → Δ_•{φ(I)/p}, linear over φ; composing with the maps above gives a Frobenius endomorphism φ of each of these presheaves. More generally Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ is defined for n ≥ 0, with maps Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ and φ̃: Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ → Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩. For each of these rings an F-crystal is a vector bundle M with φ_M: (φ^*M)[1/I] ≅ M[1/I]. Lemma (the source's Lemma 6.7): for every transversal prism (A, I) and n ≥ 0 the natural map A[1/p]^∧_I → A⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I is an isomorphism; so B_dR^+ ≅ Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I for all n ≥ 0.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
Every R in X_qrsp is p-torsion-free, so Δ_R is transversal: (p, d) is a regular sequence (node f-crystals-over-qrsp (2)).
The endomorphism φ of Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ is not a Frobenius lift: it need not be congruent to the p-th power map modulo p; forcing the congruence gives Δ_•{I/p} (the source's footnote to Construction 6.2).
Δ_R{I/p} and Δ_R{φ(I)/p} are δ-envelopes, constructed in PR.0 (PR.0/pd-envelope-as-delta-envelope: A{φ(f)/p} is the p-completed PD envelope of (f)); Δ_R{I/p} = Δ_{R/p} is PR.2/qrsp-prism for R/p.
B_dR^+(O_C) is the usual de Rham period ring of C, a discrete valuation ring (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/de-rham-period-ring with θ̃ in place of θ); the same holds for every perfectoid R in X_qrsp.
proofSteps: Define each presheaf objectwise from Δ_R with its orientation-independent ideal I; functoriality in R follows from that of Δ_R (PR.2/qrsp-prism) and IΔ_{R′} = I′ (PR.0/rigidity-prism-ideal).

The maps: φ(d) = d^p + pδ(d) gives φ(d)/p = p^{p−1}(d/p)^p + δ(d) ∈ Δ_R[d/p], whence Δ_R{φ(I)/p} → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ (the divided powers of d exist in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ because d^n/n! = (p^n/n!)(d/p)^n); Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ → Δ_R{I/p} is the universal map out of the ring obtained by adjoining d/p.

Lemma 6.7: with I = (d) and A⟨φ^n(d)/p⟩ = A[x]/(px − φ^n(d))^∧_p it suffices that A[1/p]/d → Kos(A[x]; px − φ^n(d), d)^∧_p[1/p] is an isomorphism. Write φ^n(d) = d^{p^n} + ph and y = x − h: the target is Kos(A[y]; py, d)^∧_p[1/p] ≃ Kos(A[y]; y, d)^∧_p[1/p] ≃ A/d[1/p], because py is a nonzerodivisor on A/d[y] (transversality) and the kernel of A[y]/py → A[y]/y is killed by p.
The Frobenius endomorphisms are the composites of φ̃ with the structure maps.
acceptance: R = O_C: Δ_•{I/p} = A_crys, B_dR^+ the usual ring, Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p = W(C^♭).
In Δ_R⟨I/p⟩ every element of I is divisible by p; in B_dR^+(R) the element p is a unit.
For A = Z_p[[u]], d = u − p: A⟨d/p⟩ = Z_p⟨u/p⟩ and φ(u/p) = p^{p−1}(u/p)^p ≡ 0 modulo p, while (u/p)^p is not; so φ is not a Frobenius lift on A⟨d/p⟩.

nodes.title: From filtered φ-modules to F-crystals over the open unit disc
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK. Let (D, φ_D, Fil^•) be a filtered φ-module over K: D a finite-dimensional K_0-vector space, φ_D: φ^*D ≅ D, and Fil^• a finite, exhaustive, separated filtration on D_K = D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K (the Frobenius twist is the prismatic normalisation). Then there is an F-crystal M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]), functorial in D, constructed as follows. (a) M_1 = D ⊗_{W(k)} Δ_•{I/p}, a unit F-crystal over Δ_•{I/p}[1/p] with φ induced by φ_D. (b) M_2 = M_1 ⊗_{Δ_•{I/p}, φ̃} Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, a unit F-crystal over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]. (c) M_3 = M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} is the Beauville–Laszlo glueing along the Cartier divisor I = 0 of M_2[1/I] and Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR) ∈ Vect(X_qrsp, B_dR^+) along M_2[1/I] ⊗ B_dR ≅ D ⊗_{W(k),φ} B_dR ≅ Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR)[1/I], with φ_{M_3} = φ_{M_2}[1/I]. (d) Analytic continuation: every F-crystal (M, φ_M) over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] on X_qrsp extends uniquely to F-crystals over Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] for all n ≥ 1, compatibly in n; for n = 1 the extension N is glued from φ̃^*M over Δ_•⟨φ(I)/p⟩[1/p, 1/I] and M^∧_I over B_dR^+. The compatible system M(D) = {M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}}_{n ≥ 1} has value M(D)(Y) on Y = Spf(O_C) an F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0}.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
Filtered φ-modules are those of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/filtered-phi-n-modules with N = 0, with the filtration placed on the Frobenius twist D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K; no admissibility is assumed in this node.
K acts on B_dR^+(R) for R in X_qrsp: K_0 ⊂ Δ_R[1/p] and K/K_0 is finite étale, so K lifts uniquely along B_dR^+(R) → (Δ_R/I)[1/p] ⊃ K by Hensel's lemma.
Beauville–Laszlo glueing of vector bundles along a nonzerodivisor is requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1.
proofSteps: (a): regard (D, φ_D) as an F-crystal of O_Δ[1/p]-modules on Spec(k) and pull back along W(k) → Δ_•{I/p}, a diagram of prisms over k (node crystalline-realization (1)).
(b): base change along φ̃: Δ_•{I/p} → Δ_•{φ(I)/p} → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩ (node period-sheaves-qrsp).

(c): identify B_dR^+ with Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]^∧_I (Lemma 6.7, node period-sheaves-qrsp) and glue; the result is a vector bundle over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] with M_3[1/I] ≅ M_2[1/I] and (M_3)^∧_I ≅ Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR).
(d): the contracting property of φ: φ̃ maps Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩ to Δ_•⟨φ^{n+1}(I)/p⟩, φ^*N = φ̃^*M, and both sides of φ_N: (φ^*N)[1/I] ≅ N[1/I] are identified with (φ̃^*M)[1/I] (the source's Remark 6.6).
A partial inverse over the Breuil–Kisin prism is the functor 𝒟 of node breuil-kisin-evaluation.
acceptance: D = K_0 with φ and Fil^0 = D_K, Fil^1 = 0: M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} = Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p].
D = K_0 with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and Fil^{-1} = D_K, Fil^0 = 0: M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} = Δ_•⟨I/p⟩{1}[1/p], the Breuil–Kisin twist.
The rank of M(D) is dim_{K_0} D, and M(D ⊗ D′) = M(D) ⊗ M(D′).

nodes.title: Analytic continuation for p-adic Tate twists
nodes.statement: Let R be a quasiregular semiperfectoid p-torsion-free O_C-algebra, and n ≥ 0. The natural map Δ_R{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] is an isomorphism. Here (−)^{φ=1} denotes fixed points in the ordinary (non-derived) sense: the elements x of Δ_R{n} (resp. of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}) with φ(x) = x in Δ_R{n}[1/I] (resp. in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}[1/I]).
hypotheses: R is a p-torsion-free quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebra; the O_C-structure trivialises the twists, Δ_{O_C}{1} ≅ (q − 1)^{-1}Δ_{O_C}.
The source states the proposition without a range for n; its proof and its use (the source's Lemma 6.9 (1)) concern n ≥ 0, the range of the Beilinson fibre square, and that range is stated here.

The source recalls Q_p(n)(R) with the uncompleted Nygaard-filtered Δ_R; by Bhatt–Lurie Proposition 7.4.6 the fibre of φ_n − 1 is unchanged by Nygaard completion, so this is the complex of PR.4/syntomic-complex.

Input from RefinedTraceMethods:RT.3b (Antieau–Mathew–Morrow–Nikolaus, Theorem 6.17 and 6.18–6.21): for p-torsion-free quasisyntomic R, a functorial pullback square in D(Q_p) with top row Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) and bottom row (LΩ_R^{≥n})_{Q_p} → (LΩ_R)_{Q_p}, equivalently a fibre sequence Q_p(n)(R) → Q_p(n)(R/p) → (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R)[1/p]; and for R quasiregular semiperfectoid and n > 0 the right vertical map χ_n is injective (for n = 0 the third term of the fibre sequence vanishes and steps 3-5 are not needed) with image the φ = p^n eigenspace of A_crys(R/p)[1/p] = LΩ_R[1/p], so that up to a nonzero scalar it is the forgetful map. Here LΩ_R is p-completed derived de Rham cohomology over Z_p with its Hodge filtration, and the subscript Q_p means p-completion followed by inversion of p.

Suspension dictionary: the square comes from the pullback square TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p), HC^-(R; Q_p) → HP(R; Q_p) by applying τ_{[2n−1, 2n]}; in cyclic-homology terms the cofibre of TC(R; Q_p) → TC(R/p; Q_p) is Σ^2 HC(R; Q_p), and π_{2n} of it is HC_{2n−2} = (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H)[1/p] for these R. The source's introduction writes the third term as HC(R) with the double suspension suppressed (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E76).
proofSteps: H^0(Q_p(n)(R)) → Δ_R{n}^{φ=1}[1/p] is an isomorphism: a φ-fixed element lies in Fil^n_N because the Nygaard filtration of a quasiregular semiperfectoid ring is the φ-preimage of the I-adic filtration (BS22 Definition 12.1, PR.3/nygaard-filtration-qrsp).

Δ_{R/p} = Δ_R{I/p}, and H^0(Q_p(n)(R/p)) = (Δ_R{I/p}{n})^{φ=1}[1/p] since inverting p kills the Nygaard graded quotients of Δ_{R/p}. The map b: H^0(Q_p(n)(R)) → H^0(Q_p(n)(R/p)) factors as c ∘ a through Δ_R⟨I/p⟩{n}^{φ=1}[1/p], and a, b, c are injective; so it suffices that d ∘ c = 0, where d is the map to H^0((LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R){n}[1/p]) in the exact sequence of the Beilinson fibre square (RT.3b).

By the description of χ_n (RT.3b), d is up to a nonzero scalar the forgetful map Q_p(n)(R/p) → Δ_{R/p}[1/p] ≅ LΩ_R[1/p] followed by the projection; so one must show that ((q − 1)^{-n}Δ_R⟨I/p⟩)^{φ=1}[1/p] maps into (q − 1)^{-n}Fil^n_H LΩ_R[1/p].

Frobenius induces an injection (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H LΩ_R)[1/p] → B_dR^+(R)/I^n: φ gives Δ_R/Fil^n_N → Δ_R/I^n injective, and (Δ_R/Fil^n_N)[1/p] ≅ (LΩ_R/Fil^n_H)[1/p] by the filtered absolute de Rham comparison (Bhatt–Lurie §5.4, Proposition 5.5.12; PR.5/absolute-nygaard-filtration). Dividing by (q − 1)^n, whose image under φ generates I·B_dR^+(R), gives an injection into I^{-n}B_dR^+(R)/B_dR^+(R).

On φ-fixed elements this injection is induced by the natural map (q − 1)^{-n}Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] → I^{-n}B_dR^+(R) (node period-sheaves-qrsp, Lemma 6.7), which lands in B_dR^+(R) because q − 1 is a unit there; so the composite is zero.
acceptance: R = O_C: both sides are one-dimensional over Q_p, equal to Q_p(n) as G_K-modules.
R = O_C: the sequence 0 → Q_p(n) → (B_crys^+)^{φ=p^n} → B_dR^+/Fil^n → 0 is the fundamental exact sequence (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.1/fundamental-exact-sequence), which checks the suspension dictionary.
For R = O_C and n ≥ 1 the map c is not surjective: its cokernel is B_dR^+/Fil^n.

nodes.title: Boundedness of descent data at the boundary of the open unit disc
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK; R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, and q_1, q_2 ∈ Δ_R are the images of q ∈ A_inf under the two structure maps. (A) (the source's Lemma 6.9) (1) Δ_R[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} → Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} is an isomorphism on H^0. (2) (q_1−1)(q_2−1) is invertible in Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩[1/p]. (3) 0 → Δ_R → Δ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩ ⊕ Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ → Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p, (q_1−1)^p/p⟩ → 0 is exact. (B) (the source's Proposition 6.10) Let M ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf) and suppose M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) is given a descent datum with respect to Y → X, that is a lift to Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]). Then the descent datum extends uniquely to M[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(A_inf[1/p]): the isomorphism α_{⟨I/p⟩}: p_1^*M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] over Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is the base change of a unique isomorphism α: p_1^*M[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M[1/p] over Δ_R[1/p], and α is φ-equivariant and satisfies the cocycle condition.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
M is an F-crystal over A_inf = Δ_{O_C} (a finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module); the descent datum is given only over the rational localisation with p inverted.
The rings Δ_R⟨f/g⟩ are p-completed (resp. (q_1−1)-completed) rational localisations as in the source: Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ = (Δ_R[z]/(z(q_1−1)^p − p))^∧_{(q_1−1)}.
proofSteps: (A1): Δ_R{2n} ≅ (q_1−1)^{-n}(q_2−1)^{-n}Δ_R by base change of Δ_{O_C}{n} ≅ (q−1)^{-n}Δ_{O_C} along the two maps; pass to the colimit over n and apply node tate-twist-analytic-continuation to the twists.

(A2): q_1 − 1 is invertible because (q_1−1)^p divides p. For q_2 − 1 show A = Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩/(q_2−1) is an F_p-algebra: [p]_{q_1} = u·[p]_{q_2} for a unit u (Δ_R is a prismatic envelope of A_inf ⊗ A_inf), and [p]_{q_i} ≡ (q_i−1)^{p−1} modulo p, so (q_1−1)^p = p(q_1−1)x modulo (q_2−1); then z(q_1−1)^p − p = p(ε − 1) with ε = z(q_1−1)x topologically nilpotent, so p = 0 in A.

(A3): for Z_p[u] the Mayer–Vietoris sequence of the blow-up at (p, u) is 0 → Z_p[u] → Z_p[u][u/p] ⊕ Z_p[u][p/u] → Z_p[u][p/u, u/p] → 0; base change it (p, u)-completely along the (p, u)-completely flat map Z_p[u] → A_inf → Δ_R, u ↦ (q_1−1)^p; the terms stay discrete.

(B): it suffices to show α_{⟨I/p⟩} carries p_1^*M[1/p] into p_2^*M[1/p] (apply the same to the inverse); φ-equivariance and the cocycle condition follow because Δ_•[1/p] → Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is injective on X_qrsp. By analytic continuation (node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal (d)) the datum extends over Δ_R⟨φ(I)/p⟩[1/p], hence, since φ(I) ⊂ pΔ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩, to a φ-equivariant map α_1 over Δ_R⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩[1/p].

Trivialise M[1/(q−1)] ≅ T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/(q−1)] φ-equivariantly (node bkf-modules-comparison (2)); in a basis of T the matrix of α_{⟨I/p⟩} has φ-fixed entries in Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))], which lie in Δ_R[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))] by (A1) and so in Δ_R⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩[1/p] by (A2); this defines α_2 there, compatible with α_1 on the overlap. Tensor the sequence (A3)[1/p] with the finite projective module Hom(p_1^*M[1/p], p_2^*M[1/p]) to glue α_1 and α_2 to α.
acceptance: M = A_inf: the descent datum is multiplication by a φ-fixed unit of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p], which lies in Δ_R[1/p].
M = A_inf{1}: in the bases (q_i − 1)^{-1} the datum of the crystal O_Δ{1} is a unit c of Δ_R with φ(c) = c·[p]_{q_2}/[p]_{q_1}.
Without a Frobenius structure the extension fails: a general element of Δ_R⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is not in Δ_R[1/p].

nodes.title: Weak admissibility gives a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK. Let (D, φ_D, Fil^•) be a weakly admissible filtered φ-module over K and M(D)(Y) the F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0} of node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal. Then: (1) the base change M(D)(Y)_ℛ to the Robba ring ℛ of A_inf (Fargues–Fontaine, Definition 1.8.1; the extended Robba ring R̃ of Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley lectures, Definition 13.4.3) is a trivial φ-module; (2) hence it extends, as a φ-module, to the integral Robba ring ℛ^int (R̃^int of Berkeley Definition 12.3.1); (3) hence M(D)(Y) extends to an F-crystal M′ over A_inf, i.e. a finite free Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module M′ with M′⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] ≅ M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}(Y) compatibly with φ for all n ≥ 1. The argument gives existence; it does not establish uniqueness of an integral extension. The prescribed restriction away from p=0 is fixed.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
Weak admissibility is that of PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/weak-admissibility for the filtered φ-module with filtration on D ⊗_{W(k),φ} K.

Inputs from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification (red-team finding RT-AREA-padic-2/30 (b)), cited as the source prints them: Fargues–Fontaine, Courbes et fibrés vectoriels en théorie de Hodge p-adique, Corollary 11.2.22 (φ-modules over ℛ are vector bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve X_FF), Proposition 10.5.6 (weakly admissible implies semistable of slope 0 for the associated bundle), Theorem 8.2.10 (1) (semistable bundles of slope 0 are trivial).
Inputs from AInfCohomology:AI.2: Berkeley lectures Theorem 14.2.1 (F-crystals on Spec(A_inf) and on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {x_k} agree) and the passage from a φ-module over ℛ^int to a φ-bundle near p = 0.

The argument is the A_inf-variant of Kisin's (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4/weakly-admissible-slope-zero), which works over the Robba ring of 𝔖 with Kedlaya's slope filtration; that node is not used here.
proofSteps: Identify φ-modules over ℛ with vector bundles on X_FF (Fargues–Fontaine Corollary 11.2.22) and check that the bundle attached to M(D)(Y)_ℛ is the modification of the bundle E(D, φ_D) at the point ∞ by the lattice Fil^0(D_K ⊗_K B_dR), i.e. the bundle Fargues–Fontaine attach to (D, φ_D, Fil^•): this is the matching of constructions, read off from step (c) of node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal.

By weak admissibility and Fargues–Fontaine Proposition 10.5.6 this bundle is semistable of slope 0; by Theorem 8.2.10 (1) (VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:classification/dieudonne-manin-classification-of-bundles) it is trivial. Hence (1).
A trivial φ-module over ℛ has the φ-stable lattice spanned by a φ-fixed basis over ℛ^int; this gives (2).
Glue M(D)(Y) on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {p = 0} with the φ-module over ℛ^int near p = 0 to an F-crystal on Spa(A_inf) ∖ {x_k}, and extend over the closed point by Berkeley Theorem 14.2.1. This gives (3).
acceptance: D = K_0 with φ and trivial filtration: M′ = A_inf.
D of dimension one with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and filtration jumping at −1 (weakly admissible): M′ = A_inf{1}.
D of dimension one with φ_D = p^{-1}φ and filtration jumping at 0 (not weakly admissible): the bundle on X_FF has degree ±1, so it is not trivial, and M(D)(Y) does not extend over A_inf.

nodes.title: The prismatic F-crystal of a crystalline lattice
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK. For L ∈ Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) let (D, φ_D, Fil^•) be the weakly admissible filtered φ-module attached to L[1/p] (Fontaine's D_crys, in the Frobenius-twisted normalisation of node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal). There is a prismatic F-crystal 𝔐(L) = M(D)_int ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•) ≃ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) such that: (a) 𝔐(L)(A_inf) = M′ is a Breuil–Kisin–Fargues module with M′⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p] ≅ M(D)_{⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩}(Y) for n ≥ 1; (b) the descent datum of 𝔐(L) over Δ_{O_C ⊗̂ O_C} restricts, after inverting p and passing to Δ_•⟨I/p⟩, to that of M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩}; (c) T(𝔐(L)) ≅ L as G_K-representations. The assignment L ↦ 𝔐(L) is functorial and quasi-inverse to the étale realisation.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).

L is a finite free Z_p-module with continuous G_K-action and L[1/p] crystalline; D_crys(L[1/p]) is weakly admissible (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/admissible-implies-weakly-admissible); the converse direction of Colmez–Fontaine is not used.

Step 3 below uses, for R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C, that Δ_{R,perf} is almost isomorphic to Cont(G_K, A_inf); the source asserts this without proof or reference (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E78), and it is recorded as a gap of this stage.
proofSteps: Step 1 (bounded crystal): M(D) (node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal) has value on Y extending to M′ over A_inf (node weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf); by node descent-data-boundedness the descent datum of M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩} extends to M′[1/p], giving M(D)_bdd ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•[1/p]) with M(D)_bdd(Y) = M′[1/p].

Step 2 (Galois-stable lattice): M′[1/I]^∧_p = T ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf[1/I]^∧_p with T finite free over Z_p (node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (4)); after inverting p the left side is the value on Y of a crystal on X, so T[1/p] is a G_K-representation. Choose a G_K-stable lattice L′ ⊂ T[1/p] and modify M′ along {p = 0} ⊂ Spec(A_inf) ∖ {x_k} by Beauville–Laszlo glueing, extending over x_k by node bkf-modules-comparison (4), so that T = L′; then M′ carries a G_K-equivariant structure extending that of M′[1/p].

Step 3 (integrality of the descent datum): α: p_1^*M′[1/p] ≅ p_2^*M′[1/p] carries p_1^*M′ onto p_2^*M′. As (p, I) is a regular sequence in Δ_R (R = O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C), sections of vector bundles extend over V(p, I); the claim is clear after inverting p, and by Beauville–Laszlo glueing it remains to check it over Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p. There Vect^φ(Δ_R[1/I]^∧_p) → Vect^φ(Δ_{R,perf}[1/I]^∧_p) is fully faithful, also after inverting p (node artin-schreier-riemann-hilbert (2)), and Δ_{R,perf} is almost isomorphic to Cont(G_K, A_inf); inverting I and p-completing turns almost isomorphisms into isomorphisms, and the claim becomes the G_K-stability of the lattice M′[1/I]^∧_p.

Step 4 (the lattice is L): steps 1–3 give M(D)_int ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•) with T(M(D)_int) = L′. By the argument of node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal and (b), T(M(D)_int)[1/p] ≅ L[1/p]; repeat step 2 with L′ = L.
Functoriality and the quasi-inverse property follow from full faithfulness (node etale-realization-fully-faithful).
acceptance: 𝔐(Z_p) = O_Δ and 𝔐(Z_p(n)) = O_Δ{n}.
rk 𝔐(L) = rk_{Z_p} L, and 𝔐(L ⊗ L′) ≅ 𝔐(L) ⊗ 𝔐(L′).
For two G_K-stable lattices L ⊂ L′ in the same crystalline representation, 𝔐(L) → 𝔐(L′) is an isomorphism after inverting p and the two differ by a modification along p = 0.

nodes.title: Prismatic F-crystals on O_K are lattices in crystalline representations
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic (0, p) with perfect residue field, X = Spf(O_K), and Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) the category of finite free Z_p-modules T with a continuous G_K-action such that T[1/p] is crystalline. The étale realisation functor T: Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal categories, with quasi-inverse L ↦ 𝔐(L). Under it rank corresponds to rank, O_Δ{n} to Z_p(n), and D_crys(T(E)[1/p]) ≅ E(W(k))[1/p].
hypotheses: K is complete, discretely valued, of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field of characteristic p; the residue field need not be finite.

Coefficients are finite locally free over O_Δ and lattices are finite free over Z_p. The analogue with O_Δ/p-coefficients is false (node mod-p-full-faithfulness-fails), and no classification of torsion or derived Galois representations is claimed; a statement about F-gauges needs a separate source theorem.
In the source this is Theorem 5.6 (Theorem 1.2 of the introduction); the atlas stage text cites the same number.
proofSteps: T takes values in crystalline lattices: node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal.
T is fully faithful: node etale-realization-fully-faithful (descent along Spf(O_C) → Spf(O_K) and the full faithfulness part of Fargues' theorem).

T is essentially surjective, with explicit quasi-inverse: node crystalline-lattice-to-f-crystal, which uses the filtered φ-module construction, the Fargues–Fontaine classification (node weakly-admissible-extension-over-ainf) and the boundedness of descent data (node descent-data-boundedness, resting on the Beilinson fibre square).
Symmetric monoidality is that of node etale-realization.
acceptance: Rank one: invertible prismatic F-crystals on Spf(O_K) correspond to crystalline characters G_K → Z_p^×; O_Δ{n} ↔ χ_cyc^n.

For a proper smooth formal scheme over O_K whose special fibre has torsion-free crystalline cohomology, the F-crystal H^i(R f_* O_Δ) corresponds to the lattice H^i_ét(X_C, Z_p) (the source's Example 4.6 with BMS1 Theorem 14.5).
K = Q_p: End of the unit object is Z_p on both sides.

nodes.title: Full faithfulness of the étale realisation over the Breuil–Kisin prism
nodes.statement: Notation as in OK, with a uniformizer π, the Breuil–Kisin prism (𝔖, (E(u))) and a compatible system π^♭ of p-power roots of π, K_∞ = K(π^{1/p^∞}). (1) 𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p = 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p, a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer p and residue field k((u)). (2) The étale realisation T: Vect^φ(𝔖) → Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p), M ↦ M ⊗_𝔖 𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p, is fully faithful. (3) Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p) ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}): by node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (1) the category is unchanged by passing to the perfection of (𝔖, (E)), which is A_inf of the completion of O_{K_∞}, and Laurent F-crystals over that perfectoid ring are Z_p-representations of the absolute Galois group of the completion of K_∞, which is G_{K_∞}.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).

On effective objects (2) is Kisin's Proposition 2.1.12, which the packet of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory states as R07.4/kisin-etale-full-faithfulness with Kisin's proof (as repaired in his erratum); (3) is there Fontaine's equivalence R07.4/kummer-etale-phi-modules through the field of norms. This node plans the source's independent proof, which uses neither; the two formulations are identified in node kisin-functor-comparison, and the overlap is reported in the restructure record of the stage.

The points and adic spaces used: 𝒴 = Spa(A_inf)^an ∖ {y_crys}, 𝒳 = Spa(𝔖)^an ∖ {x_crys}, π: 𝒴 → 𝒳, y_n = φ^n(y_C) with y_C the Hodge–Tate point, x_n = π(y_n), B = {x_n : n ≥ 1}. For n ≥ 0 the point x_n is 𝔖 → 𝔖 → O_K ⊂ K (first map φ^n); for n < 0 it is 𝔖 → 𝔖/φ^{-n}(E(u))[1/p] (the source prints φ^n; source issue PrismaticCohomology/E74).
proofSteps: Reduction: by internal Hom it suffices that M^{φ=1} → (M[1/E]^∧_p)^{φ=1} is bijective for M ∈ Vect^φ(𝔖); injectivity holds because M is finite free and 𝔖 → 𝔖[1/E]^∧_p is injective.
For α in the target, its image in M ⊗_𝔖 W(C^♭) lies in M ⊗_𝔖 A_inf[1/(q−1)] (BMS1 Lemma 4.26, node bkf-modules-comparison (2), applied to M ⊗_𝔖 A_inf).

Meromorphy (the source's Lemma 7.7): every f ∈ 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p ∩ A_inf[1/(q−1)] ⊂ W(C^♭) is meromorphic over 𝔖 with poles in a finite subset B′ ⊂ B. Ingredients: the classification of points of Spa(A_inf) (Lemma 7.3); finiteness of B′ = {x_m ∈ B : π^{-1}(x_m) is a single point} by a ramification count (Lemma 7.5); if h ∈ A_inf[1/(q−1)] is entire near every y_n, n ≥ 1, then h ∈ A_inf, because ker(A_inf → W(O_C)) = (q−1) (Lemma 7.6; BMS1 Lemma 3.23); Kedlaya's criterion that a function on 𝒳 which is analytic on 𝒴 is analytic (Kedlaya, Slope filtrations revisited, Definition 2.2.13, Lemma 2.3.5, Remark 2.3.8); and 𝔖 = 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p ∩ A_inf, checked modulo p as k[[u]] = k((u)) ∩ O_{C^♭}.

Conclusion: as 𝔖 is a unique factorisation domain, α = β/g with β ∈ M and g ∈ 𝔖 vanishing only at points of B. Iterating the Frobenius, φ_M^r(β ⊗ 1) = (φ^r(g)/g)·β in M[1/I_r], I_r = I·φ(I)⋯φ^{r−1}(I); the ideals I_r are invertible at every x_m, m ≥ 1, and φ^r(g) is invertible at x_m for r large (φ moves a zero at x_k to x_{k−1}); hence α ∈ M^∧_{x_m} for all m ≥ 1 and α ∈ M.

(3): the perfection of (𝔖, (E)) is (A_inf(O), ker θ̃) for O the p-completion of O_K[π^{1/p^∞}] (PR.0/prism-perfection, PR.0/perfect-prisms-perfectoid-rings); apply laurent-f-crystals-local-systems (1), (4), Fontaine–Wintenberger for the perfectoid field (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger) and the equality of the Galois groups of K_∞ and its completion (Krasner; PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation).
acceptance: K = Q_p(p^{1/p}), π = p^{1/p}: f = 1/(u − p) lies in 𝔖⟨p/u^2⟩[1/u] ∩ A_inf[1/(q−1)] and has a simple pole at x_1, so the set B′ is nonempty (the source's Example 7.8); B′ is empty when e(K/K_0) < p.

The analogous statement for A_inf fails: Hom(A_inf{1}, A_inf) = (μA_inf)^{φ=1} = 0 although both realisations are free of rank one over Z_p. Over 𝔖 the realisations of 𝔖{1} and 𝔖 are Z_p(1) and Z_p restricted to G_{K_∞}, with no nonzero map between them; the proof uses that u does not divide a power of q − 1 in A_inf.

nodes.title: Evaluation at the Breuil–Kisin prism: Kisin's full faithfulness theorems
nodes.statement: Notation as in node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism. Let D_𝔖: Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) → Vect^φ(𝔖) be the composite of the quasi-inverse 𝔐 of the étale realisation (node crystalline-lattices-theorem) with evaluation at (𝔖, (E(u))) ∈ X_Δ. (1) D_𝔖 is fully faithful. (2) The composite of D_𝔖 with Vect^φ(𝔖) → Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p) ≃ Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}) is restriction along G_{K_∞} ⊂ G_K; hence the restriction functor Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) → Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}) is fully faithful (Breuil's conjecture, proved by Kisin). (3) Rationally, the composite Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K)[1/p] → Vect^φ(𝔖)[1/p] → Vect^φ(𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) → MF^φ(K), the last functor being the functor 𝒟 below, is Fontaine's D_crys in the Frobenius-twisted normalisation. (4) Dependence on the uniformizer: for uniformizers π, π′ with compatible systems of p-power roots, the maps of prisms (𝔖_π, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃) ← (𝔖_{π′}, (E′)) give D_{𝔖_π}(L) ⊗_{𝔖_π} A_inf ≅ 𝔐(L)(A_inf) ≅ D_{𝔖_{π′}}(L) ⊗_{𝔖_{π′}} A_inf, equivariantly for φ and G_K (Liu's compatibility).
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).
The target Vect^φ(𝔖) depends on π; the equivalence of node crystalline-lattices-theorem does not.

The proof of (1) uses the main theorem, Fontaine's full faithfulness of D_crys and two elementary lemmas of Kisin on Frobenius modules over a disc (Kisin, Crystalline representations and F-crystals, Lemma 1.2.6 and Proposition 1.2.8), which are proved here over 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]; it does not use Kisin's connection N_∇, Kedlaya's slope filtration or the field of norms.
In the version read this statement is Theorem 7.9 (with Corollary 7.10 and Remark 7.12); Theorem 7.2 is node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism.
proofSteps: Faithfulness: (𝔖, (E)) covers the final object of Shv(X_Δ) (node breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers).

The functor 𝒟: Vect^φ(𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p]) → MF^φ(K). For (𝔐, φ_𝔐) put D(𝔐) = 𝔐 ⊗ K_0 along u ↦ 0, an F-isocrystal. Since φ^*𝔐 is a unit φ-module over 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] (φ(E) is invertible there), Dwork's trick gives a unique φ-equivariant isomorphism φ^*D(𝔐) ⊗_{K_0} 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≅ φ^*𝔐 lifting the identity modulo u; base change to 𝔖[1/p]^∧_I[1/I], compose with φ_𝔐 and transport the I-adic filtration of 𝔐 ⊗ 𝔖[1/p]^∧_I to a filtration on D(𝔐) ⊗_{K_0,φ} K. 𝒟 is faithful because it recovers φ^*𝔐, and it is a left inverse of D ↦ M(D)_{⟨I/p⟩}(𝔖) (node filtered-phi-module-to-crystal).

Rational full faithfulness: by the previous step and the construction of 𝔐(L) the composite in (3) is D_crys, which is fully faithful (PadicHodgeTheory:R06.2/dst-exact-tensor-fully-faithful); every functor in the composite is faithful (𝔖 → 𝔖⟨I/p⟩[1/p] is injective), so D_𝔖[1/p] is fully faithful.

Integrality: for α: D_𝔖(L) → D_𝔖(L′) some p^nα = D_𝔖(a); the forgetful functor to Z_p-modules factors through D_𝔖 followed by the étale realisation over 𝔖 (statement (2), which holds by the crystal property for 𝔖 → A_inf and node laurent-f-crystals-local-systems), so a is divisible by p^n as a map of Z_p-modules, hence of representations. This proves (1).

(2): the restriction functor is the composite of D_𝔖, the fully faithful functor of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism (2) and the equivalence (3) there. (4): the crystal property of 𝔐(L) for the two maps of prisms, and the G_K-action on the object (A_inf, ker θ̃).
acceptance: D_𝔖(Z_p) = (𝔖, φ); D_𝔖(Z_p(1)) = 𝔖{1}, free of rank one with Frobenius a unit multiple of E(u)^{-1}φ.
D_𝔖 is not essentially surjective: an object of Vect^φ(𝔖) is in the image exactly when it carries a descent datum over 𝔖^{(1)}.
For K = Q_p and π = p versus π′ = −p the modules D_𝔖(L) differ, but their base changes to A_inf agree.

nodes.title: Comparison with Kisin's modules of finite E-height
nodes.statement: Notation as in node breuil-kisin-evaluation; Kisin's objects are those of the packet of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory (stage R07.4), with Hodge–Tate weights normalised by HT(χ_cyc) = +1. (1) Rings: 𝔖, φ, E(u) are those of R07.4/bk-coefficient-rings, and the ring 𝒪_ℰ there is 𝔖[1/E(u)]^∧_p. Embeddings: R07.4 uses ι_K: 𝔖 → A_inf, u ↦ [π̃], compatible with θ; the map of prisms (𝔖, (E)) → (A_inf, ker θ̃) of node breuil-kisin-and-ainf-covers is ι = φ ∘ ι_K = ι_K ∘ φ_𝔖 (u ↦ [π̃]^p, Frobenius on W(k)). For M ∈ Vect^φ(𝔖), M ⊗_{𝔖,ι} W(C^♭) = φ^*(M ⊗_{𝔖,ι_K} W(C^♭)), and φ_M is a φ- and G_{K_∞}-equivariant isomorphism from it to M ⊗_{𝔖,ι_K} W(C^♭); the étale realisation of PR.7 is identified with Fontaine's functor through this isomorphism. (2) Modules: the effective objects of Vect^φ(𝔖) are the objects of Mod^φ_{/𝔖} (finite free, finite E-height) of R07.4/kisin-modules; every object of Vect^φ(𝔖) becomes effective after replacing φ_M by E(u)^h φ_M, which changes no Hom group. Vect^φ(𝔖[1/E]^∧_p) is the category of finite free étale φ-modules over 𝒪_ℰ, and the equivalence with Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}) of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism (3) is Fontaine's covariant functor of R07.4/kummer-etale-phi-modules; Kisin's contravariant V_𝔖(𝔐) = Hom_{𝔖,φ}(𝔐, 𝔖^ur) is the dual of the étale realisation of 𝔐. Under this dictionary statement (2) of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism, on effective objects, is R07.4/kisin-etale-full-faithfulness. (3) Lattices: for L ∈ Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K), D_𝔖(L) is effective exactly when the Hodge–Tate weights of L[1/p] are ≤ 0; in that case D_𝔖(L) is the 𝔖-lattice of finite E-height in the étale φ-module of L|_{G_{K_∞}}, unique by R07.4/finite-height-lattices (1), so D_𝔖(L) is Kisin's module 𝔐 with V_𝔖(𝔐) ≅ L^∨|_{G_{K_∞}} (R07.4/semistable-finite-height (b) for the lattice L^∨, of weights ≥ 0). For general L twist by O_Δ{n}. (4) Consequently node breuil-kisin-evaluation (1) and (2) are integral forms, for all Hodge–Tate weights, of R07.4/kisin-crystalline-embedding restricted to N = 0 and of R07.4/crystalline-restriction-full-faithfulness.
hypotheses: K is a complete discretely valued field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k of characteristic p, O_K its ring of integers, W = W(k), K_0 = W[1/p], C a completed algebraic closure of K, G_K = Gal(K̄/K); X = Spf(O_K), Y = Spf(O_C). O_K and O_C are W-algebras through the unique Frobenius-equivariant section k → O_K/p (the source's Notation 5.1).

Red-team findings RT-AREA-padic-2/4 and RT-AREA-padic-2/30 (c): the comparison rests on four targets of R07.4, which its packet now states as nodes: the Kummer-tower field of norms and Fontaine's étale φ-module equivalence for G_{K_∞} (kummer-etale-phi-modules), modules of finite E-height (kisin-modules, phi-n-nabla-modules), the slope-zero characterisation of weak admissibility (weakly-admissible-slope-zero), and the lattice functor with full faithfulness of restriction to G_{K_∞} (finite-height-lattices, semistable-finite-height, crystalline-restriction-full-faithfulness). What is still requested from the stage is listed in the requests of this stage.

The source's Remark 7.11 deduces the comparison from "Corollary 7.10"; what the argument uses is the full faithfulness of Vect^φ(𝔖) → Rep_{Z_p}(G_{K_∞}), i.e. Theorem 7.2 (source issue PrismaticCohomology/E75).
R07.4 is not upstream of PR.7 in the atlas; the edge R07.4 → PR.7 is acyclic and is requested.
proofSteps: (1)–(2): E(u) ≡ u^e modulo p, so inverting E(u) and completing p-adically is the same as inverting u and completing. Compare the two descriptions of étale φ-modules: the perfection of 𝔖[1/u]^∧_p is W of the completed perfection of k((u)), which is the tilt of the completion of K_∞, and Fontaine's 𝒪̂_{ℰ^ur} embeds in W(C^♭) compatibly with φ and G_{K_∞}; so (W(C^♭) ⊗ M)^{φ=1} = (𝒪̂_{ℰ^ur} ⊗ M)^{φ=1}.

Effectivity in (3): by node crystalline-representation-of-f-crystal (3) the lattice φ^*M ⊗ B_dR^+ at the Hodge–Tate point is D_dR(L[1/p]) ⊗_K B_dR^+, which lies in L ⊗ B_dR^+ exactly when Fil^0 D_dR = D_dR, i.e. when the weights are ≤ 0; an effective object has finite E-height because φ_M is an isomorphism after inverting E(u).

Identification in (3): D_𝔖(L) and Kisin's module are two 𝔖-lattices of finite E-height in the same étale φ-module, by node breuil-kisin-evaluation (2) and R07.4/semistable-finite-height; they coincide by R07.4/finite-height-lattices (1). Equivalently (the source's Remark 7.11): both functors become restriction to G_{K_∞} after the fully faithful functor of node etale-realization-over-breuil-kisin-prism.
(4) is a restatement under the dictionary.
acceptance: L = Z_p(−1): D_𝔖(L) = 𝔖{−1}, of E-height 1, and Kisin's module of the lattice Z_p(1) of weight 1.

p-divisible groups: for G over O_K the lattice T_p(G)^∨ has Hodge–Tate weights in {−1, 0}, so D_𝔖 of it has E-height at most 1; it is to be compared with the module of R07.4/kisin-p-divisible-classification, up to the duality convention of that node.
The two proofs of full faithfulness of restriction to G_{K_∞} (Kisin's and the prismatic one) have the same statement after inverting p.

nodes.title: Failure of full faithfulness with mod p coefficients
nodes.statement: Let K = Q_p and X = Spf(Z_p). The invertible F-crystal E = O_Δ{p−1}/p ∈ Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ/p) has étale realisation T(E) = Z/p(p−1) ≅ Z/p, the trivial local system, but E is not isomorphic to the unit object O_Δ/p; in fact E ≅ I_Δ^{-1}/p as O_Δ/p-modules, and I_Δ/p is a non-trivial invertible O_Δ/p-module. Hence the étale realisation Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ/p) → Vect(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]/p)^{φ=1} is not fully faithful, and the analogue of node crystalline-lattices-theorem with mod p coefficients is false. More generally the stage makes no claim that finite locally free prismatic F-crystals with torsion or derived coefficients classify torsion or derived Galois representations.
hypotheses: X = Spf(Z_p); any prime p.

The source attributes the failure to the fact that sections of vector bundles on Spec(A_inf/p) change when the closed point is removed, unlike on Spec(A_inf) (Kedlaya), which is what full faithfulness in Fargues' theorem uses.
The Sen-operator computation is quoted by the source from Bhatt–Lurie §3.5 ("one can show"); it is taken from PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor.
proofSteps: T is symmetric monoidal and T(O_Δ{1}) = Z_p(1) (node etale-realization), so T(E) = Z/p(p−1), which is trivial because χ_cyc^{p−1} ≡ 1 modulo p.

O_Δ{p}/p ≅ φ^*O_Δ{1}/p because the Frobenius pullback of an invertible module over an F_p-algebra is its p-th tensor power, and φ^*O_Δ{1} ≅ I_Δ^{-1} ⊗ O_Δ{1} (PR.3/breuil-kisin-twist); hence E = O_Δ{p}/p ⊗ O_Δ{−1}/p ≅ I_Δ^{-1}/p.

I_Δ/p is not trivial: restrict to the Hodge–Tate locus; I_Δ/p ⊗ Ō_Δ/p = Ō_Δ{1}/p carries the Sen operator with weight 1 and Ō_Δ/p with weight 0 (Bhatt–Lurie §3.5; PR.5/hodge-tate-divisor, PR.5/prismatic-crystals-on-wcart), and 1 ≠ 0 in F_p.
acceptance: p = 2: E = O_Δ{1}/2 has trivial realisation Z/2(1) ≅ Z/2 and is not trivial.
With Z_p-coefficients the same twist O_Δ{p−1} is distinguished from O_Δ by its realisation Z_p(p−1).
The correct torsion and derived objects are expected to be perfect complexes on Drinfeld's stack Σ″ (F-gauges), which also record the Nygaard filtration; none is planned in this stage.

nodes.title: Fpqc local surjectivity of Frobenius
nodes.statement: For a δ-ring A and x∈A there is a faithfully flat δ-map A→B and y∈B with φ_B(y)=x. The ring B is the pushout of Z{t}→A, t↦x, and Z{t}→Z{s}, t↦φ(s).
hypotheses: p is prime; no p-torsion-freeness or completion of A is assumed.
proofSteps: Use the free δ-ring universal property to define both maps.
Compute the pushout on underlying rings using delta-ring-category.
The second map is faithfully flat: it is the Frobenius of the free one-generator δ-ring followed by a renaming of generators. Faithful flatness survives base change. The image of s gives y.
acceptance: For x=p in Z_(p), the construction adjoins a Frobenius preimage without requiring one in Z_(p).
This is a local surjectivity assertion, not surjectivity of φ on every δ-ring.

nodes.title: δ and prime power nilpotence
nodes.statement: On Z_(p), if v_p(a)=n>0 then v_p(δ(a))=n−1. In particular δ^n(p^n) is a unit. No nonzero δ-ring has p^n=0 for any n>0.
hypotheses: p is prime; the valuation formula concerns Z_(p), while the nilpotence conclusion concerns all δ-rings.
proofSteps: For a=p^n u with u a p-adic unit, δ(a)=(a−a^p)/p = p^(n−1)u(1−a^(p−1)); the last two factors are units.
Iterate the valuation formula to reach a unit in n steps.
The canonical δ-map Z_(p)→A exists because every integer prime to p becomes a unit if p is nilpotent. It sends δ^n(p^n) to δ^n(0)=0, forcing the zero ring.
acceptance: For p=2, δ(4)=−6 has valuation one and δ²(4)=−21 is odd.
The assertion rules out nonzero rings Z/p^n, including n>1.

nodes.title: Prismatic hyperdescent
nodes.statement: On the flat site of bounded prisms, the assignments (B,J)↦B and (B,J)↦B/J, valued in the respective derived categories, satisfy hyperdescent. A flat hypercover of an object computes its derived sections by totalisation. The same holds on a relative prismatic site and after derived pushforward to the small étale site.
hypotheses: Bounded prisms; finite jointly completely faithfully flat covering families; a universe cut-off is fixed.
The statement uses derived totalisations, not an ordinary equalizer of rings.
proofSteps: The structure sheaves are acyclic on every object by prismatic-structure-sheaf; their derived-section values are therefore the indicated degree-zero rings.

The hyperdescent theorem for derived sections of a sheaf identifies the value on an object with totalisation over any hypercover. Equivalently, the nonnegative cohomological t-structure makes these derived-section sheaves hypercomplete.
Apply the same argument on the category of elements defining the relative site; derived pushforward preserves the relevant limits.
acceptance: The Čech hypercover of a flat cover recovers Corollary 3.12.
The zero prism has the empty covering family and zero derived module of sections.

nodes.title: δ on the Nygaard completion
nodes.statement: For Δ_S of a quasiregular semiperfectoid S over an oriented perfect prism (A,(d)), δ is uniformly continuous for the topology generated by Fil^i_NΔ_S+(p,d)^jΔ_S. It extends uniquely to the Nygaard completion as a δ-structure. It commutes with the extended Frobenius and agrees with δ on Δ_S; this is not an application of δ-adic completion with the Nygaard filtration as an adic ideal.
hypotheses: Δ_S is a δ-ring, derived (p,d)-complete and classically complete by bounded complete flatness.
Fil^i_N=φ^(-1)(d^iΔ_S); d is distinguished.
proofSteps: The product formula gives δ((d)^(i+1))⊂(d)^i and δ((p,d)^(j+1))⊂(p,d)^j.
Use δφ=φδ to get δ(Fil^(i+1)_N)⊂Fil^i_N. The integral addition correction lies in any ideal containing its second argument, so perturbations in Fil^(i+1)_N+(p,d)^(j+1) change δ by Fil^i_N+(p,d)^j.
Extend the resulting uniformly continuous operation to the separated completion. Extend the polynomial δ-identities by continuity; uniqueness follows from density.
acceptance: For S perfectoid, this extension agrees with the complete δ-ring on A_inf(S).
The proof uses filtration estimates, and does not assert that the Nygaard topology is generated by powers of one ideal.

sources.locator: Theorem 13.1, Lemma 13.2 and the proof of Theorem 14.1, §§13–14
sources.match: The completion is the one entering the BMS comparison; the continuity estimate supplies the δ-extension explicitly.
sources.pageReference: Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 94, 97.
sources.proofPages: §13, pp.94–95; proof of Theorem 14.1, pp.100–101. The continuity estimate is supplied by this node rather than attributed to an unstated source lemma.

nodes.title: Étale comparison after perfecting the base
nodes.statement: Let (A,I) be any bounded prism, let f:(A,I)→(A_∞,I_∞) be its completed perfect prism, and let R be a p-completely smooth A/I-algebra. Put R_∞=(R⊗_(A/I)A_∞/I_∞)^∧_p. For n≥1 and a generator d_∞ of I_∞, there is a canonical equivalence RΓ_ét(Spec(R_∞[1/p]),Z/p^n) ≃ ((Δ_(R/A)⊗̂^L_A A_∞)[1/d_∞]/p^n)^(φ=1). This specifies the scalar-extension version for a general base prism. Its étale side is the base-changed algebra R_∞.
hypotheses: The completion of the prism perfection is essential; its raw Frobenius colimit need not be separated.
R is p-completely smooth, so ordinary completed base change gives the derived base-changed algebra.
The right side has the Frobenius transported through the canonical base-change equivalence; it is not an arbitrary endomorphism.
proofSteps: Construct the perfect prism A_∞ using PR.0/prism-perfection; it is bounded by perfect-prism-properties and its ideal is principal.
Apply PR.2/derived-prismatic-base-change (or the smooth PR.1/prismatic-base-change) to identify Δ_(R_∞/A_∞) with completed scalar extension of Δ_(R/A), respecting Frobenius.
Apply PR.4/etale-comparison over the perfect prism A_∞, and substitute the specified equivalence. Localisation at different generators of I_∞ yields the same complex.
Functoriality follows from the universal property of prism perfection and functoriality of both comparison maps.
acceptance: For a perfect base prism, A_∞=A and R_∞=R, giving Theorem 9.1.
For a crystalline base the base-changed R_∞ has characteristic p, its generic fibre is empty, and localising Δ at d_∞=p before reducing modulo p^n gives zero.
Changing d_∞ by a unit has no effect because only localisation at its ideal occurs.

sources.match: Combines prism perfection, smooth derived base change and the perfect-base étale theorem. The scalar-extension variant is derived here; it is not quoted as a theorem over the original generic fibre.
sources.pageReference: Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 4, 31, 56, 71.

nodes.title: Crystalline logarithmic exact sequence
nodes.statement: Let R be a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra and J=ker(R^♭→R). There is a natural exact sequence 0→(1+J)^×→^(log[·])Fil^1_NA_crys(R)→^(φ/p−1)A_crys(R)→0. The first map is the crystalline logarithm of the Teichmüller lift, not a logarithm of an arbitrary unit of R.
hypotheses: Use the canonical PD envelope A_crys(R), its Frobenius, and its Nygaard filtration.
proofSteps: Use p-completeness and p-torsion-freeness of the three groups to reduce exactness modulo p. Isolate the first conjugate-filtration step of A_crys(R)/p and identify its degree-zero quotient with R♭/φ(J).

The divided Frobenius on the quotient of Fil_N^1 by p has a degree-zero piece supplied by multiplication by p. Remove that piece; the remaining exactness problem lies in ker(Fil_1^conj(A/p)→R), with target gr_1^conj(A/p).

Expand log[1−x] modulo p using terms of degrees at most p. On J/J² this induces the crystalline conjugate identification −[x]^p/p. Reduce the remaining logarithm to a homomorphism (1+J²)/(1+φ(J))→J²/φ(J).

For injectivity choose a finitely generated ideal K⊆J with x∈K². Vanishing of the logarithm modulo p improves x modulo φ(J) to successively higher powers of K; K^(pm)⊆φ(K) for m generators finishes the argument.

For surjectivity reduce to products uv in J². On their nilpotent principal ideal modulo φ(J), the truncated logarithm has linear coefficient one; its compositional inverse recovers every such product. Lift exactness back p-adically.
acceptance: For R perfect, J=0 and φ/p−1:pW(R)→W(R) is bijective via multiplication by p followed by 1−pφ^(-1).
The nontrivial kernel for a semiperfect quotient consists of lifted units 1+J, not all units of R^♭.

sources.match: The theorem identifies both the logarithmic kernel and the surjection by divided Frobenius.
sources.pageReference: Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 167.

nodes.title: Crystalline first Chern class as a syntomic fibre
nodes.statement: For a quasisyntomic F_p-scheme X there is a natural fibre sequence RΓ_ét(X,G_m)^∧_p[−1]→^(c_1^crys)Fil^1_NRΓ_crys(X)→^(φ/p−1)RΓ_crys(X). The first Chern class gives the canonical weight-one comparison.
hypotheses: The crystalline complex is the canonical derived crystalline complex; the left side is untruncated étale G_m cohomology.
proofSteps: Construct the crystalline first Chern class on the quasisyntomic site, compatibly with Frobenius, so it lands in the fibre of φ/p−1 on Fil_N^1 crystalline cohomology.
Both that fibre and the p-completed étale G_m complex shifted by −1 satisfy descent; use a pro-syntomic cover which is simultaneously pro-fppf and quasisyntomic.

On a quasiregular semiperfect F_p-algebra, Proposition 7.2.5 identifies the G_m complex with T_p(R×). Theorem 7.1.1 identifies this with the logarithmic fibre, proving the comparison and its naturality.
acceptance: For a perfect affine ring the chartwise kernel is zero.
Using Pic alone in place of untruncated RΓ_ét(G_m) loses the Brauer contribution and fails on fields with p-primary Brauer classes.

sources.match: Weight-one crystalline syntomic cohomology is identified with p-completed G_m cohomology.
sources.pageReference: Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed pages 175, 176, 177.
sources.proofPages: Construction 7.3.1, Variant 7.3.3 and proof of Theorem 7.3.5, pp.176–177.

nodes.title: Joyal operations and Witt-coordinate identities
nodes.statement: For a δ-ring A, define δ_n(x) as the n-th Witt coordinate of the canonical δ-map w_A:A→W(A). Then δ_0(x)=x, δ_1(x)=δ(x), and φ^n(x)=∑_(i=0)^n p^iδ_i(x)^(p^(n−i)). In the free δ-ring δ_n(x) equals δ^n(x) plus a polynomial in the previous iterates. Thus the free δ-ring is also the polynomial ring on the δ_n(x).
hypotheses: The cofree Witt δ-ring and its canonical unit are those of delta-ring-category; its unresolved proof is inherited explicitly.
The identity is polynomial and therefore valid with p-torsion; division by p^n is used only in the universal torsion-free ring.
proofSteps: Take the coordinates of w_A and compute its n-th ghost component. Since w_A is a δ-map, that component is φ^n(x).
In the universal torsion-free free δ-ring, recursively solve the ghost identities to obtain δ_n=δ^n plus lower iterates. The leading coefficient is one.
Evaluate the resulting integral universal polynomials in any δ-ring; triangularity gives the alternative algebraically independent generators.
acceptance: The n=0 and n=1 identities recover x and δ(x).
At p=2,n=2, φ²(x)=x⁴+2δ(x)²+4δ_2(x); δ_2 need not equal δ∘δ.

sources.match: Witt coordinates supply the higher operations and the triangular change of generators.
sources.pageReference: Numbered statement headings in the specified arXiv PDF, printed page 16.

nodes.title: Cyclotomic chart and its Hodge–Tate torsor
nodes.statement: Write q=1+t and p̃=∑_(e∈F_p)q^[e] in Z_p[[t]], where [e] is the Teichmüller representative. Then (p̃)=([p]_q), Z_p[[t]]^(F_p^×)=Z_p[[p̃]], and (Z_p[[p̃]],(p̃)) is a transversal prism. Its Hodge–Tate point is isomorphic to the canonical point η:Spf Z_p→WCart^HT. Choosing this isomorphism trivializes the G_m^♯-torsor after every perfect-prism base change; choices differ by G_m^♯(Z_p)=(1+pZ_p)^×.
hypotheses: The F_p^× action is through Teichmüller units by q↦q^u. The torsor trivialization is a choice, not a canonical identity.
The chart and torsor identification work also at p=2; the separate fully faithful quotient calculation of BL Theorem 3.8.3 requires odd p and is not asserted here.
proofSteps: Each q^[e] differs from q^e by a multiple of q^p−1; therefore p̃=[p]_q(1+t f) with the last factor a unit.
Invariants under F_p^× are exact because p−1 is invertible. Modulo p̃ they are Z_p, and completeness gives Z_p[[p̃]] (BL Corollary 3.8.8).

The Witt lift of the cyclotomic quotient sends p̃ to V(1): applying F gives p and p-torsion-freeness forces the coefficient to be 1. Descend the resulting Hodge–Tate-point isomorphism under F_p^× (BL Proposition 3.8.12).
Base change the isomorphism to a perfect prism; the Hodge–Tate gerbe description and G_m^♯ classify its trivialization and ambiguity.
acceptance: A chosen torsor trivialization changes under multiplication by a G_m^♯ point; no uniqueness is claimed.

sources.locator: Notation 3.8.1; Proposition 3.8.6; Corollary 3.8.8; Proposition 3.8.12 and Warning 3.8.13, §3.8
sources.match: The invariant cyclotomic prism gives the explicit Hodge–Tate torsor used in Lemma 5.6.14.
